ffserver - ffserver video server 

<h2>Synopsis</h2>ffserver [<i>options</i>]
<h2>Description</h2><b>ffserver</b> is a streaming server for both audio and video. It supports several live feeds, streaming from files and time shifting on live feeds. You can seek to positions in the past on each live feed, provided you specify a big enough feed storage. 

 <b>ffserver</b> is configured through a configuration file, which is read at startup. If not explicitly specified, it will read from <i>/etc/ffserver.conf</i>. 

 <b>ffserver</b> receives prerecorded files or <font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> streams from some <b>ffmpeg</b> instance as input, then streams them over <font SIZE="-1">RTP/RTSP/HTTP.</font> 

 An <b>ffserver</b> instance will listen on some port as specified in the configuration file. You can launch one or more instances of <b>ffmpeg</b> and send one or more <font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> streams to the port where ffserver is expecting to receive them. Alternately, you can make <b>ffserver</b> launch such <b>ffmpeg</b> instances at startup. 

 Input streams are called feeds, and each one is specified by a <tt>&quot;&lt;Feed&gt;&quot;</tt> section in the configuration file. 

 For each feed you can have different output streams in various formats, each one specified by a <tt>&quot;&lt;Stream&gt;&quot;</tt> section in the configuration file.
<h2>Detailed Description</h2><b>ffserver</b> works by forwarding streams encoded by <b>ffmpeg</b>, or pre-recorded streams which are read from disk. 

 Precisely, <b>ffserver</b> acts as an <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server, accepting <font SIZE="-1">POST</font> requests from <b>ffmpeg</b> to acquire the stream to publish, and serving <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> clients or <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> clients <font SIZE="-1">GET</font> requests with the stream media content. 

 A feed is an <font SIZE="-1"><b>FFM</b></font> stream created by <b>ffmpeg</b>, and sent to a port where <b>ffserver</b> is listening. 

 Each feed is identified by a unique name, corresponding to the name of the resource published on <b>ffserver</b>, and is configured by a dedicated <tt>&quot;Feed&quot;</tt> section in the configuration file. 

 The feed publish <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> is given by: 

 <pre> http://&lt;ffserver_ip_address&gt;:&lt;http_port&gt;/&lt;feed_name&gt;</pre>where <i>ffserver_ip_address</i> is the <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address of the machine where <b>ffserver</b> is installed, <i>http_port</i> is the port number of the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server (configured through the <b>HTTPPort</b> option), and <i>feed_name</i> is the name of the corresponding feed defined in the configuration file. 

 Each feed is associated to a file which is stored on disk. This stored file is used to send pre-recorded data to a player as fast as possible when new content is added in real-time to the stream. 

 A ``live-stream'' or ``stream'' is a resource published by <b>ffserver</b>, and made accessible through the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> protocol to clients. 

 A stream can be connected to a feed, or to a file. In the first case, the published stream is forwarded from the corresponding feed generated by a running instance of <b>ffmpeg</b>, in the second case the stream is read from a pre-recorded file. 

 Each stream is identified by a unique name, corresponding to the name of the resource served by <b>ffserver</b>, and is configured by a dedicated <tt>&quot;Stream&quot;</tt> section in the configuration file. 

 The stream access <font SIZE="-1">HTTP URL</font> is given by: 

 <pre> http://&lt;ffserver_ip_address&gt;:&lt;http_port&gt;/&lt;stream_name&gt;[&lt;options&gt;]</pre>The stream access <font SIZE="-1">RTSP URL</font> is given by: 

 <pre> http://&lt;ffserver_ip_address&gt;:&lt;rtsp_port&gt;/&lt;stream_name&gt;[&lt;options&gt;]</pre><i>stream_name</i> is the name of the corresponding stream defined in the configuration file. <i>options</i> is a list of options specified after the <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> which affects how the stream is served by <b>ffserver</b>. <i>http_port</i> and <i>rtsp_port</i> are the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> and <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> ports configured with the options <i>HTTPPort</i> and <i>RTSPPort</i> respectively. 

 In case the stream is associated to a feed, the encoding parameters must be configured in the stream configuration. They are sent to <b>ffmpeg</b> when setting up the encoding. This allows <b>ffserver</b> to define the encoding parameters used by the <b>ffmpeg</b> encoders. 

 The <b>ffmpeg</b> <b>override_ffserver</b> commandline option allows one to override the encoding parameters set by the server. 

 Multiple streams can be connected to the same feed. 

 For example, you can have a situation described by the following graph: 

 <pre> _________ __________
 | | | |
 ffmpeg 1 -----| feed 1 |-----| stream 1 |
 \ |_________|\ |__________|
 \ \
 \ \ __________
 \ \ | |
 \ \| stream 2 |
 \ |__________|
 \
 \ _________ __________
 \ | | | |
 \| feed 2 |-----| stream 3 |
 |_________| |__________|
 
 _________ __________
 | | | |
 ffmpeg 2 -----| feed 3 |-----| stream 4 |
 |_________| |__________|
 
 _________ __________
 | | | |
 | file 1 |-----| stream 5 |
 |_________| |__________|</pre><h3><font SIZE="-1">FFM, FFM2</font> formats</h3><font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> and <font SIZE="-1">FFM2</font> are formats used by ffserver. They allow storing a wide variety of video and audio streams and encoding options, and can store a moving time segment of an infinite movie or a whole movie. 

 <font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> is version specific, and there is limited compatibility of <font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> files generated by one version of ffmpeg/ffserver and another version of ffmpeg/ffserver. It may work but it is not guaranteed to work. 

 <font SIZE="-1">FFM2</font> is extensible while maintaining compatibility and should work between differing versions of tools. <font SIZE="-1">FFM2</font> is the default.
<h3>Status stream</h3><b>ffserver</b> supports an <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> interface which exposes the current status of the server. 

 Simply point your browser to the address of the special status stream specified in the configuration file. 

 For example if you have: 

 <pre> &lt;Stream status.html&gt;
 Format status
 
 # Only allow local people to get the status
 ACL allow localhost
 ACL allow 192.168.0.0 192.168.255.255
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre>then the server will post a page with the status information when the special stream <i>status.html</i> is requested.
<h3>How do I make it work?</h3>As a simple test, just run the following two command lines where <font SIZE="-1">INPUTFILE</font> is some file which you can decode with ffmpeg: 

 <pre> ffserver -f doc/ffserver.conf &amp;
 ffmpeg -i INPUTFILE <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:8090/feed1.ffm">http://localhost:8090/feed1.ffm</a></pre>At this point you should be able to go to your Windows machine and fire up Windows Media Player (<font SIZE="-1">WMP</font>). Go to Open <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> and enter 

 <pre> http://&lt;linuxbox&gt;:8090/test.asf</pre>You should (after a short delay) see video and hear audio. 

 <font SIZE="-1">WARNING:</font> trying to stream test1.mpg doesn't work with <font SIZE="-1">WMP</font> as it tries to transfer the entire file before starting to play. The same is true of <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> files. 

 You should edit the <i>ffserver.conf</i> file to suit your needs (in terms of frame rates etc). Then install <b>ffserver</b> and <b>ffmpeg</b>, write a script to start them up, and off you go.
<h3>What else can it do?</h3>You can replay video from .ffm files that was recorded earlier. However, there are a number of caveats, including the fact that the ffserver parameters must match the original parameters used to record the file. If they do not, then ffserver deletes the file before recording into it. (Now that I write this, it seems broken). 

 You can fiddle with many of the codec choices and encoding parameters, and there are a bunch more parameters that you cannot control. Post a message to the mailing list if there are some 'must have' parameters. Look in ffserver.conf for a list of the currently available controls. 

 It will automatically generate the <font SIZE="-1">ASX</font> or <font SIZE="-1">RAM</font> files that are often used in browsers. These files are actually redirections to the underlying <font SIZE="-1">ASF</font> or <font SIZE="-1">RM</font> file. The reason for this is that the browser often fetches the entire file before starting up the external viewer. The redirection files are very small and can be transferred quickly. [The stream itself is often 'infinite' and thus the browser tries to download it and never finishes.]
<h3>Tips</h3>* When you connect to a live stream, most players (<font SIZE="-1">WMP, RA,</font> etc) want to buffer a certain number of seconds of material so that they can display the signal continuously. However, ffserver (by default) starts sending data in realtime. This means that there is a pause of a few seconds while the buffering is being done by the player. The good news is that this can be cured by adding a '?buffer=5' to the end of the <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font> This means that the stream should start 5 seconds in the past --- and so the first 5 seconds of the stream are sent as fast as the network will allow. It will then slow down to real time. This noticeably improves the startup experience. 

 You can also add a 'Preroll 15' statement into the ffserver.conf that will add the 15 second prebuffering on all requests that do not otherwise specify a time. In addition, ffserver will skip frames until a key_frame is found. This further reduces the startup delay by not transferring data that will be discarded.
<h3>Why does the ?buffer / Preroll stop working after a time?</h3>It turns out that (on my machine at least) the number of frames successfully grabbed is marginally less than the number that ought to be grabbed. This means that the timestamp in the encoded data stream gets behind realtime. This means that if you say 'Preroll 10', then when the stream gets 10 or more seconds behind, there is no Preroll left. 

 Fixing this requires a change in the internals of how timestamps are handled.
<h3>Does the ?date= stuff work.</h3>Yes (subject to the limitation outlined above). Also note that whenever you start ffserver, it deletes the ffm file (if any parameters have changed), thus wiping out what you had recorded before. 

 The format of the <tt>&quot;?date=xxxxxx&quot;</tt> is fairly flexible. You should use one of the following formats (the 'T' is literal): 

 <pre> * YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (localtime)
 * YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (UTC)</pre>You can omit the YYYY-MM-DD, and then it refers to the current day. However note that <b>?date=16:00:00</b> refers to 16:00 on the current day --- this may be in the future and so is unlikely to be useful. 

 You use this by adding the ?date= to the end of the <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> for the stream. For example: <b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://localhost:8080/test.asf?date=2002-07-26T23:05:00">http://localhost:8080/test.asf?date=2002-07-26T23:05:00</a></b>.
<h2>Options</h2>All the numerical options, if not specified otherwise, accept a string representing a number as input, which may be followed by one of the <font SIZE="-1">SI</font> unit prefixes, for example: 'K', 'M', or 'G'. 

 If 'i' is appended to the <font SIZE="-1">SI</font> unit prefix, the complete prefix will be interpreted as a unit prefix for binary multiples, which are based on powers of 1024 instead of powers of 1000. Appending 'B' to the <font SIZE="-1">SI</font> unit prefix multiplies the value by 8. This allows using, for example: '<font SIZE="-1">KB</font>', 'MiB', 'G' and 'B' as number suffixes. 

 Options which do not take arguments are boolean options, and set the corresponding value to true. They can be set to false by prefixing the option name with ``no''. For example using ``-nofoo'' will set the boolean option with name ``foo'' to false.
<h3>Stream specifiers</h3>Some options are applied per-stream, e.g. bitrate or codec. Stream specifiers are used to precisely specify which stream(s) a given option belongs to. 

 A stream specifier is a string generally appended to the option name and separated from it by a colon. E.g. <tt>&quot;-codec:a:1 ac3&quot;</tt> contains the <tt>&quot;a:1&quot;</tt> stream specifier, which matches the second audio stream. Therefore, it would select the ac3 codec for the second audio stream. 

 A stream specifier can match several streams, so that the option is applied to all of them. E.g. the stream specifier in <tt>&quot;-b:a 128k&quot;</tt> matches all audio streams. 

 An empty stream specifier matches all streams. For example, <tt>&quot;-codec copy&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;-codec: copy&quot;</tt> would copy all the streams without reencoding. 

 Possible forms of stream specifiers are:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>stream_index</i>
<dd>Matches the stream with this index. E.g. <tt>&quot;-threads:1 4&quot;</tt> would set the thread count for the second stream to 4.
<dt><i>stream_type</i><b>[:</b><i>stream_index</i><b>]</b>
<dd><i>stream_type</i> is one of following: 'v' or 'V' for video, 'a' for audio, 's' for subtitle, 'd' for data, and 't' for attachments. 'v' matches all video streams, 'V' only matches video streams which are not attached pictures, video thumbnails or cover arts. If <i>stream_index</i> is given, then it matches stream number <i>stream_index</i> of this type. Otherwise, it matches all streams of this type.
<dt><b>p:</b><i>program_id</i><b>[:</b><i>stream_index</i><b>]</b>
<dd>If <i>stream_index</i> is given, then it matches the stream with number <i>stream_index</i> in the program with the id <i>program_id</i>. Otherwise, it matches all streams in the program.
<dt><b>#</b><i>stream_id</i> <b>or i:</b><i>stream_id</i>
<dd>Match the stream by stream id (e.g. <font SIZE="-1">PID</font> in MPEG-TS container).
<dt><b>m:</b><i>key</i><b>[:</b><i>value</i><b>]</b>
<dd>Matches streams with the metadata tag <i>key</i> having the specified value. If <i>value</i> is not given, matches streams that contain the given tag with any value.
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd>Matches streams with usable configuration, the codec must be defined and the essential information such as video dimension or audio sample rate must be present. 

 Note that in <b>ffmpeg</b>, matching by metadata will only work properly for input files.</dl><h3>Generic options</h3>These options are shared amongst the ff* tools.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-L</b>
<dd>Show license.
<dt><b>-h, -?, -help, --help [</b><i>arg</i><b>]</b>
<dd>Show help. An optional parameter may be specified to print help about a specific item. If no argument is specified, only basic (non advanced) tool options are shown. 

 Possible values of <i>arg</i> are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>long</b>
<dd>Print advanced tool options in addition to the basic tool options.
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd>Print complete list of options, including shared and private options for encoders, decoders, demuxers, muxers, filters, etc.
<dt><b>decoder=</b><i>decoder_name</i>
<dd>Print detailed information about the decoder named <i>decoder_name</i>. Use the <b>-decoders</b> option to get a list of all decoders.
<dt><b>encoder=</b><i>encoder_name</i>
<dd>Print detailed information about the encoder named <i>encoder_name</i>. Use the <b>-encoders</b> option to get a list of all encoders.
<dt><b>demuxer=</b><i>demuxer_name</i>
<dd>Print detailed information about the demuxer named <i>demuxer_name</i>. Use the <b>-formats</b> option to get a list of all demuxers and muxers.
<dt><b>muxer=</b><i>muxer_name</i>
<dd>Print detailed information about the muxer named <i>muxer_name</i>. Use the <b>-formats</b> option to get a list of all muxers and demuxers.
<dt><b>filter=</b><i>filter_name</i>
<dd>Print detailed information about the filter name <i>filter_name</i>. Use the <b>-filters</b> option to get a list of all filters.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-version</b>
<dd>Show version.
<dt><b>-formats</b>
<dd>Show available formats (including devices).
<dt><b>-demuxers</b>
<dd>Show available demuxers.
<dt><b>-muxers</b>
<dd>Show available muxers.
<dt><b>-devices</b>
<dd>Show available devices.
<dt><b>-codecs</b>
<dd>Show all codecs known to libavcodec. 

 Note that the term 'codec' is used throughout this documentation as a shortcut for what is more correctly called a media bitstream format.
<dt><b>-decoders</b>
<dd>Show available decoders.
<dt><b>-encoders</b>
<dd>Show all available encoders.
<dt><b>-bsfs</b>
<dd>Show available bitstream filters.
<dt><b>-protocols</b>
<dd>Show available protocols.
<dt><b>-filters</b>
<dd>Show available libavfilter filters.
<dt><b>-pix_fmts</b>
<dd>Show available pixel formats.
<dt><b>-sample_fmts</b>
<dd>Show available sample formats.
<dt><b>-layouts</b>
<dd>Show channel names and standard channel layouts.
<dt><b>-colors</b>
<dd>Show recognized color names.
<dt><b>-sources</b> <i>device</i><b>[,</b><i>opt1</i><b>=</b><i>val1</i><b>[,</b><i>opt2</i><b>=</b><i>val2</i><b>]...]</b>
<dd>Show autodetected sources of the input device. Some devices may provide system-dependent source names that cannot be autodetected. The returned list cannot be assumed to be always complete. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -sources pulse,server=192.168.0.4</pre><dt><b>-sinks</b> <i>device</i><b>[,</b><i>opt1</i><b>=</b><i>val1</i><b>[,</b><i>opt2</i><b>=</b><i>val2</i><b>]...]</b>
<dd>Show autodetected sinks of the output device. Some devices may provide system-dependent sink names that cannot be autodetected. The returned list cannot be assumed to be always complete. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -sinks pulse,server=192.168.0.4</pre><dt><b>-loglevel [repeat+]</b><i>loglevel</i> <b>| -v [repeat+]</b><i>loglevel</i>
<dd>Set the logging level used by the library. Adding ``repeat+'' indicates that repeated log output should not be compressed to the first line and the ``Last message repeated n times'' line will be omitted. ``repeat'' can also be used alone. If ``repeat'' is used alone, and with no prior loglevel set, the default loglevel will be used. If multiple loglevel parameters are given, using 'repeat' will not change the loglevel. <i>loglevel</i> is a string or a number containing one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>quiet, -8</b>
<dd>Show nothing at all; be silent.
<dt><b>panic, 0</b>
<dd>Only show fatal errors which could lead the process to crash, such as an assertion failure. This is not currently used for anything.
<dt><b>fatal, 8</b>
<dd>Only show fatal errors. These are errors after which the process absolutely cannot continue.
<dt><b>error, 16</b>
<dd>Show all errors, including ones which can be recovered from.
<dt><b>warning, 24</b>
<dd>Show all warnings and errors. Any message related to possibly incorrect or unexpected events will be shown.
<dt><b>info, 32</b>
<dd>Show informative messages during processing. This is in addition to warnings and errors. This is the default value.
<dt><b>verbose, 40</b>
<dd>Same as <tt>&quot;info&quot;</tt>, except more verbose.
<dt><b>debug, 48</b>
<dd>Show everything, including debugging information.
<dt><b>trace, 56</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>By default the program logs to stderr. If coloring is supported by the terminal, colors are used to mark errors and warnings. Log coloring can be disabled setting the environment variable <font SIZE="-1"><b>AV_LOG_FORCE_NOCOLOR</b></font> or <font SIZE="-1"><b>NO_COLOR</b></font>, or can be forced setting the environment variable <font SIZE="-1"><b>AV_LOG_FORCE_COLOR</b></font>. The use of the environment variable <font SIZE="-1"><b>NO_COLOR</b></font> is deprecated and will be dropped in a future FFmpeg version.</dl><dt><b>-report</b>
<dd>Dump full command line and console output to a file named <tt>&quot;</tt>program<tt>-</tt>YYYYMMDD<tt>-</tt>HHMMSS<tt>.log&quot;</tt> in the current directory. This file can be useful for bug reports. It also implies <tt>&quot;-loglevel verbose&quot;</tt>. 

 Setting the environment variable <font SIZE="-1"><b>FFREPORT</b></font> to any value has the same effect. If the value is a ':'-separated key=value sequence, these options will affect the report; option values must be escaped if they contain special characters or the options delimiter ':' (see the ``Quoting and escaping'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual). 

 The following options are recognized:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>file</b>
<dd>set the file name to use for the report; <tt>%p</tt> is expanded to the name of the program, <tt>%t</tt> is expanded to a timestamp, <tt>&quot;%%&quot;</tt> is expanded to a plain <tt>&quot;%&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd>set the log verbosity level using a numerical value (see <tt>&quot;-loglevel&quot;</tt>).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>For example, to output a report to a file named <i>ffreport.log</i> using a log level of <tt>32</tt> (alias for log level <tt>&quot;info&quot;</tt>): 

 <pre> FFREPORT=file=ffreport.log:level=32 ffmpeg -i input output</pre>Errors in parsing the environment variable are not fatal, and will not appear in the report.</dl><dt><b>-hide_banner</b>
<dd>Suppress printing banner. 

 All FFmpeg tools will normally show a copyright notice, build options and library versions. This option can be used to suppress printing this information.
<dt><b>-cpuflags flags (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Allows setting and clearing cpu flags. This option is intended for testing. Do not use it unless you know what you're doing. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -cpuflags -sse+mmx ...
 ffmpeg -cpuflags mmx ...
 ffmpeg -cpuflags 0 ...</pre>Possible flags for this option are:

</dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-opencl_bench</b>
<dd>This option is used to benchmark all available OpenCL devices and print the results. This option is only available when FFmpeg has been compiled with <tt>&quot;--enable-opencl&quot;</tt>. 

 When FFmpeg is configured with <tt>&quot;--enable-opencl&quot;</tt>, the options for the global OpenCL context are set via <b>-opencl_options</b>. See the ``OpenCL Options'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual for the complete list of supported options. Amongst others, these options include the ability to select a specific platform and device to run the OpenCL code on. By default, FFmpeg will run on the first device of the first platform. While the options for the global OpenCL context provide flexibility to the user in selecting the OpenCL device of their choice, most users would probably want to select the fastest OpenCL device for their system. 

 This option assists the selection of the most efficient configuration by identifying the appropriate device for the user's system. The built-in benchmark is run on all the OpenCL devices and the performance is measured for each device. The devices in the results list are sorted based on their performance with the fastest device listed first. The user can subsequently invoke <b>ffmpeg</b> using the device deemed most appropriate via <b>-opencl_options</b> to obtain the best performance for the OpenCL accelerated code. 

 Typical usage to use the fastest OpenCL device involve the following steps. 

 Run the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -opencl_bench</pre>Note down the platform <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> (<i>pidx</i>) and device <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> (<i>didx</i>) of the first i.e. fastest device in the list. Select the platform and device using the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -opencl_options platform_idx=&lt;pidx&gt;:device_idx=&lt;didx&gt; ...</pre><dt><b>-opencl_options options (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set OpenCL environment options. This option is only available when FFmpeg has been compiled with <tt>&quot;--enable-opencl&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>options</i> must be a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> option pairs separated by ':'. See the ``OpenCL Options'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual for the list of supported options.</dl><h3>AVOptions</h3>These options are provided directly by the libavformat, libavdevice and libavcodec libraries. To see the list of available AVOptions, use the <b>-help</b> option. They are separated into two categories:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>generic</b>
<dd>These options can be set for any container, codec or device. Generic options are listed under AVFormatContext options for containers/devices and under AVCodecContext options for codecs.
<dt><b>private</b>
<dd>These options are specific to the given container, device or codec. Private options are listed under their corresponding containers/devices/codecs.</dl>
 

 For example to write an ID3v2.3 header instead of a default ID3v2.4 to an <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> file, use the <b>id3v2_version</b> private option of the <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> muxer: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.flac -id3v2_version 3 out.mp3</pre>All codec AVOptions are per-stream, and thus a stream specifier should be attached to them. 

 Note: the <b>-nooption</b> syntax cannot be used for boolean AVOptions, use <b>-option 0</b>/<b>-option 1</b>. 

 Note: the old undocumented way of specifying per-stream AVOptions by prepending v/a/s to the options name is now obsolete and will be removed soon.
<h3>Main options</h3><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-f</b> <i>configfile</i>
<dd>Read configuration file <i>configfile</i>. If not specified it will read by default from <i>/etc/ffserver.conf</i>.
<dt><b>-n</b>
<dd>Enable no-launch mode. This option disables all the <tt>&quot;Launch&quot;</tt> directives within the various <tt>&quot;&lt;Feed&gt;&quot;</tt> sections. Since <b>ffserver</b> will not launch any <b>ffmpeg</b> instances, you will have to launch them manually.
<dt><b>-d</b>
<dd>Enable debug mode. This option increases log verbosity, and directs log messages to stdout. When specified, the <b>CustomLog</b> option is ignored.</dl><h2>Configuration File Syntax</h2><b>ffserver</b> reads a configuration file containing global options and settings for each stream and feed. 

 The configuration file consists of global options and dedicated sections, which must be introduced by &quot;&lt;<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SECTION_NAME</i></font><i></i> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>ARGS</i></font><i></i>&gt;`` on a separate line and must be terminated by a line in the form ''&lt;/<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SECTION_NAME</i></font><i></i>&gt;&quot;. <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>ARGS</i></font><i></i> is optional. 

 Currently the following sections are recognized: <b>Feed</b>, <b>Stream</b>, <b>Redirect</b>. 

 A line starting with <tt>&quot;#&quot;</tt> is ignored and treated as a comment. 

 Name of options and sections are case-insensitive.
<h3><font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> syntax</h3>An <font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> (Access Control List) specifies the address which are allowed to access a given stream, or to write a given feed. 

 It accepts the following forms
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Allow/deny access to <i>address</i>. 

 <pre> ACL ALLOW &lt;address&gt;
 ACL DENY &lt;address&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Allow/deny access to ranges of addresses from <i>first_address</i> to <i>last_address</i>. 

 <pre> ACL ALLOW &lt;first_address&gt; &lt;last_address&gt;
 ACL DENY &lt;first_address&gt; &lt;last_address&gt;</pre></dl>
 

 You can repeat the <font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> allow/deny as often as you like. It is on a per stream basis. The first match defines the action. If there are no matches, then the default is the inverse of the last <font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> statement. 

 Thus '<font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> allow localhost' only allows access from localhost. '<font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> deny 1.0.0.0 1.255.255.255' would deny the whole of network 1 and allow everybody else.
<h3>Global options</h3><dl COMPACT><dt><b>HTTPPort</b> <i>port_number</i>
<dd><dt><b>Port</b> <i>port_number</i>
<dd><dt><b>RTSPPort</b> <i>port_number</i>
<dd><i>HTTPPort</i> sets the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server listening <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> port number, <i>RTSPPort</i> sets the <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> server listening <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> port number. 

 <i>Port</i> is the equivalent of <i>HTTPPort</i> and is deprecated. 

 You must select a different port from your standard <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> web server if it is running on the same computer. 

 If not specified, no corresponding server will be created.
<dt><b>HTTPBindAddress</b> <i>ip_address</i>
<dd><dt><b>BindAddress</b> <i>ip_address</i>
<dd><dt><b>RTSPBindAddress</b> <i>ip_address</i>
<dd>Set address on which the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP/RTSP</font> server is bound. Only useful if you have several network interfaces. 

 <i>BindAddress</i> is the equivalent of <i>HTTPBindAddress</i> and is deprecated.
<dt><b>MaxHTTPConnections</b> <i>n</i>
<dd>Set number of simultaneous <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> connections that can be handled. It has to be defined <i>before</i> the <b>MaxClients</b> parameter, since it defines the <b>MaxClients</b> maximum limit. 

 Default value is 2000.
<dt><b>MaxClients</b> <i>n</i>
<dd>Set number of simultaneous requests that can be handled. Since <b>ffserver</b> is very fast, it is more likely that you will want to leave this high and use <b>MaxBandwidth</b>. 

 Default value is 5.
<dt><b>MaxBandwidth</b> <i>kbps</i>
<dd>Set the maximum amount of kbit/sec that you are prepared to consume when streaming to clients. 

 Default value is 1000.
<dt><b>CustomLog</b> <i>filename</i>
<dd>Set access log file (uses standard Apache log file format). '-' is the standard output. 

 If not specified <b>ffserver</b> will produce no log. 

 In case the commandline option <b>-d</b> is specified this option is ignored, and the log is written to standard output.
<dt><b>NoDaemon</b>
<dd>Set no-daemon mode. This option is currently ignored since now <b>ffserver</b> will always work in no-daemon mode, and is deprecated.
<dt><b>UseDefaults</b>
<dd><dt><b>NoDefaults</b>
<dd>Control whether default codec options are used for the all streams or not. Each stream may overwrite this setting for its own. Default is <i>UseDefaults</i>. The last occurrence overrides the previous if multiple definitions exist.</dl><h3>Feed section</h3>A Feed section defines a feed provided to <b>ffserver</b>. 

 Each live feed contains one video and/or audio sequence coming from an <b>ffmpeg</b> encoder or another <b>ffserver</b>. This sequence may be encoded simultaneously with several codecs at several resolutions. 

 A feed instance specification is introduced by a line in the form: 

 <pre> &lt;Feed FEED_FILENAME&gt;</pre>where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>FEED_FILENAME</i></font><i></i> specifies the unique name of the <font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> stream. 

 The following options are recognized within a Feed section.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>File</b> <i>filename</i>
<dd><dt><b>ReadOnlyFile</b> <i>filename</i>
<dd>Set the path where the feed file is stored on disk. 

 If not specified, the <i>/tmp/FEED.ffm</i> is assumed, where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>FEED</i></font><i></i> is the feed name. 

 If <b>ReadOnlyFile</b> is used the file is marked as read-only and it will not be deleted or updated.
<dt><b>Truncate</b>
<dd>Truncate the feed file, rather than appending to it. By default <b>ffserver</b> will append data to the file, until the maximum file size value is reached (see <b>FileMaxSize</b> option).
<dt><b>FileMaxSize</b> <i>size</i>
<dd>Set maximum size of the feed file in bytes. 0 means unlimited. The postfixes <tt>&quot;K&quot;</tt> (2^10), <tt>&quot;M&quot;</tt> (2^20), and <tt>&quot;G&quot;</tt> (2^30) are recognized. 

 Default value is 5M.
<dt><b>Launch</b> <i>args</i>
<dd>Launch an <b>ffmpeg</b> command when creating <b>ffserver</b>. 

 <i>args</i> must be a sequence of arguments to be provided to an <b>ffmpeg</b> instance. The first provided argument is ignored, and it is replaced by a path with the same dirname of the <b>ffserver</b> instance, followed by the remaining argument and terminated with a path corresponding to the feed. 

 When the launched process exits, <b>ffserver</b> will launch another program instance. 

 In case you need a more complex <b>ffmpeg</b> configuration, e.g. if you need to generate multiple <font SIZE="-1">FFM</font> feeds with a single <b>ffmpeg</b> instance, you should launch <b>ffmpeg</b> by hand. 

 This option is ignored in case the commandline option <b>-n</b> is specified.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ACL</b></font> <i>spec</i>
<dd>Specify the list of <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address which are allowed or denied to write the feed. Multiple <font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> options can be specified.</dl><h3>Stream section</h3>A Stream section defines a stream provided by <b>ffserver</b>, and identified by a single name. 

 The stream is sent when answering a request containing the stream name. 

 A stream section must be introduced by the line: 

 <pre> &lt;Stream STREAM_NAME&gt;</pre>where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>STREAM_NAME</i></font><i></i> specifies the unique name of the stream. 

 The following options are recognized within a Stream section. 

 Encoding options are marked with the <i>encoding</i> tag, and they are used to set the encoding parameters, and are mapped to libavcodec encoding options. Not all encoding options are supported, in particular it is not possible to set encoder private options. In order to override the encoding options specified by <b>ffserver</b>, you can use the <b>ffmpeg</b> <b>override_ffserver</b> commandline option. 

 Only one of the <b>Feed</b> and <b>File</b> options should be set.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>Feed</b> <i>feed_name</i>
<dd>Set the input feed. <i>feed_name</i> must correspond to an existing feed defined in a <tt>&quot;Feed&quot;</tt> section. 

 When this option is set, encoding options are used to setup the encoding operated by the remote <b>ffmpeg</b> process.
<dt><b>File</b> <i>filename</i>
<dd>Set the filename of the pre-recorded input file to stream. 

 When this option is set, encoding options are ignored and the input file content is re-streamed as is.
<dt><b>Format</b> <i>format_name</i>
<dd>Set the format of the output stream. 

 Must be the name of a format recognized by FFmpeg. If set to <b>status</b>, it is treated as a status stream.
<dt><b>InputFormat</b> <i>format_name</i>
<dd>Set input format. If not specified, it is automatically guessed.
<dt><b>Preroll</b> <i>n</i>
<dd>Set this to the number of seconds backwards in time to start. Note that most players will buffer 5-10 seconds of video, and also you need to allow for a keyframe to appear in the data stream. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>StartSendOnKey</b>
<dd>Do not send stream until it gets the first key frame. By default <b>ffserver</b> will send data immediately.
<dt><b>MaxTime</b> <i>n</i>
<dd>Set the number of seconds to run. This value set the maximum duration of the stream a client will be able to receive. 

 A value of 0 means that no limit is set on the stream duration.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ACL</b></font> <i>spec</i>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">ACL</font> for the stream.
<dt><b>DynamicACL</b> <i>spec</i>
<dd><dt><b>RTSPOption</b> <i>option</i>
<dd><dt><b>MulticastAddress</b> <i>address</i>
<dd><dt><b>MulticastPort</b> <i>port</i>
<dd><dt><b>MulticastTTL</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>NoLoop</b>
<dd><dt><b>FaviconURL</b> <i>url</i>
<dd>Set favicon (favourite icon) for the server status page. It is ignored for regular streams.
<dt><b>Author</b> <i>value</i>
<dd><dt><b>Comment</b> <i>value</i>
<dd><dt><b>Copyright</b> <i>value</i>
<dd><dt><b>Title</b> <i>value</i>
<dd>Set metadata corresponding to the option. All these options are deprecated in favor of <b>Metadata</b>.
<dt><b>Metadata</b> <i>key</i><i>value</i>
<dd>Set metadata value on the output stream.
<dt><b>UseDefaults</b>
<dd><dt><b>NoDefaults</b>
<dd>Control whether default codec options are used for the stream or not. Default is <i>UseDefaults</i> unless disabled globally.
<dt><b>NoAudio</b>
<dd><dt><b>NoVideo</b>
<dd>Suppress audio/video.
<dt><b>AudioCodec</b> <i>codec_name</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set audio codec.
<dt><b>AudioBitRate</b> <i>rate</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate for the audio stream in kbits per second.
<dt><b>AudioChannels</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of audio channels.
<dt><b>AudioSampleRate</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set sampling frequency for audio. When using low bitrates, you should lower this frequency to 22050 or 11025. The supported frequencies depend on the selected audio codec.
<dt><b>AVOptionAudio [</b><i>codec</i><b>:]</b><i>option</i><i>value</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set generic or private option for audio stream. Private option must be prefixed with codec name or codec must be defined before.
<dt><b>AVPresetAudio</b> <i>preset</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set preset for audio stream.
<dt><b>VideoCodec</b> <i>codec_name</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video codec.
<dt><b>VideoBitRate</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate for the video stream in kbits per second.
<dt><b>VideoBitRateRange</b> <i>range</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video bitrate range. 

 A range must be specified in the form <i>minrate</i>-<i>maxrate</i>, and specifies the <b>minrate</b> and <b>maxrate</b> encoding options expressed in kbits per second.
<dt><b>VideoBitRateRangeTolerance</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video bitrate tolerance in kbits per second.
<dt><b>PixelFormat</b> <i>pixel_format</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video pixel format.
<dt><b>Debug</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video <b>debug</b> encoding option.
<dt><b>Strict</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video <b>strict</b> encoding option.
<dt><b>VideoBufferSize</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set ratecontrol buffer size, expressed in <font SIZE="-1">KB.</font>
<dt><b>VideoFrameRate</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of video frames per second.
<dt><b>VideoSize (</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set size of the video frame, must be an abbreviation or in the form <i>W</i>x<i>H</i>. See <b>the Video size section in the </b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a><b>(1) manual</b>. 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;160x128&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>VideoIntraOnly (</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Transmit only intra frames (useful for low bitrates, but kills frame rate).
<dt><b>VideoGopSize</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>If non-intra only, an intra frame is transmitted every VideoGopSize frames. Video synchronization can only begin at an intra frame.
<dt><b>VideoTag</b> <i>tag</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video tag.
<dt><b>VideoHighQuality (</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>Video4MotionVector (</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>BitExact (</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitexact encoding flag.
<dt><b>IdctSimple (</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set simple <font SIZE="-1">IDCT</font> algorithm.
<dt><b>Qscale</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable constant quality encoding, and set video qscale (quantization scale) value, expressed in <i>n</i> <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> units.
<dt><b>VideoQMin</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>VideoQMax</b> <i>n</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video qmin/qmax.
<dt><b>VideoQDiff</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video <b>qdiff</b> encoding option.
<dt><b>LumiMask</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>DarkMask</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <b>lumi_mask</b>/<b>dark_mask</b> encoding options.
<dt><b>AVOptionVideo [</b><i>codec</i><b>:]</b><i>option</i><i>value</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set generic or private option for video stream. Private option must be prefixed with codec name or codec must be defined before.
<dt><b>AVPresetVideo</b> <i>preset</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set preset for video stream. 

 <i>preset</i> must be the path of a preset file.</dl>
 

 <i>Server status stream</i> 

 A server status stream is a special stream which is used to show statistics about the <b>ffserver</b> operations. 

 It must be specified setting the option <b>Format</b> to <b>status</b>.
<h3>Redirect section</h3>A redirect section specifies where to redirect the requested <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> to another page. 

 A redirect section must be introduced by the line: 

 <pre> &lt;Redirect NAME&gt;</pre>where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NAME</i></font><i></i> is the name of the page which should be redirected. 

 It only accepts the option <font SIZE="-1"><b>URL</b></font>, which specify the redirection <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font>
<h2>Stream Examples</h2><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Multipart <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.mjpg&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format mpjpeg
 VideoFrameRate 2
 VideoIntraOnly
 NoAudio
 Strict -1
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Single <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.jpg&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format jpeg
 VideoFrameRate 2
 VideoIntraOnly
 VideoSize 352x240
 NoAudio
 Strict -1
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Flash 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.swf&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format swf
 VideoFrameRate 2
 VideoIntraOnly
 NoAudio
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd><font SIZE="-1">ASF</font> compatible 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.asf&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format asf
 VideoFrameRate 15
 VideoSize 352x240
 VideoBitRate 256
 VideoBufferSize 40
 VideoGopSize 30
 AudioBitRate 64
 StartSendOnKey
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd><font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> audio 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.mp3&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format mp2
 AudioCodec mp3
 AudioBitRate 64
 AudioChannels 1
 AudioSampleRate 44100
 NoVideo
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Ogg Vorbis audio 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.ogg&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Metadata title &quot;Stream title&quot;
 AudioBitRate 64
 AudioChannels 2
 AudioSampleRate 44100
 NoVideo
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Real with audio only at 32 kbits 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.ra&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format rm
 AudioBitRate 32
 NoVideo
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Real with audio and video at 64 kbits 

 <pre> &lt;Stream test.rm&gt;
 Feed feed1.ffm
 Format rm
 AudioBitRate 32
 VideoBitRate 128
 VideoFrameRate 25
 VideoGopSize 25
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>For stream coming from a file: you only need to set the input filename and optionally a new format. 

 <pre> &lt;Stream file.rm&gt;
 File &quot;/usr/local/httpd/htdocs/tlive.rm&quot;
 NoAudio
 &lt;/Stream&gt;
 
 &lt;Stream file.asf&gt;
 File &quot;/usr/local/httpd/htdocs/test.asf&quot;
 NoAudio
 Metadata author &quot;Me&quot;
 Metadata copyright &quot;Super MegaCorp&quot;
 Metadata title &quot;Test stream from disk&quot;
 Metadata comment &quot;Test comment&quot;
 &lt;/Stream&gt;</pre></dl><h2>Syntax</h2>This section documents the syntax and formats employed by the FFmpeg libraries and tools.
<h3>Quoting and escaping</h3>FFmpeg adopts the following quoting and escaping mechanism, unless explicitly specified. The following rules are applied:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd><b>'</b> and <b>\</b> are special characters (respectively used for quoting and escaping). In addition to them, there might be other special characters depending on the specific syntax where the escaping and quoting are employed.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>A special character is escaped by prefixing it with a <b>\</b>.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>All characters enclosed between <b>''</b> are included literally in the parsed string. The quote character <b>'</b> itself cannot be quoted, so you may need to close the quote and escape it.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Leading and trailing whitespaces, unless escaped or quoted, are removed from the parsed string.</dl>
 

 Note that you may need to add a second level of escaping when using the command line or a script, which depends on the syntax of the adopted shell language. 

 The function <tt>&quot;av_get_token&quot;</tt> defined in <i>libavutil/avstring.h</i> can be used to parse a token quoted or escaped according to the rules defined above. 

 The tool <i>tools/ffescape</i> in the FFmpeg source tree can be used to automatically quote or escape a string in a script. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Escape the string <tt>&quot;Crime d'Amour&quot;</tt> containing the <tt>&quot;'&quot;</tt> special character: 

 <pre> Crime d\'Amour</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>The string above contains a quote, so the <tt>&quot;'&quot;</tt> needs to be escaped when quoting it: 

 <pre> 'Crime d'\''Amour'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Include leading or trailing whitespaces using quoting: 

 <pre> ' this string starts and ends with whitespaces '</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Escaping and quoting can be mixed together: 

 <pre> ' The string '\'string\'' is a string '</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>To include a literal <b>\</b> you can use either escaping or quoting: 

 <pre> 'c:\foo' can be written as c:\\foo</pre></dl><h3>Date</h3>The accepted syntax is: 

 <pre> [(YYYY-MM-DD|YYYYMMDD)[T|t| ]]((HH:MM:SS[.m...]]])|(HHMMSS[.m...]]]))[Z]
 now</pre>If the value is ``now'' it takes the current time. 

 Time is local time unless Z is appended, in which case it is interpreted as <font SIZE="-1">UTC.</font> If the year-month-day part is not specified it takes the current year-month-day.
<h3>Time duration</h3>There are two accepted syntaxes for expressing time duration. 

 <pre> [-][&lt;HH&gt;:]&lt;MM&gt;:&lt;SS&gt;[.&lt;m&gt;...]</pre><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>HH</i></font><i></i> expresses the number of hours, <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>MM</i></font><i></i> the number of minutes for a maximum of 2 digits, and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SS</i></font><i></i> the number of seconds for a maximum of 2 digits. The <i>m</i> at the end expresses decimal value for <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SS</i></font><i></i>. 

 <i>or</i> 

 <pre> [-]&lt;S&gt;+[.&lt;m&gt;...]</pre><i>S</i> expresses the number of seconds, with the optional decimal part <i>m</i>. 

 In both expressions, the optional <b>-</b> indicates negative duration. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 The following examples are all valid time duration:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>55</b>
<dd>55 seconds
<dt><b>12:03:45</b>
<dd>12 hours, 03 minutes and 45 seconds
<dt><b>23.189</b>
<dd>23.189 seconds</dl><h3>Video size</h3>Specify the size of the sourced video, it may be a string of the form <i>width</i>x<i>height</i>, or the name of a size abbreviation. 

 The following abbreviations are recognized:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>ntsc</b>
<dd>720x480
<dt><b>pal</b>

<dt><b>uhd2160</b>
<dd>3840x2160
<dt><b>uhd4320</b>
<dd>7680x4320</dl><h3>Video rate</h3>Specify the frame rate of a video, expressed as the number of frames generated per second. It has to be a string in the format <i>frame_rate_num</i>/<i>frame_rate_den</i>, an integer number, a float number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. 

 The following abbreviations are recognized:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>ntsc</b>
<dd>30000/1001
<dt><b>pal</b>
<dd>25/1
<dt><b>qntsc</b>
<dd>30000/1001
<dt><b>qpal</b>
<dd>25/1
<dt><b>sntsc</b>
<dd>30000/1001
<dt><b>spal</b>
<dd>25/1
<dt><b>film</b>
<dd>24/1
<dt><b>ntsc-film</b>
<dd>24000/1001</dl><h3>Ratio</h3>A ratio can be expressed as an expression, or in the form <i>numerator</i>:<i>denominator</i>. 

 Note that a ratio with infinite (1/0) or negative value is considered valid, so you should check on the returned value if you want to exclude those values. 

 The undefined value can be expressed using the ``0:0'' string.
<h3>Color</h3>It can be the name of a color as defined below (case insensitive match) or a <tt>&quot;[0x|#]RRGGBB[AA]&quot;</tt> sequence, possibly followed by @ and a string representing the alpha component. 

 The alpha component may be a string composed by ``0x'' followed by an hexadecimal number or a decimal number between 0.0 and 1.0, which represents the opacity value (<b>0x00</b> or <b>0.0</b> means completely transparent, <b>0xff</b> or <b>1.0</b> completely opaque). If the alpha component is not specified then <b>0xff</b> is assumed. 

 The string <b>random</b> will result in a random color.

<dd>0xF5F5F5
<dt><b>Yellow</b>
<dd>0xFFFF00
<dt><b>YellowGreen</b>
<dd>0x9ACD32</dl><h3>Channel Layout</h3>A channel layout specifies the spatial disposition of the channels in a multi-channel audio stream. To specify a channel layout, FFmpeg makes use of a special syntax. 

 Individual channels are identified by an id, as given by the table below:
<dl COMPACT><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FL</b></font>
<dd>front left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FR</b></font>
<dd>front right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FC</b></font>
<dd>front center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>LFE</b></font>
<dd>low frequency
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BL</b></font>
<dd>back left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BR</b></font>
<dd>back right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FLC</b></font>
<dd>front left-of-center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FRC</b></font>
<dd>front right-of-center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BC</b></font>
<dd>back center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SL</b></font>
<dd>side left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SR</b></font>
<dd>side right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TC</b></font>
<dd>top center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TFL</b></font>
<dd>top front left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TFC</b></font>
<dd>top front center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TFR</b></font>
<dd>top front right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TBL</b></font>
<dd>top back left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TBC</b></font>
<dd>top back center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TBR</b></font>
<dd>top back right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>DL</b></font>
<dd>downmix left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>DR</b></font>
<dd>downmix right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>WL</b></font>
<dd>wide left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>WR</b></font>
<dd>wide right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SDL</b></font>
<dd>surround direct left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SDR</b></font>
<dd>surround direct right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>LFE2</b></font>
<dd>low frequency 2</dl>
 

 Standard channel layout compositions can be specified by using the following identifiers:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mono</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FC</font>
<dt><b>stereo</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR</font>
<dt><b>2.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+LFE</font>
<dt><b>3.0</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC</font>
<dt><b>3.0(back)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+BC</font>
<dt><b>4.0</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BC</font>
<dt><b>quad</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+BL+BR</font>
<dt><b>quad(side)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>3.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE</font>
<dt><b>5.0</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR</font>
<dt><b>5.0(side)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>4.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BC</font>
<dt><b>5.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR</font>
<dt><b>5.1(side)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>6.0</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>6.0(front)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>hexagonal</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+BC</font>
<dt><b>6.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>6.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR+BC</font>
<dt><b>6.1(front)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+LFE+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.0</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.0(front)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.1(wide)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR+FLC+FRC</font>
<dt><b>7.1(wide-side)</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>octagonal</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+BC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>downmix</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">DL+DR</font></dl>
 

 A custom channel layout can be specified as a sequence of terms, separated by '+' or '|'. Each term can be:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>the name of a standard channel layout (e.g. <b>mono</b>, <b>stereo</b>, <b>4.0</b>, <b>quad</b>, <b>5.0</b>, etc.)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>the name of a single channel (e.g. <font SIZE="-1"><b>FL</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>FR</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>FC</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>LFE</b></font>, etc.)
<dt>&bull;
<dd>a number of channels, in decimal, followed by 'c', yielding the default channel layout for that number of channels (see the function <tt>&quot;av_get_default_channel_layout&quot;</tt>). Note that not all channel counts have a default layout.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>a number of channels, in decimal, followed by 'C', yielding an unknown channel layout with the specified number of channels. Note that not all channel layout specification strings support unknown channel layouts.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>a channel layout mask, in hexadecimal starting with ``0x'' (see the <tt>&quot;AV_CH_*&quot;</tt> macros in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.h</i>.</dl>
 

 Before libavutil version 53 the trailing character ``c'' to specify a number of channels was optional, but now it is required, while a channel layout mask can also be specified as a decimal number (if and only if not followed by ``c'' or ``C''). 

 See also the function <tt>&quot;av_get_channel_layout&quot;</tt> defined in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.h</i>.
<h2>Expression Evaluation</h2>When evaluating an arithmetic expression, FFmpeg uses an internal formula evaluator, implemented through the <i>libavutil/eval.h</i> interface. 

 An expression may contain unary, binary operators, constants, and functions. 

 Two expressions <i>expr1</i> and <i>expr2</i> can be combined to form another expression &quot;<i>expr1</i>;<i>expr2</i>&quot;. <i>expr1</i> and <i>expr2</i> are evaluated in turn, and the new expression evaluates to the value of <i>expr2</i>. 

 The following binary operators are available: <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;-&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;*&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;/&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;^&quot;</tt>. 

 The following unary operators are available: <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;-&quot;</tt>. 

 The following functions are available:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>abs(x)</b>
<dd>Compute absolute value of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>acos(x)</b>
<dd>Compute arccosine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>asin(x)</b>
<dd>Compute arcsine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>atan(x)</b>
<dd>Compute arctangent of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>atan2(x, y)</b>
<dd>Compute principal value of the arc tangent of <i>y</i>/<i>x</i>.
<dt><b>between(x, min, max)</b>
<dd>Return 1 if <i>x</i> is greater than or equal to <i>min</i> and lesser than or equal to <i>max</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>bitand(x, y)</b>
<dd><dt><b>bitor(x, y)</b>
<dd>Compute bitwise and/or operation on <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>. 

 The results of the evaluation of <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are converted to integers before executing the bitwise operation. 

 Note that both the conversion to integer and the conversion back to floating point can lose precision. Beware of unexpected results for large numbers (usually 2^53 and larger).
<dt><b>ceil(expr)</b>
<dd>Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> upwards to the nearest integer. For example, ``ceil(1.5)'' is ``2.0''.
<dt><b>clip(x, min, max)</b>
<dd>Return the value of <i>x</i> clipped between <i>min</i> and <i>max</i>.
<dt><b>cos(x)</b>
<dd>Compute cosine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>cosh(x)</b>
<dd>Compute hyperbolic cosine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>eq(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return 1 if <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are equivalent, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>exp(x)</b>
<dd>Compute exponential of <i>x</i> (with base <tt>&quot;e&quot;</tt>, the Euler's number).
<dt><b>floor(expr)</b>
<dd>Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> downwards to the nearest integer. For example, ``floor(-1.5)'' is ``-2.0''.
<dt><b>gauss(x)</b>
<dd>Compute Gauss function of <i>x</i>, corresponding to <tt>&quot;exp(-x*x/2) / sqrt(2*PI)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>gcd(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the greatest common divisor of <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>. If both <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are 0 or either or both are less than zero then behavior is undefined.
<dt><b>gt(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return 1 if <i>x</i> is greater than <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>gte(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return 1 if <i>x</i> is greater than or equal to <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>hypot(x, y)</b>
<dd>This function is similar to the C function with the same name; it returns &quot;sqrt(<i>x</i>*<i>x</i> + <i>y</i>*<i>y</i>)&quot;, the length of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with sides of length <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>, or the distance of the point (<i>x</i>, <i>y</i>) from the origin.
<dt><b>if(x, y)</b>
<dd>Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is non-zero return the result of the evaluation of <i>y</i>, return 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>if(x, y, z)</b>
<dd>Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is non-zero return the evaluation result of <i>y</i>, otherwise the evaluation result of <i>z</i>.
<dt><b>ifnot(x, y)</b>
<dd>Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is zero return the result of the evaluation of <i>y</i>, return 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>ifnot(x, y, z)</b>
<dd>Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is zero return the evaluation result of <i>y</i>, otherwise the evaluation result of <i>z</i>.
<dt><b>isinf(x)</b>
<dd>Return 1.0 if <i>x</i> is +/-INFINITY, 0.0 otherwise.
<dt><b>isnan(x)</b>
<dd>Return 1.0 if <i>x</i> is <font SIZE="-1">NAN, 0.0</font> otherwise.
<dt><b>ld(var)</b>
<dd>Load the value of the internal variable with number <i>var</i>, which was previously stored with st(<i>var</i>, <i>expr</i>). The function returns the loaded value.
<dt><b>lerp(x, y, z)</b>
<dd>Return linear interpolation between <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> by amount of <i>z</i>.
<dt><b>log(x)</b>
<dd>Compute natural logarithm of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>lt(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return 1 if <i>x</i> is lesser than <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>lte(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return 1 if <i>x</i> is lesser than or equal to <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>max(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the maximum between <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>.
<dt><b>min(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the minimum between <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>.
<dt><b>mod(x, y)</b>
<dd>Compute the remainder of division of <i>x</i> by <i>y</i>.
<dt><b>not(expr)</b>
<dd>Return 1.0 if <i>expr</i> is zero, 0.0 otherwise.
<dt><b>pow(x, y)</b>
<dd>Compute the power of <i>x</i> elevated <i>y</i>, it is equivalent to &quot;(<i>x</i>)^(<i>y</i>)&quot;.
<dt><b>print(t)</b>
<dd><dt><b>print(t, l)</b>
<dd>Print the value of expression <i>t</i> with loglevel <i>l</i>. If <i>l</i> is not specified then a default log level is used. Returns the value of the expression printed. 

 Prints t with loglevel l
<dt><b>random(x)</b>
<dd>Return a pseudo random value between 0.0 and 1.0. <i>x</i> is the index of the internal variable which will be used to save the seed/state.
<dt><b>root(expr, max)</b>
<dd>Find an input value for which the function represented by <i>expr</i> with argument <i>ld(0)</i> is 0 in the interval 0..<i>max</i>. 

 The expression in <i>expr</i> must denote a continuous function or the result is undefined. 

 <i>ld(0)</i> is used to represent the function input value, which means that the given expression will be evaluated multiple times with various input values that the expression can access through <tt>ld(0)</tt>. When the expression evaluates to 0 then the corresponding input value will be returned.
<dt><b>round(expr)</b>
<dd>Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> to the nearest integer. For example, ``round(1.5)'' is ``2.0''.
<dt><b>sin(x)</b>
<dd>Compute sine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>sinh(x)</b>
<dd>Compute hyperbolic sine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>sqrt(expr)</b>
<dd>Compute the square root of <i>expr</i>. This is equivalent to &quot;(<i>expr</i>)^.5&quot;.
<dt><b>squish(x)</b>
<dd>Compute expression <tt>&quot;1/(1 + exp(4*x))&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>st(var, expr)</b>
<dd>Store the value of the expression <i>expr</i> in an internal variable. <i>var</i> specifies the number of the variable where to store the value, and it is a value ranging from 0 to 9. The function returns the value stored in the internal variable. Note, Variables are currently not shared between expressions.
<dt><b>tan(x)</b>
<dd>Compute tangent of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>tanh(x)</b>
<dd>Compute hyperbolic tangent of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>taylor(expr, x)</b>
<dd><dt><b>taylor(expr, x, id)</b>
<dd>Evaluate a Taylor series at <i>x</i>, given an expression representing the <tt>&quot;ld(id)&quot;</tt>-th derivative of a function at 0. 

 When the series does not converge the result is undefined. 

 <i>ld(id)</i> is used to represent the derivative order in <i>expr</i>, which means that the given expression will be evaluated multiple times with various input values that the expression can access through <tt>&quot;ld(id)&quot;</tt>. If <i>id</i> is not specified then 0 is assumed. 

 Note, when you have the derivatives at y instead of 0, <tt>&quot;taylor(expr, x-y)&quot;</tt> can be used.
<dt>time<b>(0)</b>
<dd>Return the current (wallclock) time in seconds.
<dt><b>trunc(expr)</b>
<dd>Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> towards zero to the nearest integer. For example, ``trunc(-1.5)'' is ``-1.0''.
<dt><b>while(cond, expr)</b>
<dd>Evaluate expression <i>expr</i> while the expression <i>cond</i> is non-zero, and returns the value of the last <i>expr</i> evaluation, or <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if <i>cond</i> was always false.</dl>
 

 The following constants are available:
<dl COMPACT><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PI</b></font>
<dd>area of the unit disc, approximately 3.14
<dt><b>E</b>
<dd><i><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-exp/">exp</a></i>(1) (Euler's number), approximately 2.718
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PHI</b></font>
<dd>golden ratio (1+<i><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/5-sqrt/">sqrt</a></i>(5))/2, approximately 1.618</dl>
 

 Assuming that an expression is considered ``true'' if it has a non-zero value, note that: 

 <tt>&quot;*&quot;</tt> works like <font SIZE="-1">AND</font> 

 <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt> works like <font SIZE="-1">OR</font> 

 For example the construct: 

 <pre> if (A AND B) then C</pre>is equivalent to: 

 <pre> if(A*B, C)</pre>In your C code, you can extend the list of unary and binary functions, and define recognized constants, so that they are available for your expressions. 

 The evaluator also recognizes the International System unit prefixes. If 'i' is appended after the prefix, binary prefixes are used, which are based on powers of 1024 instead of powers of 1000. The 'B' postfix multiplies the value by 8, and can be appended after a unit prefix or used alone. This allows using for example '<font SIZE="-1">KB</font>', 'MiB', 'G' and 'B' as number postfix. 

 The list of available International System prefixes follows, with indication of the corresponding powers of 10 and of 2.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>10^-24 / 2^-80
<dt><b>z</b>
<dd>10^-21 / 2^-70
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>10^-18 / 2^-60
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd>10^-15 / 2^-50
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd>10^-12 / 2^-40
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd>10^-9 / 2^-30
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd>10^-6 / 2^-20
<dt><b>m</b>
<dd>10^-3 / 2^-10
<dt><b>c</b>
<dd>10^-2
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd>10^-1
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd>10^2
<dt><b>k</b>
<dd>10^3 / 2^10
<dt><b>K</b>
<dd>10^3 / 2^10
<dt><b>M</b>
<dd>10^6 / 2^20
<dt><b>G</b>
<dd>10^9 / 2^30
<dt><b>T</b>
<dd>10^12 / 2^40
<dt><b>P</b>
<dd>10^15 / 2^40
<dt><b>E</b>
<dd>10^18 / 2^50
<dt><b>Z</b>
<dd>10^21 / 2^60
<dt><b>Y</b>
<dd>10^24 / 2^70</dl><h2>Opencl Options</h2>When FFmpeg is configured with <tt>&quot;--enable-opencl&quot;</tt>, it is possible to set the options for the global OpenCL context. 

 The list of supported options follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>build_options</b>
<dd>Set build options used to compile the registered kernels. 

 See reference ``OpenCL Specification Version: 1.2 chapter 5.6.4''.
<dt><b>platform_idx</b>
<dd>Select the index of the platform to run OpenCL code. 

 The specified index must be one of the indexes in the device list which can be obtained with <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -opencl_bench&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;av_opencl_get_device_list()&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>device_idx</b>
<dd>Select the index of the device used to run OpenCL code. 

 The specified index must be one of the indexes in the device list which can be obtained with <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -opencl_bench&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;av_opencl_get_device_list()&quot;</tt>.</dl><h2>Codec Options</h2>libavcodec provides some generic global options, which can be set on all the encoders and decoders. In addition each codec may support so-called private options, which are specific for a given codec. 

 Sometimes, a global option may only affect a specific kind of codec, and may be nonsensical or ignored by another, so you need to be aware of the meaning of the specified options. Also some options are meant only for decoding or encoding. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, or by setting the value explicitly in the <tt>&quot;AVCodecContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use. 

 The list of supported options follow:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate in bits/s. Default value is 200K.
<dt><b>ab</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set audio bitrate (in bits/s). Default value is 128K.
<dt><b>bt</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video bitrate tolerance (in bits/s). In 1-pass mode, bitrate tolerance specifies how far ratecontrol is willing to deviate from the target average bitrate value. This is not related to min/max bitrate. Lowering tolerance too much has an adverse effect on quality.
<dt><b>flags</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video,subtitles</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set generic flags. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>mv4</b>
<dd>Use four motion vector by macroblock (mpeg4).
<dt><b>qpel</b>
<dd>Use 1/4 pel motion compensation.
<dt><b>loop</b>
<dd>Use loop filter.
<dt><b>qscale</b>
<dd>Use fixed qscale.
<dt><b>gmc</b>
<dd>Use gmc.
<dt><b>mv0</b>
<dd>Always try a mb with mv=&lt;0,0&gt;.
<dt><b>input_preserved</b>
<dd><dt><b>pass1</b>
<dd>Use internal 2pass ratecontrol in first pass mode.
<dt><b>pass2</b>
<dd>Use internal 2pass ratecontrol in second pass mode.
<dt><b>gray</b>
<dd>Only decode/encode grayscale.
<dt><b>emu_edge</b>
<dd>Do not draw edges.
<dt><b>psnr</b>
<dd>Set error[?] variables during encoding.
<dt><b>truncated</b>
<dd><dt><b>naq</b>
<dd>Normalize adaptive quantization.
<dt><b>ildct</b>
<dd>Use interlaced <font SIZE="-1">DCT.</font>
<dt><b>low_delay</b>
<dd>Force low delay.
<dt><b>global_header</b>
<dd>Place global headers in extradata instead of every keyframe.
<dt><b>bitexact</b>
<dd>Only write platform-, build- and time-independent data. (except (I)DCT). This ensures that file and data checksums are reproducible and match between platforms. Its primary use is for regression testing.
<dt><b>aic</b>
<dd>Apply H263 advanced intra coding / mpeg4 ac prediction.
<dt><b>cbp</b>
<dd>Deprecated, use mpegvideo private options instead.
<dt><b>qprd</b>
<dd>Deprecated, use mpegvideo private options instead.
<dt><b>ilme</b>
<dd>Apply interlaced motion estimation.
<dt><b>cgop</b>
<dd>Use closed gop.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>me_method</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set motion estimation method. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>zero</b>
<dd>zero motion estimation (fastest)
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd>full motion estimation (slowest)
<dt><b>epzs</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">EPZS</font> motion estimation (default)
<dt><b>esa</b>
<dd>esa motion estimation (alias for full)
<dt><b>tesa</b>
<dd>tesa motion estimation
<dt><b>dia</b>
<dd>dia motion estimation (alias for epzs)
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd>log motion estimation
<dt><b>phods</b>
<dd>phods motion estimation
<dt><b>x1</b>
<dd>X1 motion estimation
<dt><b>hex</b>
<dd>hex motion estimation
<dt><b>umh</b>
<dd>umh motion estimation
<dt><b>iter</b>
<dd>iter motion estimation</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>extradata_size</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Set extradata size.
<dt><b>time_base</b> <i>rational number</i>
<dd>Set codec time base. 

 It is the fundamental unit of time (in seconds) in terms of which frame timestamps are represented. For fixed-fps content, timebase should be <tt>&quot;1 / frame_rate&quot;</tt> and timestamp increments should be identically 1.
<dt><b>g</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the group of picture (<font SIZE="-1">GOP</font>) size. Default value is 12.
<dt><b>ar</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set audio sampling rate (in Hz).
<dt><b>ac</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of audio channels.
<dt><b>cutoff</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set cutoff bandwidth. (Supported only by selected encoders, see their respective documentation sections.)
<dt><b>frame_size</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set audio frame size. 

 Each submitted frame except the last must contain exactly frame_size samples per channel. May be 0 when the codec has <font SIZE="-1">CODEC_CAP_VARIABLE_FRAME_SIZE</font> set, in that case the frame size is not restricted. It is set by some decoders to indicate constant frame size.
<dt><b>frame_number</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Set the frame number.
<dt><b>delay</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>qcomp</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video quantizer scale compression (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>). It is used as a constant in the ratecontrol equation. Recommended range for default rc_eq: 0.0-1.0.
<dt><b>qblur</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set video quantizer scale blur (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).
<dt><b>qmin</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set min video quantizer scale (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>). Must be included between -1 and 69, default value is 2.
<dt><b>qmax</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max video quantizer scale (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>). Must be included between -1 and 1024, default value is 31.
<dt><b>qdiff</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max difference between the quantizer scale (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).
<dt><b>bf</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max number of B frames between non-B-frames. 

 Must be an integer between -1 and 16. 0 means that B-frames are disabled. If a value of -1 is used, it will choose an automatic value depending on the encoder. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>b_qfactor</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set qp factor between P and B frames.
<dt><b>rc_strategy</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set ratecontrol method.
<dt><b>b_strategy</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set strategy to choose between I/P/B-frames.
<dt><b>ps</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> payload size in bytes.
<dt><b>mv_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>header_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>i_tex_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>p_tex_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>i_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>p_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>skip_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>misc_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>frame_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>codec_tag</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>bug</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Workaround not auto detected encoder bugs. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>autodetect</b>
<dd><dt><b>old_msmpeg4</b>
<dd>some old lavc generated msmpeg4v3 files (no autodetection)
<dt><b>xvid_ilace</b>
<dd>Xvid interlacing bug (autodetected if fourcc==XVIX)
<dt><b>ump4</b>
<dd>(autodetected if fourcc==UMP4)
<dt><b>no_padding</b>
<dd>padding bug (autodetected)
<dt><b>amv</b>
<dd><dt><b>ac_vlc</b>
<dd>illegal vlc bug (autodetected per fourcc)
<dt><b>qpel_chroma</b>
<dd><dt><b>std_qpel</b>
<dd>old standard qpel (autodetected per fourcc/version)
<dt><b>qpel_chroma2</b>
<dd><dt><b>direct_blocksize</b>
<dd>direct-qpel-blocksize bug (autodetected per fourcc/version)
<dt><b>edge</b>
<dd>edge padding bug (autodetected per fourcc/version)
<dt><b>hpel_chroma</b>
<dd><dt><b>dc_clip</b>
<dd><dt><b>ms</b>
<dd>Workaround various bugs in microsoft broken decoders.
<dt><b>trunc</b>
<dd>trancated frames</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>lelim</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set single coefficient elimination threshold for luminance (negative values also consider <font SIZE="-1">DC</font> coefficient).
<dt><b>celim</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set single coefficient elimination threshold for chrominance (negative values also consider dc coefficient)
<dt><b>strict</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Specify how strictly to follow the standards. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>very</b>
<dd>strictly conform to an older more strict version of the spec or reference software
<dt><b>strict</b>
<dd>strictly conform to all the things in the spec no matter what consequences
<dt><b>normal</b>
<dd><dt><b>unofficial</b>
<dd>allow unofficial extensions
<dt><b>experimental</b>
<dd>allow non standardized experimental things, experimental (unfinished/work in progress/not well tested) decoders and encoders. Note: experimental decoders can pose a security risk, do not use this for decoding untrusted input.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>b_qoffset</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> offset between P and B frames.
<dt><b>err_detect</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set error detection flags. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>crccheck</b>
<dd>verify embedded CRCs
<dt><b>bitstream</b>
<dd>detect bitstream specification deviations
<dt><b>buffer</b>
<dd>detect improper bitstream length
<dt><b>explode</b>
<dd>abort decoding on minor error detection
<dt><b>ignore_err</b>
<dd>ignore decoding errors, and continue decoding. This is useful if you want to analyze the content of a video and thus want everything to be decoded no matter what. This option will not result in a video that is pleasing to watch in case of errors.
<dt><b>careful</b>
<dd>consider things that violate the spec and have not been seen in the wild as errors
<dt><b>compliant</b>
<dd>consider all spec non compliancies as errors
<dt><b>aggressive</b>
<dd>consider things that a sane encoder should not do as an error</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>has_b_frames</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>block_align</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>mpeg_quant</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> quantizers instead of H.263.
<dt><b>qsquish</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>How to keep quantizer between qmin and qmax (0 = clip, 1 = use differentiable function).
<dt><b>rc_qmod_amp</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set experimental quantizer modulation.
<dt><b>rc_qmod_freq</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set experimental quantizer modulation.
<dt><b>rc_override_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd><dt><b>rc_eq</b> <i>string</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set rate control equation. When computing the expression, besides the standard functions defined in the section 'Expression Evaluation', the following functions are available: bits2qp(bits), qp2bits(qp). Also the following constants are available: iTex pTex tex mv fCode iCount mcVar var isI isP isB avgQP qComp avgIITex avgPITex avgPPTex avgBPTex avgTex.
<dt><b>maxrate</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max bitrate tolerance (in bits/s). Requires bufsize to be set.
<dt><b>minrate</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set min bitrate tolerance (in bits/s). Most useful in setting up a <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> encode. It is of little use elsewise.
<dt><b>bufsize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set ratecontrol buffer size (in bits).
<dt><b>rc_buf_aggressivity</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Currently useless.
<dt><b>i_qfactor</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>

<dd><dt><b>xvidmmx</b>
<dd><dt><b>faani</b>

<dt><b>bf</b>
<dd>forward predicted MVs of B-frames
<dt><b>bb</b>
<dd>backward predicted MVs of B-frames</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>cmp</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>

 Possible values:

<dd><dt><b>mbd</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set macroblock decision algorithm (high quality mode). 

 Possible values:

<dd>use mbcmp (default)

<dt><b>flags2</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>fast</b>
<dd>Allow non spec compliant speedup tricks.
<dt><b>sgop</b>
<dd>Deprecated, use mpegvideo private options instead.
<dt><b>noout</b>
<dd>Skip bitstream encoding.
<dt><b>ignorecrop</b>

<dt><b>local_header</b>
<dd>Place global headers at every keyframe instead of in extradata.
<dt><b>chunks</b>
<dd>Frame data might be split into multiple chunks.
<dt><b>showall</b>
<dd>Show all frames before the first keyframe.
<dt><b>skiprd</b>
<dd>Deprecated, use mpegvideo private options instead.
<dt><b>export_mvs</b>
<dd>Export motion vectors into frame side-data (see <tt>&quot;AV_FRAME_DATA_MOTION_VECTORS&quot;</tt>) for codecs that support it. See also <i>doc/examples/export_mvs.c</i>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>error</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>qns</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Deprecated, use mpegvideo private options instead.

<dd>Set the number of threads to be used, in case the selected codec implementation supports multi-threading. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto, 0</b>
<dd>automatically select the number of threads to set</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>auto</b>.</dl><dt><b>me_threshold</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set motion estimation threshold.

<dd>Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>unknown</b>

<dd><dt><b>aac_ssr</b>
<dd><dt><b>aac_ltp</b>

<dd><dt><b>mpeg2_aac_he</b>
<dd><dt><b>mpeg4_sp</b>
<dd><dt><b>mpeg4_core</b>
<dd><dt><b>mpeg4_main</b>
<dd><dt><b>mpeg4_asp</b>
<dd><dt><b>dts</b>
<dd><dt><b>dts_es</b>
<dd><dt><b>dts_96_24</b>
<dd><dt><b>dts_hd_hra</b>
<dd><dt><b>dts_hd_ma</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>level</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>unknown</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>lowres</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Decode at 1= 1/2, 2=1/4, 3=1/8 resolutions.
<dt><b>skip_threshold</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set frame skip threshold.
<dt><b>skip_factor</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set frame skip factor.
<dt><b>skip_exp</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set frame skip exponent. Negative values behave identical to the corresponding positive ones, except that the score is normalized. Positive values exist primarily for compatibility reasons and are not so useful.

<dd>Set frame skip compare function. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>sad</b>

<dt><b>sse</b>

<dd>sum of absolute <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> transformed differences
