<dd>sum of squared quantization errors (avoid, low quality)
<dt><b>bit</b>
<dd>number of bits needed for the block
<dt><b>rd</b>
<dd>rate distortion optimal, slow
<dt><b>zero</b>
<dd>0
<dt><b>vsad</b>
<dd>sum of absolute vertical differences
<dt><b>vsse</b>
<dd>sum of squared vertical differences
<dt><b>nsse</b>
<dd>noise preserving sum of squared differences

<dd>5/3 wavelet, only used in snow
<dt><b>w97</b>

<dd><dt><b>chroma</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>border_mask</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Increase the quantizer for macroblocks close to borders.
<dt><b>mblmin</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set min macroblock lagrange factor (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).
<dt><b>mblmax</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max macroblock lagrange factor (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).
<dt><b>mepc</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set motion estimation bitrate penalty compensation (1.0 = 256).
<dt><b>skip_loop_filter</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>skip_idct</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>skip_frame</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Make decoder discard processing depending on the frame type selected by the option value. 

 <b>skip_loop_filter</b> skips frame loop filtering, <b>skip_idct</b> skips frame IDCT/dequantization, <b>skip_frame</b> skips decoding. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Discard no frame.
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd>Discard useless frames like 0-sized frames.
<dt><b>noref</b>
<dd>Discard all non-reference frames.
<dt><b>bidir</b>
<dd>Discard all bidirectional frames.
<dt><b>nokey</b>
<dd>Discard all frames excepts keyframes.
<dt><b>all</b>
<dd>Discard all frames.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>default</b>.</dl><dt><b>bidir_refine</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Refine the two motion vectors used in bidirectional macroblocks.
<dt><b>brd_scale</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Downscale frames for dynamic B-frame decision.
<dt><b>keyint_min</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>

<dt><b>refs</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set reference frames to consider for motion compensation.
<dt><b>chromaoffset</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>

<dt><b>request_channel_layout</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,audio</i><b>)</b>

<dd>If used as input parameter, it serves as a hint to the decoder, which color_range the input has. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>tv</b>

<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>log_level_offset</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Set the log level offset.
<dt><b>slices</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Number of slices, used in parallelized encoding.
<dt><b>thread_type</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Select which multithreading methods to use. 

 Use of <b>frame</b> will increase decoding delay by one frame per thread, so clients which cannot provide future frames should not use it. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>slice</b>
<dd>Decode more than one part of a single frame at once. 

 Multithreading using slices works only when the video was encoded with slices.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Decode more than one frame at once.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>slice+frame</b>.</dl><dt><b>audio_service_type</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set audio service type. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>ma</b>
<dd>Main Audio Service
<dt><b>ef</b>
<dd>Effects
<dt><b>vi</b>
<dd>Visually Impaired
<dt><b>hi</b>
<dd>Hearing Impaired
<dt><b>di</b>
<dd>Dialogue
<dt><b>co</b>
<dd>Commentary
<dt><b>em</b>
<dd>Emergency
<dt><b>vo</b>
<dd>Voice Over
<dt><b>ka</b>
<dd>Karaoke</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>request_sample_fmt</b> <i>sample_fmt</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set sample format audio decoders should prefer. Default value is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>pkt_timebase</b> <i>rational number</i>
<dd><dt><b>sub_charenc</b> <i>encoding</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,subtitles</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the input subtitles character encoding.
<dt><b>field_order</b> <i>field_order</i> <b>(</b><i>video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set/override the field order of the video. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>progressive</b>
<dd>Progressive video
<dt><b>tt</b>
<dd>Interlaced video, top field coded and displayed first
<dt><b>bb</b>
<dd>Interlaced video, bottom field coded and displayed first
<dt><b>tb</b>
<dd>Interlaced video, top coded first, bottom displayed first
<dt><b>bt</b>
<dd>Interlaced video, bottom coded first, top displayed first</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>skip_alpha</b> <i>bool</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set to 1 to disable processing alpha (transparency). This works like the <b>gray</b> flag in the <b>flags</b> option which skips chroma information instead of alpha. Default is 0.
<dt><b>codec_whitelist</b> <i>list</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>``,'' separated list of allowed decoders. By default all are allowed.
<dt><b>dump_separator</b> <i>string</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Separator used to separate the fields printed on the command line about the Stream parameters. For example to separate the fields with newlines and indention: 

 <pre> ffprobe -dump_separator &quot;
 &quot; -i ~/videos/matrixbench_mpeg2.mpg</pre><dt><b>max_pixels</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Maximum number of pixels per image. This value can be used to avoid out of memory failures due to large images.
<dt><b>apply_cropping</b> <i>bool</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable cropping if cropping parameters are multiples of the required alignment for the left and top parameters. If the alignment is not met the cropping will be partially applied to maintain alignment. Default is 1 (enabled). Note: The required alignment depends on if <tt>&quot;AV_CODEC_FLAG_UNALIGNED&quot;</tt> is set and the <font SIZE="-1">CPU.</font> <tt>&quot;AV_CODEC_FLAG_UNALIGNED&quot;</tt> cannot be changed from the command line. Also hardware decoders will not apply left/top Cropping.</dl><h2>Decoders</h2>Decoders are configured elements in FFmpeg which allow the decoding of multimedia streams. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported native decoders are enabled by default. Decoders requiring an external library must be enabled manually via the corresponding <tt>&quot;--enable-lib&quot;</tt> option. You can list all available decoders using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-decoders&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the decoders with the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-decoders&quot;</tt> and selectively enable / disable single decoders with the options <tt>&quot;--enable-decoder=</tt>DECODER<tt>&quot;</tt> / <tt>&quot;--disable-decoder=</tt>DECODER<tt>&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-decoders&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of enabled decoders.
<h2>Video Decoders</h2>A description of some of the currently available video decoders follows.
<h3>hevc</h3><font SIZE="-1">HEVC / H.265</font> decoder. 

 Note: the <b>skip_loop_filter</b> option has effect only at level <tt>&quot;all&quot;</tt>.
<h3>rawvideo</h3>Raw video decoder. 

 This decoder decodes rawvideo streams. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>top</b> <i>top_field_first</i>
<dd>Specify the assumed field type of the input video.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-1</b>
<dd>the video is assumed to be progressive (default)
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd>bottom-field-first is assumed
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd>top-field-first is assumed</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h2>Audio Decoders</h2>A description of some of the currently available audio decoders follows.
<h3>ac3</h3><font SIZE="-1">AC-3</font> audio decoder. 

 This decoder implements part of <font SIZE="-1">ATSC A/52:2010</font> and <font SIZE="-1">ETSI TS 102 366,</font> as well as the undocumented RealAudio 3 (a.k.a. dnet). 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AC-3</i></font><i> Decoder Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-drc_scale</b> <i>value</i>
<dd>Dynamic Range Scale Factor. The factor to apply to dynamic range values from the <font SIZE="-1">AC-3</font> stream. This factor is applied exponentially. There are 3 notable scale factor ranges:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>drc_scale == 0</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">DRC</font> disabled. Produces full range audio.
<dt><b>0 &lt; drc_scale &lt;= 1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">DRC</font> enabled. Applies a fraction of the stream <font SIZE="-1">DRC</font> value. Audio reproduction is between full range and full compression.
<dt><b>drc_scale &gt; 1</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">DRC</font> enabled. Applies drc_scale asymmetrically. Loud sounds are fully compressed. Soft sounds are enhanced.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>flac</h3><font SIZE="-1">FLAC</font> audio decoder. 

 This decoder aims to implement the complete <font SIZE="-1">FLAC</font> specification from Xiph. 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>FLAC</i></font><i> Decoder options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-use_buggy_lpc</b>
<dd>The lavc <font SIZE="-1">FLAC</font> encoder used to produce buggy streams with high lpc values (like the default value). This option makes it possible to decode such streams correctly by using lavc's old buggy lpc logic for decoding.</dl><h3>ffwavesynth</h3>Internal wave synthesizer. 

 This decoder generates wave patterns according to predefined sequences. Its use is purely internal and the format of the data it accepts is not publicly documented.
<h3>libcelt</h3>libcelt decoder wrapper. 

 libcelt allows libavcodec to decode the Xiph <font SIZE="-1">CELT</font> ultra-low delay audio codec. Requires the presence of the libcelt headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libcelt&quot;</tt>.
<h3>libgsm</h3>libgsm decoder wrapper. 

 libgsm allows libavcodec to decode the <font SIZE="-1">GSM</font> full rate audio codec. Requires the presence of the libgsm headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libgsm&quot;</tt>. 

 This decoder supports both the ordinary <font SIZE="-1">GSM</font> and the Microsoft variant.
<h3>libilbc</h3>libilbc decoder wrapper. 

 libilbc allows libavcodec to decode the Internet Low Bitrate Codec (iLBC) audio codec. Requires the presence of the libilbc headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libilbc&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following option is supported by the libilbc wrapper.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>enhance</b>
<dd>Enable the enhancement of the decoded audio when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).</dl><h3>libopencore-amrnb</h3>libopencore-amrnb decoder wrapper. 

 libopencore-amrnb allows libavcodec to decode the Adaptive Multi-Rate Narrowband audio codec. Using it requires the presence of the libopencore-amrnb headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopencore-amrnb&quot;</tt>. 

 An FFmpeg native decoder for AMR-NB exists, so users can decode AMR-NB without this library.
<h3>libopencore-amrwb</h3>libopencore-amrwb decoder wrapper. 

 libopencore-amrwb allows libavcodec to decode the Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband audio codec. Using it requires the presence of the libopencore-amrwb headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopencore-amrwb&quot;</tt>. 

 An FFmpeg native decoder for AMR-WB exists, so users can decode AMR-WB without this library.
<h3>libopus</h3>libopus decoder wrapper. 

 libopus allows libavcodec to decode the Opus Interactive Audio Codec. Requires the presence of the libopus headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopus&quot;</tt>. 

 An FFmpeg native decoder for Opus exists, so users can decode Opus without this library.
<h2>Subtitles Decoders</h2><h3>dvbsub</h3><i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>compute_clut</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-1</b>
<dd>Compute clut if no matching <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> is in the stream.
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd>Never compute <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font>
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd>Always compute <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> and override the one provided in the stream.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>dvb_substream</b>
<dd>Selects the dvb substream, or all substreams if -1 which is default.</dl><h3>dvdsub</h3>This codec decodes the bitmap subtitles used in DVDs; the same subtitles can also be found in VobSub file pairs and in some Matroska files. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>palette</b>
<dd>Specify the global palette used by the bitmaps. When stored in VobSub, the palette is normally specified in the index file; in Matroska, the palette is stored in the codec extra-data in the same format as in VobSub. In DVDs, the palette is stored in the <font SIZE="-1">IFO</font> file, and therefore not available when reading from dumped <font SIZE="-1">VOB</font> files. 

 The format for this option is a string containing 16 24-bits hexadecimal numbers (without 0x prefix) separated by comas, for example <tt>&quot;0d00ee, ee450d, 101010, eaeaea, 0ce60b, ec14ed, ebff0b, 0d617a, 7b7b7b, d1d1d1, 7b2a0e, 0d950c, 0f007b, cf0dec, cfa80c, 7c127b&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>ifo_palette</b>
<dd>Specify the <font SIZE="-1">IFO</font> file from which the global palette is obtained. (experimental)
<dt><b>forced_subs_only</b>
<dd>Only decode subtitle entries marked as forced. Some titles have forced and non-forced subtitles in the same track. Setting this flag to <tt>1</tt> will only keep the forced subtitles. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.</dl><h3>libzvbi-teletext</h3>Libzvbi allows libavcodec to decode <font SIZE="-1">DVB</font> teletext pages and <font SIZE="-1">DVB</font> teletext subtitles. Requires the presence of the libzvbi headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libzvbi&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>txt_page</b>
<dd>List of teletext page numbers to decode. You may use the special * string to match all pages. Pages that do not match the specified list are dropped. Default value is *.
<dt><b>txt_chop_top</b>
<dd>Discards the top teletext line. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>txt_format</b>
<dd>Specifies the format of the decoded subtitles. The teletext decoder is capable of decoding the teletext pages to bitmaps or to simple text, you should use ``bitmap'' for teletext pages, because certain graphics and colors cannot be expressed in simple text. You might use ``text'' for teletext based subtitles if your application can handle simple text based subtitles. Default value is bitmap.
<dt><b>txt_left</b>
<dd>X offset of generated bitmaps, default is 0.
<dt><b>txt_top</b>
<dd>Y offset of generated bitmaps, default is 0.
<dt><b>txt_chop_spaces</b>
<dd>Chops leading and trailing spaces and removes empty lines from the generated text. This option is useful for teletext based subtitles where empty spaces may be present at the start or at the end of the lines or empty lines may be present between the subtitle lines because of double-sized teletext characters. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>txt_duration</b>
<dd>Sets the display duration of the decoded teletext pages or subtitles in milliseconds. Default value is 30000 which is 30 seconds.
<dt><b>txt_transparent</b>
<dd>Force transparent background of the generated teletext bitmaps. Default value is 0 which means an opaque background.
<dt><b>txt_opacity</b>
<dd>Sets the opacity (0-255) of the teletext background. If <b>txt_transparent</b> is not set, it only affects characters between a start box and an end box, typically subtitles. Default value is 0 if <b>txt_transparent</b> is set, 255 otherwise.</dl><h2>Encoders</h2>Encoders are configured elements in FFmpeg which allow the encoding of multimedia streams. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported native encoders are enabled by default. Encoders requiring an external library must be enabled manually via the corresponding <tt>&quot;--enable-lib&quot;</tt> option. You can list all available encoders using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-encoders&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the encoders with the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-encoders&quot;</tt> and selectively enable / disable single encoders with the options <tt>&quot;--enable-encoder=</tt>ENCODER<tt>&quot;</tt> / <tt>&quot;--disable-encoder=</tt>ENCODER<tt>&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-encoders&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of enabled encoders.
<h2>Audio Encoders</h2>A description of some of the currently available audio encoders follows.
<h3>aac</h3>Advanced Audio Coding (<font SIZE="-1">AAC</font>) encoder. 

 This encoder is the default <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> encoder, natively implemented into FFmpeg. Its quality is on par or better than libfdk_aac at the default bitrate of 128kbps. This encoder also implements more options, profiles and samplerates than other encoders (with only the AAC-HE profile pending to be implemented) so this encoder has become the default and is the recommended choice. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set bit rate in bits/s. Setting this automatically activates constant bit rate (<font SIZE="-1">CBR</font>) mode. If this option is unspecified it is set to 128kbps.
<dt><b>q</b>
<dd>Set quality for variable bit rate (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>) mode. This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.
<dt><b>cutoff</b>
<dd>Set cutoff frequency. If unspecified will allow the encoder to dynamically adjust the cutoff to improve clarity on low bitrates.
<dt><b>aac_coder</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> encoder coding method. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>twoloop</b>
<dd>Two loop searching (<font SIZE="-1">TLS</font>) method. 

 This method first sets quantizers depending on band thresholds and then tries to find an optimal combination by adding or subtracting a specific value from all quantizers and adjusting some individual quantizer a little. Will tune itself based on whether <b>aac_is</b>, <b>aac_ms</b> and <b>aac_pns</b> are enabled. This is the default choice for a coder.
<dt><b>anmr</b>
<dd>Average noise to mask ratio (<font SIZE="-1">ANMR</font>) trellis-based solution. 

 This is an experimental coder which currently produces a lower quality, is more unstable and is slower than the default twoloop coder but has potential. Currently has no support for the <b>aac_is</b> or <b>aac_pns</b> options. Not currently recommended.
<dt><b>fast</b>
<dd>Constant quantizer method. 

 This method sets a constant quantizer for all bands. This is the fastest of all the methods and has no rate control or support for <b>aac_is</b> or <b>aac_pns</b>. Not recommended.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>aac_ms</b>
<dd>Sets mid/side coding mode. The default value of ``auto'' will automatically use M/S with bands which will benefit from such coding. Can be forced for all bands using the value ``enable'', which is mainly useful for debugging or disabled using ``disable''.
<dt><b>aac_is</b>
<dd>Sets intensity stereo coding tool usage. By default, it's enabled and will automatically toggle <font SIZE="-1">IS</font> for similar pairs of stereo bands if it's beneficial. Can be disabled for debugging by setting the value to ``disable''.
<dt><b>aac_pns</b>
<dd>Uses perceptual noise substitution to replace low entropy high frequency bands with imperceptible white noise during the decoding process. By default, it's enabled, but can be disabled for debugging purposes by using ``disable''.
<dt><b>aac_tns</b>
<dd>Enables the use of a multitap <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> filter which spans through the high frequency bands to hide quantization noise during the encoding process and is reverted by the decoder. As well as decreasing unpleasant artifacts in the high range this also reduces the entropy in the high bands and allows for more bits to be used by the mid-low bands. By default it's enabled but can be disabled for debugging by setting the option to ``disable''.
<dt><b>aac_ltp</b>
<dd>Enables the use of the long term prediction extension which increases coding efficiency in very low bandwidth situations such as encoding of voice or solo piano music by extending constant harmonic peaks in bands throughout frames. This option is implied by profile:a aac_low and is incompatible with aac_pred. Use in conjunction with <b>-ar</b> to decrease the samplerate.
<dt><b>aac_pred</b>
<dd>Enables the use of a more traditional style of prediction where the spectral coefficients transmitted are replaced by the difference of the current coefficients minus the previous ``predicted'' coefficients. In theory and sometimes in practice this can improve quality for low to mid bitrate audio. This option implies the aac_main profile and is incompatible with aac_ltp.
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd>Sets the encoding profile, possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>aac_low</b>
<dd>The default, <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> ``Low-complexity'' profile. Is the most compatible and produces decent quality.
<dt><b>mpeg2_aac_low</b>
<dd>Equivalent to <tt>&quot;-profile:a aac_low -aac_pns 0&quot;</tt>. <font SIZE="-1">PNS</font> was introduced with the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG4</font> specifications.
<dt><b>aac_ltp</b>
<dd>Long term prediction profile, is enabled by and will enable the <b>aac_ltp</b> option. Introduced in <font SIZE="-1">MPEG4.</font>
<dt><b>aac_main</b>
<dd>Main-type prediction profile, is enabled by and will enable the <b>aac_pred</b> option. Introduced in <font SIZE="-1">MPEG2.</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>If this option is unspecified it is set to <b>aac_low</b>.</dl></dl><h3>ac3 and ac3_fixed</h3><font SIZE="-1">AC-3</font> audio encoders. 

 These encoders implement part of <font SIZE="-1">ATSC A/52:2010</font> and <font SIZE="-1">ETSI TS 102 366,</font> as well as the undocumented RealAudio 3 (a.k.a. dnet). 

 The <i>ac3</i> encoder uses floating-point math, while the <i>ac3_fixed</i> encoder only uses fixed-point integer math. This does not mean that one is always faster, just that one or the other may be better suited to a particular system. The floating-point encoder will generally produce better quality audio for a given bitrate. The <i>ac3_fixed</i> encoder is not the default codec for any of the output formats, so it must be specified explicitly using the option <tt>&quot;-acodec ac3_fixed&quot;</tt> in order to use it. 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AC-3</i></font><i> Metadata</i> 

 The <font SIZE="-1">AC-3</font> metadata options are used to set parameters that describe the audio, but in most cases do not affect the audio encoding itself. Some of the options do directly affect or influence the decoding and playback of the resulting bitstream, while others are just for informational purposes. A few of the options will add bits to the output stream that could otherwise be used for audio data, and will thus affect the quality of the output. Those will be indicated accordingly with a note in the option list below. 

 These parameters are described in detail in several publicly-available documents.
<dl COMPACT><dt>*&lt;&lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.atsc.org/cms/standards/a_52-2010.pdf">http://www.atsc.org/cms/standards/a_52-2010.pdf</a></b>&gt;&gt;
<dd><dt>*&lt;&lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.atsc.org/cms/standards/a_54a_with_corr_1.pdf">http://www.atsc.org/cms/standards/a_54a_with_corr_1.pdf</a></b>&gt;&gt;
<dd><dt>*&lt;&lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.dolby.com/uploadedFiles/zz-_Shared_Assets/English_PDFs/Professional/18_Metadata.Guide.pdf">http://www.dolby.com/uploadedFiles/zz-_Shared_Assets/English_PDFs/Professional/18_Metadata.Guide.pdf</a></b>&gt;&gt;
<dd><dt>*&lt;&lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.dolby.com/uploadedFiles/zz-_Shared_Assets/English_PDFs/Professional/46_DDEncodingGuidelines.pdf">http://www.dolby.com/uploadedFiles/zz-_Shared_Assets/English_PDFs/Professional/46_DDEncodingGuidelines.pdf</a></b>&gt;&gt;
<dd></dl>
 

 Metadata Control Options
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-per_frame_metadata</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Allow Per-Frame Metadata. Specifies if the encoder should check for changing metadata for each frame.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd>The metadata values set at initialization will be used for every frame in the stream. (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd>Metadata values can be changed before encoding each frame.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 Downmix Levels
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-center_mixlev</b> <i>level</i>
<dd>Center Mix Level. The amount of gain the decoder should apply to the center channel when downmixing to stereo. This field will only be written to the bitstream if a center channel is present. The value is specified as a scale factor. There are 3 valid values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0.707</b>
<dd>Apply -3dB gain
<dt><b>0.595</b>
<dd>Apply -4.5dB gain (default)
<dt><b>0.500</b>
<dd>Apply -6dB gain</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-surround_mixlev</b> <i>level</i>
<dd>Surround Mix Level. The amount of gain the decoder should apply to the surround channel(s) when downmixing to stereo. This field will only be written to the bitstream if one or more surround channels are present. The value is specified as a scale factor. There are 3 valid values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0.707</b>
<dd>Apply -3dB gain
<dt><b>0.500</b>
<dd>Apply -6dB gain (default)
<dt><b>0.000</b>
<dd>Silence Surround Channel(s)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 Audio Production Information 

 Audio Production Information is optional information describing the mixing environment. Either none or both of the fields are written to the bitstream.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-mixing_level</b> <i>number</i>
<dd>Mixing Level. Specifies peak sound pressure level (<font SIZE="-1">SPL</font>) in the production environment when the mix was mastered. Valid values are 80 to 111, or -1 for unknown or not indicated. The default value is -1, but that value cannot be used if the Audio Production Information is written to the bitstream. Therefore, if the <tt>&quot;room_type&quot;</tt> option is not the default value, the <tt>&quot;mixing_level&quot;</tt> option must not be -1.
<dt><b>-room_type</b> <i>type</i>
<dd>Room Type. Describes the equalization used during the final mixing session at the studio or on the dubbing stage. A large room is a dubbing stage with the industry standard X-curve equalization; a small room has flat equalization. This field will not be written to the bitstream if both the <tt>&quot;mixing_level&quot;</tt> option and the <tt>&quot;room_type&quot;</tt> option have the default values.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>notindicated</b>
<dd>Not Indicated (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>large</b>
<dd>Large Room
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd><dt><b>small</b>
<dd>Small Room</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 Other Metadata Options
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-copyright</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Copyright Indicator. Specifies whether a copyright exists for this audio.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>No Copyright Exists (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Copyright Exists</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-dialnorm</b> <i>value</i>
<dd>Dialogue Normalization. Indicates how far the average dialogue level of the program is below digital 100% full scale (0 dBFS). This parameter determines a level shift during audio reproduction that sets the average volume of the dialogue to a preset level. The goal is to match volume level between program sources. A value of -31dB will result in no volume level change, relative to the source volume, during audio reproduction. Valid values are whole numbers in the range -31 to -1, with -31 being the default.
<dt><b>-dsur_mode</b> <i>mode</i>
<dd>Dolby Surround Mode. Specifies whether the stereo signal uses Dolby Surround (Pro Logic). This field will only be written to the bitstream if the audio stream is stereo. Using this option does <font SIZE="-1"><b>NOT</b></font> mean the encoder will actually apply Dolby Surround processing.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>notindicated</b>
<dd>Not Indicated (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Not Dolby Surround Encoded
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Dolby Surround Encoded</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-original</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Original Bit Stream Indicator. Specifies whether this audio is from the original source and not a copy.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Not Original Source
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Original Source (default)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 <i>Extended Bitstream Information</i> 

 The extended bitstream options are part of the Alternate Bit Stream Syntax as specified in Annex D of the A/52:2010 standard. It is grouped into 2 parts. If any one parameter in a group is specified, all values in that group will be written to the bitstream. Default values are used for those that are written but have not been specified. If the mixing levels are written, the decoder will use these values instead of the ones specified in the <tt>&quot;center_mixlev&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;surround_mixlev&quot;</tt> options if it supports the Alternate Bit Stream Syntax. 

 Extended Bitstream Information - Part 1
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-dmix_mode</b> <i>mode</i>
<dd>Preferred Stereo Downmix Mode. Allows the user to select either Lt/Rt (Dolby Surround) or Lo/Ro (normal stereo) as the preferred stereo downmix mode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>notindicated</b>
<dd>Not Indicated (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>ltrt</b>
<dd>Lt/Rt Downmix Preferred
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd><dt><b>loro</b>
<dd>Lo/Ro Downmix Preferred</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-ltrt_cmixlev</b> <i>level</i>
<dd>Lt/Rt Center Mix Level. The amount of gain the decoder should apply to the center channel when downmixing to stereo in Lt/Rt mode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>1.414</b>
<dd>Apply +3dB gain
<dt><b>1.189</b>
<dd>Apply +1.5dB gain
<dt><b>1.000</b>
<dd>Apply 0dB gain
<dt><b>0.841</b>
<dd>Apply -1.5dB gain
<dt><b>0.707</b>
<dd>Apply -3.0dB gain
<dt><b>0.595</b>
<dd>Apply -4.5dB gain (default)
<dt><b>0.500</b>
<dd>Apply -6.0dB gain
<dt><b>0.000</b>
<dd>Silence Center Channel</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-ltrt_surmixlev</b> <i>level</i>
<dd>Lt/Rt Surround Mix Level. The amount of gain the decoder should apply to the surround channel(s) when downmixing to stereo in Lt/Rt mode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0.841</b>
<dd>Apply -1.5dB gain
<dt><b>0.707</b>
<dd>Apply -3.0dB gain
<dt><b>0.595</b>
<dd>Apply -4.5dB gain
<dt><b>0.500</b>
<dd>Apply -6.0dB gain (default)
<dt><b>0.000</b>
<dd>Silence Surround Channel(s)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-loro_cmixlev</b> <i>level</i>
<dd>Lo/Ro Center Mix Level. The amount of gain the decoder should apply to the center channel when downmixing to stereo in Lo/Ro mode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>1.414</b>
<dd>Apply +3dB gain
<dt><b>1.189</b>
<dd>Apply +1.5dB gain
<dt><b>1.000</b>
<dd>Apply 0dB gain
<dt><b>0.841</b>
<dd>Apply -1.5dB gain
<dt><b>0.707</b>
<dd>Apply -3.0dB gain
<dt><b>0.595</b>
<dd>Apply -4.5dB gain (default)
<dt><b>0.500</b>
<dd>Apply -6.0dB gain
<dt><b>0.000</b>
<dd>Silence Center Channel</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-loro_surmixlev</b> <i>level</i>
<dd>Lo/Ro Surround Mix Level. The amount of gain the decoder should apply to the surround channel(s) when downmixing to stereo in Lo/Ro mode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0.841</b>
<dd>Apply -1.5dB gain
<dt><b>0.707</b>
<dd>Apply -3.0dB gain
<dt><b>0.595</b>
<dd>Apply -4.5dB gain
<dt><b>0.500</b>
<dd>Apply -6.0dB gain (default)
<dt><b>0.000</b>
<dd>Silence Surround Channel(s)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 Extended Bitstream Information - Part 2
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-dsurex_mode</b> <i>mode</i>
<dd>Dolby Surround <font SIZE="-1">EX</font> Mode. Indicates whether the stream uses Dolby Surround <font SIZE="-1">EX</font> (7.1 matrixed to 5.1). Using this option does <font SIZE="-1"><b>NOT</b></font> mean the encoder will actually apply Dolby Surround <font SIZE="-1">EX</font> processing.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>notindicated</b>
<dd>Not Indicated (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Dolby Surround <font SIZE="-1">EX</font> Off
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Dolby Surround <font SIZE="-1">EX</font> On</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-dheadphone_mode</b> <i>mode</i>
<dd>Dolby Headphone Mode. Indicates whether the stream uses Dolby Headphone encoding (multi-channel matrixed to 2.0 for use with headphones). Using this option does <font SIZE="-1"><b>NOT</b></font> mean the encoder will actually apply Dolby Headphone processing.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>notindicated</b>
<dd>Not Indicated (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Dolby Headphone Off
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Dolby Headphone On</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-ad_conv_type</b> <i>type</i>
<dd>A/D Converter Type. Indicates whether the audio has passed through <font SIZE="-1">HDCD A/D</font> conversion.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>standard</b>
<dd>Standard A/D Converter (default)
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>hdcd</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">HDCD A/D</font> Converter</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 <i>Other </i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AC-3</i></font><i> Encoding Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-stereo_rematrixing</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Stereo Rematrixing. Enables/Disables use of rematrixing for stereo input. This is an optional <font SIZE="-1">AC-3</font> feature that increases quality by selectively encoding the left/right channels as mid/side. This option is enabled by default, and it is highly recommended that it be left as enabled except for testing purposes.
<dt><b>cutoff</b> <i>frequency</i>
<dd>Set lowpass cutoff frequency. If unspecified, the encoder selects a default determined by various other encoding parameters.</dl>
 

 <i>Floating-Point-Only </i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AC-3</i></font><i> Encoding Options</i> 

 These options are only valid for the floating-point encoder and do not exist for the fixed-point encoder due to the corresponding features not being implemented in fixed-point.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-channel_coupling</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Enables/Disables use of channel coupling, which is an optional <font SIZE="-1">AC-3</font> feature that increases quality by combining high frequency information from multiple channels into a single channel. The per-channel high frequency information is sent with less accuracy in both the frequency and time domains. This allows more bits to be used for lower frequencies while preserving enough information to reconstruct the high frequencies. This option is enabled by default for the floating-point encoder and should generally be left as enabled except for testing purposes or to increase encoding speed.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-1</b>
<dd><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Selected by Encoder (default)
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Disable Channel Coupling
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Enable Channel Coupling</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>-cpl_start_band</b> <i>number</i>
<dd>Coupling Start Band. Sets the channel coupling start band, from 1 to 15. If a value higher than the bandwidth is used, it will be reduced to 1 less than the coupling end band. If <i>auto</i> is used, the start band will be determined by the encoder based on the bit rate, sample rate, and channel layout. This option has no effect if channel coupling is disabled.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-1</b>
<dd><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Selected by Encoder (default)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>flac</h3><font SIZE="-1">FLAC</font> (Free Lossless Audio Codec) Encoder 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by FFmpeg's flac encoder.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>compression_level</b>
<dd>Sets the compression level, which chooses defaults for many other options if they are not set explicitly. Valid values are from 0 to 12, 5 is the default.
<dt><b>frame_size</b>
<dd>Sets the size of the frames in samples per channel.
<dt><b>lpc_coeff_precision</b>
<dd>Sets the <font SIZE="-1">LPC</font> coefficient precision, valid values are from 1 to 15, 15 is the default.
<dt><b>lpc_type</b>
<dd>Sets the first stage <font SIZE="-1">LPC</font> algorithm
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">LPC</font> is not used
<dt><b>fixed</b>
<dd>fixed <font SIZE="-1">LPC</font> coefficients
<dt><b>levinson</b>
<dd><dt><b>cholesky</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>lpc_passes</b>
<dd>Number of passes to use for Cholesky factorization during <font SIZE="-1">LPC</font> analysis
<dt><b>min_partition_order</b>
<dd>The minimum partition order
<dt><b>max_partition_order</b>
<dd>The maximum partition order
<dt><b>prediction_order_method</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>estimation</b>
<dd><dt><b>2level</b>
<dd><dt><b>4level</b>
<dd><dt><b>8level</b>
<dd><dt><b>search</b>
<dd>Bruteforce search
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>ch_mode</b>
<dd>Channel mode
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>The mode is chosen automatically for each frame
<dt><b>indep</b>
<dd>Channels are independently coded
<dt><b>left_side</b>
<dd><dt><b>right_side</b>
<dd><dt><b>mid_side</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>exact_rice_parameters</b>
<dd>Chooses if rice parameters are calculated exactly or approximately. if set to 1 then they are chosen exactly, which slows the code down slightly and improves compression slightly.
<dt><b>multi_dim_quant</b>
<dd>Multi Dimensional Quantization. If set to 1 then a 2nd stage <font SIZE="-1">LPC</font> algorithm is applied after the first stage to finetune the coefficients. This is quite slow and slightly improves compression.</dl><h3>opus</h3>Opus encoder. 

 This is a native FFmpeg encoder for the Opus format. Currently its in development and only implements the <font SIZE="-1">CELT</font> part of the codec. Its quality is usually worse and at best is equal to the libopus encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set bit rate in bits/s. If unspecified it uses the number of channels and the layout to make a good guess.
<dt><b>opus_delay</b>
<dd>Sets the maximum delay in milliseconds. Lower delays than 20ms will very quickly decrease quality.</dl><h3>libfdk_aac</h3>libfdk-aac <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> (Advanced Audio Coding) encoder wrapper. 

 The libfdk-aac library is based on the Fraunhofer <font SIZE="-1">FDK AAC</font> code from the Android project. 

 Requires the presence of the libfdk-aac headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libfdk-aac&quot;</tt>. The library is also incompatible with <font SIZE="-1">GPL,</font> so if you allow the use of <font SIZE="-1">GPL,</font> you should configure with <tt>&quot;--enable-gpl --enable-nonfree --enable-libfdk-aac&quot;</tt>. 

 This encoder is considered to produce output on par or worse at 128kbps to the <b>the native FFmpeg </b><font SIZE="-1"><b>AAC</b></font><b> encoder</b> but can often produce better sounding audio at identical or lower bitrates and has support for the AAC-HE profiles. 

 <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> encoding, enabled through the <b>vbr</b> or <b>flags +qscale</b> options, is experimental and only works with some combinations of parameters. 

 Support for encoding 7.1 audio is only available with libfdk-aac 0.1.3 or higher. 

 For more information see the fdk-aac project at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://sourceforge.net/p/opencore-amr/fdk-aac/">http://sourceforge.net/p/opencore-amr/fdk-aac/</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are mapped on the shared FFmpeg codec options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set bit rate in bits/s. If the bitrate is not explicitly specified, it is automatically set to a suitable value depending on the selected profile. 

 In case <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode is enabled the option is ignored.
<dt><b>ar</b>
<dd>Set audio sampling rate (in Hz).
<dt><b>channels</b>
<dd>Set the number of audio channels.
<dt><b>flags +qscale</b>
<dd>Enable fixed quality, <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> (Variable Bit Rate) mode. Note that <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> is implicitly enabled when the <b>vbr</b> value is positive.
<dt><b>cutoff</b>
<dd>Set cutoff frequency. If not specified (or explicitly set to 0) it will use a value automatically computed by the library. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd>Set audio profile. 

 The following profiles are recognized:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>aac_low</b>
<dd>Low Complexity <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> (<font SIZE="-1">LC</font>)
<dt><b>aac_he</b>
<dd>High Efficiency <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> (HE-AAC)
<dt><b>aac_he_v2</b>
<dd>High Efficiency <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> version 2 (HE-AACv2)
<dt><b>aac_ld</b>
<dd>Low Delay <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> (<font SIZE="-1">LD</font>)
<dt><b>aac_eld</b>
<dd>Enhanced Low Delay <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> (<font SIZE="-1">ELD</font>)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>If not specified it is set to <b>aac_low</b>.</dl></dl>
 

 The following are private options of the libfdk_aac encoder.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>afterburner</b>
<dd>Enable afterburner feature if set to 1, disabled if set to 0. This improves the quality but also the required processing power. 

 Default value is 1.
<dt><b>eld_sbr</b>
<dd>Enable <font SIZE="-1">SBR</font> (Spectral Band Replication) for <font SIZE="-1">ELD</font> if set to 1, disabled if set to 0. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>signaling</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">SBR/PS</font> signaling style. 

 It can assume one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>default</b>
<dd>choose signaling implicitly (explicit hierarchical by default, implicit if global header is disabled)
<dt><b>implicit</b>
<dd>implicit backwards compatible signaling
<dt><b>explicit_sbr</b>
<dd>explicit <font SIZE="-1">SBR,</font> implicit <font SIZE="-1">PS</font> signaling
<dt><b>explicit_hierarchical</b>
<dd>explicit hierarchical signaling</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>default</b>.</dl><dt><b>latm</b>
<dd>Output <font SIZE="-1">LATM/LOAS</font> encapsulated data if set to 1, disabled if set to 0. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>header_period</b>
<dd>Set StreamMuxConfig and <font SIZE="-1">PCE</font> repetition period (in frames) for sending in-band configuration buffers within <font SIZE="-1">LATM/LOAS</font> transport layer. 

 Must be a 16-bits non-negative integer. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>vbr</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode, from 1 to 5. 1 is lowest quality (though still pretty good) and 5 is highest quality. A value of 0 will disable <font SIZE="-1">VBR,</font> and <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> (Constant Bit Rate) is enabled. 

 Currently only the <b>aac_low</b> profile supports <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> encoding. 

 <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> modes 1-5 correspond to roughly the following average bit rates:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>1</b>
<dd>32 kbps/channel
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd>40 kbps/channel
<dt><b>3</b>
<dd>48-56 kbps/channel
<dt><b>4</b>
<dd>64 kbps/channel
<dt><b>5</b>
<dd>about 80-96 kbps/channel</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is 0.</dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to convert an audio file to <font SIZE="-1">VBR AAC</font> in an M4A (<font SIZE="-1">MP4</font>) container: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.wav -codec:a libfdk_aac -vbr 3 output.m4a</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to convert an audio file to <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> 64k kbps <font SIZE="-1">AAC,</font> using the High-Efficiency <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> profile: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.wav -c:a libfdk_aac -profile:a aac_he -b:a 64k output.m4a</pre></dl><h3>libmp3lame</h3><font SIZE="-1">LAME</font> (Lame Ain't an <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> Encoder) <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libmp3lame headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libmp3lame&quot;</tt>. 

 See <b>libshine</b> for a fixed-point <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> encoder, although with a lower quality. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libmp3lame wrapper. The <b>lame</b>-equivalent of the options are listed in parentheses.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>-b</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate expressed in bits/s for <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> or <font SIZE="-1">ABR. LAME</font> <tt>&quot;bitrate&quot;</tt> is expressed in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>q (</b><i>-V</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set constant quality setting for <font SIZE="-1">VBR.</font> This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.
<dt><b>compression_level (</b><i>-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set algorithm quality. Valid arguments are integers in the 0-9 range, with 0 meaning highest quality but slowest, and 9 meaning fastest while producing the worst quality.
<dt><b>cutoff (</b><i>--lowpass</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set lowpass cutoff frequency. If unspecified, the encoder dynamically adjusts the cutoff.
<dt><b>reservoir</b>
<dd>Enable use of bit reservoir when set to 1. Default value is 1. <font SIZE="-1">LAME</font> has this enabled by default, but can be overridden by use <b>--nores</b> option.
<dt><b>joint_stereo (</b><i>-m j</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable the encoder to use (on a frame by frame basis) either L/R stereo or mid/side stereo. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>abr (</b><i>--abr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable the encoder to use <font SIZE="-1">ABR</font> when set to 1. The <b>lame</b> <b>--abr</b> sets the target bitrate, while this options only tells FFmpeg to use <font SIZE="-1">ABR</font> still relies on <b>b</b> to set bitrate.</dl><h3>libopencore-amrnb</h3>OpenCORE Adaptive Multi-Rate Narrowband encoder. 

 Requires the presence of the libopencore-amrnb headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopencore-amrnb --enable-version3&quot;</tt>. 

 This is a mono-only encoder. Officially it only supports 8000Hz sample rate, but you can override it by setting <b>strict</b> to <b>unofficial</b> or lower. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set bitrate in bits per second. Only the following bitrates are supported, otherwise libavcodec will round to the nearest valid bitrate.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>4750</b>
<dd><dt><b>5150</b>
<dd><dt><b>5900</b>
<dd><dt><b>6700</b>
<dd><dt><b>7400</b>
<dd><dt><b>7950</b>
<dd><dt><b>10200</b>
<dd><dt><b>12200</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>dtx</b>
<dd>Allow discontinuous transmission (generate comfort noise) when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).</dl><h3>libopus</h3>libopus Opus Interactive Audio Codec encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libopus headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopus&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Option Mapping</i> 

 Most libopus options are modelled after the <b>opusenc</b> utility from opus-tools. The following is an option mapping chart describing options supported by the libopus wrapper, and their <b>opusenc</b>-equivalent in parentheses.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>bitrate</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the bit rate in bits/s. FFmpeg's <b>b</b> option is expressed in bits/s, while <b>opusenc</b>'s <b>bitrate</b> in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>vbr (</b><i>vbr</i><b>,</b> <i>hard-cbr</i><b>, and</b> <i>cvbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode. The FFmpeg <b>vbr</b> option has the following valid arguments, with the <b>opusenc</b> equivalent options in parentheses:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>off (</b><i>hard-cbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Use constant bit rate encoding.
<dt><b>on (</b><i>vbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Use variable bit rate encoding (the default).
<dt><b>constrained (</b><i>cvbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Use constrained variable bit rate encoding.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>compression_level (</b><i>comp</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set encoding algorithm complexity. Valid options are integers in the 0-10 range. 0 gives the fastest encodes but lower quality, while 10 gives the highest quality but slowest encoding. The default is 10.
<dt><b>frame_duration (</b><i>framesize</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set maximum frame size, or duration of a frame in milliseconds. The argument must be exactly the following: 2.5, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60. Smaller frame sizes achieve lower latency but less quality at a given bitrate. Sizes greater than 20ms are only interesting at fairly low bitrates. The default is 20ms.
<dt><b>packet_loss (</b><i>expect-loss</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set expected packet loss percentage. The default is 0.
<dt><b>application (N.A.)</b>
<dd>Set intended application type. Valid options are listed below:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>voip</b>
<dd>Favor improved speech intelligibility.
<dt><b>audio</b>
<dd>Favor faithfulness to the input (the default).
<dt><b>lowdelay</b>
<dd>Restrict to only the lowest delay modes.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>cutoff (N.A.)</b>
<dd>Set cutoff bandwidth in Hz. The argument must be exactly one of the following: 4000, 6000, 8000, 12000, or 20000, corresponding to narrowband, mediumband, wideband, super wideband, and fullband respectively. The default is 0 (cutoff disabled).
<dt><b>mapping_family (</b><i>mapping_family</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set channel mapping family to be used by the encoder. The default value of -1 uses mapping family 0 for mono and stereo inputs, and mapping family 1 otherwise. The default also disables the surround masking and <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> bandwidth optimzations in libopus, and requires that the input contains 8 channels or fewer. 

 Other values include 0 for mono and stereo, 1 for surround sound with masking and <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> bandwidth optimizations, and 255 for independent streams with an unspecified channel layout.</dl><h3>libshine</h3>Shine Fixed-Point <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> encoder wrapper. 

 Shine is a fixed-point <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> encoder. It has a far better performance on platforms without an <font SIZE="-1">FPU,</font> e.g. armel CPUs, and some phones and tablets. However, as it is more targeted on performance than quality, it is not on par with <font SIZE="-1">LAME</font> and other production-grade encoders quality-wise. Also, according to the project's homepage, this encoder may not be free of bugs as the code was written a long time ago and the project was dead for at least 5 years. 

 This encoder only supports stereo and mono input. This is also CBR-only. 

 The original project (last updated in early 2007) is at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://sourceforge.net/projects/libshine-fxp/">http://sourceforge.net/projects/libshine-fxp/</a></b>&gt;. We only support the updated fork by the Savonet/Liquidsoap project at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/savonet/shine">https://github.com/savonet/shine</a></b>&gt;. 

 Requires the presence of the libshine headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libshine&quot;</tt>. 

 See also <b>libmp3lame</b>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libshine wrapper. The <b>shineenc</b>-equivalent of the options are listed in parentheses.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>-b</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate expressed in bits/s for <font SIZE="-1">CBR.</font> <b>shineenc</b> <b>-b</b> option is expressed in kilobits/s.</dl><h3>libtwolame</h3>TwoLAME <font SIZE="-1">MP2</font> encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libtwolame headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libtwolame&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libtwolame wrapper. The <b>twolame</b>-equivalent options follow the FFmpeg ones and are in parentheses.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>-b</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate expressed in bits/s for <font SIZE="-1">CBR.</font> <b>twolame</b> <b>b</b> option is expressed in kilobits/s. Default value is 128k.
<dt><b>q (</b><i>-V</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set quality for experimental <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> support. Maximum value range is from -50 to 50, useful range is from -10 to 10. The higher the value, the better the quality. This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.
<dt><b>mode (</b><i>--mode</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the mode of the resulting audio. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Choose mode automatically based on the input. This is the default.
<dt><b>stereo</b>
<dd>Stereo
<dt><b>joint_stereo</b>
<dd>Joint stereo
<dt><b>dual_channel</b>
<dd>Dual channel
<dt><b>mono</b>
<dd>Mono</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>psymodel (</b><i>--psyc-mode</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set psychoacoustic model to use in encoding. The argument must be an integer between -1 and 4, inclusive. The higher the value, the better the quality. The default value is 3.
<dt><b>energy_levels (</b><i>--energy</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable energy levels extensions when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>error_protection (</b><i>--protect</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> error protection when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>copyright (</b><i>--copyright</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> audio copyright flag when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>original (</b><i>--original</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> audio original flag when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).</dl><h3>libvo-amrwbenc</h3>VisualOn Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband encoder. 

 Requires the presence of the libvo-amrwbenc headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvo-amrwbenc --enable-version3&quot;</tt>. 

 This is a mono-only encoder. Officially it only supports 16000Hz sample rate, but you can override it by setting <b>strict</b> to <b>unofficial</b> or lower. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set bitrate in bits/s. Only the following bitrates are supported, otherwise libavcodec will round to the nearest valid bitrate.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>6600</b>
<dd><dt><b>8850</b>
<dd><dt><b>12650</b>
<dd><dt><b>14250</b>
<dd><dt><b>15850</b>
<dd><dt><b>18250</b>
<dd><dt><b>19850</b>
<dd><dt><b>23050</b>
<dd><dt><b>23850</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>dtx</b>
<dd>Allow discontinuous transmission (generate comfort noise) when set to 1. The default value is 0 (disabled).</dl><h3>libvorbis</h3>libvorbis encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libvorbisenc headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvorbis&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libvorbis wrapper. The <b>oggenc</b>-equivalent of the options are listed in parentheses. 

 To get a more accurate and extensive documentation of the libvorbis options, consult the libvorbisenc's and <b>oggenc</b>'s documentations. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://xiph.org/vorbis/">http://xiph.org/vorbis/</a></b>&gt;, &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://wiki.xiph.org/Vorbis-tools">http://wiki.xiph.org/Vorbis-tools</a></b>&gt;, and <i><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-oggenc/">oggenc</a></i>(1).
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>-b</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate expressed in bits/s for <font SIZE="-1">ABR.</font> <b>oggenc</b> <b>-b</b> is expressed in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>q (</b><i>-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set constant quality setting for <font SIZE="-1">VBR.</font> The value should be a float number in the range of -1.0 to 10.0. The higher the value, the better the quality. The default value is <b>3.0</b>. 

 This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.
<dt><b>cutoff (</b><i>--advanced-encode-option lowpass_frequency=N</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set cutoff bandwidth in Hz, a value of 0 disables cutoff. <b>oggenc</b>'s related option is expressed in kHz. The default value is <b>0</b> (cutoff disabled).
<dt><b>minrate (</b><i>-m</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set minimum bitrate expressed in bits/s. <b>oggenc</b> <b>-m</b> is expressed in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>maxrate (</b><i>-M</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set maximum bitrate expressed in bits/s. <b>oggenc</b> <b>-M</b> is expressed in kilobits/s. This only has effect on <font SIZE="-1">ABR</font> mode.
<dt><b>iblock (</b><i>--advanced-encode-option impulse_noisetune=N</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set noise floor bias for impulse blocks. The value is a float number from -15.0 to 0.0. A negative bias instructs the encoder to pay special attention to the crispness of transients in the encoded audio. The tradeoff for better transient response is a higher bitrate.</dl><h3>libwavpack</h3>A wrapper providing WavPack encoding through libwavpack. 

 Only lossless mode using 32-bit integer samples is supported currently. 

 Requires the presence of the libwavpack headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libwavpack&quot;</tt>. 

 Note that a libavcodec-native encoder for the WavPack codec exists so users can encode audios with this codec without using this encoder. See <b>wavpackenc</b>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 <b>wavpack</b> command line utility's corresponding options are listed in parentheses, if any.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>frame_size (</b><i>--blocksize</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Default is 32768.
<dt><b>compression_level</b>
<dd>Set speed vs. compression tradeoff. Acceptable arguments are listed below:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0 (</b><i>-f</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Fast mode.
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd>Normal (default) settings.
<dt><b>2 (</b><i>-h</i><b>)</b>
<dd>High quality.
<dt><b>3 (</b><i>-hh</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Very high quality.
<dt><b>4-8 (</b><i>-hh -x</i><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>EXTRAPROC</i></font><i></i><b>)</b>
<dd>Same as <b>3</b>, but with extra processing enabled. 

 <b>4</b> is the same as <b>-x2</b> and <b>8</b> is the same as <b>-x6</b>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>mjpeg</h3>Motion <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>huffman</b>
<dd>Set the huffman encoding strategy. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>default</b>
<dd>Use the default huffman tables. This is the default strategy.
<dt><b>optimal</b>
<dd>Compute and use optimal huffman tables.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>wavpack</h3>WavPack lossless audio encoder. 

 This is a libavcodec-native WavPack encoder. There is also an encoder based on libwavpack, but there is virtually no reason to use that encoder. 

 See also <b>libwavpack</b>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The equivalent options for <b>wavpack</b> command line utility are listed in parentheses. 

 Shared options 

 The following shared options are effective for this encoder. Only special notes about this particular encoder will be documented here. For the general meaning of the options, see <b>the Codec Options chapter</b>.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>frame_size (</b><i>--blocksize</i><b>)</b>
<dd>For this encoder, the range for this option is between 128 and 131072. Default is automatically decided based on sample rate and number of channel. 

 For the complete formula of calculating default, see <i>libavcodec/wavpackenc.c</i>.
<dt><b>compression_level (</b><i>-f</i><b>,</b> <i>-h</i><b>,</b> <i>-hh</i><b>, and</b> <i>-x</i><b>)</b>
<dd>This option's syntax is consistent with <b>libwavpack</b>'s.</dl>
 

 Private options
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>joint_stereo (</b><i>-j</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set whether to enable joint stereo. Valid values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>on (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Force mid/side audio encoding.
<dt><b>off (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Force left/right audio encoding.
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Let the encoder decide automatically.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>optimize_mono</b>
<dd>Set whether to enable optimization for mono. This option is only effective for non-mono streams. Available values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>on</b>
<dd>enabled
<dt><b>off</b>
<dd>disabled</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h2>Video Encoders</h2>A description of some of the currently available video encoders follows.
<h3>Hap</h3>Vidvox Hap video encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>format</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Specifies the Hap format to encode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>hap</b>
<dd><dt><b>hap_alpha</b>
<dd><dt><b>hap_q</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>hap</b>.</dl><dt><b>chunks</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Specifies the number of chunks to split frames into, between 1 and 64. This permits multithreaded decoding of large frames, potentially at the cost of data-rate. The encoder may modify this value to divide frames evenly. 

 Default value is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>compressor</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Specifies the second-stage compressor to use. If set to <b>none</b>, <b>chunks</b> will be limited to 1, as chunked uncompressed frames offer no benefit.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd><dt><b>snappy</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>snappy</b>.</dl></dl><h3>jpeg2000</h3>The native jpeg 2000 encoder is lossy by default, the <tt>&quot;-q:v&quot;</tt> option can be used to set the encoding quality. Lossless encoding can be selected with <tt>&quot;-pred 1&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>format</b>
<dd>Can be set to either <tt>&quot;j2k&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;jp2&quot;</tt> (the default) that makes it possible to store non-rgb pix_fmts.</dl><h3>libkvazaar</h3>Kvazaar H.265/HEVC encoder. 

 Requires the presence of the libkvazaar headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <b>--enable-libkvazaar</b>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set target video bitrate in bit/s and enable rate control.
<dt><b>kvazaar-params</b>
<dd>Set kvazaar parameters as a list of <i>name</i>=<i>value</i> pairs separated by commas (,). See kvazaar documentation for a list of options.</dl><h3>libopenh264</h3>Cisco libopenh264 H.264/MPEG-4 <font SIZE="-1">AVC</font> encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libopenh264 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopenh264&quot;</tt>. The library is detected using <b>pkg-config</b>. 

 For more information about the library see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.openh264.org">http://www.openh264.org</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following FFmpeg global options affect the configurations of the libopenh264 encoder.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set the bitrate (as a number of bits per second).
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd>Set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>maxrate</b>
<dd>Set the max bitrate (as a number of bits per second).
<dt><b>flags +global_header</b>
<dd>Set global header in the bitstream.
<dt><b>slices</b>
<dd>Set the number of slices, used in parallelized encoding. Default value is 0. This is only used when <b>slice_mode</b> is set to <b>fixed</b>.
<dt><b>slice_mode</b>
<dd>Set slice mode. Can assume one of the following possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>fixed</b>
<dd>a fixed number of slices
<dt><b>rowmb</b>
<dd>one slice per row of macroblocks
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>automatic number of slices according to number of threads
<dt><b>dyn</b>
<dd>dynamic slicing</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>auto</b>.</dl><dt><b>loopfilter</b>
<dd>Enable loop filter, if set to 1 (automatically enabled). To disable set a value of 0.
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd>Set profile restrictions. If set to the value of <b>main</b> enable <font SIZE="-1">CABAC</font> (set the <tt>&quot;SEncParamExt.iEntropyCodingModeFlag&quot;</tt> flag to 1).
<dt><b>max_nal_size</b>
<dd>Set maximum <font SIZE="-1">NAL</font> size in bytes.
<dt><b>allow_skip_frames</b>
<dd>Allow skipping frames to hit the target bitrate if set to 1.</dl><h3>libtheora</h3>libtheora Theora encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libtheora headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libtheora&quot;</tt>. 

 For more information about the libtheora project see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.theora.org/">http://www.theora.org/</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following global options are mapped to internal libtheora options which affect the quality and the bitrate of the encoded stream.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Set the video bitrate in bit/s for <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> (Constant Bit Rate) mode. In case <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> (Variable Bit Rate) mode is enabled this option is ignored.
<dt><b>flags</b>
<dd>Used to enable constant quality mode (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>) encoding through the <b>qscale</b> flag, and to enable the <tt>&quot;pass1&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;pass2&quot;</tt> modes.
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd>Set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>global_quality</b>
<dd>Set the global quality as an integer in lambda units. 

 Only relevant when <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode is enabled with <tt>&quot;flags +qscale&quot;</tt>. The value is converted to <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> units by dividing it by <tt>&quot;FF_QP2LAMBDA&quot;</tt>, clipped in the [0 - 10] range, and then multiplied by 6.3 to get a value in the native libtheora range [0-63]. A higher value corresponds to a higher quality.
<dt><b>q</b>
<dd>Enable <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode when set to a non-negative value, and set constant quality value as a double floating point value in <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> units. 

 The value is clipped in the [0-10] range, and then multiplied by 6.3 to get a value in the native libtheora range [0-63]. 

 This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Set maximum constant quality (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>) encoding with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -codec:v libtheora -q:v 10 OUTPUT.ogg</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to convert a <font SIZE="-1">CBR 1000</font> kbps Theora video stream: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -codec:v libtheora -b:v 1000k OUTPUT.ogg</pre></dl><h3>libvpx</h3><font SIZE="-1">VP8/VP9</font> format supported through libvpx. 

 Requires the presence of the libvpx headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvpx&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libvpx wrapper. The <b>vpxenc</b>-equivalent options or values are listed in parentheses for easy migration. 

 To reduce the duplication of documentation, only the private options and some others requiring special attention are documented here. For the documentation of the undocumented generic options, see <b>the Codec Options chapter</b>. 

 To get more documentation of the libvpx options, invoke the command <b>ffmpeg -h encoder=libvpx</b>, <b>ffmpeg -h encoder=libvpx-vp9</b> or <b>vpxenc --help</b>. Further information is available in the libvpx <font SIZE="-1">API</font> documentation.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>target-bitrate</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate in bits/s. Note that FFmpeg's <b>b</b> option is expressed in bits/s, while <b>vpxenc</b>'s <b>target-bitrate</b> is in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>g (</b><i>kf-max-dist</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>keyint_min (</b><i>kf-min-dist</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>qmin (</b><i>min-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>qmax (</b><i>max-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>bufsize (</b><i>buf-sz</i><b>,</b> <i>buf-optimal-sz</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set ratecontrol buffer size (in bits). Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s options are specified in milliseconds, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;buf-sz = bufsize * 1000 / bitrate&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;buf-optimal-sz = bufsize * 1000 / bitrate * 5 / 6&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rc_init_occupancy (</b><i>buf-initial-sz</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of bits which should be loaded into the rc buffer before decoding starts. Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s option is specified in milliseconds, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;rc_init_occupancy * 1000 / bitrate&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>undershoot-pct</b>
<dd>Set datarate undershoot (min) percentage of the target bitrate.
<dt><b>overshoot-pct</b>
<dd>Set datarate overshoot (max) percentage of the target bitrate.
<dt><b>skip_threshold (</b><i>drop-frame</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>qcomp (</b><i>bias-pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>maxrate (</b><i>maxsection-pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> max bitrate in bits/s. Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s option is specified as a percentage of the target bitrate, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;(maxrate * 100 / bitrate)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>minrate (</b><i>minsection-pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> min bitrate in bits/s. Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s option is specified as a percentage of the target bitrate, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;(minrate * 100 / bitrate)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>minrate, maxrate, b</b> <i>end-usage=cbr</i>
<dd><tt>&quot;(minrate == maxrate == bitrate)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>crf (</b><i>end-usage=cq</i><b>,</b> <i>cq-level</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>tune (</b><i>tune</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>psnr (</b><i>psnr</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>ssim (</b><i>ssim</i><b>)</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>quality, deadline (</b><i>deadline</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>best</b>
<dd>Use best quality deadline. Poorly named and quite slow, this option should be avoided as it may give worse quality output than good.
<dt><b>good</b>
<dd>Use good quality deadline. This is a good trade-off between speed and quality when used with the <b>cpu-used</b> option.
<dt><b>realtime</b>
<dd>Use realtime quality deadline.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>speed, cpu-used (</b><i>cpu-used</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set quality/speed ratio modifier. Higher values speed up the encode at the cost of quality.
<dt><b>nr (</b><i>noise-sensitivity</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>static-thresh</b>
<dd>Set a change threshold on blocks below which they will be skipped by the encoder.
<dt><b>slices (</b><i>token-parts</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Note that FFmpeg's <b>slices</b> option gives the total number of partitions, while <b>vpxenc</b>'s <b>token-parts</b> is given as <tt>&quot;log2(partitions)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>max-intra-rate</b>
<dd>Set maximum I-frame bitrate as a percentage of the target bitrate. A value of 0 means unlimited.
<dt><b>force_key_frames</b>
<dd><tt>&quot;VPX_EFLAG_FORCE_KF&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>Alternate reference frame related</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto-alt-ref</b>
<dd>Enable use of alternate reference frames (2-pass only).
<dt><b>arnr-max-frames</b>
<dd>Set altref noise reduction max frame count.
<dt><b>arnr-type</b>
<dd>Set altref noise reduction filter type: backward, forward, centered.
<dt><b>arnr-strength</b>
<dd>Set altref noise reduction filter strength.
<dt><b>rc-lookahead, lag-in-frames (</b><i>lag-in-frames</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of frames to look ahead for frametype and ratecontrol.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>error-resilient</b>
<dd>Enable error resiliency features.
<dt><b>VP9-specific options</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>lossless</b>
<dd>Enable lossless mode.
<dt><b>tile-columns</b>
<dd>Set number of tile columns to use. Note this is given as <tt>&quot;log2(tile_columns)&quot;</tt>. For example, 8 tile columns would be requested by setting the <b>tile-columns</b> option to 3.
<dt><b>tile-rows</b>
<dd>Set number of tile rows to use. Note this is given as <tt>&quot;log2(tile_rows)&quot;</tt>. For example, 4 tile rows would be requested by setting the <b>tile-rows</b> option to 2.
<dt><b>frame-parallel</b>
<dd>Enable frame parallel decodability features.
<dt><b>aq-mode</b>
<dd>Set adaptive quantization mode (0: off (default), 1: variance 2: complexity, 3: cyclic refresh, 4: equator360).
<dt><b>colorspace</b> <i>color-space</i>
<dd>Set input color space. The <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> bitstream supports signaling the following colorspaces:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>rgb </b>sRGB
<dd><dt><b>bt709 </b>bt709
<dd><dt><b>unspecified </b>unknown
<dd><dt><b>bt470bg </b>bt601
<dd><dt><b>smpte170m </b>smpte170
<dd><dt><b>smpte240m </b>smpte240
<dd><dt><b>bt2020_ncl </b>bt2020
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>row-mt</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Enable row based multi-threading.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 For more information about libvpx see: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.webmproject.org/">http://www.webmproject.org/</a></b>&gt;
<h3>libwebp</h3>libwebp WebP Image encoder wrapper 

 libwebp is Google's official encoder for WebP images. It can encode in either lossy or lossless mode. Lossy images are essentially a wrapper around a <font SIZE="-1">VP8</font> frame. Lossless images are a separate codec developed by Google. 

 <i>Pixel Format</i> 

 Currently, libwebp only supports <font SIZE="-1">YUV420</font> for lossy and <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> for lossless due to limitations of the format and libwebp. Alpha is supported for either mode. Because of <font SIZE="-1">API</font> limitations, if <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> is passed in when encoding lossy or <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> is passed in for encoding lossless, the pixel format will automatically be converted using functions from libwebp. This is not ideal and is done only for convenience. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-lossless</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Enables/Disables use of lossless mode. Default is 0.
<dt><b>-compression_level</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>For lossy, this is a quality/speed tradeoff. Higher values give better quality for a given size at the cost of increased encoding time. For lossless, this is a size/speed tradeoff. Higher values give smaller size at the cost of increased encoding time. More specifically, it controls the number of extra algorithms and compression tools used, and varies the combination of these tools. This maps to the <i>method</i> option in libwebp. The valid range is 0 to 6. Default is 4.
<dt><b>-qscale</b> <i>float</i>
<dd>For lossy encoding, this controls image quality, 0 to 100. For lossless encoding, this controls the effort and time spent at compressing more. The default value is 75. Note that for usage via libavcodec, this option is called <i>global_quality</i> and must be multiplied by <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>FF_QP2LAMBDA</i></font><i></i>.
<dt><b>-preset</b> <i>type</i>
<dd>Configuration preset. This does some automatic settings based on the general type of the image.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Do not use a preset.
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd>Use the encoder default.
<dt><b>picture</b>
<dd>Digital picture, like portrait, inner shot
<dt><b>photo</b>
<dd>Outdoor photograph, with natural lighting
<dt><b>drawing</b>
<dd>Hand or line drawing, with high-contrast details
<dt><b>icon</b>
<dd>Small-sized colorful images
<dt><b>text</b>
<dd>Text-like</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>libx264, libx264rgb</h3>x264 H.264/MPEG-4 <font SIZE="-1">AVC</font> encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libx264 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libx264&quot;</tt>. 

 libx264 supports an impressive number of features, including 8x8 and 4x4 adaptive spatial transform, adaptive B-frame placement, <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC/CABAC</font> entropy coding, interlacing (<font SIZE="-1">MBAFF</font>), lossless mode, psy optimizations for detail retention (adaptive quantization, psy-RD, psy-trellis). 

 Many libx264 encoder options are mapped to FFmpeg global codec options, while unique encoder options are provided through private options. Additionally the <b>x264opts</b> and <b>x264-params</b> private options allows one to pass a list of key=value tuples as accepted by the libx264 <tt>&quot;x264_param_parse&quot;</tt> function. 

 The x264 project website is at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html">http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html</a></b>&gt;. 

 The libx264rgb encoder is the same as libx264, except it accepts packed <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> pixel formats as input instead of <font SIZE="-1">YUV.</font> 

 <i>Supported Pixel Formats</i> 

 x264 supports 8- to 10-bit color spaces. The exact bit depth is controlled at x264's configure time. FFmpeg only supports one bit depth in one particular build. In other words, it is not possible to build one FFmpeg with multiple versions of x264 with different bit depths. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libx264 wrapper. The <b>x264</b>-equivalent options or values are listed in parentheses for easy migration. 

 To reduce the duplication of documentation, only the private options and some others requiring special attention are documented here. For the documentation of the undocumented generic options, see <b>the Codec Options chapter</b>. 

 To get a more accurate and extensive documentation of the libx264 options, invoke the command <b>x264 --fullhelp</b> or consult the libx264 documentation.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b (</b><i>bitrate</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set bitrate in bits/s. Note that FFmpeg's <b>b</b> option is expressed in bits/s, while <b>x264</b>'s <b>bitrate</b> is in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>bf (</b><i>bframes</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>g (</b><i>keyint</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>qmin (</b><i>qpmin</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Minimum quantizer scale.
<dt><b>qmax (</b><i>qpmax</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Maximum quantizer scale.
<dt><b>qdiff (</b><i>qpstep</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Maximum difference between quantizer scales.
<dt><b>qblur (</b><i>qblur</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Quantizer curve blur
<dt><b>qcomp (</b><i>qcomp</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Quantizer curve compression factor
<dt><b>refs (</b><i>ref</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Number of reference frames each P-frame can use. The range is from <i>0-16</i>.
<dt><b>sc_threshold (</b><i>scenecut</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Sets the threshold for the scene change detection.
<dt><b>trellis (</b><i>trellis</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Performs Trellis quantization to increase efficiency. Enabled by default.
<dt><b>nr (</b><i>nr</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>me_range (</b><i>merange</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Maximum range of the motion search in pixels.
<dt><b>me_method (</b><i>me</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set motion estimation method. Possible values in the decreasing order of speed:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>dia (</b><i>dia</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>epzs (</b><i>dia</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Diamond search with radius 1 (fastest). <b>epzs</b> is an alias for <b>dia</b>.
<dt><b>hex (</b><i>hex</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Hexagonal search with radius 2.
<dt><b>umh (</b><i>umh</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Uneven multi-hexagon search.
<dt><b>esa (</b><i>esa</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Exhaustive search.
<dt><b>tesa (</b><i>tesa</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Hadamard exhaustive search (slowest).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>forced-idr</b>
<dd>Normally, when forcing a I-frame type, the encoder can select any type of I-frame. This option forces it to choose an IDR-frame.
<dt><b>subq (</b><i>subme</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Sub-pixel motion estimation method.
