<dt><b>b_strategy (</b><i>b-adapt</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Adaptive B-frame placement decision algorithm. Use only on first-pass.
<dt><b>keyint_min (</b><i>min-keyint</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Minimum <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>coder</b>
<dd>Set entropy encoder. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>ac</b>
<dd>Enable <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font>
<dt><b>vlc</b>
<dd>Enable <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC</font> and disable <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font> It generates the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-cabac</b> option.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>cmp</b>
<dd>Set full pixel motion estimation comparison algorithm. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>chroma</b>
<dd>Enable chroma in motion estimation.
<dt><b>sad</b>
<dd>Ignore chroma in motion estimation. It generates the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-chroma-me</b> option.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>threads (</b><i>threads</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Number of encoding threads.
<dt><b>thread_type</b>
<dd>Set multithreading technique. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>slice</b>
<dd>Slice-based multithreading. It generates the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--sliced-threads</b> option.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Frame-based multithreading.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>flags</b>
<dd>Set encoding flags. It can be used to disable closed <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> and enable open <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> by setting it to <tt>&quot;-cgop&quot;</tt>. The result is similar to the behavior of <b>x264</b>'s <b>--open-gop</b> option.
<dt><b>rc_init_occupancy (</b><i>vbv-init</i><b>)</b>
<dd><dt><b>preset (</b><i>preset</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the encoding preset.
<dt><b>tune (</b><i>tune</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set tuning of the encoding params.
<dt><b>profile (</b><i>profile</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set profile restrictions.
<dt><b>fastfirstpass</b>
<dd>Enable fast settings when encoding first pass, when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect of <b>x264</b>'s <b>--slow-firstpass</b> option.
<dt><b>crf (</b><i>crf</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the quality for constant quality mode.
<dt><b>crf_max (</b><i>crf-max</i><b>)</b>
<dd>In <font SIZE="-1">CRF</font> mode, prevents <font SIZE="-1">VBV</font> from lowering quality beyond this point.
<dt><b>qp (</b><i>qp</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set constant quantization rate control method parameter.
<dt><b>aq-mode (</b><i>aq-mode</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> method. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Disabled.
<dt><b>variance (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Variance <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> (complexity mask).
<dt><b>autovariance (</b><i>2</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Auto-variance <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> (experimental).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>aq-strength (</b><i>aq-strength</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> strength, reduce blocking and blurring in flat and textured areas.
<dt><b>psy</b>
<dd>Use psychovisual optimizations when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-psy</b> option.
<dt><b>psy-rd (</b><i>psy-rd</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set strength of psychovisual optimization, in <i>psy-rd</i>:<i>psy-trellis</i> format.
<dt><b>rc-lookahead (</b><i>rc-lookahead</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of frames to look ahead for frametype and ratecontrol.
<dt><b>weightb</b>
<dd>Enable weighted prediction for B-frames when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-weightb</b> option.
<dt><b>weightp (</b><i>weightp</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set weighted prediction method for P-frames. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Disabled
<dt><b>simple (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable only weighted refs
<dt><b>smart (</b><i>2</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable both weighted refs and duplicates</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>ssim (</b><i>ssim</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable calculation and printing <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> stats after the encoding.
<dt><b>intra-refresh (</b><i>intra-refresh</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable the use of Periodic Intra Refresh instead of <font SIZE="-1">IDR</font> frames when set to 1.
<dt><b>avcintra-class (</b><i>class</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Configure the encoder to generate AVC-Intra. Valid values are 50,100 and 200
<dt><b>bluray-compat (</b><i>bluray-compat</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Configure the encoder to be compatible with the bluray standard. It is a shorthand for setting ``bluray-compat=1 force-cfr=1''.
<dt><b>b-bias (</b><i>b-bias</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the influence on how often B-frames are used.
<dt><b>b-pyramid (</b><i>b-pyramid</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set method for keeping of some B-frames as references. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Disabled.
<dt><b>strict (</b><i>strict</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Strictly hierarchical pyramid.
<dt><b>normal (</b><i>normal</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Non-strict (not Blu-ray compatible).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>mixed-refs</b>
<dd>Enable the use of one reference per partition, as opposed to one reference per macroblock when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-mixed-refs</b> option.
<dt><b>8x8dct</b>
<dd>Enable adaptive spatial transform (high profile 8x8 transform) when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-8x8dct</b> option.
<dt><b>fast-pskip</b>
<dd>Enable early <font SIZE="-1">SKIP</font> detection on P-frames when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-fast-pskip</b> option.
<dt><b>aud (</b><i>aud</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable use of access unit delimiters when set to 1.
<dt><b>mbtree</b>
<dd>Enable use macroblock tree ratecontrol when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-mbtree</b> option.
<dt><b>deblock (</b><i>deblock</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set loop filter parameters, in <i>alpha</i>:<i>beta</i> form.
<dt><b>cplxblur (</b><i>cplxblur</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set fluctuations reduction in <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> (before curve compression).
<dt><b>partitions (</b><i>partitions</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set partitions to consider as a comma-separated list of. Possible values in the list:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>p8x8</b>
<dd>8x8 P-frame partition.
<dt><b>p4x4</b>
<dd>4x4 P-frame partition.
<dt><b>b8x8</b>
<dd>4x4 B-frame partition.
<dt><b>i8x8</b>
<dd>8x8 I-frame partition.
<dt><b>i4x4</b>
<dd>4x4 I-frame partition. (Enabling <b>p4x4</b> requires <b>p8x8</b> to be enabled. Enabling <b>i8x8</b> requires adaptive spatial transform (<b>8x8dct</b> option) to be enabled.)
<dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Do not consider any partitions.
<dt><b>all (</b><i>all</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Consider every partition.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>direct-pred (</b><i>direct</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set direct <font SIZE="-1">MV</font> prediction mode. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Disable <font SIZE="-1">MV</font> prediction.
<dt><b>spatial (</b><i>spatial</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable spatial predicting.
<dt><b>temporal (</b><i>temporal</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Enable temporal predicting.
<dt><b>auto (</b><i>auto</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Automatically decided.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>slice-max-size (</b><i>slice-max-size</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the limit of the size of each slice in bytes. If not specified but <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> payload size (<b>ps</b>) is specified, that is used.
<dt><b>stats (</b><i>stats</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the file name for multi-pass stats.
<dt><b>nal-hrd (</b><i>nal-hrd</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set signal <font SIZE="-1">HRD</font> information (requires <b>vbv-bufsize</b> to be set). Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Disable <font SIZE="-1">HRD</font> information signaling.
<dt><b>vbr (</b><i>vbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Variable bit rate.
<dt><b>cbr (</b><i>cbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Constant bit rate (not allowed in <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> container).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>x264opts (N.A.)</b>
<dd>Set any x264 option, see <b>x264 --fullhelp</b> for a list. 

 Argument is a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> couples separated by ``:''. In <i>filter</i> and <i>psy-rd</i> options that use ``:'' as a separator themselves, use ``,'' instead. They accept it as well since long ago but this is kept undocumented for some reason. 

 For example to specify libx264 encoding options with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i foo.mpg -c:v libx264 -x264opts keyint=123:min-keyint=20 -an out.mkv</pre><dt><b>a53cc</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd>Import closed captions (which must be <font SIZE="-1">ATSC</font> compatible format) into output. Only the mpeg2 and h264 decoders provide these. Default is 1 (on).
<dt><b>x264-params (N.A.)</b>
<dd>Override the x264 configuration using a :-separated list of key=value parameters. 

 This option is functionally the same as the <b>x264opts</b>, but is duplicated for compatibility with the Libav fork. 

 For example to specify libx264 encoding options with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v libx264 -x264-params level=30:bframes=0:weightp=0:\
 cabac=0:ref=1:vbv-maxrate=768:vbv-bufsize=2000:analyse=all:me=umh:\
 no-fast-pskip=1:subq=6:8x8dct=0:trellis=0 OUTPUT</pre></dl>
 

 Encoding ffpresets for common usages are provided so they can be used with the general presets system (e.g. passing the <b>pre</b> option).
<h3>libx265</h3>x265 H.265/HEVC encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libx265 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <b>--enable-libx265</b>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>preset</b>
<dd>Set the x265 preset.
<dt><b>tune</b>
<dd>Set the x265 tune parameter.
<dt><b>forced-idr</b>
<dd>Normally, when forcing a I-frame type, the encoder can select any type of I-frame. This option forces it to choose an IDR-frame.
<dt><b>x265-params</b>
<dd>Set x265 options using a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> couples separated by ``:''. See <b>x265 --help</b> for a list of options. 

 For example to specify libx265 encoding options with <b>-x265-params</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input -c:v libx265 -x265-params crf=26:psy-rd=1 output.mp4</pre></dl><h3>libxvid</h3>Xvid <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Part 2 encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libxvidcore headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libxvid --enable-gpl&quot;</tt>. 

 The native <tt>&quot;mpeg4&quot;</tt> encoder supports the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Part 2 format, so users can encode to this format without this library. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libxvid wrapper. Some of the following options are listed but are not documented, and correspond to shared codec options. See <b>the Codec Options chapter</b> for their documentation. The other shared options which are not listed have no effect for the libxvid encoder.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd><dt><b>g</b>
<dd><dt><b>qmin</b>
<dd><dt><b>qmax</b>
<dd><dt><b>mpeg_quant</b>
<dd><dt><b>threads</b>
<dd><dt><b>bf</b>
<dd><dt><b>b_qfactor</b>
<dd><dt><b>b_qoffset</b>
<dd><dt><b>flags</b>
<dd>Set specific encoding flags. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>mv4</b>
<dd>Use four motion vector by macroblock.
<dt><b>aic</b>
<dd>Enable high quality <font SIZE="-1">AC</font> prediction.
<dt><b>gray</b>
<dd>Only encode grayscale.
<dt><b>gmc</b>
<dd>Enable the use of global motion compensation (<font SIZE="-1">GMC</font>).
<dt><b>qpel</b>
<dd>Enable quarter-pixel motion compensation.
<dt><b>cgop</b>
<dd>Enable closed <font SIZE="-1">GOP.</font>
<dt><b>global_header</b>
<dd>Place global headers in extradata instead of every keyframe.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>trellis</b>
<dd><dt><b>me_method</b>
<dd>Set motion estimation method. Possible values in decreasing order of speed and increasing order of quality:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>zero</b>
<dd>Use no motion estimation (default).
<dt><b>phods</b>
<dd><dt><b>x1</b>
<dd><dt><b>log</b>
<dd>Enable advanced diamond zonal search for 16x16 blocks and half-pixel refinement for 16x16 blocks. <b>x1</b> and <b>log</b> are aliases for <b>phods</b>.
<dt><b>epzs</b>
<dd>Enable all of the things described above, plus advanced diamond zonal search for 8x8 blocks, half-pixel refinement for 8x8 blocks, and motion estimation on chroma planes.
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd>Enable all of the things described above, plus extended 16x16 and 8x8 blocks search.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>mbd</b>
<dd>Set macroblock decision algorithm. Possible values in the increasing order of quality:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>simple</b>
<dd>Use macroblock comparing function algorithm (default).
<dt><b>bits</b>
<dd>Enable rate distortion-based half pixel and quarter pixel refinement for 16x16 blocks.
<dt><b>rd</b>
<dd>Enable all of the things described above, plus rate distortion-based half pixel and quarter pixel refinement for 8x8 blocks, and rate distortion-based search using square pattern.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>lumi_aq</b>
<dd>Enable lumi masking adaptive quantization when set to 1. Default is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>variance_aq</b>
<dd>Enable variance adaptive quantization when set to 1. Default is 0 (disabled). 

 When combined with <b>lumi_aq</b>, the resulting quality will not be better than any of the two specified individually. In other words, the resulting quality will be the worse one of the two effects.
<dt><b>ssim</b>
<dd>Set structural similarity (<font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font>) displaying method. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Disable displaying of <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> information.
<dt><b>avg</b>
<dd>Output average <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> at the end of encoding to stdout. The format of showing the average <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> is: 

 <pre> Average SSIM: %f</pre>For users who are not familiar with C, <tt>%f</tt> means a float number, or a decimal (e.g. 0.939232).
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Output both per-frame <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> data during encoding and average <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> at the end of encoding to stdout. The format of per-frame information is: 

 <pre> SSIM: avg: %1.3f min: %1.3f max: %1.3f</pre>For users who are not familiar with C, <tt>%1</tt>.3f means a float number rounded to 3 digits after the dot (e.g. 0.932).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>ssim_acc</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> accuracy. Valid options are integers within the range of 0-4, while 0 gives the most accurate result and 4 computes the fastest.</dl><h3>mpeg2</h3><font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> video encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>seq_disp_ext</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Specifies if the encoder should write a sequence_display_extension to the output.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-1</b>
<dd><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Decide automatically to write it or not (this is the default) by checking if the data to be written is different from the default or unspecified values.
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd><dt><b>never</b>
<dd>Never write it.
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd><dt><b>always</b>
<dd>Always write it.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>png</h3><font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> image encoder. 

 <i>Private options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dpi</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Set physical density of pixels, in dots per inch, unset by default
<dt><b>dpm</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Set physical density of pixels, in dots per meter, unset by default</dl><h3>ProRes</h3>Apple ProRes encoder. 

 FFmpeg contains 2 ProRes encoders, the prores-aw and prores-ks encoder. The used encoder can be chosen with the <tt>&quot;-vcodec&quot;</tt> option. 

 <i>Private Options for prores-ks</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>profile</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Select the ProRes profile to encode
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>proxy</b>
<dd><dt><b>lt</b>
<dd><dt><b>standard</b>
<dd><dt><b>hq</b>
<dd><dt><b>4444</b>
<dd><dt><b>4444xq</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>quant_mat</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Select quantization matrix.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd><dt><b>default</b>
<dd><dt><b>proxy</b>
<dd><dt><b>lt</b>
<dd><dt><b>standard</b>
<dd><dt><b>hq</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>If set to <i>auto</i>, the matrix matching the profile will be picked. If not set, the matrix providing the highest quality, <i>default</i>, will be picked.</dl><dt><b>bits_per_mb</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>How many bits to allot for coding one macroblock. Different profiles use between 200 and 2400 bits per macroblock, the maximum is 8000.
<dt><b>mbs_per_slice</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Number of macroblocks in each slice (1-8); the default value (8) should be good in almost all situations.
<dt><b>vendor</b> <i>string</i>
<dd>Override the 4-byte vendor <font SIZE="-1">ID. A</font> custom vendor <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> like <i>apl0</i> would claim the stream was produced by the Apple encoder.
<dt><b>alpha_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>Specify number of bits for alpha component. Possible values are <i>0</i>, <i>8</i> and <i>16</i>. Use <i>0</i> to disable alpha plane coding.</dl>
 

 <i>Speed considerations</i> 

 In the default mode of operation the encoder has to honor frame constraints (i.e. not produce frames with size bigger than requested) while still making output picture as good as possible. A frame containing a lot of small details is harder to compress and the encoder would spend more time searching for appropriate quantizers for each slice. 

 Setting a higher <b>bits_per_mb</b> limit will improve the speed. 

 For the fastest encoding speed set the <b>qscale</b> parameter (4 is the recommended value) and do not set a size constraint.
<h3><font SIZE="-1">QSV</font> encoders</h3>The family of Intel QuickSync Video encoders (<font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2, H.264</font> and <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font>) 

 The ratecontrol method is selected as follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>When <b>global_quality</b> is specified, a quality-based mode is used. Specifically this means either
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CQP</i></font><i></i> - constant quantizer scale, when the <b>qscale</b> codec flag is also set (the <b>-qscale</b> ffmpeg option).
<dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>LA_ICQ</i></font><i></i> - intelligent constant quality with lookahead, when the <b>look_ahead</b> option is also set.
<dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>ICQ</i></font><i></i> --- intelligent constant quality otherwise.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt>&bull;
<dd>Otherwise, a bitrate-based mode is used. For all of those, you should specify at least the desired average bitrate with the <b>b</b> option.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>LA</i></font><i></i> - <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> with lookahead, when the <b>look_ahead</b> option is specified.
<dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>VCM</i></font><i></i> - video conferencing mode, when the <b>vcm</b> option is set.
<dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CBR</i></font><i></i> - constant bitrate, when <b>maxrate</b> is specified and equal to the average bitrate.
<dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>VBR</i></font><i></i> - variable bitrate, when <b>maxrate</b> is specified, but is higher than the average bitrate.
<dt>-
<dd><i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AVBR</i></font><i></i> - average <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode, when <b>maxrate</b> is not specified. This mode is further configured by the <b>avbr_accuracy</b> and <b>avbr_convergence</b> options.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 Note that depending on your system, a different mode than the one you specified may be selected by the encoder. Set the verbosity level to <i>verbose</i> or higher to see the actual settings used by the <font SIZE="-1">QSV</font> runtime. 

 Additional libavcodec global options are mapped to <font SIZE="-1">MSDK</font> options as follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd><b>g/gop_size</b> -&gt; <b>GopPicSize</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>bf/max_b_frames</b>+1 -&gt; <b>GopRefDist</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>rc_init_occupancy/rc_initial_buffer_occupancy</b> -&gt; <b>InitialDelayInKB</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>slices</b> -&gt; <b>NumSlice</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>refs</b> -&gt; <b>NumRefFrame</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>b_strategy/b_frame_strategy</b> -&gt; <b>BRefType</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>cgop/CLOSED_GOP</b> codec flag -&gt; <b>GopOptFlag</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>For the <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CQP</i></font><i></i> mode, the <b>i_qfactor/i_qoffset</b> and <b>b_qfactor/b_qoffset</b> set the difference between <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPP</i></font><i></i> and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPI</i></font><i></i>, and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPP</i></font><i></i> and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPB</i></font><i></i> respectively.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Setting the <b>coder</b> option to the value <i>vlc</i> will make the H.264 encoder use <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC</font> instead of <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font></dl><h3>snow</h3><i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>iterative_dia_size</b>
<dd>dia size for the iterative motion estimation</dl><h3><font SIZE="-1">VAAPI</font> encoders</h3>Wrappers for hardware encoders accessible via <font SIZE="-1">VAAPI.</font> 

 These encoders only accept input in <font SIZE="-1">VAAPI</font> hardware surfaces. If you have input in software frames, use the <b>hwupload</b> filter to upload them to the <font SIZE="-1">GPU.</font> 

 The following standard libavcodec options are used:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd><b>g</b> / <b>gop_size</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>bf</b> / <b>max_b_frames</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>profile</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>level</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>b</b> / <b>bit_rate</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>maxrate</b> / <b>rc_max_rate</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>bufsize</b> / <b>rc_buffer_size</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>rc_init_occupancy</b> / <b>rc_initial_buffer_occupancy</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>compression_level</b> 

 Speed / quality tradeoff: higher values are faster / worse quality.
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>q</b> / <b>global_quality</b> 

 Size / quality tradeoff: higher values are smaller / worse quality.
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>qmin</b> (only: <b>qmax</b> is not supported)
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>i_qfactor</b> / <b>i_quant_factor</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>i_qoffset</b> / <b>i_quant_offset</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>b_qfactor</b> / <b>b_quant_factor</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd><b>b_qoffset</b> / <b>b_quant_offset</b>
<dt><b>h264_vaapi</b>
<dd><b>profile</b> sets the value of <i>profile_idc</i> and the <i>constraint_set*_flag</i>s. <b>level</b> sets the value of <i>level_idc</i>.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>low_power</b>
<dd>Use low-power encoding mode.
<dt><b>coder</b>
<dd>Set entropy encoder (default is <i>cabac</i>). Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>ac</b>
<dd><dt><b>cabac</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font>
<dt><b>vlc</b>
<dd><dt><b>cavlc</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC.</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
</dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>hevc_vaapi</b>
<dd><b>profile</b> and <b>level</b> set the values of <i>general_profile_idc</i> and <i>general_level_idc</i> respectively.
<dt><b>mjpeg_vaapi</b>
<dd>Always encodes using the standard quantisation and huffman tables - <b>global_quality</b> scales the standard quantisation table (range 1-100).
<dt><b>mpeg2_vaapi</b>
<dd><b>profile</b> and <b>level</b> set the value of <i>profile_and_level_indication</i>. 

 No rate control is supported.
<dt><b>vp8_vaapi</b>
<dd>B-frames are not supported. 

 <b>global_quality</b> sets the <i>q_idx</i> used for non-key frames (range 0-127).
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>loop_filter_level</b>
<dd><dt><b>loop_filter_sharpness</b>
<dd>Manually set the loop filter parameters.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>vp9_vaapi</b>
<dd><b>global_quality</b> sets the <i>q_idx</i> used for P-frames (range 0-255).
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>loop_filter_level</b>
<dd><dt><b>loop_filter_sharpness</b>
<dd>Manually set the loop filter parameters.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>B-frames are supported, but the output stream is always in encode order rather than display order. If B-frames are enabled, it may be necessary to use the <b>vp9_raw_reorder</b> bitstream filter to modify the output stream to display frames in the correct order. 

 Only normal frames are produced - the <b>vp9_superframe</b> bitstream filter may be required to produce a stream usable with all decoders.</dl></dl><h3>vc2</h3><font SIZE="-1">SMPTE VC-2</font> (previously <font SIZE="-1">BBC</font> Dirac Pro). This codec was primarily aimed at professional broadcasting but since it supports yuv420, yuv422 and yuv444 at 8 (limited range or full range), 10 or 12 bits, this makes it suitable for other tasks which require low overhead and low compression (like screen recording). 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Sets target video bitrate. Usually that's around 1:6 of the uncompressed video bitrate (e.g. for 1920x1080 50fps yuv422p10 that's around 400Mbps). Higher values (close to the uncompressed bitrate) turn on lossless compression mode.
<dt><b>field_order</b>
<dd>Enables field coding when set (e.g. to tt - top field first) for interlaced inputs. Should increase compression with interlaced content as it splits the fields and encodes each separately.
<dt><b>wavelet_depth</b>
<dd>Sets the total amount of wavelet transforms to apply, between 1 and 5 (default). Lower values reduce compression and quality. Less capable decoders may not be able to handle values of <b>wavelet_depth</b> over 3.
<dt><b>wavelet_type</b>
<dd>Sets the transform type. Currently only <i>5_3</i> (LeGall) and <i>9_7</i> (Deslauriers-Dubuc) are implemented, with 9_7 being the one with better compression and thus is the default.
<dt><b>slice_width</b>
<dd><dt><b>slice_height</b>
<dd>Sets the slice size for each slice. Larger values result in better compression. For compatibility with other more limited decoders use <b>slice_width</b> of 32 and <b>slice_height</b> of 8.
<dt><b>tolerance</b>
<dd>Sets the undershoot tolerance of the rate control system in percent. This is to prevent an expensive search from being run.
<dt><b>qm</b>
<dd>Sets the quantization matrix preset to use by default or when <b>wavelet_depth</b> is set to 5
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>-
<dd><i>default</i> Uses the default quantization matrix from the specifications, extended with values for the fifth level. This provides a good balance between keeping detail and omitting artifacts.
<dt>-
<dd><i>flat</i> Use a completely zeroed out quantization matrix. This increases <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> but might reduce perception. Use in bogus benchmarks.
<dt>-
<dd><i>color</i> Reduces detail but attempts to preserve color at extremely low bitrates.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h2>Subtitles Encoders</h2><h3>dvdsub</h3>This codec encodes the bitmap subtitle format that is used in DVDs. Typically they are stored in <font SIZE="-1">VOBSUB</font> file pairs (*.idx + *.sub), and they can also be used in Matroska files. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>even_rows_fix</b>
<dd>When set to 1, enable a work-around that makes the number of pixel rows even in all subtitles. This fixes a problem with some players that cut off the bottom row if the number is odd. The work-around just adds a fully transparent row if needed. The overhead is low, typically one byte per subtitle on average. 

 By default, this work-around is disabled.</dl><h2>Bitstream Filters</h2>When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported bitstream filters are enabled by default. You can list all available ones using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-bsfs&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the bitstream filters using the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-bsfs&quot;</tt>, and selectively enable any bitstream filter using the option <tt>&quot;--enable-bsf=BSF&quot;</tt>, or you can disable a particular bitstream filter using the option <tt>&quot;--disable-bsf=BSF&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-bsfs&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of all the supported bitstream filters included in your build. 

 The ff* tools have a -bsf option applied per stream, taking a comma-separated list of filters, whose parameters follow the filter name after a '='. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v copy -bsf:v filter1[=opt1=str1:opt2=str2][,filter2] OUTPUT</pre>Below is a description of the currently available bitstream filters, with their parameters, if any.
<h3>aac_adtstoasc</h3>Convert <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2/4 AAC ADTS</font> to an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Audio Specific Configuration bitstream. 

 This filter creates an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> AudioSpecificConfig from an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2/4 ADTS</font> header and removes the <font SIZE="-1">ADTS</font> header. 

 This filter is required for example when copying an <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> stream from a raw <font SIZE="-1">ADTS AAC</font> or an MPEG-TS container to <font SIZE="-1">MP4A-LATM,</font> to an <font SIZE="-1">FLV</font> file, or to <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> files and related formats such as 3GP or M4A. Please note that it is auto-inserted for <font SIZE="-1">MP4A-LATM</font> and <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> and related formats.
<h3>chomp</h3>Remove zero padding at the end of a packet.
<h3>dca_core</h3>Extract the core from a <font SIZE="-1">DCA/DTS</font> stream, dropping extensions such as DTS-HD.
<h3>dump_extra</h3>Add extradata to the beginning of the filtered packets. 

 The additional argument specifies which packets should be filtered. It accepts the values:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>a</b>
<dd>add extradata to all key packets, but only if <i>local_header</i> is set in the <b>flags2</b> codec context field
<dt><b>k</b>
<dd>add extradata to all key packets
<dt><b>e</b>
<dd>add extradata to all packets</dl>
 

 If not specified it is assumed <b>k</b>. 

 For example the following <b>ffmpeg</b> command forces a global header (thus disabling individual packet headers) in the H.264 packets generated by the <tt>&quot;libx264&quot;</tt> encoder, but corrects them by adding the header stored in extradata to the key packets: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -map 0 -flags:v +global_header -c:v libx264 -bsf:v dump_extra out.ts</pre><h3>extract_extradata</h3>Extract the in-band extradata. 

 Certain codecs allow the long-term headers (e.g. <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> sequence headers, or H.264/HEVC (<font SIZE="-1">VPS/</font>)SPS/PPS) to be transmitted either ``in-band'' (i.e. as a part of the bitstream containing the coded frames) or ``out of band'' (e.g. on the container level). This latter form is called ``extradata'' in FFmpeg terminology. 

 This bitstream filter detects the in-band headers and makes them available as extradata.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>remove</b>
<dd>When this option is enabled, the long-term headers are removed from the bitstream after extraction.</dl><h3>h264_mp4toannexb</h3>Convert an H.264 bitstream from length prefixed mode to start code prefixed mode (as defined in the Annex B of the ITU-T H.264 specification). 

 This is required by some streaming formats, typically the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> transport stream format (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>). 

 For example to remux an <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> file containing an H.264 stream to mpegts format with <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can use the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT.mp4 -codec copy -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb OUTPUT.ts</pre>Please note that this filter is auto-inserted for MPEG-TS (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>) and raw H.264 (muxer <tt>&quot;h264&quot;</tt>) output formats.
<h3>hevc_mp4toannexb</h3>Convert an <font SIZE="-1">HEVC/H.265</font> bitstream from length prefixed mode to start code prefixed mode (as defined in the Annex B of the ITU-T H.265 specification). 

 This is required by some streaming formats, typically the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> transport stream format (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>). 

 For example to remux an <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> file containing an <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font> stream to mpegts format with <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can use the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT.mp4 -codec copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb OUTPUT.ts</pre>Please note that this filter is auto-inserted for MPEG-TS (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>) and raw <font SIZE="-1">HEVC/H.265</font> (muxer <tt>&quot;h265&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;hevc&quot;</tt>) output formats.
<h3>imxdump</h3>Modifies the bitstream to fit in <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font> and to be usable by the Final Cut Pro decoder. This filter only applies to the mpeg2video codec, and is likely not needed for Final Cut Pro 7 and newer with the appropriate <b>-tag:v</b>. 

 For example, to remux 30 MB/sec <font SIZE="-1">NTSC IMX</font> to <font SIZE="-1">MOV:</font> 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.mxf -c copy -bsf:v imxdump -tag:v mx3n output.mov</pre><h3>mjpeg2jpeg</h3>Convert <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG/AVI1</font> packets to full <font SIZE="-1">JPEG/JFIF</font> packets. 

 <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> is a video codec wherein each video frame is essentially a <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> image. The individual frames can be extracted without loss, e.g. by 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i ../some_mjpeg.avi -c:v copy frames_%d.jpg</pre>Unfortunately, these chunks are incomplete <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> images, because they lack the <font SIZE="-1">DHT</font> segment required for decoding. Quoting from &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.digitalpreservation.gov/formats/fdd/fdd000063.shtml">http://www.digitalpreservation.gov/formats/fdd/fdd000063.shtml</a></b>&gt;: 

 Avery Lee, writing in the rec.video.desktop newsgroup in 2001, commented that ``<font SIZE="-1">MJPEG,</font> or at least the <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> in AVIs having the <font SIZE="-1">MJPG</font> fourcc, is restricted <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> with a fixed --- and *omitted* --- Huffman table. The <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> must be YCbCr colorspace, it must be 4:2:2, and it must use basic Huffman encoding, not arithmetic or progressive. . . . You can indeed extract the <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> frames and decode them with a regular <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> decoder, but you have to prepend the <font SIZE="-1">DHT</font> segment to them, or else the decoder won't have any idea how to decompress the data. The exact table necessary is given in the OpenDML spec.'' 

 This bitstream filter patches the header of frames extracted from an <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> stream (carrying the <font SIZE="-1">AVI1</font> header <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> and lacking a <font SIZE="-1">DHT</font> segment) to produce fully qualified <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> images. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i mjpeg-movie.avi -c:v copy -bsf:v mjpeg2jpeg frame_%d.jpg
 exiftran -i -9 frame*.jpg
 ffmpeg -i frame_%d.jpg -c:v copy rotated.avi</pre><h3>mjpegadump</h3>Add an <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG A</font> header to the bitstream, to enable decoding by Quicktime.
<h3>mov2textsub</h3>Extract a representable text file from <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font> subtitles, stripping the metadata header from each subtitle packet. 

 See also the <b>text2movsub</b> filter.
<h3>mp3decomp</h3>Decompress non-standard compressed <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> audio headers.
<h3>mpeg4_unpack_bframes</h3>Unpack DivX-style packed B-frames. 

 DivX-style packed B-frames are not valid <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> and were only a workaround for the broken Video for Windows subsystem. They use more space, can cause minor <font SIZE="-1">AV</font> sync issues, require more <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> power to decode (unless the player has some decoded picture queue to compensate the 2,0,2,0 frame per packet style) and cause trouble if copied into a standard container like mp4 or mpeg-ps/ts, because <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> decoders may not be able to decode them, since they are not valid <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4.</font> 

 For example to fix an <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> file containing an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> stream with DivX-style packed B-frames using <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can use the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT.avi -codec copy -bsf:v mpeg4_unpack_bframes OUTPUT.avi</pre><h3>noise</h3>Damages the contents of packets or simply drops them without damaging the container. Can be used for fuzzing or testing error resilience/concealment. 

 Parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>amount</b>
<dd>A numeral string, whose value is related to how often output bytes will be modified. Therefore, values below or equal to 0 are forbidden, and the lower the more frequent bytes will be modified, with 1 meaning every byte is modified.
<dt><b>dropamount</b>
<dd>A numeral string, whose value is related to how often packets will be dropped. Therefore, values below or equal to 0 are forbidden, and the lower the more frequent packets will be dropped, with 1 meaning every packet is dropped.</dl>
 

 The following example applies the modification to every byte but does not drop any packets. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -c copy -bsf noise[=1] output.mkv</pre><h3>null</h3>This bitstream filter passes the packets through unchanged.
<h3>remove_extra</h3>Remove extradata from packets. 

 It accepts the following parameter:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>freq</b>
<dd>Set which frame types to remove extradata from.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>k</b>
<dd>Remove extradata from non-keyframes only.
<dt><b>keyframe</b>
<dd>Remove extradata from keyframes only.
<dt><b>e, all</b>
<dd>Remove extradata from all frames.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>text2movsub</h3>Convert text subtitles to <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font> subtitles (as used by the <tt>&quot;mov_text&quot;</tt> codec) with metadata headers. 

 See also the <b>mov2textsub</b> filter.
<h3>vp9_superframe</h3>Merge <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> invisible (alt-ref) frames back into <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> superframes. This fixes merging of split/segmented <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> streams where the alt-ref frame was split from its visible counterpart.
<h3>vp9_superframe_split</h3>Split <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> superframes into single frames.
<h3>vp9_raw_reorder</h3>Given a <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> stream with correct timestamps but possibly out of order, insert additional show-existing-frame packets to correct the ordering.
<h2>Format Options</h2>The libavformat library provides some generic global options, which can be set on all the muxers and demuxers. In addition each muxer or demuxer may support so-called private options, which are specific for that component. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, or by setting the value explicitly in the <tt>&quot;AVFormatContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use. 

 The list of supported options follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>avioflags</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>direct</b>
<dd>Reduce buffering.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>probesize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set probing size in bytes, i.e. the size of the data to analyze to get stream information. A higher value will enable detecting more information in case it is dispersed into the stream, but will increase latency. Must be an integer not lesser than 32. It is 5000000 by default.
<dt><b>packetsize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set packet size.
<dt><b>fflags</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set format flags. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>ignidx</b>
<dd>Ignore index.
<dt><b>fastseek</b>
<dd>Enable fast, but inaccurate seeks for some formats.
<dt><b>genpts</b>
<dd>Generate <font SIZE="-1">PTS.</font>
<dt><b>nofillin</b>
<dd>Do not fill in missing values that can be exactly calculated.
<dt><b>noparse</b>
<dd>Disable AVParsers, this needs <tt>&quot;+nofillin&quot;</tt> too.
<dt><b>igndts</b>
<dd>Ignore <font SIZE="-1">DTS.</font>
<dt><b>discardcorrupt</b>
<dd>Discard corrupted frames.
<dt><b>sortdts</b>
<dd>Try to interleave output packets by <font SIZE="-1">DTS.</font>
<dt><b>keepside</b>
<dd>Do not merge side data.
<dt><b>latm</b>
<dd>Enable <font SIZE="-1">RTP MP4A-LATM</font> payload.
<dt><b>nobuffer</b>
<dd>Reduce the latency introduced by optional buffering
<dt><b>bitexact</b>
<dd>Only write platform-, build- and time-independent data. This ensures that file and data checksums are reproducible and match between platforms. Its primary use is for regression testing.
<dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd>Stop muxing at the end of the shortest stream. It may be needed to increase max_interleave_delta to avoid flushing the longer streams before <font SIZE="-1">EOF.</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>seek2any</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Allow seeking to non-keyframes on demuxer level when supported if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>analyzeduration</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Specify how many microseconds are analyzed to probe the input. A higher value will enable detecting more accurate information, but will increase latency. It defaults to 5,000,000 microseconds = 5 seconds.
<dt><b>cryptokey</b> <i>hexadecimal string</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set decryption key.
<dt><b>indexmem</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max memory used for timestamp index (per stream).
<dt><b>rtbufsize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set max memory used for buffering real-time frames.
<dt><b>fdebug</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Print specific debug info. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>ts</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>max_delay</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set maximum muxing or demuxing delay in microseconds.
<dt><b>fpsprobesize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of frames used to probe fps.
<dt><b>audio_preload</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set microseconds by which audio packets should be interleaved earlier.
<dt><b>chunk_duration</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set microseconds for each chunk.
<dt><b>chunk_size</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set size in bytes for each chunk.
<dt><b>err_detect, f_err_detect</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set error detection flags. <tt>&quot;f_err_detect&quot;</tt> is deprecated and should be used only via the <b>ffmpeg</b> tool. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>crccheck</b>
<dd>Verify embedded CRCs.
<dt><b>bitstream</b>
<dd>Detect bitstream specification deviations.
<dt><b>buffer</b>
<dd>Detect improper bitstream length.
<dt><b>explode</b>
<dd>Abort decoding on minor error detection.
<dt><b>careful</b>
<dd>Consider things that violate the spec and have not been seen in the wild as errors.
<dt><b>compliant</b>
<dd>Consider all spec non compliancies as errors.
<dt><b>aggressive</b>
<dd>Consider things that a sane encoder should not do as an error.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>max_interleave_delta</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set maximum buffering duration for interleaving. The duration is expressed in microseconds, and defaults to 1000000 (1 second). 

 To ensure all the streams are interleaved correctly, libavformat will wait until it has at least one packet for each stream before actually writing any packets to the output file. When some streams are ``sparse'' (i.e. there are large gaps between successive packets), this can result in excessive buffering. 

 This field specifies the maximum difference between the timestamps of the first and the last packet in the muxing queue, above which libavformat will output a packet regardless of whether it has queued a packet for all the streams. 

 If set to 0, libavformat will continue buffering packets until it has a packet for each stream, regardless of the maximum timestamp difference between the buffered packets.
<dt><b>use_wallclock_as_timestamps</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Use wallclock as timestamps if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>avoid_negative_ts</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>make_non_negative</b>
<dd>Shift timestamps to make them non-negative. Also note that this affects only leading negative timestamps, and not non-monotonic negative timestamps.
<dt><b>make_zero</b>
<dd>Shift timestamps so that the first timestamp is 0.
<dt><b>auto (default)</b>
<dd>Enables shifting when required by the target format.
<dt><b>disabled</b>
<dd>Disables shifting of timestamp.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>When shifting is enabled, all output timestamps are shifted by the same amount. Audio, video, and subtitles desynching and relative timestamp differences are preserved compared to how they would have been without shifting.</dl><dt><b>skip_initial_bytes</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set number of bytes to skip before reading header and frames if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>correct_ts_overflow</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Correct single timestamp overflows if set to 1. Default is 1.
<dt><b>flush_packets</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Flush the underlying I/O stream after each packet. Default is -1 (auto), which means that the underlying protocol will decide, 1 enables it, and has the effect of reducing the latency, 0 disables it and may increase <font SIZE="-1">IO</font> throughput in some cases.
<dt><b>output_ts_offset</b> <i>offset</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Set the output time offset. 

 <i>offset</i> must be a time duration specification, see <b>the Time duration section in the </b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a><b>(1) manual</b>. 

 The offset is added by the muxer to the output timestamps. 

 Specifying a positive offset means that the corresponding streams are delayed bt the time duration specified in <i>offset</i>. Default value is <tt>0</tt> (meaning that no offset is applied).
<dt><b>format_whitelist</b> <i>list</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>``,'' separated list of allowed demuxers. By default all are allowed.
<dt><b>dump_separator</b> <i>string</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Separator used to separate the fields printed on the command line about the Stream parameters. For example to separate the fields with newlines and indention: 

 <pre> ffprobe -dump_separator &quot;
 &quot; -i ~/videos/matrixbench_mpeg2.mpg</pre><dt><b>max_streams</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd>Specifies the maximum number of streams. This can be used to reject files that would require too many resources due to a large number of streams.</dl><h3>Format stream specifiers</h3>Format stream specifiers allow selection of one or more streams that match specific properties. 

 Possible forms of stream specifiers are:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>stream_index</i>
<dd>Matches the stream with this index.
<dt><i>stream_type</i><b>[:</b><i>stream_index</i><b>]</b>
<dd><i>stream_type</i> is one of following: 'v' for video, 'a' for audio, 's' for subtitle, 'd' for data, and 't' for attachments. If <i>stream_index</i> is given, then it matches the stream number <i>stream_index</i> of this type. Otherwise, it matches all streams of this type.
<dt><b>p:</b><i>program_id</i><b>[:</b><i>stream_index</i><b>]</b>
<dd>If <i>stream_index</i> is given, then it matches the stream with number <i>stream_index</i> in the program with the id <i>program_id</i>. Otherwise, it matches all streams in the program.
<dt><b>#</b><i>stream_id</i>
<dd>Matches the stream by a format-specific <font SIZE="-1">ID.</font></dl>
 

 The exact semantics of stream specifiers is defined by the <tt>&quot;avformat_match_stream_specifier()&quot;</tt> function declared in the <i>libavformat/avformat.h</i> header.
<h2>Demuxers</h2>Demuxers are configured elements in FFmpeg that can read the multimedia streams from a particular type of file. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported demuxers are enabled by default. You can list all available ones using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-demuxers&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the demuxers using the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-demuxers&quot;</tt>, and selectively enable a single demuxer with the option <tt>&quot;--enable-demuxer=</tt>DEMUXER<tt>&quot;</tt>, or disable it with the option <tt>&quot;--disable-demuxer=</tt>DEMUXER<tt>&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-demuxers&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of enabled demuxers. Use <tt>&quot;-formats&quot;</tt> to view a combined list of enabled demuxers and muxers. 

 The description of some of the currently available demuxers follows.
<h3>aa</h3>Audible Format 2, 3, and 4 demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux Audible Format 2, 3, and 4 (.aa) files.
<h3>applehttp</h3>Apple <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Live Streaming demuxer. 

 This demuxer presents all AVStreams from all variant streams. The id field is set to the bitrate variant index number. By setting the discard flags on AVStreams (by pressing 'a' or 'v' in ffplay), the caller can decide which variant streams to actually receive. The total bitrate of the variant that the stream belongs to is available in a metadata key named ``variant_bitrate''.
<h3>apng</h3>Animated Portable Network Graphics demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux <font SIZE="-1">APNG</font> files. All headers, but the <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> signature, up to (but not including) the first fcTL chunk are transmitted as extradata. Frames are then split as being all the chunks between two fcTL ones, or between the last fcTL and <font SIZE="-1">IEND</font> chunks.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-ignore_loop</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd>Ignore the loop variable in the file if set.
<dt><b>-max_fps</b> <i>int</i>
<dd>Maximum framerate in frames per second (0 for no limit).
<dt><b>-default_fps</b> <i>int</i>
<dd>Default framerate in frames per second when none is specified in the file (0 meaning as fast as possible).</dl><h3>asf</h3>Advanced Systems Format demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux <font SIZE="-1">ASF</font> files and <font SIZE="-1">MMS</font> network streams.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-no_resync_search</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd>Do not try to resynchronize by looking for a certain optional start code.</dl><h3>concat</h3>Virtual concatenation script demuxer. 

 This demuxer reads a list of files and other directives from a text file and demuxes them one after the other, as if all their packets had been muxed together. 

 The timestamps in the files are adjusted so that the first file starts at 0 and each next file starts where the previous one finishes. Note that it is done globally and may cause gaps if all streams do not have exactly the same length. 

 All files must have the same streams (same codecs, same time base, etc.). 

 The duration of each file is used to adjust the timestamps of the next file: if the duration is incorrect (because it was computed using the bit-rate or because the file is truncated, for example), it can cause artifacts. The <tt>&quot;duration&quot;</tt> directive can be used to override the duration stored in each file. 

 <i>Syntax</i> 

 The script is a text file in extended-ASCII, with one directive per line. Empty lines, leading spaces and lines starting with '#' are ignored. The following directive is recognized:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&quot;file path&quot;
<dd>Path to a file to read; special characters and spaces must be escaped with backslash or single quotes. 

 All subsequent file-related directives apply to that file.
<dt>&quot;ffconcat version 1.0&quot;
<dd>Identify the script type and version. It also sets the <b>safe</b> option to 1 if it was -1. 

 To make FFmpeg recognize the format automatically, this directive must appear exactly as is (no extra space or byte-order-mark) on the very first line of the script.
<dt>&quot;duration dur&quot;
<dd>Duration of the file. This information can be specified from the file; specifying it here may be more efficient or help if the information from the file is not available or accurate. 

 If the duration is set for all files, then it is possible to seek in the whole concatenated video.
<dt>&quot;inpoint timestamp&quot;
<dd>In point of the file. When the demuxer opens the file it instantly seeks to the specified timestamp. Seeking is done so that all streams can be presented successfully at In point. 

 This directive works best with intra frame codecs, because for non-intra frame ones you will usually get extra packets before the actual In point and the decoded content will most likely contain frames before In point too. 

 For each file, packets before the file In point will have timestamps less than the calculated start timestamp of the file (negative in case of the first file), and the duration of the files (if not specified by the <tt>&quot;duration&quot;</tt> directive) will be reduced based on their specified In point. 

 Because of potential packets before the specified In point, packet timestamps may overlap between two concatenated files.
<dt>&quot;outpoint timestamp&quot;
<dd>Out point of the file. When the demuxer reaches the specified decoding timestamp in any of the streams, it handles it as an end of file condition and skips the current and all the remaining packets from all streams. 

 Out point is exclusive, which means that the demuxer will not output packets with a decoding timestamp greater or equal to Out point. 

 This directive works best with intra frame codecs and formats where all streams are tightly interleaved. For non-intra frame codecs you will usually get additional packets with presentation timestamp after Out point therefore the decoded content will most likely contain frames after Out point too. If your streams are not tightly interleaved you may not get all the packets from all streams before Out point and you may only will be able to decode the earliest stream until Out point. 

 The duration of the files (if not specified by the <tt>&quot;duration&quot;</tt> directive) will be reduced based on their specified Out point.
<dt>&quot;file_packet_metadata key=value&quot;
<dd>Metadata of the packets of the file. The specified metadata will be set for each file packet. You can specify this directive multiple times to add multiple metadata entries.
<dt>&quot;stream&quot;
<dd>Introduce a stream in the virtual file. All subsequent stream-related directives apply to the last introduced stream. Some streams properties must be set in order to allow identifying the matching streams in the subfiles. If no streams are defined in the script, the streams from the first file are copied.
<dt>&quot;exact_stream_id id&quot;
<dd>Set the id of the stream. If this directive is given, the string with the corresponding id in the subfiles will be used. This is especially useful for MPEG-PS (<font SIZE="-1">VOB</font>) files, where the order of the streams is not reliable.</dl>
 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This demuxer accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>safe</b>
<dd>If set to 1, reject unsafe file paths. A file path is considered safe if it does not contain a protocol specification and is relative and all components only contain characters from the portable character set (letters, digits, period, underscore and hyphen) and have no period at the beginning of a component. 

 If set to 0, any file name is accepted. 

 The default is 1. 

 -1 is equivalent to 1 if the format was automatically probed and 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>auto_convert</b>
<dd>If set to 1, try to perform automatic conversions on packet data to make the streams concatenable. The default is 1. 

 Currently, the only conversion is adding the h264_mp4toannexb bitstream filter to H.264 streams in <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> format. This is necessary in particular if there are resolution changes.
<dt><b>segment_time_metadata</b>
<dd>If set to 1, every packet will contain the <i>lavf.concat.start_time</i> and the <i>lavf.concat.duration</i> packet metadata values which are the start_time and the duration of the respective file segments in the concatenated output expressed in microseconds. The duration metadata is only set if it is known based on the concat file. The default is 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use absolute filenames and include some comments: 

 <pre> # my first filename
 file /mnt/share/file-1.wav
 # my second filename including whitespace
 file '/mnt/share/file 2.wav'
 # my third filename including whitespace plus single quote
 file '/mnt/share/file 3'\''.wav'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Allow for input format auto-probing, use safe filenames and set the duration of the first file: 

 <pre> ffconcat version 1.0
 
 file file-1.wav
 duration 20.0
 
 file subdir/file-2.wav</pre></dl><h3>flv, live_flv</h3>Adobe Flash Video Format demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux <font SIZE="-1">FLV</font> files and <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> network streams. In case of live network streams, if you force format, you may use live_flv option instead of flv to survive timestamp discontinuities. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f flv -i myfile.flv ...
 ffmpeg -f live_flv -i rtmp://&lt;any.server&gt;/anything/key ....</pre><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-flv_metadata</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd>Allocate the streams according to the onMetaData array content.</dl><h3>gif</h3>Animated <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> demuxer. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>min_delay</b>
<dd>Set the minimum valid delay between frames in hundredths of seconds. Range is 0 to 6000. Default value is 2.
<dt><b>max_gif_delay</b>
<dd>Set the maximum valid delay between frames in hundredth of seconds. Range is 0 to 65535. Default value is 65535 (nearly eleven minutes), the maximum value allowed by the specification.
<dt><b>default_delay</b>
<dd>Set the default delay between frames in hundredths of seconds. Range is 0 to 6000. Default value is 10.
<dt><b>ignore_loop</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> files can contain information to loop a certain number of times (or infinitely). If <b>ignore_loop</b> is set to 1, then the loop setting from the input will be ignored and looping will not occur. If set to 0, then looping will occur and will cycle the number of times according to the <font SIZE="-1">GIF.</font> Default value is 1.</dl>
 

 For example, with the overlay filter, place an infinitely looping <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> over another video: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -ignore_loop 0 -i input.gif -filter_complex overlay=shortest=1 out.mkv</pre>Note that in the above example the shortest option for overlay filter is used to end the output video at the length of the shortest input file, which in this case is <i>input.mp4</i> as the <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> in this example loops infinitely.
<h3>hls</h3><font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> demuxer 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>live_start_index</b>
<dd>segment index to start live streams at (negative values are from the end).
<dt><b>allowed_extensions</b>
<dd>',' separated list of file extensions that hls is allowed to access.
<dt><b>max_reload</b>
<dd>Maximum number of times a insufficient list is attempted to be reloaded. Default value is 1000.</dl><h3>image2</h3>Image file demuxer. 

 This demuxer reads from a list of image files specified by a pattern. The syntax and meaning of the pattern is specified by the option <i>pattern_type</i>. 

 The pattern may contain a suffix which is used to automatically determine the format of the images contained in the files. 

 The size, the pixel format, and the format of each image must be the same for all the files in the sequence. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Set the frame rate for the video stream. It defaults to 25.
<dt><b>loop</b>
<dd>If set to 1, loop over the input. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>pattern_type</b>
<dd>Select the pattern type used to interpret the provided filename. 

 <i>pattern_type</i> accepts one of the following values.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Disable pattern matching, therefore the video will only contain the specified image. You should use this option if you do not want to create sequences from multiple images and your filenames may contain special pattern characters.
<dt><b>sequence</b>
<dd>Select a sequence pattern type, used to specify a sequence of files indexed by sequential numbers. 

 A sequence pattern may contain the string ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d``, which specifies the position of the characters representing a sequential number in each filename matched by the pattern. If the form ''%d0<i>N</i>d&quot; is used, the string representing the number in each filename is 0-padded and <i>N</i> is the total number of 0-padded digits representing the number. The literal character '%' can be specified in the pattern with the string ``%%''. 

 If the sequence pattern contains ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d&quot;, the first filename of the file list specified by the pattern must contain a number inclusively contained between <i>start_number</i> and <i>start_number</i>+<i>start_number_range</i>-1, and all the following numbers must be sequential. 

 For example the pattern ``img-%03d.bmp'' will match a sequence of filenames of the form <i>img-001.bmp</i>, <i>img-002.bmp</i>, ..., <i>img-010.bmp</i>, etc.; the pattern ``i%%m%%g-%d.jpg'' will match a sequence of filenames of the form <i>i%m%g-1.jpg</i>, <i>i%m%g-2.jpg</i>, ..., <i>i%m%g-10.jpg</i>, etc. 

 Note that the pattern must not necessarily contain ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d&quot;, for example to convert a single image file <i>img.jpeg</i> you can employ the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i img.jpeg img.png</pre><dt><b>glob</b>
<dd>Select a glob wildcard pattern type. 

 The pattern is interpreted like a <tt>&quot;glob()&quot;</tt> pattern. This is only selectable if libavformat was compiled with globbing support.
<dt><b>glob_sequence</b> <i>(deprecated, will be removed)</i>
<dd>Select a mixed glob wildcard/sequence pattern. 

 If your version of libavformat was compiled with globbing support, and the provided pattern contains at least one glob meta character among <tt>&quot;%*?[]{}&quot;</tt> that is preceded by an unescaped ``%'', the pattern is interpreted like a <tt>&quot;glob()&quot;</tt> pattern, otherwise it is interpreted like a sequence pattern. 

 All glob special characters <tt>&quot;%*?[]{}&quot;</tt> must be prefixed with ``%''. To escape a literal ``%'' you shall use ``%%''. 

 For example the pattern <tt>&quot;foo-%*.jpeg&quot;</tt> will match all the filenames prefixed by ``foo-'' and terminating with ``.jpeg'', and <tt>&quot;foo-%?%?%?.jpeg&quot;</tt> will match all the filenames prefixed with ``foo-'', followed by a sequence of three characters, and terminating with ``.jpeg''. 

 This pattern type is deprecated in favor of <i>glob</i> and <i>sequence</i>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>glob_sequence</i>.</dl><dt><b>pixel_format</b>
<dd>Set the pixel format of the images to read. If not specified the pixel format is guessed from the first image file in the sequence.
<dt><b>start_number</b>
<dd>Set the index of the file matched by the image file pattern to start to read from. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>start_number_range</b>
<dd>Set the index interval range to check when looking for the first image file in the sequence, starting from <i>start_number</i>. Default value is 5.
<dt><b>ts_from_file</b>
<dd>If set to 1, will set frame timestamp to modification time of image file. Note that monotonity of timestamps is not provided: images go in the same order as without this option. Default value is 0. If set to 2, will set frame timestamp to the modification time of the image file in nanosecond precision.
<dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd>Set the video size of the images to read. If not specified the video size is guessed from the first image file in the sequence.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> for creating a video from the images in the file sequence <i>img-001.jpeg</i>, <i>img-002.jpeg</i>, ..., assuming an input frame rate of 10 frames per second: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -framerate 10 -i 'img-%03d.jpeg' out.mkv</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>As above, but start by reading from a file with index 100 in the sequence: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -framerate 10 -start_number 100 -i 'img-%03d.jpeg' out.mkv</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Read images matching the ``*.png'' glob pattern , that is all the files terminating with the ``.png'' suffix: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -framerate 10 -pattern_type glob -i &quot;*.png&quot; out.mkv</pre></dl><h3>libgme</h3>The Game Music Emu library is a collection of video game music file emulators. 

 See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://code.google.com/p/game-music-emu/">http://code.google.com/p/game-music-emu/</a></b>&gt; for more information. 

 Some files have multiple tracks. The demuxer will pick the first track by default. The <b>track_index</b> option can be used to select a different track. Track indexes start at 0. The demuxer exports the number of tracks as <i>tracks</i> meta data entry. 

 For very large files, the <b>max_size</b> option may have to be adjusted.
<h3>libopenmpt</h3>libopenmpt based module demuxer 

 See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://lib.openmpt.org/libopenmpt/">https://lib.openmpt.org/libopenmpt/</a></b>&gt; for more information. 

 Some files have multiple subsongs (tracks) this can be set with the <b>subsong</b> option. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>subsong</b>
<dd>Set the subsong index. This can be either 'all', 'auto', or the index of the subsong. Subsong indexes start at 0. The default is 'auto'. 

 The default value is to let libopenmpt choose.
<dt><b>layout</b>
<dd>Set the channel layout. Valid values are 1, 2, and 4 channel layouts. The default value is <font SIZE="-1">STEREO.</font>
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd>Set the sample rate for libopenmpt to output. Range is from 1000 to <font SIZE="-1">INT_MAX.</font> The value default is 48000.</dl><h3>mov/mp4/3gp/QuickTime</h3>QuickTime / <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> demuxer. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>enable_drefs</b>
<dd>Enable loading of external tracks, disabled by default. Enabling this can theoretically leak information in some use cases.
<dt><b>use_absolute_path</b>
<dd>Allows loading of external tracks via absolute paths, disabled by default. Enabling this poses a security risk. It should only be enabled if the source is known to be non malicious.</dl><h3>mpegts</h3><font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> transport stream demuxer. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>resync_size</b>
<dd>Set size limit for looking up a new synchronization. Default value is 65536.
<dt><b>fix_teletext_pts</b>
<dd>Override teletext packet <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> values with the timestamps calculated from the <font SIZE="-1">PCR</font> of the first program which the teletext stream is part of and is not discarded. Default value is 1, set this option to 0 if you want your teletext packet <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> values untouched.
<dt><b>ts_packetsize</b>
<dd>Output option carrying the raw packet size in bytes. Show the detected raw packet size, cannot be set by the user.
<dt><b>scan_all_pmts</b>
<dd>Scan and combine all PMTs. The value is an integer with value from -1 to 1 (-1 means automatic setting, 1 means enabled, 0 means disabled). Default value is -1.</dl><h3>mpjpeg</h3><font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> encapsulated in multi-part <font SIZE="-1">MIME</font> demuxer. 

 This demuxer allows reading of <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG,</font> where each frame is represented as a part of multipart/x-mixed-replace stream.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>strict_mime_boundary</b>
<dd>Default implementation applies a relaxed standard to multi-part <font SIZE="-1">MIME</font> boundary detection, to prevent regression with numerous existing endpoints not generating a proper <font SIZE="-1">MIME MJPEG</font> stream. Turning this option on by setting it to 1 will result in a stricter check of the boundary value.</dl><h3>rawvideo</h3>Raw video demuxer. 

 This demuxer allows one to read raw video data. Since there is no header specifying the assumed video parameters, the user must specify them in order to be able to decode the data correctly. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Set input video frame rate. Default value is 25.
<dt><b>pixel_format</b>
<dd>Set the input video pixel format. Default value is <tt>&quot;yuv420p&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd>Set the input video size. This value must be specified explicitly.</dl>
 

 For example to read a rawvideo file <i>input.raw</i> with <b>ffplay</b>, assuming a pixel format of <tt>&quot;rgb24&quot;</tt>, a video size of <tt>&quot;320x240&quot;</tt>, and a frame rate of 10 images per second, use the command: 

 <pre> ffplay -f rawvideo -pixel_format rgb24 -video_size 320x240 -framerate 10 input.raw</pre><h3>sbg</h3>SBaGen script demuxer. 

 This demuxer reads the script language used by SBaGen &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://uazu.net/sbagen/">http://uazu.net/sbagen/</a></b>&gt; to generate binaural beats sessions. A <font SIZE="-1">SBG</font> script looks like that: 

 <pre> -SE
 a: 300-2.5/3 440+4.5/0
 b: 300-2.5/0 440+4.5/3
 off: -
 NOW == a
 +0:07:00 == b
 +0:14:00 == a
 +0:21:00 == b
 +0:30:00 off</pre>A <font SIZE="-1">SBG</font> script can mix absolute and relative timestamps. If the script uses either only absolute timestamps (including the script start time) or only relative ones, then its layout is fixed, and the conversion is straightforward. On the other hand, if the script mixes both kind of timestamps, then the <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NOW</i></font><i></i> reference for relative timestamps will be taken from the current time of day at the time the script is read, and the script layout will be frozen according to that reference. That means that if the script is directly played, the actual times will match the absolute timestamps up to the sound controller's clock accuracy, but if the user somehow pauses the playback or seeks, all times will be shifted accordingly.
<h3>tedcaptions</h3><font SIZE="-1">JSON</font> captions used for &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.ted.com/">http://www.ted.com/</a></b>&gt;. 

 <font SIZE="-1">TED</font> does not provide links to the captions, but they can be guessed from the page. The file <i>tools/bookmarklets.html</i> from the FFmpeg source tree contains a bookmarklet to expose them. 

 This demuxer accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>start_time</b>
<dd>Set the start time of the <font SIZE="-1">TED</font> talk, in milliseconds. The default is 15000 (15s). It is used to sync the captions with the downloadable videos, because they include a 15s intro.</dl>
 

 Example: convert the captions to a format most players understand: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.ted.com/talks/subtitles/id/1/lang/en">http://www.ted.com/talks/subtitles/id/1/lang/en</a> talk1-en.srt</pre><h2>Muxers</h2>Muxers are configured elements in FFmpeg which allow writing multimedia streams to a particular type of file. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported muxers are enabled by default. You can list all available muxers using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-muxers&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the muxers with the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-muxers&quot;</tt> and selectively enable / disable single muxers with the options <tt>&quot;--enable-muxer=</tt>MUXER<tt>&quot;</tt> / <tt>&quot;--disable-muxer=</tt>MUXER<tt>&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-muxers&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of enabled muxers. Use <tt>&quot;-formats&quot;</tt> to view a combined list of enabled demuxers and muxers. 

 A description of some of the currently available muxers follows.
<h3>aiff</h3>Audio Interchange File Format muxer. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>write_id3v2</b>
<dd>Enable ID3v2 tags writing when set to 1. Default is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>id3v2_version</b>
<dd>Select ID3v2 version to write. Currently only version 3 and 4 (aka. ID3v2.3 and ID3v2.4) are supported. The default is version 4.</dl><h3>asf</h3>Advanced Systems Format muxer. 

 Note that Windows Media Audio (wma) and Windows Media Video (wmv) use this muxer too. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>packet_size</b>
<dd>Set the muxer packet size. By tuning this setting you may reduce data fragmentation or muxer overhead depending on your source. Default value is 3200, minimum is 100, maximum is 64k.</dl><h3>avi</h3>Audio Video Interleaved muxer. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>reserve_index_space</b>
<dd>Reserve the specified amount of bytes for the OpenDML master index of each stream within the file header. By default additional master indexes are embedded within the data packets if there is no space left in the first master index and are linked together as a chain of indexes. This index structure can cause problems for some use cases, e.g. third-party software strictly relying on the OpenDML index specification or when file seeking is slow. Reserving enough index space in the file header avoids these problems. 

 The required index space depends on the output file size and should be about 16 bytes per gigabyte. When this option is omitted or set to zero the necessary index space is guessed.
<dt><b>write_channel_mask</b>
<dd>Write the channel layout mask into the audio stream header. 

 This option is enabled by default. Disabling the channel mask can be useful in specific scenarios, e.g. when merging multiple audio streams into one for compatibility with software that only supports a single audio stream in <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> (see <b>the ``amerge'' section in the ffmpeg-filters manual</b>).</dl><h3>chromaprint</h3>Chromaprint fingerprinter 

 This muxer feeds audio data to the Chromaprint library, which generates a fingerprint for the provided audio data. It takes a single signed native-endian 16-bit raw audio stream. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>silence_threshold</b>
<dd>Threshold for detecting silence, ranges from 0 to 32767. -1 for default (required for use with the AcoustID service).
<dt><b>algorithm</b>
<dd>Algorithm index to fingerprint with.
<dt><b>fp_format</b>
<dd>Format to output the fingerprint as. Accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>raw</b>
<dd>Binary raw fingerprint
<dt><b>compressed</b>
<dd>Binary compressed fingerprint
<dt><b>base64</b>
<dd>Base64 compressed fingerprint</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>crc</h3><font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> (Cyclic Redundancy Check) testing format. 

 This muxer computes and prints the Adler-32 <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of all the input audio and video frames. By default audio frames are converted to signed 16-bit raw audio and video frames to raw video before computing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC.</font> 

 The output of the muxer consists of a single line of the form: CRC=0x<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CRC</i></font><i></i>, where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CRC</i></font><i></i> is a hexadecimal number 0-padded to 8 digits containing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> for all the decoded input frames. 

 See also the <b>framecrc</b> muxer. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 For example to compute the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of the input, and store it in the file <i>out.crc</i>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -f crc out.crc</pre>You can print the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> to stdout with the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -f crc -</pre>You can select the output format of each frame with <b>ffmpeg</b> by specifying the audio and video codec and format. For example to compute the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of the input audio converted to <font SIZE="-1">PCM</font> unsigned 8-bit and the input video converted to <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> video, use the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:a pcm_u8 -c:v mpeg2video -f crc -</pre><h3>flv</h3>Adobe Flash Video Format muxer. 

 This muxer accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>flvflags</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd>Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>aac_seq_header_detect</b>
<dd>Place <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> sequence header based on audio stream data.
<dt><b>no_sequence_end</b>
<dd>Disable sequence end tag.
<dt><b>no_metadata</b>
<dd>Disable metadata tag.
<dt><b>no_duration_filesize</b>
<dd>Disable duration and filesize in metadata when they are equal to zero at the end of stream. (Be used to non-seekable living stream).
<dt><b>add_keyframe_index</b>
<dd>Used to facilitate seeking; particularly for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> pseudo streaming.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>dash</h3>Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">DASH</font>) muxer that creates segments and manifest files according to the MPEG-DASH standard <font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC 23009-1:2014.</font> 

 For more information see:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd><font SIZE="-1">ISO DASH</font> Specification: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/c065274_ISO_IEC_23009-1_2014.zip">http://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/c065274_ISO_IEC_23009-1_2014.zip</a></b>&gt;
<dt>&bull;
<dd>WebM <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> Specification: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://sites.google.com/a/webmproject.org/wiki/adaptive-streaming/webm-dash-specification">https://sites.google.com/a/webmproject.org/wiki/adaptive-streaming/webm-dash-specification</a></b>&gt;</dl>
 

 It creates a <font SIZE="-1">MPD</font> manifest file and segment files for each stream. 

 The segment filename might contain pre-defined identifiers used with SegmentTemplate as defined in section 5.3.9.4.4 of the standard. Available identifiers are ``$RepresentationID$'', ``$Number$'', ``$Bandwidth$'' and ``$Time$''. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -map 0 -map 0 -c:a libfdk_aac -c:v libx264
 -b:v:0 800k -b:v:1 300k -s:v:1 320x170 -profile:v:1 baseline
 -profile:v:0 main -bf 1 -keyint_min 120 -g 120 -sc_threshold 0
 -b_strategy 0 -ar:a:1 22050 -use_timeline 1 -use_template 1
 -window_size 5 -adaptation_sets &quot;id=0,streams=v id=1,streams=a&quot;
 -f dash /path/to/out.mpd</pre><dl COMPACT><dt><b>-min_seg_duration</b> <i>microseconds</i>
<dd>Set the segment length in microseconds.
<dt><b>-window_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd>Set the maximum number of segments kept in the manifest.
<dt><b>-extra_window_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd>Set the maximum number of segments kept outside of the manifest before removing from disk.
<dt><b>-remove_at_exit</b> <i>remove</i>
<dd>Enable (1) or disable (0) removal of all segments when finished.
<dt><b>-use_template</b> <i>template</i>
<dd>Enable (1) or disable (0) use of SegmentTemplate instead of SegmentList.
<dt><b>-use_timeline</b> <i>timeline</i>
<dd>Enable (1) or disable (0) use of SegmentTimeline in SegmentTemplate.
<dt><b>-single_file</b> <i>single_file</i>
<dd>Enable (1) or disable (0) storing all segments in one file, accessed using byte ranges.
<dt><b>-single_file_name</b> <i>file_name</i>
<dd>DASH-templated name to be used for baseURL. Implies <i>single_file</i> set to ``1''.
<dt><b>-init_seg_name</b> <i>init_name</i>
<dd>DASH-templated name to used for the initialization segment. Default is ``init-stream$RepresentationID$.m4s''
<dt><b>-media_seg_name</b> <i>segment_name</i>
<dd>DASH-templated name to used for the media segments. Default is ``chunk-stream$RepresentationID$-$Number%05d$.m4s''
<dt><b>-utc_timing_url</b> <i>utc_url</i>
