 A file <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> can have the form: 

 <pre> file:&lt;filename&gt;</pre>where <i>filename</i> is the path of the file to read. 

 An <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> that does not have a protocol prefix will be assumed to be a file <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font> Depending on the build, an <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> that looks like a Windows path with the drive letter at the beginning will also be assumed to be a file <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> (usually not the case in builds for unix-like systems). 

 For example to read from a file <i>input.mpeg</i> with <b>ffmpeg</b> use the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i file:input.mpeg output.mpeg</pre>This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>truncate</b>
<dd>Truncate existing files on write, if set to 1. A value of 0 prevents truncating. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>blocksize</b>
<dd>Set I/O operation maximum block size, in bytes. Default value is <tt>&quot;INT_MAX&quot;</tt>, which results in not limiting the requested block size. Setting this value reasonably low improves user termination request reaction time, which is valuable for files on slow medium.</dl><h3>ftp</h3><font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> (File Transfer Protocol). 

 Read from or write to remote resources using <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> protocol. 

 Following syntax is required. 

 <pre> <a HREF="ftp://[user[:password]@]server[:port]/path/to/remote/resource.mpeg">ftp://[user[:password]@]server[:port]/path/to/remote/resource.mpeg</a></pre>This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Set timeout in microseconds of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>ftp-anonymous-password</b>
<dd>Password used when login as anonymous user. Typically an e-mail address should be used.
<dt><b>ftp-write-seekable</b>
<dd>Control seekability of connection during encoding. If set to 1 the resource is supposed to be seekable, if set to 0 it is assumed not to be seekable. Default value is 0.</dl>
 

 <font SIZE="-1">NOTE:</font> Protocol can be used as output, but it is recommended to not do it, unless special care is taken (tests, customized server configuration etc.). Different <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> servers behave in different way during seek operation. ff* tools may produce incomplete content due to server limitations. 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>follow</b>
<dd>If set to 1, the protocol will retry reading at the end of the file, allowing reading files that still are being written. In order for this to terminate, you either need to use the rw_timeout option, or use the interrupt callback (for <font SIZE="-1">API</font> users).</dl><h3>gopher</h3>Gopher protocol.
<h3>hls</h3>Read Apple <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Live Streaming compliant segmented stream as a uniform one. The M3U8 playlists describing the segments can be remote <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> resources or local files, accessed using the standard file protocol. The nested protocol is declared by specifying &quot;+<i>proto</i>&quot; after the hls <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> scheme name, where <i>proto</i> is either ``file'' or ``http''. 

 <pre> hls+<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://host/path/to/remote/resource.m3u8">http://host/path/to/remote/resource.m3u8</a>
 hls+file://path/to/local/resource.m3u8</pre>Using this protocol is discouraged - the hls demuxer should work just as well (if not, please report the issues) and is more complete. To use the hls demuxer instead, simply use the direct URLs to the m3u8 files.
<h3>http</h3><font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol). 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>seekable</b>
<dd>Control seekability of connection. If set to 1 the resource is supposed to be seekable, if set to 0 it is assumed not to be seekable, if set to -1 it will try to autodetect if it is seekable. Default value is -1.
<dt><b>chunked_post</b>
<dd>If set to 1 use chunked Transfer-Encoding for posts, default is 1.
<dt><b>content_type</b>
<dd>Set a specific content type for the <font SIZE="-1">POST</font> messages or for listen mode.
<dt><b>http_proxy</b>
<dd>set <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> proxy to tunnel through e.g. <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com:1234">http://example.com:1234</a>
<dt><b>headers</b>
<dd>Set custom <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> headers, can override built in default headers. The value must be a string encoding the headers.
<dt><b>multiple_requests</b>
<dd>Use persistent connections if set to 1, default is 0.
<dt><b>post_data</b>
<dd>Set custom <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> post data.
<dt><b>user_agent</b>
<dd>Override the User-Agent header. If not specified the protocol will use a string describing the libavformat build. (``Lavf/&lt;version&gt;'')
<dt><b>user-agent</b>
<dd>This is a deprecated option, you can use user_agent instead it.
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Set timeout in microseconds of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>reconnect_at_eof</b>
<dd>If set then eof is treated like an error and causes reconnection, this is useful for live / endless streams.
<dt><b>reconnect_streamed</b>
<dd>If set then even streamed/non seekable streams will be reconnected on errors.
<dt><b>reconnect_delay_max</b>
<dd>Sets the maximum delay in seconds after which to give up reconnecting
<dt><b>mime_type</b>
<dd>Export the <font SIZE="-1">MIME</font> type.
<dt><b>icy</b>
<dd>If set to 1 request <font SIZE="-1">ICY</font> (SHOUTcast) metadata from the server. If the server supports this, the metadata has to be retrieved by the application by reading the <b>icy_metadata_headers</b> and <b>icy_metadata_packet</b> options. The default is 1.
<dt><b>icy_metadata_headers</b>
<dd>If the server supports <font SIZE="-1">ICY</font> metadata, this contains the ICY-specific <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> reply headers, separated by newline characters.
<dt><b>icy_metadata_packet</b>
<dd>If the server supports <font SIZE="-1">ICY</font> metadata, and <b>icy</b> was set to 1, this contains the last non-empty metadata packet sent by the server. It should be polled in regular intervals by applications interested in mid-stream metadata updates.
<dt><b>cookies</b>
<dd>Set the cookies to be sent in future requests. The format of each cookie is the same as the value of a Set-Cookie <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> response field. Multiple cookies can be delimited by a newline character.
<dt><b>offset</b>
<dd>Set initial byte offset.
<dt><b>end_offset</b>
<dd>Try to limit the request to bytes preceding this offset.
<dt><b>method</b>
<dd>When used as a client option it sets the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method for the request. 

 When used as a server option it sets the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method that is going to be expected from the client(s). If the expected and the received <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method do not match the client will be given a Bad Request response. When unset the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method is not checked for now. This will be replaced by autodetection in the future.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd>If set to 1 enables experimental <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server. This can be used to send data when used as an output option, or read data from a client with <font SIZE="-1">HTTP POST</font> when used as an input option. If set to 2 enables experimental multi-client <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server. This is not yet implemented in ffmpeg.c or ffserver.c and thus must not be used as a command line option. 

 <pre> # Server side (sending):
 ffmpeg -i somefile.ogg -c copy -listen 1 -f ogg http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
 
 # Client side (receiving):
 ffmpeg -i http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt; -c copy somefile.ogg
 
 # Client can also be done with wget:
 wget http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt; -O somefile.ogg
 
 # Server side (receiving):
 ffmpeg -listen 1 -i http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt; -c copy somefile.ogg
 
 # Client side (sending):
 ffmpeg -i somefile.ogg -chunked_post 0 -c copy -f ogg http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
 
 # Client can also be done with wget:
 wget --post-file=somefile.ogg http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</pre></dl>
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>HTTP</i></font><i> Cookies</i> 

 Some <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests will be denied unless cookie values are passed in with the request. The <b>cookies</b> option allows these cookies to be specified. At the very least, each cookie must specify a value along with a path and domain. <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests that match both the domain and path will automatically include the cookie value in the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Cookie header field. Multiple cookies can be delimited by a newline. 

 The required syntax to play a stream specifying a cookie is: 

 <pre> ffplay -cookies &quot;nlqptid=nltid=tsn; path=/; domain=somedomain.com;&quot; <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://somedomain.com/somestream.m3u8">http://somedomain.com/somestream.m3u8</a></pre><h3>Icecast</h3>Icecast protocol (stream to Icecast servers) 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>ice_genre</b>
<dd>Set the stream genre.
<dt><b>ice_name</b>
<dd>Set the stream name.
<dt><b>ice_description</b>
<dd>Set the stream description.
<dt><b>ice_url</b>
<dd>Set the stream website <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font>
<dt><b>ice_public</b>
<dd>Set if the stream should be public. The default is 0 (not public).
<dt><b>user_agent</b>
<dd>Override the User-Agent header. If not specified a string of the form ``Lavf/&lt;version&gt;'' will be used.
<dt><b>password</b>
<dd>Set the Icecast mountpoint password.
<dt><b>content_type</b>
<dd>Set the stream content type. This must be set if it is different from audio/mpeg.
<dt><b>legacy_icecast</b>
<dd>This enables support for Icecast versions &lt; 2.4.0, that do not support the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP PUT</font> method but the <font SIZE="-1">SOURCE</font> method.</dl>
 

 <pre> icecast://[&lt;username&gt;[:&lt;password&gt;]@]&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;/&lt;mountpoint&gt;</pre><h3>mmst</h3><font SIZE="-1">MMS</font> (Microsoft Media Server) protocol over <font SIZE="-1">TCP.</font>
<h3>mmsh</h3><font SIZE="-1">MMS</font> (Microsoft Media Server) protocol over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP.</font> 

 The required syntax is: 

 <pre> mmsh://&lt;server&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][/&lt;app&gt;][/&lt;playpath&gt;]</pre><h3>md5</h3><font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> output protocol. 

 Computes the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash of the data to be written, and on close writes this to the designated output or stdout if none is specified. It can be used to test muxers without writing an actual file. 

 Some examples follow. 

 <pre> # Write the MD5 hash of the encoded AVI file to the file output.avi.md5.
 ffmpeg -i input.flv -f avi -y md5:output.avi.md5
 
 # Write the MD5 hash of the encoded AVI file to stdout.
 ffmpeg -i input.flv -f avi -y md5:</pre>Note that some formats (typically <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font>) require the output protocol to be seekable, so they will fail with the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> output protocol.
<h3>pipe</h3><font SIZE="-1">UNIX</font> pipe access protocol. 

 Read and write from <font SIZE="-1">UNIX</font> pipes. 

 The accepted syntax is: 

 <pre> pipe:[&lt;number&gt;]</pre><i>number</i> is the number corresponding to the file descriptor of the pipe (e.g. 0 for stdin, 1 for stdout, 2 for stderr). If <i>number</i> is not specified, by default the stdout file descriptor will be used for writing, stdin for reading. 

 For example to read from stdin with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> cat test.wav | ffmpeg -i pipe:0
 # ...this is the same as...
 cat test.wav | ffmpeg -i pipe:</pre>For writing to stdout with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i test.wav -f avi pipe:1 | cat &gt; test.avi
 # ...this is the same as...
 ffmpeg -i test.wav -f avi pipe: | cat &gt; test.avi</pre>This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>blocksize</b>
<dd>Set I/O operation maximum block size, in bytes. Default value is <tt>&quot;INT_MAX&quot;</tt>, which results in not limiting the requested block size. Setting this value reasonably low improves user termination request reaction time, which is valuable if data transmission is slow.</dl>
 

 Note that some formats (typically <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font>), require the output protocol to be seekable, so they will fail with the pipe output protocol.
<h3>prompeg</h3>Pro-MPEG Code of Practice #3 Release 2 <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> protocol. 

 The Pro-MPEG CoP#3 <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> is a 2D parity-check forward error correction mechanism for <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> Transport Streams sent over <font SIZE="-1">RTP.</font> 

 This protocol must be used in conjunction with the <tt>&quot;rtp_mpegts&quot;</tt> muxer and the <tt>&quot;rtp&quot;</tt> protocol. 

 The required syntax is: 

 <pre> -f rtp_mpegts -fec prompeg=&lt;option&gt;=&lt;val&gt;... rtp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</pre>The destination <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> ports are <tt>&quot;port + 2&quot;</tt> for the column <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> stream and <tt>&quot;port + 4&quot;</tt> for the row <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> stream. 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>l=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>The number of columns (4-20, LxD &lt;= 100)
<dt><b>d=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>The number of rows (4-20, LxD &lt;= 100)</dl>
 

 Example usage: 

 <pre> -f rtp_mpegts -fec prompeg=l=8:d=4 rtp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</pre><h3>rtmp</h3>Real-Time Messaging Protocol. 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content across a <font SIZE="-1">TCP/IP</font> network. 

 The required syntax is: 

 <pre> <a HREF="rtmp://[">rtmp://[</a>&lt;username&gt;:&lt;password&gt;@]&lt;server&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][/&lt;app&gt;][/&lt;instance&gt;][/&lt;playpath&gt;]</pre>The accepted parameters are:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>username</b>
<dd>An optional username (mostly for publishing).
<dt><b>password</b>
<dd>An optional password (mostly for publishing).
<dt><b>server</b>
<dd>The address of the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server.
<dt><b>port</b>
<dd>The number of the <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> port to use (by default is 1935).
<dt><b>app</b>
<dd>It is the name of the application to access. It usually corresponds to the path where the application is installed on the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server (e.g. <i>/ondemand/</i>, <i>/flash/live/</i>, etc.). You can override the value parsed from the <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> through the <tt>&quot;rtmp_app&quot;</tt> option, too.
<dt><b>playpath</b>
<dd>It is the path or name of the resource to play with reference to the application specified in <i>app</i>, may be prefixed by ``mp4:''. You can override the value parsed from the <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> through the <tt>&quot;rtmp_playpath&quot;</tt> option, too.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd>Act as a server, listening for an incoming connection.
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Maximum time to wait for the incoming connection. Implies listen.</dl>
 

 Additionally, the following parameters can be set via command line options (or in code via <tt>&quot;AVOption&quot;</tt>s):
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>rtmp_app</b>
<dd>Name of application to connect on the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server. This option overrides the parameter specified in the <font SIZE="-1">URI.</font>
<dt><b>rtmp_buffer</b>
<dd>Set the client buffer time in milliseconds. The default is 3000.
<dt><b>rtmp_conn</b>
<dd>Extra arbitrary <font SIZE="-1">AMF</font> connection parameters, parsed from a string, e.g. like <tt>&quot;B:1 S:authMe O:1 NN:code:1.23 NS:flag:ok O:0&quot;</tt>. Each value is prefixed by a single character denoting the type, B for Boolean, N for number, S for string, O for object, or Z for null, followed by a colon. For Booleans the data must be either 0 or 1 for <font SIZE="-1">FALSE</font> or <font SIZE="-1">TRUE,</font> respectively. Likewise for Objects the data must be 0 or 1 to end or begin an object, respectively. Data items in subobjects may be named, by prefixing the type with 'N' and specifying the name before the value (i.e. <tt>&quot;NB:myFlag:1&quot;</tt>). This option may be used multiple times to construct arbitrary <font SIZE="-1">AMF</font> sequences.
<dt><b>rtmp_flashver</b>
<dd>Version of the Flash plugin used to run the <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> player. The default is <font SIZE="-1">LNX 9,0,124,2.</font> (When publishing, the default is <font SIZE="-1">FMLE/3.0</font> (compatible; &lt;libavformat version&gt;).)
<dt><b>rtmp_flush_interval</b>
<dd>Number of packets flushed in the same request (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPT</font> only). The default is 10.
<dt><b>rtmp_live</b>
<dd>Specify that the media is a live stream. No resuming or seeking in live streams is possible. The default value is <tt>&quot;any&quot;</tt>, which means the subscriber first tries to play the live stream specified in the playpath. If a live stream of that name is not found, it plays the recorded stream. The other possible values are <tt>&quot;live&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;recorded&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rtmp_pageurl</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the web page in which the media was embedded. By default no value will be sent.
<dt><b>rtmp_playpath</b>
<dd>Stream identifier to play or to publish. This option overrides the parameter specified in the <font SIZE="-1">URI.</font>
<dt><b>rtmp_subscribe</b>
<dd>Name of live stream to subscribe to. By default no value will be sent. It is only sent if the option is specified or if rtmp_live is set to live.
<dt><b>rtmp_swfhash</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">SHA256</font> hash of the decompressed <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> file (32 bytes).
<dt><b>rtmp_swfsize</b>
<dd>Size of the decompressed <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> file, required for SWFVerification.
<dt><b>rtmp_swfurl</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> player for the media. By default no value will be sent.
<dt><b>rtmp_swfverify</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">URL</font> to player swf file, compute hash/size automatically.
<dt><b>rtmp_tcurl</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the target stream. Defaults to <a HREF="proto://host[:port]/app.">proto://host[:port]/app.</a></dl>
 

 For example to read with <b>ffplay</b> a multimedia resource named ``sample'' from the application ``vod'' from an <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server ``myserver'': 

 <pre> ffplay <a HREF="rtmp://myserver/vod/sample">rtmp://myserver/vod/sample</a></pre>To publish to a password protected server, passing the playpath and app names separately: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f flv -rtmp_playpath some/long/path -rtmp_app long/app/name <a HREF="rtmp://username:password@myserver/">rtmp://username:password@myserver/</a></pre><h3>rtmpe</h3>Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol. 

 The Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPE</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within standard cryptographic primitives, consisting of Diffie-Hellman key exchange and <font SIZE="-1">HMACSHA256,</font> generating a pair of <font SIZE="-1">RC4</font> keys.
<h3>rtmps</h3>Real-Time Messaging Protocol over a secure <font SIZE="-1">SSL</font> connection. 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPS</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content across an encrypted connection.
<h3>rtmpt</h3>Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP.</font> 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPT</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests to traverse firewalls.
<h3>rtmpte</h3>Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP.</font> 

 The Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPTE</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests to traverse firewalls.
<h3>rtmpts</h3>Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS.</font> 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPTS</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS</font> requests to traverse firewalls.
<h3>libsmbclient</h3>libsmbclient permits one to manipulate <font SIZE="-1">CIFS/SMB</font> network resources. 

 Following syntax is required. 

 <pre> <a HREF="smb://[[domain:]user[:password@]]server[/share[/path[/file]]]">smb://[[domain:]user[:password@]]server[/share[/path[/file]]]</a></pre>This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Set timeout in milliseconds of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>truncate</b>
<dd>Truncate existing files on write, if set to 1. A value of 0 prevents truncating. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>workgroup</b>
<dd>Set the workgroup used for making connections. By default workgroup is not specified.</dl>
 

 For more information see: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.samba.org/">http://www.samba.org/</a></b>&gt;.
<h3>libssh</h3>Secure File Transfer Protocol via libssh 

 Read from or write to remote resources using <font SIZE="-1">SFTP</font> protocol. 

 Following syntax is required. 

 <pre> <a HREF="sftp://[user[:password]@]server[:port]/path/to/remote/resource.mpeg">sftp://[user[:password]@]server[:port]/path/to/remote/resource.mpeg</a></pre>This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Set timeout of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>truncate</b>
<dd>Truncate existing files on write, if set to 1. A value of 0 prevents truncating. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>private_key</b>
<dd>Specify the path of the file containing private key to use during authorization. By default libssh searches for keys in the <i>~/.ssh/</i> directory.</dl>
 

 Example: Play a file stored on remote server. 

 <pre> ffplay <a HREF="sftp://user:password@server_address:22/home/user/resource.mpeg">sftp://user:password@server_address:22/home/user/resource.mpeg</a></pre><h3>librtmp rtmp, rtmpe, rtmps, rtmpt, rtmpte</h3>Real-Time Messaging Protocol and its variants supported through librtmp. 

 Requires the presence of the librtmp headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with ``--enable-librtmp''. If enabled this will replace the native <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> protocol. 

 This protocol provides most client functions and a few server functions needed to support <font SIZE="-1">RTMP, RTMP</font> tunneled in <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPT</font>), encrypted <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPE</font>), <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> over <font SIZE="-1">SSL/TLS</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPS</font>) and tunneled variants of these encrypted types (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPTE, RTMPTS</font>). 

 The required syntax is: 

 <pre> &lt;rtmp_proto&gt;://&lt;server&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][/&lt;app&gt;][/&lt;playpath&gt;] &lt;options&gt;</pre>where <i>rtmp_proto</i> is one of the strings ``rtmp'', ``rtmpt'', ``rtmpe'', ``rtmps'', ``rtmpte'', ``rtmpts'' corresponding to each <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> variant, and <i>server</i>, <i>port</i>, <i>app</i> and <i>playpath</i> have the same meaning as specified for the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> native protocol. <i>options</i> contains a list of space-separated options of the form <i>key</i>=<i>val</i>. 

 See the librtmp manual page (man 3 librtmp) for more information. 

 For example, to stream a file in real-time to an <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i myfile -f flv <a HREF="rtmp://myserver/live/mystream">rtmp://myserver/live/mystream</a></pre>To play the same stream using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay &quot;<a HREF="rtmp://myserver/live/mystream">rtmp://myserver/live/mystream</a> live=1&quot;</pre><h3>rtp</h3>Real-time Transport Protocol. 

 The required syntax for an <font SIZE="-1">RTP URL</font> is: rtp://<i>hostname</i>[:<i>port</i>][?<i>option</i>=<i>val</i>...] 

 <i>port</i> specifies the <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port to use. 

 The following <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> options are supported:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>ttl=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>Set the <font SIZE="-1">TTL</font> (Time-To-Live) value (for multicast only).
<dt><b>rtcpport=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>Set the remote <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>localrtpport=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>Set the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>localrtcpport=</b><i>n</i><b>'</b>
<dd>Set the local <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>pkt_size=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>Set max packet size (in bytes) to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>connect=0|1</b>
<dd>Do a <tt>&quot;connect()&quot;</tt> on the <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> socket (if set to 1) or not (if set to 0).
<dt><b>sources=</b><i>ip</i><b>[,</b><i>ip</i><b>]</b>
<dd>List allowed source <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> addresses.
<dt><b>block=</b><i>ip</i><b>[,</b><i>ip</i><b>]</b>
<dd>List disallowed (blocked) source <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> addresses.
<dt><b>write_to_source=0|1</b>
<dd>Send packets to the source address of the latest received packet (if set to 1) or to a default remote address (if set to 0).
<dt><b>localport=</b><i>n</i>
<dd>Set the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port to <i>n</i>. 

 This is a deprecated option. Instead, <b>localrtpport</b> should be used.</dl>
 

 Important notes:
<dl COMPACT><dt>1.
<dd>If <b>rtcpport</b> is not set the <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port will be set to the <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port value plus 1.
<dt>2.
<dd>If <b>localrtpport</b> (the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port) is not set any available port will be used for the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> and <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> ports.
<dt>3.
<dd>If <b>localrtcpport</b> (the local <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port) is not set it will be set to the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port value plus 1.</dl><h3>rtsp</h3>Real-Time Streaming Protocol. 

 <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> is not technically a protocol handler in libavformat, it is a demuxer and muxer. The demuxer supports both normal <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> (with data transferred over <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font>; this is used by e.g. Apple and Microsoft) and Real-RTSP (with data transferred over <font SIZE="-1">RDT</font>). 

 The muxer can be used to send a stream using <font SIZE="-1">RTSP ANNOUNCE</font> to a server supporting it (currently Darwin Streaming Server and Mischa Spiegelmock's &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/revmischa/rtsp-server">https://github.com/revmischa/rtsp-server</a></b>&gt;). 

 The required syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> url is: 

 <pre> rtsp://&lt;hostname&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;]/&lt;path&gt;</pre>Options can be set on the <b>ffmpeg</b>/<b>ffplay</b> command line, or set in code via <tt>&quot;AVOption&quot;</tt>s or in <tt>&quot;avformat_open_input&quot;</tt>. 

 The following options are supported.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>initial_pause</b>
<dd>Do not start playing the stream immediately if set to 1. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>rtsp_transport</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> transport protocols. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>udp</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> as lower transport protocol.
<dt><b>tcp</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> (interleaving within the <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> control channel) as lower transport protocol.
<dt><b>udp_multicast</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> multicast as lower transport protocol.
<dt><b>http</b>
<dd>Use <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> tunneling as lower transport protocol, which is useful for passing proxies.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Multiple lower transport protocols may be specified, in that case they are tried one at a time (if the setup of one fails, the next one is tried). For the muxer, only the <b>tcp</b> and <b>udp</b> options are supported.</dl><dt><b>rtsp_flags</b>
<dd>Set <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> flags. 

 The following values are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>filter_src</b>
<dd>Accept packets only from negotiated peer address and port.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd>Act as a server, listening for an incoming connection.
<dt><b>prefer_tcp</b>
<dd>Try <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> for <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> transport first, if <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> is available as <font SIZE="-1">RTSP RTP</font> transport.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>none</b>.</dl><dt><b>allowed_media_types</b>
<dd>Set media types to accept from the server. 

 The following flags are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>video</b>
<dd><dt><b>audio</b>
<dd><dt><b>data</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>By default it accepts all media types.</dl><dt><b>min_port</b>
<dd>Set minimum local <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> port. Default value is 5000.
<dt><b>max_port</b>
<dd>Set maximum local <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> port. Default value is 65000.
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Set maximum timeout (in seconds) to wait for incoming connections. 

 A value of -1 means infinite (default). This option implies the <b>rtsp_flags</b> set to <b>listen</b>.
<dt><b>reorder_queue_size</b>
<dd>Set number of packets to buffer for handling of reordered packets.
<dt><b>stimeout</b>
<dd>Set socket <font SIZE="-1">TCP I/O</font> timeout in microseconds.
<dt><b>user-agent</b>
<dd>Override User-Agent header. If not specified, it defaults to the libavformat identifier string.</dl>
 

 When receiving data over <font SIZE="-1">UDP,</font> the demuxer tries to reorder received packets (since they may arrive out of order, or packets may get lost totally). This can be disabled by setting the maximum demuxing delay to zero (via the <tt>&quot;max_delay&quot;</tt> field of AVFormatContext). 

 When watching multi-bitrate Real-RTSP streams with <b>ffplay</b>, the streams to display can be chosen with <tt>&quot;-vst&quot;</tt> <i>n</i> and <tt>&quot;-ast&quot;</tt> <i>n</i> for video and audio respectively, and can be switched on the fly by pressing <tt>&quot;v&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;a&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 The following examples all make use of the <b>ffplay</b> and <b>ffmpeg</b> tools.
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Watch a stream over <font SIZE="-1">UDP,</font> with a max reordering delay of 0.5 seconds: 

 <pre> ffplay -max_delay 500000 -rtsp_transport udp <a HREF="rtsp://server/video.mp4">rtsp://server/video.mp4</a></pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Watch a stream tunneled over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP:</font> 

 <pre> ffplay -rtsp_transport http <a HREF="rtsp://server/video.mp4">rtsp://server/video.mp4</a></pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Send a stream in realtime to a <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> server, for others to watch: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f rtsp -muxdelay 0.1 <a HREF="rtsp://server/live.sdp">rtsp://server/live.sdp</a></pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Receive a stream in realtime: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -rtsp_flags listen -i <a HREF="rtsp://ownaddress/live.sdp">rtsp://ownaddress/live.sdp</a> &lt;output&gt;</pre></dl><h3>sap</h3>Session Announcement Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RFC 2974</font>). This is not technically a protocol handler in libavformat, it is a muxer and demuxer. It is used for signalling of <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> streams, by announcing the <font SIZE="-1">SDP</font> for the streams regularly on a separate port. 

 <i>Muxer</i> 

 The syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> url given to the muxer is: 

 <pre> sap://&lt;destination&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][?&lt;options&gt;]</pre>The <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> packets are sent to <i>destination</i> on port <i>port</i>, or to port 5004 if no port is specified. <i>options</i> is a <tt>&quot;&amp;&quot;</tt>-separated list. The following options are supported:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>announce_addr=</b><i>address</i>
<dd>Specify the destination <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address for sending the announcements to. If omitted, the announcements are sent to the commonly used <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> announcement multicast address 224.2.127.254 (sap.mcast.net), or ff0e::2:7ffe if <i>destination</i> is an IPv6 address.
<dt><b>announce_port=</b><i>port</i>
<dd>Specify the port to send the announcements on, defaults to 9875 if not specified.
<dt><b>ttl=</b><i>ttl</i>
<dd>Specify the time to live value for the announcements and <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> packets, defaults to 255.
<dt><b>same_port=</b><i>0|1</i>
<dd>If set to 1, send all <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> streams on the same port pair. If zero (the default), all streams are sent on unique ports, with each stream on a port 2 numbers higher than the previous. VLC/Live555 requires this to be set to 1, to be able to receive the stream. The <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> stack in libavformat for receiving requires all streams to be sent on unique ports.</dl>
 

 Example command lines follow. 

 To broadcast a stream on the local subnet, for watching in <font SIZE="-1">VLC:</font> 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f sap <a HREF="sap://224.0.0.255?same_port=1">sap://224.0.0.255?same_port=1</a></pre>Similarly, for watching in <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f sap <a HREF="sap://224.0.0.255">sap://224.0.0.255</a></pre>And for watching in <b>ffplay</b>, over IPv6: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f sap <a HREF="sap://[ff0e::1:2:3:4]">sap://[ff0e::1:2:3:4]</a></pre><i>Demuxer</i> 

 The syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> url given to the demuxer is: 

 <pre> <a HREF="sap://[">sap://[</a>&lt;address&gt;][:&lt;port&gt;]</pre><i>address</i> is the multicast address to listen for announcements on, if omitted, the default 224.2.127.254 (sap.mcast.net) is used. <i>port</i> is the port that is listened on, 9875 if omitted. 

 The demuxers listens for announcements on the given address and port. Once an announcement is received, it tries to receive that particular stream. 

 Example command lines follow. 

 To play back the first stream announced on the normal <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> multicast address: 

 <pre> ffplay sap://</pre>To play back the first stream announced on one the default IPv6 <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> multicast address: 

 <pre> ffplay <a HREF="sap://[ff0e::2:7ffe]">sap://[ff0e::2:7ffe]</a></pre><h3>sctp</h3>Stream Control Transmission Protocol. 

 The accepted <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> syntax is: 

 <pre> sctp://&lt;host&gt;:&lt;port&gt;[?&lt;options&gt;]</pre>The protocol accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>listen</b>
<dd>If set to any value, listen for an incoming connection. Outgoing connection is done by default.
<dt><b>max_streams</b>
<dd>Set the maximum number of streams. By default no limit is set.</dl><h3>srtp</h3>Secure Real-time Transport Protocol. 

 The accepted options are:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>srtp_in_suite</b>
<dd><dt><b>srtp_out_suite</b>
<dd>Select input and output encoding suites. 

 Supported values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>AES_CM_128_HMAC_SHA1_80</b></font>
<dd><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SRTP_AES128_CM_HMAC_SHA1_80</b></font>
<dd><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>AES_CM_128_HMAC_SHA1_32</b></font>
<dd><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SRTP_AES128_CM_HMAC_SHA1_32</b></font>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>srtp_in_params</b>
<dd><dt><b>srtp_out_params</b>
<dd>Set input and output encoding parameters, which are expressed by a base64-encoded representation of a binary block. The first 16 bytes of this binary block are used as master key, the following 14 bytes are used as master salt.</dl><h3>subfile</h3>Virtually extract a segment of a file or another stream. The underlying stream must be seekable. 

 Accepted options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>start</b>
<dd>Start offset of the extracted segment, in bytes.
<dt><b>end</b>
<dd>End offset of the extracted segment, in bytes.</dl>
 

 Examples: 

 Extract a chapter from a <font SIZE="-1">DVD VOB</font> file (start and end sectors obtained externally and multiplied by 2048): 

 <pre> subfile,,start,153391104,end,268142592,,:/media/dvd/VIDEO_TS/VTS_08_1.VOB</pre>Play an <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> file directly from a <font SIZE="-1">TAR</font> archive: 

 <pre> subfile,,start,183241728,end,366490624,,:archive.tar</pre><h3>tee</h3>Writes the output to multiple protocols. The individual outputs are separated by | 

 <pre> tee:file://path/to/local/this.avi|file://path/to/local/that.avi</pre><h3>tcp</h3>Transmission Control Protocol. 

 The required syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> url is: 

 <pre> tcp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;[?&lt;options&gt;]</pre><i>options</i> contains a list of &amp;-separated options of the form <i>key</i>=<i>val</i>. 

 The list of supported options follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>listen=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>Listen for an incoming connection. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>timeout=</b><i>microseconds</i>
<dd>Set raise error timeout, expressed in microseconds. 

 This option is only relevant in read mode: if no data arrived in more than this time interval, raise error.
<dt><b>listen_timeout=</b><i>milliseconds</i>
<dd>Set listen timeout, expressed in milliseconds.
<dt><b>recv_buffer_size=</b><i>bytes</i>
<dd>Set receive buffer size, expressed bytes.
<dt><b>send_buffer_size=</b><i>bytes</i>
<dd>Set send buffer size, expressed bytes.</dl>
 

 The following example shows how to setup a listening <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> connection with <b>ffmpeg</b>, which is then accessed with <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i &lt;input&gt; -f &lt;format&gt; tcp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;?listen
 ffplay tcp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</pre><h3>tls</h3>Transport Layer Security (<font SIZE="-1">TLS</font>) / Secure Sockets Layer (<font SIZE="-1">SSL</font>) 

 The required syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">TLS/SSL</font> url is: 

 <pre> tls://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;[?&lt;options&gt;]</pre>The following parameters can be set via command line options (or in code via <tt>&quot;AVOption&quot;</tt>s):
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>ca_file, cafile=</b><i>filename</i>
<dd>A file containing certificate authority (<font SIZE="-1">CA</font>) root certificates to treat as trusted. If the linked <font SIZE="-1">TLS</font> library contains a default this might not need to be specified for verification to work, but not all libraries and setups have defaults built in. The file must be in OpenSSL <font SIZE="-1">PEM</font> format.
<dt><b>tls_verify=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>If enabled, try to verify the peer that we are communicating with. Note, if using OpenSSL, this currently only makes sure that the peer certificate is signed by one of the root certificates in the <font SIZE="-1">CA</font> database, but it does not validate that the certificate actually matches the host name we are trying to connect to. (With GnuTLS, the host name is validated as well.) 

 This is disabled by default since it requires a <font SIZE="-1">CA</font> database to be provided by the caller in many cases.
<dt><b>cert_file, cert=</b><i>filename</i>
<dd>A file containing a certificate to use in the handshake with the peer. (When operating as server, in listen mode, this is more often required by the peer, while client certificates only are mandated in certain setups.)
<dt><b>key_file, key=</b><i>filename</i>
<dd>A file containing the private key for the certificate.
<dt><b>listen=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>If enabled, listen for connections on the provided port, and assume the server role in the handshake instead of the client role.</dl>
 

 Example command lines: 

 To create a <font SIZE="-1">TLS/SSL</font> server that serves an input stream. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i &lt;input&gt; -f &lt;format&gt; tls://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;?listen&amp;cert=&lt;server.crt&gt;&amp;key=&lt;server.key&gt;</pre>To play back a stream from the <font SIZE="-1">TLS/SSL</font> server using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay tls://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</pre><h3>udp</h3>User Datagram Protocol. 

 The required syntax for an <font SIZE="-1">UDP URL</font> is: 

 <pre> udp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;[?&lt;options&gt;]</pre><i>options</i> contains a list of &amp;-separated options of the form <i>key</i>=<i>val</i>. 

 In case threading is enabled on the system, a circular buffer is used to store the incoming data, which allows one to reduce loss of data due to <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> socket buffer overruns. The <i>fifo_size</i> and <i>overrun_nonfatal</i> options are related to this buffer. 

 The list of supported options follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>buffer_size=</b><i>size</i>
<dd>Set the <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> maximum socket buffer size in bytes. This is used to set either the receive or send buffer size, depending on what the socket is used for. Default is 64KB. See also <i>fifo_size</i>.
<dt><b>bitrate=</b><i>bitrate</i>
<dd>If set to nonzero, the output will have the specified constant bitrate if the input has enough packets to sustain it.
<dt><b>burst_bits=</b><i>bits</i>
<dd>When using <i>bitrate</i> this specifies the maximum number of bits in packet bursts.
<dt><b>localport=</b><i>port</i>
<dd>Override the local <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> port to bind with.
<dt><b>localaddr=</b><i>addr</i>
<dd>Choose the local <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address. This is useful e.g. if sending multicast and the host has multiple interfaces, where the user can choose which interface to send on by specifying the <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address of that interface.
<dt><b>pkt_size=</b><i>size</i>
<dd>Set the size in bytes of <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> packets.
<dt><b>reuse=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>Explicitly allow or disallow reusing <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> sockets.
<dt><b>ttl=</b><i>ttl</i>
<dd>Set the time to live value (for multicast only).
<dt><b>connect=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>Initialize the <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> socket with <tt>&quot;connect()&quot;</tt>. In this case, the destination address can't be changed with ff_udp_set_remote_url later. If the destination address isn't known at the start, this option can be specified in ff_udp_set_remote_url, too. This allows finding out the source address for the packets with getsockname, and makes writes return with <font SIZE="-1">AVERROR</font>(<font SIZE="-1">ECONNREFUSED</font>) if ``destination unreachable'' is received. For receiving, this gives the benefit of only receiving packets from the specified peer address/port.
<dt><b>sources=</b><i>address</i><b>[,</b><i>address</i><b>]</b>
<dd>Only receive packets sent to the multicast group from one of the specified sender <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> addresses.
<dt><b>block=</b><i>address</i><b>[,</b><i>address</i><b>]</b>
<dd>Ignore packets sent to the multicast group from the specified sender <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> addresses.
<dt><b>fifo_size=</b><i>units</i>
<dd>Set the <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> receiving circular buffer size, expressed as a number of packets with size of 188 bytes. If not specified defaults to 7*4096.
<dt><b>overrun_nonfatal=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>Survive in case of <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> receiving circular buffer overrun. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>timeout=</b><i>microseconds</i>
<dd>Set raise error timeout, expressed in microseconds. 

 This option is only relevant in read mode: if no data arrived in more than this time interval, raise error.
<dt><b>broadcast=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd>Explicitly allow or disallow <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> broadcasting. 

 Note that broadcasting may not work properly on networks having a broadcast storm protection.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to stream over <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> to a remote endpoint: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i &lt;input&gt; -f &lt;format&gt; udp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to stream in mpegts format over <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> using 188 sized <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> packets, using a large input buffer: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i &lt;input&gt; -f mpegts udp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;?pkt_size=188&amp;buffer_size=65535</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to receive over <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> from a remote endpoint: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i <a HREF="udp://[">udp://[</a>&lt;multicast-address&gt;]:&lt;port&gt; ...</pre></dl><h3>unix</h3>Unix local socket 

 The required syntax for a Unix socket <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> is: 

 <pre> unix://&lt;filepath&gt;</pre>The following parameters can be set via command line options (or in code via <tt>&quot;AVOption&quot;</tt>s):
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd>Timeout in ms.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd>Create the Unix socket in listening mode.</dl><h2>Device Options</h2>The libavdevice library provides the same interface as libavformat. Namely, an input device is considered like a demuxer, and an output device like a muxer, and the interface and generic device options are the same provided by libavformat (see the ffmpeg-formats manual). 

 In addition each input or output device may support so-called private options, which are specific for that component. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, or by setting the value explicitly in the device <tt>&quot;AVFormatContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use.
<h2>Input Devices</h2>Input devices are configured elements in FFmpeg which enable accessing the data coming from a multimedia device attached to your system. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported input devices are enabled by default. You can list all available ones using the configure option ``--list-indevs''. 

 You can disable all the input devices using the configure option ``--disable-indevs'', and selectively enable an input device using the option &quot;--enable-indev=<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>INDEV</i></font><i></i>``, or you can disable a particular input device using the option ''--disable-indev=<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>INDEV</i></font><i></i>&quot;. 

 The option ``-devices'' of the ff* tools will display the list of supported input devices. 

 A description of the currently available input devices follows.
<h3>alsa</h3><font SIZE="-1">ALSA</font> (Advanced Linux Sound Architecture) input device. 

 To enable this input device during configuration you need libasound installed on your system. 

 This device allows capturing from an <font SIZE="-1">ALSA</font> device. The name of the device to capture has to be an <font SIZE="-1">ALSA</font> card identifier. 

 An <font SIZE="-1">ALSA</font> identifier has the syntax: 

 <pre> hw:&lt;CARD&gt;[,&lt;DEV&gt;[,&lt;SUBDEV&gt;]]</pre>where the <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>DEV</i></font><i></i> and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SUBDEV</i></font><i></i> components are optional. 

 The three arguments (in order: <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CARD</i></font><i></i>,<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>DEV</i></font><i></i>,<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SUBDEV</i></font><i></i>) specify card number or identifier, device number and subdevice number (-1 means any). 

 To see the list of cards currently recognized by your system check the files <i>/proc/asound/cards</i> and <i>/proc/asound/devices</i>. 

 For example to capture with <b>ffmpeg</b> from an <font SIZE="-1">ALSA</font> device with card id 0, you may run the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f alsa -i hw:0 alsaout.wav</pre>For more information see: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.alsa-project.org/alsa-doc/alsa-lib/pcm.html">http://www.alsa-project.org/alsa-doc/alsa-lib/pcm.html</a></b>&gt; 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd>Set the sample rate in Hz. Default is 48000.
<dt><b>channels</b>
<dd>Set the number of channels. Default is 2.</dl><h3>avfoundation</h3>AVFoundation input device. 

 AVFoundation is the currently recommended framework by Apple for streamgrabbing on <font SIZE="-1">OSX</font> &gt;= 10.7 as well as on iOS. 

 The input filename has to be given in the following syntax: 

 <pre> -i &quot;[[VIDEO]:[AUDIO]]&quot;</pre>The first entry selects the video input while the latter selects the audio input. The stream has to be specified by the device name or the device index as shown by the device list. Alternatively, the video and/or audio input device can be chosen by index using the 

 <pre> B&lt;-video_device_index E&lt;lt&gt;INDEXE&lt;gt&gt;&gt;</pre>and/or 

 <pre> B&lt;-audio_device_index E&lt;lt&gt;INDEXE&lt;gt&gt;&gt;</pre>, overriding any device name or index given in the input filename. 

 All available devices can be enumerated by using <b>-list_devices true</b>, listing all device names and corresponding indices. 

 There are two device name aliases:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&quot;default&quot;
<dd>Select the AVFoundation default device of the corresponding type.
<dt>&quot;none&quot;
<dd>Do not record the corresponding media type. This is equivalent to specifying an empty device name or index.</dl>
 

 <i>Options</i> 

 AVFoundation supports the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>-list_devices &lt;TRUE|FALSE&gt;</b>
<dd>If set to true, a list of all available input devices is given showing all device names and indices.
<dt><b>-video_device_index &lt;</b><font SIZE="-1"><b>INDEX</b></font><b>&gt;</b>
<dd>Specify the video device by its index. Overrides anything given in the input filename.
<dt><b>-audio_device_index &lt;</b><font SIZE="-1"><b>INDEX</b></font><b>&gt;</b>
<dd>Specify the audio device by its index. Overrides anything given in the input filename.
<dt><b>-pixel_format &lt;</b><font SIZE="-1"><b>FORMAT</b></font><b>&gt;</b>
<dd>Request the video device to use a specific pixel format. If the specified format is not supported, a list of available formats is given and the first one in this list is used instead. Available pixel formats are: <tt>&quot;monob, rgb555be, rgb555le, rgb565be, rgb565le, rgb24, bgr24, 0rgb, bgr0, 0bgr, rgb0, 
&nbsp;bgr48be, uyvy422, yuva444p, yuva444p16le, yuv444p, yuv422p16, yuv422p10, yuv444p10, 
&nbsp;yuv420p, nv12, yuyv422, gray&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>-framerate</b>
<dd>Set the grabbing frame rate. Default is <tt>&quot;ntsc&quot;</tt>, corresponding to a frame rate of <tt>&quot;30000/1001&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>-video_size</b>
<dd>Set the video frame size.
<dt><b>-capture_cursor</b>
<dd>Capture the mouse pointer. Default is 0.
<dt><b>-capture_mouse_clicks</b>
<dd>Capture the screen mouse clicks. Default is 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Print the list of AVFoundation supported devices and exit: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i &quot;&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Record video from video device 0 and audio from audio device 0 into out.avi: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f avfoundation -i &quot;0:0&quot; out.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Record video from video device 2 and audio from audio device 1 into out.avi: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f avfoundation -video_device_index 2 -i &quot;:1&quot; out.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Record video from the system default video device using the pixel format bgr0 and do not record any audio into out.avi: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f avfoundation -pixel_format bgr0 -i &quot;default:none&quot; out.avi</pre></dl><h3>bktr</h3><font SIZE="-1">BSD</font> video input device. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Set the frame rate.
<dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd>Set the video frame size. Default is <tt>&quot;vga&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>standard</b>
<dd>Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>pal</b>
<dd><dt><b>ntsc</b>
<dd><dt><b>secam</b>
<dd><dt><b>paln</b>
<dd><dt><b>palm</b>
<dd><dt><b>ntscj</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>decklink</h3>The decklink input device provides capture capabilities for Blackmagic DeckLink devices. 

 To enable this input device, you need the Blackmagic DeckLink <font SIZE="-1">SDK</font> and you need to configure with the appropriate <tt>&quot;--extra-cflags&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;--extra-ldflags&quot;</tt>. On Windows, you need to run the <font SIZE="-1">IDL</font> files through <b>widl</b>. 

 DeckLink is very picky about the formats it supports. Pixel format of the input can be set with <b>raw_format</b>. Framerate and video size must be determined for your device with <b>-list_formats 1</b>. Audio sample rate is always 48 kHz and the number of channels can be 2, 8 or 16. Note that all audio channels are bundled in one single audio track. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>list_devices</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of devices and exit. Defaults to <b>false</b>.
<dt><b>list_formats</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of supported formats and exit. Defaults to <b>false</b>.
<dt><b>format_code &lt;FourCC&gt;</b>
<dd>This sets the input video format to the format given by the FourCC. To see the supported values of your device(s) use <b>list_formats</b>. Note that there is a FourCC <b>'pal '</b> that can also be used as <b>pal</b> (3 letters).
<dt><b>bm_v210</b>
<dd>This is a deprecated option, you can use <b>raw_format</b> instead. If set to <b>1</b>, video is captured in 10 bit v210 instead of uyvy422. Not all Blackmagic devices support this option.
<dt><b>raw_format</b>
<dd>Set the pixel format of the captured video. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>uyvy422</b>
<dd><dt><b>yuv422p10</b>
<dd><dt><b>argb</b>
<dd><dt><b>bgra</b>
<dd><dt><b>rgb10</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>teletext_lines</b>
<dd>If set to nonzero, an additional teletext stream will be captured from the vertical ancillary data. Both <font SIZE="-1">SD PAL</font> (576i) and <font SIZE="-1">HD</font> (1080i or 1080p) sources are supported. In case of <font SIZE="-1">HD</font> sources, <font SIZE="-1">OP47</font> packets are decoded. 

 This option is a bitmask of the <font SIZE="-1">SD PAL VBI</font> lines captured, specifically lines 6 to 22, and lines 318 to 335. Line 6 is the <font SIZE="-1">LSB</font> in the mask. Selected lines which do not contain teletext information will be ignored. You can use the special <b>all</b> constant to select all possible lines, or <b>standard</b> to skip lines 6, 318 and 319, which are not compatible with all receivers. 

 For <font SIZE="-1">SD</font> sources, ffmpeg needs to be compiled with <tt>&quot;--enable-libzvbi&quot;</tt>. For <font SIZE="-1">HD</font> sources, on older (pre-4K) DeckLink card models you have to capture in 10 bit mode.
<dt><b>channels</b>
<dd>Defines number of audio channels to capture. Must be <b>2</b>, <b>8</b> or <b>16</b>. Defaults to <b>2</b>.
<dt><b>duplex_mode</b>
<dd>Sets the decklink device duplex mode. Must be <b>unset</b>, <b>half</b> or <b>full</b>. Defaults to <b>unset</b>.
<dt><b>video_input</b>
<dd>Sets the video input source. Must be <b>unset</b>, <b>sdi</b>, <b>hdmi</b>, <b>optical_sdi</b>, <b>component</b>, <b>composite</b> or <b>s_video</b>. Defaults to <b>unset</b>.
<dt><b>audio_input</b>
<dd>Sets the audio input source. Must be <b>unset</b>, <b>embedded</b>, <b>aes_ebu</b>, <b>analog</b>, <b>analog_xlr</b>, <b>analog_rca</b> or <b>microphone</b>. Defaults to <b>unset</b>.
<dt><b>video_pts</b>
<dd>Sets the video packet timestamp source. Must be <b>video</b>, <b>audio</b>, <b>reference</b> or <b>wallclock</b>. Defaults to <b>video</b>.
<dt><b>audio_pts</b>
<dd>Sets the audio packet timestamp source. Must be <b>video</b>, <b>audio</b>, <b>reference</b> or <b>wallclock</b>. Defaults to <b>audio</b>.
<dt><b>draw_bars</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, color bars are drawn in the event of a signal loss. Defaults to <b>true</b>.
<dt><b>queue_size</b>
<dd>Sets maximum input buffer size in bytes. If the buffering reaches this value, incoming frames will be dropped. Defaults to <b>1073741824</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>List input devices: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f decklink -list_devices 1 -i dummy</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>List supported formats: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f decklink -list_formats 1 -i 'Intensity Pro'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Capture video clip at 1080i50: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -format_code Hi50 -f decklink -i 'Intensity Pro' -c:a copy -c:v copy output.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Capture video clip at 1080i50 10 bit: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -bm_v210 1 -format_code Hi50 -f decklink -i 'UltraStudio Mini Recorder' -c:a copy -c:v copy output.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Capture video clip at 1080i50 with 16 audio channels: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -channels 16 -format_code Hi50 -f decklink -i 'UltraStudio Mini Recorder' -c:a copy -c:v copy output.avi</pre></dl><h3>kmsgrab</h3><font SIZE="-1">KMS</font> video input device. 

 Captures the <font SIZE="-1">KMS</font> scanout framebuffer associated with a specified <font SIZE="-1">CRTC</font> or plane as a <font SIZE="-1">DRM</font> object that can be passed to other hardware functions. 

 Requires either <font SIZE="-1">DRM</font> master or <font SIZE="-1">CAP_SYS_ADMIN</font> to run. 

 If you don't understand what all of that means, you probably don't want this. Look at <b>x11grab</b> instead. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>device</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">DRM</font> device to capture on. Defaults to <b>/dev/dri/card0</b>.
<dt><b>format</b>
<dd>Pixel format of the framebuffer. Defaults to <b>bgr0</b>.
<dt><b>format_modifier</b>
<dd>Format modifier to signal on output frames. This is necessary to import correctly into some APIs, but can't be autodetected. See the libdrm documentation for possible values.
<dt><b>crtc_id</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">KMS CRTC ID</font> to define the capture source. The first active plane on the given <font SIZE="-1">CRTC</font> will be used.
<dt><b>plane_id</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">KMS</font> plane <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> to define the capture source. Defaults to the first active plane found if neither <b>crtc_id</b> nor <b>plane_id</b> are specified.
<dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Framerate to capture at. This is not synchronised to any page flipping or framebuffer changes - it just defines the interval at which the framebuffer is sampled. Sampling faster than the framebuffer update rate will generate independent frames with the same content. Defaults to <tt>30</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Capture from the first active plane, download the result to normal frames and encode. This will only work if the framebuffer is both linear and mappable - if not, the result may be scrambled or fail to download. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f kmsgrab -i - -vf 'hwdownload,format=bgr0' output.mp4</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Capture from <font SIZE="-1">CRTC ID 42</font> at 60fps, map the result to <font SIZE="-1">VAAPI,</font> convert to <font SIZE="-1">NV12</font> and encode as H.264. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -crtc_id 42 -framerate 60 -f kmsgrab -i - -vf 'hwmap=derive_device=vaapi,scale_vaapi=w=1920:h=1080:format=nv12' -c:v h264_vaapi output.mp4</pre></dl><h3>libndi_newtek</h3>The libndi_newtek input device provides capture capabilities for using <font SIZE="-1">NDI</font> (Network Device Interface, standard created by NewTek). 

 Input filename is a <font SIZE="-1">NDI</font> source name that could be found by sending -find_sources 1 to command line - it has no specific syntax but human-readable formatted. 

 To enable this input device, you need the <font SIZE="-1">NDI SDK</font> and you need to configure with the appropriate <tt>&quot;--extra-cflags&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;--extra-ldflags&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>find_sources</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of found/available <font SIZE="-1">NDI</font> sources and exit. Defaults to <b>false</b>.
<dt><b>wait_sources</b>
<dd>Override time to wait until the number of online sources have changed. Defaults to <b>0.5</b>.
<dt><b>allow_video_fields</b>
<dd>When this flag is <b>false</b>, all video that you receive will be progressive. Defaults to <b>true</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>List input devices: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f libndi_newtek -find_sources 1 -i dummy</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Restream to <font SIZE="-1">NDI:</font> 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f libndi_newtek -i &quot;DEV-5.INTERNAL.M1STEREO.TV (NDI_SOURCE_NAME_1)&quot; -f libndi_newtek -y NDI_SOURCE_NAME_2</pre></dl><h3>dshow</h3>Windows DirectShow input device. 

 DirectShow support is enabled when FFmpeg is built with the mingw-w64 project. Currently only audio and video devices are supported. 

 Multiple devices may be opened as separate inputs, but they may also be opened on the same input, which should improve synchronism between them. 

 The input name should be in the format: 

 <pre> &lt;TYPE&gt;=&lt;NAME&gt;[:&lt;TYPE&gt;=&lt;NAME&gt;]</pre>where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>TYPE</i></font><i></i> can be either <i>audio</i> or <i>video</i>, and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NAME</i></font><i></i> is the device's name or alternative name.. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 If no options are specified, the device's defaults are used. If the device does not support the requested options, it will fail to open.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd>Set the video size in the captured video.
<dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Set the frame rate in the captured video.
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd>Set the sample rate (in Hz) of the captured audio.
<dt><b>sample_size</b>
<dd>Set the sample size (in bits) of the captured audio.
<dt><b>channels</b>
<dd>Set the number of channels in the captured audio.
<dt><b>list_devices</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of devices and exit.
<dt><b>list_options</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of selected device's options and exit.
<dt><b>video_device_number</b>
<dd>Set video device number for devices with the same name (starts at 0, defaults to 0).
<dt><b>audio_device_number</b>
<dd>Set audio device number for devices with the same name (starts at 0, defaults to 0).
<dt><b>pixel_format</b>
<dd>Select pixel format to be used by DirectShow. This may only be set when the video codec is not set or set to rawvideo.
<dt><b>audio_buffer_size</b>
<dd>Set audio device buffer size in milliseconds (which can directly impact latency, depending on the device). Defaults to using the audio device's default buffer size (typically some multiple of 500ms). Setting this value too low can degrade performance. See also &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/dd377582(v=vs.85).aspx">http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/dd377582(v=vs.85).aspx</a></b>&gt;
<dt><b>video_pin_name</b>
<dd>Select video capture pin to use by name or alternative name.
<dt><b>audio_pin_name</b>
<dd>Select audio capture pin to use by name or alternative name.
<dt><b>crossbar_video_input_pin_number</b>
<dd>Select video input pin number for crossbar device. This will be routed to the crossbar device's Video Decoder output pin. Note that changing this value can affect future invocations (sets a new default) until system reboot occurs.
<dt><b>crossbar_audio_input_pin_number</b>
<dd>Select audio input pin number for crossbar device. This will be routed to the crossbar device's Audio Decoder output pin. Note that changing this value can affect future invocations (sets a new default) until system reboot occurs.
<dt><b>show_video_device_dialog</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, before capture starts, popup a display dialog to the end user, allowing them to change video filter properties and configurations manually. Note that for crossbar devices, adjusting values in this dialog may be needed at times to toggle between <font SIZE="-1">PAL</font> (25 fps) and <font SIZE="-1">NTSC</font> (29.97) input frame rates, sizes, interlacing, etc. Changing these values can enable different scan rates/frame rates and avoiding green bars at the bottom, flickering scan lines, etc. Note that with some devices, changing these properties can also affect future invocations (sets new defaults) until system reboot occurs.
<dt><b>show_audio_device_dialog</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, before capture starts, popup a display dialog to the end user, allowing them to change audio filter properties and configurations manually.
<dt><b>show_video_crossbar_connection_dialog</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, before capture starts, popup a display dialog to the end user, allowing them to manually modify crossbar pin routings, when it opens a video device.
<dt><b>show_audio_crossbar_connection_dialog</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, before capture starts, popup a display dialog to the end user, allowing them to manually modify crossbar pin routings, when it opens an audio device.
<dt><b>show_analog_tv_tuner_dialog</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, before capture starts, popup a display dialog to the end user, allowing them to manually modify <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> channels and frequencies.
<dt><b>show_analog_tv_tuner_audio_dialog</b>
<dd>If set to <b>true</b>, before capture starts, popup a display dialog to the end user, allowing them to manually modify <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> audio (like mono vs. stereo, Language A,B or C).
<dt><b>audio_device_load</b>
<dd>Load an audio capture filter device from file instead of searching it by name. It may load additional parameters too, if the filter supports the serialization of its properties to. To use this an audio capture source has to be specified, but it can be anything even fake one.
<dt><b>audio_device_save</b>
<dd>Save the currently used audio capture filter device and its parameters (if the filter supports it) to a file. If a file with the same name exists it will be overwritten.
<dt><b>video_device_load</b>
<dd>Load a video capture filter device from file instead of searching it by name. It may load additional parameters too, if the filter supports the serialization of its properties to. To use this a video capture source has to be specified, but it can be anything even fake one.
<dt><b>video_device_save</b>
<dd>Save the currently used video capture filter device and its parameters (if the filter supports it) to a file. If a file with the same name exists it will be overwritten.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Print the list of DirectShow supported devices and exit: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Open video device <i>Camera</i>: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f dshow -i video=&quot;Camera&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Open second video device with name <i>Camera</i>: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f dshow -video_device_number 1 -i video=&quot;Camera&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Open video device <i>Camera</i> and audio device <i>Microphone</i>: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f dshow -i video=&quot;Camera&quot;:audio=&quot;Microphone&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Print the list of supported options in selected device and exit: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -list_options true -f dshow -i video=&quot;Camera&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Specify pin names to capture by name or alternative name, specify alternative device name: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f dshow -audio_pin_name &quot;Audio Out&quot; -video_pin_name 2 -i video=video=&quot;@device_pnp_\\?\pci#ven_1a0a&amp;dev_6200&amp;subsys_62021461&amp;rev_01#4&amp;e2c7dd6&amp;0&amp;00e1#{65e8773d-8f56-11d0-a3b9-00a0c9223196}\{ca465100-deb0-4d59-818f-8c477184adf6}&quot;:audio=&quot;Microphone&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Configure a crossbar device, specifying crossbar pins, allow user to adjust video capture properties at startup: 

 <pre> $ ffmpeg -f dshow -show_video_device_dialog true -crossbar_video_input_pin_number 0
 -crossbar_audio_input_pin_number 3 -i video=&quot;AVerMedia BDA Analog Capture&quot;:audio=&quot;AVerMedia BDA Analog Capture&quot;</pre></dl><h3>fbdev</h3>Linux framebuffer input device. 

 The Linux framebuffer is a graphic hardware-independent abstraction layer to show graphics on a computer monitor, typically on the console. It is accessed through a file device node, usually <i>/dev/fb0</i>. 

 For more detailed information read the file Documentation/fb/framebuffer.txt included in the Linux source tree. 

 See also &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://linux-fbdev.sourceforge.net/">http://linux-fbdev.sourceforge.net/</a></b>&gt;, and <i><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-fbset/">fbset</a></i>(1). 

 To record from the framebuffer device <i>/dev/fb0</i> with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f fbdev -framerate 10 -i /dev/fb0 out.avi</pre>You can take a single screenshot image with the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f fbdev -framerate 1 -i /dev/fb0 -frames:v 1 screenshot.jpeg</pre><i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Set the frame rate. Default is 25.</dl><h3>gdigrab</h3>Win32 GDI-based screen capture device. 

 This device allows you to capture a region of the display on Windows. 

 There are two options for the input filename: 

 <pre> desktop</pre>or 

 <pre> title=&lt;window_title&gt;</pre>The first option will capture the entire desktop, or a fixed region of the desktop. The second option will instead capture the contents of a single window, regardless of its position on the screen. 

 For example, to grab the entire desktop using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f gdigrab -framerate 6 -i desktop out.mpg</pre>Grab a 640x480 region at position <tt>&quot;10,20&quot;</tt>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f gdigrab -framerate 6 -offset_x 10 -offset_y 20 -video_size vga -i desktop out.mpg</pre>Grab the contents of the window named ``Calculator'' 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f gdigrab -framerate 6 -i title=Calculator out.mpg</pre><i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>draw_mouse</b>
<dd>Specify whether to draw the mouse pointer. Use the value <tt>0</tt> to not draw the pointer. Default value is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>Set the grabbing frame rate. Default value is <tt>&quot;ntsc&quot;</tt>, corresponding to a frame rate of <tt>&quot;30000/1001&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>show_region</b>
<dd>Show grabbed region on screen. 

 If <i>show_region</i> is specified with <tt>1</tt>, then the grabbing region will be indicated on screen. With this option, it is easy to know what is being grabbed if only a portion of the screen is grabbed. 

 Note that <i>show_region</i> is incompatible with grabbing the contents of a single window. 

 For example: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f gdigrab -show_region 1 -framerate 6 -video_size cif -offset_x 10 -offset_y 20 -i desktop out.mpg</pre><dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd>Set the video frame size. The default is to capture the full screen if <i>desktop</i> is selected, or the full window size if <i>title=window_title</i> is selected.
<dt><b>offset_x</b>
<dd>When capturing a region with <i>video_size</i>, set the distance from the left edge of the screen or desktop. 

 Note that the offset calculation is from the top left corner of the primary monitor on Windows. If you have a monitor positioned to the left of your primary monitor, you will need to use a negative <i>offset_x</i> value to move the region to that monitor.
<dt><b>offset_y</b>
<dd>When capturing a region with <i>video_size</i>, set the distance from the top edge of the screen or desktop. 

 Note that the offset calculation is from the top left corner of the primary monitor on Windows. If you have a monitor positioned above your primary monitor, you will need to use a negative <i>offset_y</i> value to move the region to that monitor.</dl><h3>iec61883</h3>FireWire <font SIZE="-1">DV/HDV</font> input device using libiec61883. 

 To enable this input device, you need libiec61883, libraw1394 and libavc1394 installed on your system. Use the configure option <tt>&quot;--enable-libiec61883&quot;</tt> to compile with the device enabled. 

 The iec61883 capture device supports capturing from a video device connected via <font SIZE="-1">IEEE1394</font> (FireWire), using libiec61883 and the new Linux FireWire stack (juju). This is the default <font SIZE="-1">DV/HDV</font> input method in Linux Kernel 2.6.37 and later, since the old FireWire stack was removed. 

 Specify the FireWire port to be used as input file, or ``auto'' to choose the first port connected. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dvtype</b>
<dd>Override autodetection of <font SIZE="-1">DV/HDV.</font> This should only be used if auto detection does not work, or if usage of a different device type should be prohibited. Treating a <font SIZE="-1">DV</font> device as <font SIZE="-1">HDV</font> (or vice versa) will not work and result in undefined behavior. The values <b>auto</b>, <b>dv</b> and <b>hdv</b> are supported.
<dt><b>dvbuffer</b>
<dd>Set maximum size of buffer for incoming data, in frames. For <font SIZE="-1">DV,</font> this is an exact value. For <font SIZE="-1">HDV,</font> it is not frame exact, since <font SIZE="-1">HDV</font> does not have a fixed frame size.
<dt><b>dvguid</b>
<dd>Select the capture device by specifying its <font SIZE="-1">GUID.</font> Capturing will only be performed from the specified device and fails if no device with the given <font SIZE="-1">GUID</font> is found. This is useful to select the input if multiple devices are connected at the same time. Look at /sys/bus/firewire/devices to find out the GUIDs.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Grab and show the input of a FireWire <font SIZE="-1">DV/HDV</font> device. 

 <pre> ffplay -f iec61883 -i auto</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Grab and record the input of a FireWire <font SIZE="-1">DV/HDV</font> device, using a packet buffer of 100000 packets if the source is <font SIZE="-1">HDV.</font> 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f iec61883 -i auto -hdvbuffer 100000 out.mpg</pre></dl><h3>jack</h3><font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> input device. 

 To enable this input device during configuration you need libjack installed on your system. 

 A <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> input device creates one or more <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> writable clients, one for each audio channel, with name <i>client_name</i>:input_<i>N</i>, where <i>client_name</i> is the name provided by the application, and <i>N</i> is a number which identifies the channel. Each writable client will send the acquired data to the FFmpeg input device. 

 Once you have created one or more <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> readable clients, you need to connect them to one or more <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> writable clients. 

 To connect or disconnect <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> clients you can use the <b>jack_connect</b> and <b>jack_disconnect</b> programs, or do it through a graphical interface, for example with <b>qjackctl</b>. 

 To list the <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> clients and their properties you can invoke the command <b>jack_lsp</b>. 

 Follows an example which shows how to capture a <font SIZE="-1">JACK</font> readable client with <b>ffmpeg</b>. 

 <pre> # Create a JACK writable client with name &quot;ffmpeg&quot;.
 $ ffmpeg -f jack -i ffmpeg -y out.wav
 
 # Start the sample jack_metro readable client.
 $ jack_metro -b 120 -d 0.2 -f 4000
 
 # List the current JACK clients.
 $ jack_lsp -c
 system:capture_1
 system:capture_2
 system:playback_1
 system:playback_2
 ffmpeg:input_1
 metro:120_bpm
 
 # Connect metro to the ffmpeg writable client.
 $ jack_connect metro:120_bpm ffmpeg:input_1</pre>For more information read: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://jackaudio.org/">http://jackaudio.org/</a></b>&gt; 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>channels</b>
<dd>Set the number of channels. Default is 2.</dl><h3>lavfi</h3>Libavfilter input virtual device. 

 This input device reads data from the open output pads of a libavfilter filtergraph. 

 For each filtergraph open output, the input device will create a corresponding stream which is mapped to the generated output. Currently only video data is supported. The filtergraph is specified through the option <b>graph</b>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>graph</b>
<dd>Specify the filtergraph to use as input. Each video open output must be labelled by a unique string of the form &quot;out<i>N</i>&quot;, where <i>N</i> is a number starting from 0 corresponding to the mapped input stream generated by the device. The first unlabelled output is automatically assigned to the ``out0'' label, but all the others need to be specified explicitly. 

 The suffix ``+subcc'' can be appended to the output label to create an extra stream with the closed captions packets attached to that output (experimental; only for <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608 / CEA-708</font> for now). The subcc streams are created after all the normal streams, in the order of the corresponding stream. For example, if there is ``out19+subcc'', ``out7+subcc'' and up to ``out42'', the stream #43 is subcc for stream #7 and stream #44 is subcc for stream #19. 

 If not specified defaults to the filename specified for the input device.
<dt><b>graph_file</b>
<dd>Set the filename of the filtergraph to be read and sent to the other filters. Syntax of the filtergraph is the same as the one specified by the option <i>graph</i>.
<dt><b>dumpgraph</b>
<dd>Dump graph to stderr.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Create a color video stream and play it back with <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi -graph &quot;color=c=pink [out0]&quot; dummy</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>As the previous example, but use filename for specifying the graph description, and omit the ``out0'' label: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi color=c=pink</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Create three different video test filtered sources and play them: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi -graph &quot;testsrc [out0]; testsrc,hflip [out1]; testsrc,negate [out2]&quot; test3</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Read an audio stream from a file using the amovie source and play it back with <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi &quot;amovie=test.wav&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Read an audio stream and a video stream and play it back with <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi &quot;movie=test.avi[out0];amovie=test.wav[out1]&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Dump decoded frames to images and closed captions to a file (experimental): 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f lavfi -i &quot;movie=test.ts[out0+subcc]&quot; -map v frame%08d.png -map s -c copy -f rawvideo subcc.bin</pre></dl><h3>libcdio</h3>Audio-CD input device based on libcdio. 

 To enable this input device during configuration you need libcdio installed on your system. It requires the configure option <tt>&quot;--enable-libcdio&quot;</tt>. 

 This device allows playing and grabbing from an Audio-CD. 

 For example to copy with <b>ffmpeg</b> the entire Audio-CD in <i>/dev/sr0</i>, you may run the command: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f libcdio -i /dev/sr0 cd.wav</pre><i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>speed</b>
<dd>Set drive reading speed. Default value is 0. 

 The speed is specified CD-ROM speed units. The speed is set through the libcdio <tt>&quot;cdio_cddap_speed_set&quot;</tt> function. On many CD-ROM drives, specifying a value too large will result in using the fastest speed.
<dt><b>paranoia_mode</b>
<dd>Set paranoia recovery mode flags. It accepts one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>disable</b>
<dd><dt><b>verify</b>
<dd><dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd><dt><b>neverskip</b>
<dd><dt><b>full</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>disable</b>. 

 For more information about the available recovery modes, consult the paranoia project documentation.</dl></dl><h3>libdc1394</h3><font SIZE="-1">IIDC1394</font> input device, based on libdc1394 and libraw1394. 

 Requires the configure option <tt>&quot;--enable-libdc1394&quot;</tt>.
<h3>openal</h3>The OpenAL input device provides audio capture on all systems with a working OpenAL 1.1 implementation. 

 To enable this input device during configuration, you need OpenAL headers and libraries installed on your system, and need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-openal&quot;</tt>. 

 OpenAL headers and libraries should be provided as part of your OpenAL implementation, or as an additional download (an <font SIZE="-1">SDK</font>). Depending on your installation you may need to specify additional flags via the <tt>&quot;--extra-cflags&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;--extra-ldflags&quot;</tt> for allowing the build system to locate the OpenAL headers and libraries. 

 An incomplete list of OpenAL implementations follows:
