 <pre> dctdnoiz=4.5</pre>The same operation can be achieved using the expression system: 

 <pre> dctdnoiz=e='gte(c, 4.5*3)'</pre>Violent denoise using a block size of <tt>&quot;16x16&quot;</tt>: 

 <pre> dctdnoiz=15:n=4</pre><h3>deband</h3>Remove banding artifacts from input video. It works by replacing banded pixels with average value of referenced pixels. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>1thr</b>
<dd><dt><b>2thr</b>
<dd><dt><b>3thr</b>
<dd><dt><b>4thr</b>
<dd>Set banding detection threshold for each plane. Default is 0.02. Valid range is 0.00003 to 0.5. If difference between current pixel and reference pixel is less than threshold, it will be considered as banded.
<dt><b>range, r</b>
<dd>Banding detection range in pixels. Default is 16. If positive, random number in range 0 to set value will be used. If negative, exact absolute value will be used. The range defines square of four pixels around current pixel.
<dt><b>direction, d</b>
<dd>Set direction in radians from which four pixel will be compared. If positive, random direction from 0 to set direction will be picked. If negative, exact of absolute value will be picked. For example direction 0, -PI or -2*PI radians will pick only pixels on same row and -PI/2 will pick only pixels on same column.
<dt><b>blur, b</b>
<dd>If enabled, current pixel is compared with average value of all four surrounding pixels. The default is enabled. If disabled current pixel is compared with all four surrounding pixels. The pixel is considered banded if only all four differences with surrounding pixels are less than threshold.
<dt><b>coupling, c</b>
<dd>If enabled, current pixel is changed if and only if all pixel components are banded, e.g. banding detection threshold is triggered for all color components. The default is disabled.</dl><h3>decimate</h3>Drop duplicated frames at regular intervals. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>cycle</b>
<dd>Set the number of frames from which one will be dropped. Setting this to <i>N</i> means one frame in every batch of <i>N</i> frames will be dropped. Default is <tt>5</tt>.
<dt><b>dupthresh</b>
<dd>Set the threshold for duplicate detection. If the difference metric for a frame is less than or equal to this value, then it is declared as duplicate. Default is <tt>1.1</tt>
<dt><b>scthresh</b>
<dd>Set scene change threshold. Default is <tt>15</tt>.
<dt><b>blockx</b>
<dd><dt><b>blocky</b>
<dd>Set the size of the x and y-axis blocks used during metric calculations. Larger blocks give better noise suppression, but also give worse detection of small movements. Must be a power of two. Default is <tt>32</tt>.
<dt><b>ppsrc</b>
<dd>Mark main input as a pre-processed input and activate clean source input stream. This allows the input to be pre-processed with various filters to help the metrics calculation while keeping the frame selection lossless. When set to <tt>1</tt>, the first stream is for the pre-processed input, and the second stream is the clean source from where the kept frames are chosen. Default is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>chroma</b>
<dd>Set whether or not chroma is considered in the metric calculations. Default is <tt>1</tt>.</dl><h3>deflate</h3>Apply deflate effect to the video. 

 This filter replaces the pixel by the local(3x3) average by taking into account only values lower than the pixel. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold0</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold1</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold2</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold3</b>
<dd>Limit the maximum change for each plane, default is 65535. If 0, plane will remain unchanged.</dl><h3>deflicker</h3>Remove temporal frame luminance variations. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set moving-average filter size in frames. Default is 5. Allowed range is 2 - 129.
<dt><b>mode, m</b>
<dd>Set averaging mode to smooth temporal luminance variations. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>am</b>
<dd>Arithmetic mean
<dt><b>gm</b>
<dd>Geometric mean
<dt><b>hm</b>
<dd>Harmonic mean
<dt><b>qm</b>
<dd>Quadratic mean
<dt><b>cm</b>
<dd>Cubic mean
<dt><b>pm</b>
<dd>Power mean
<dt><b>median</b>
<dd>Median</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>bypass</b>
<dd>Do not actually modify frame. Useful when one only wants metadata.</dl><h3>dejudder</h3>Remove judder produced by partially interlaced telecined content. 

 Judder can be introduced, for instance, by <b>pullup</b> filter. If the original source was partially telecined content then the output of <tt>&quot;pullup,dejudder&quot;</tt> will have a variable frame rate. May change the recorded frame rate of the container. Aside from that change, this filter will not affect constant frame rate video. 

 The option available in this filter is:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>cycle</b>
<dd>Specify the length of the window over which the judder repeats. 

 Accepts any integer greater than 1. Useful values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>4</b>
<dd>If the original was telecined from 24 to 30 fps (Film to <font SIZE="-1">NTSC</font>).
<dt><b>5</b>
<dd>If the original was telecined from 25 to 30 fps (<font SIZE="-1">PAL</font> to <font SIZE="-1">NTSC</font>).
<dt><b>20</b>
<dd>If a mixture of the two.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The default is <b>4</b>.</dl></dl><h3>delogo</h3>Suppress a <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> station logo by a simple interpolation of the surrounding pixels. Just set a rectangle covering the logo and watch it disappear (and sometimes something even uglier appear - your mileage may vary). 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Specify the top left corner coordinates of the logo. They must be specified.
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>Specify the width and height of the logo to clear. They must be specified.
<dt><b>band, t</b>
<dd>Specify the thickness of the fuzzy edge of the rectangle (added to <i>w</i> and <i>h</i>). The default value is 1. This option is deprecated, setting higher values should no longer be necessary and is not recommended.
<dt><b>show</b>
<dd>When set to 1, a green rectangle is drawn on the screen to simplify finding the right <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i>, and <i>h</i> parameters. The default value is 0. 

 The rectangle is drawn on the outermost pixels which will be (partly) replaced with interpolated values. The values of the next pixels immediately outside this rectangle in each direction will be used to compute the interpolated pixel values inside the rectangle.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Set a rectangle covering the area with top left corner coordinates 0,0 and size 100x77, and a band of size 10: 

 <pre> delogo=x=0:y=0:w=100:h=77:band=10</pre></dl><h3>deshake</h3>Attempt to fix small changes in horizontal and/or vertical shift. This filter helps remove camera shake from hand-holding a camera, bumping a tripod, moving on a vehicle, etc. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd><dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>Specify a rectangular area where to limit the search for motion vectors. If desired the search for motion vectors can be limited to a rectangular area of the frame defined by its top left corner, width and height. These parameters have the same meaning as the drawbox filter which can be used to visualise the position of the bounding box. 

 This is useful when simultaneous movement of subjects within the frame might be confused for camera motion by the motion vector search. 

 If any or all of <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i> and <i>h</i> are set to -1 then the full frame is used. This allows later options to be set without specifying the bounding box for the motion vector search. 

 Default - search the whole frame.
<dt><b>rx</b>
<dd><dt><b>ry</b>
<dd>Specify the maximum extent of movement in x and y directions in the range 0-64 pixels. Default 16.
<dt><b>edge</b>
<dd>Specify how to generate pixels to fill blanks at the edge of the frame. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>blank, 0</b>
<dd>Fill zeroes at blank locations
<dt><b>original, 1</b>
<dd>Original image at blank locations
<dt><b>clamp, 2</b>
<dd>Extruded edge value at blank locations
<dt><b>mirror, 3</b>
<dd>Mirrored edge at blank locations</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>mirror</b>.</dl><dt><b>blocksize</b>
<dd>Specify the blocksize to use for motion search. Range 4-128 pixels, default 8.
<dt><b>contrast</b>
<dd>Specify the contrast threshold for blocks. Only blocks with more than the specified contrast (difference between darkest and lightest pixels) will be considered. Range 1-255, default 125.
<dt><b>search</b>
<dd>Specify the search strategy. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>exhaustive, 0</b>
<dd>Set exhaustive search
<dt><b>less, 1</b>
<dd>Set less exhaustive search.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>exhaustive</b>.</dl><dt><b>filename</b>
<dd>If set then a detailed log of the motion search is written to the specified file.
<dt><b>opencl</b>
<dd>If set to 1, specify using OpenCL capabilities, only available if FFmpeg was configured with <tt>&quot;--enable-opencl&quot;</tt>. Default value is 0.</dl><h3>despill</h3>Remove unwanted contamination of foreground colors, caused by reflected color of greenscreen or bluescreen. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>type</b>
<dd>Set what type of despill to use.
<dt><b>mix</b>
<dd>Set how spillmap will be generated.
<dt><b>expand</b>
<dd>Set how much to get rid of still remaining spill.
<dt><b>red</b>
<dd>Controls amount of red in spill area.
<dt><b>green</b>
<dd>Controls amount of green in spill area. Should be -1 for greenscreen.
<dt><b>blue</b>
<dd>Controls amount of blue in spill area. Should be -1 for bluescreen.
<dt><b>brightness</b>
<dd>Controls brightness of spill area, preserving colors.
<dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd>Modify alpha from generated spillmap.</dl><h3>detelecine</h3>Apply an exact inverse of the telecine operation. It requires a predefined pattern specified using the pattern option which must be the same as that passed to the telecine filter. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>first_field</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>top, t</b>
<dd>top field first
<dt><b>bottom, b</b>
<dd>bottom field first The default value is <tt>&quot;top&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>pattern</b>
<dd>A string of numbers representing the pulldown pattern you wish to apply. The default value is <tt>23</tt>.
<dt><b>start_frame</b>
<dd>A number representing position of the first frame with respect to the telecine pattern. This is to be used if the stream is cut. The default value is <tt>0</tt>.</dl><h3>dilation</h3>Apply dilation effect to the video. 

 This filter replaces the pixel by the local(3x3) maximum. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold0</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold1</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold2</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold3</b>
<dd>Limit the maximum change for each plane, default is 65535. If 0, plane will remain unchanged.
<dt><b>coordinates</b>
<dd>Flag which specifies the pixel to refer to. Default is 255 i.e. all eight pixels are used. 

 Flags to local 3x3 coordinates maps like this: 

 <pre> 1 2 3
 4 5
 6 7 8</pre></dl><h3>displace</h3>Displace pixels as indicated by second and third input stream. 

 It takes three input streams and outputs one stream, the first input is the source, and second and third input are displacement maps. 

 The second input specifies how much to displace pixels along the x-axis, while the third input specifies how much to displace pixels along the y-axis. If one of displacement map streams terminates, last frame from that displacement map will be used. 

 Note that once generated, displacements maps can be reused over and over again. 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>edge</b>
<dd>Set displace behavior for pixels that are out of range. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>blank</b>
<dd>Missing pixels are replaced by black pixels.
<dt><b>smear</b>
<dd>Adjacent pixels will spread out to replace missing pixels.
<dt><b>wrap</b>
<dd>Out of range pixels are wrapped so they point to pixels of other side.
<dt><b>mirror</b>
<dd>Out of range pixels will be replaced with mirrored pixels.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <b>smear</b>.</dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Add ripple effect to rgb input of video size hd720: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -f lavfi -i nullsrc=s=hd720,lutrgb=128:128:128 -f lavfi -i nullsrc=s=hd720,geq='r=128+30*sin(2*PI*X/400+T):g=128+30*sin(2*PI*X/400+T):b=128+30*sin(2*PI*X/400+T)' -lavfi '[0][1][2]displace' OUTPUT</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Add wave effect to rgb input of video size hd720: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -f lavfi -i nullsrc=hd720,geq='r=128+80*(sin(sqrt((X-W/2)*(X-W/2)+(Y-H/2)*(Y-H/2))/220*2*PI+T)):g=128+80*(sin(sqrt((X-W/2)*(X-W/2)+(Y-H/2)*(Y-H/2))/220*2*PI+T)):b=128+80*(sin(sqrt((X-W/2)*(X-W/2)+(Y-H/2)*(Y-H/2))/220*2*PI+T))' -lavfi '[1]split[x][y],[0][x][y]displace' OUTPUT</pre></dl><h3>drawbox</h3>Draw a colored box on the input image. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The expressions which specify the top left corner coordinates of the box. It defaults to 0.
<dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd>The expressions which specify the width and height of the box; if 0 they are interpreted as the input width and height. It defaults to 0.
<dt><b>color, c</b>
<dd>Specify the color of the box to write. For the general syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. If the special value <tt>&quot;invert&quot;</tt> is used, the box edge color is the same as the video with inverted luma.
<dt><b>thickness, t</b>
<dd>The expression which sets the thickness of the box edge. Default value is <tt>3</tt>. 

 See below for the list of accepted constants.</dl>
 

 The parameters for <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i> and <i>h</i> and <i>t</i> are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>The input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (<i>w</i> / <i>h</i>) * <i>sar</i>.
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd><dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd>horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><b>in_h, ih</b>
<dd><dt><b>in_w, iw</b>
<dd>The input width and height.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>The input sample aspect ratio.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The x and y offset coordinates where the box is drawn.
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>The width and height of the drawn box.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>The thickness of the drawn box. 

 These constants allow the <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i>, <i>h</i> and <i>t</i> expressions to refer to each other, so you may for example specify <tt>&quot;y=x/dar&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;h=w/dar&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw a black box around the edge of the input image: 

 <pre> drawbox</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw a box with color red and an opacity of 50%: 

 <pre> drawbox=10:20:200:60:red@0.5</pre>The previous example can be specified as: 

 <pre> drawbox=x=10:y=20:w=200:h=60:color=red@0.5</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Fill the box with pink color: 

 <pre> drawbox=x=10:y=10:w=100:h=100:color=pink@0.5:t=max</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw a 2-pixel red 2.40:1 mask: 

 <pre> drawbox=x=-t:y=0.5*(ih-iw/2.4)-t:w=iw+t*2:h=iw/2.4+t*2:t=2:c=red</pre></dl><h3>drawgrid</h3>Draw a grid on the input image. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The expressions which specify the coordinates of some point of grid intersection (meant to configure offset). Both default to 0.
<dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd>The expressions which specify the width and height of the grid cell, if 0 they are interpreted as the input width and height, respectively, minus <tt>&quot;thickness&quot;</tt>, so image gets framed. Default to 0.
<dt><b>color, c</b>
<dd>Specify the color of the grid. For the general syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. If the special value <tt>&quot;invert&quot;</tt> is used, the grid color is the same as the video with inverted luma.
<dt><b>thickness, t</b>
<dd>The expression which sets the thickness of the grid line. Default value is <tt>1</tt>. 

 See below for the list of accepted constants.</dl>
 

 The parameters for <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i> and <i>h</i> and <i>t</i> are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>The input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (<i>w</i> / <i>h</i>) * <i>sar</i>.
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd><dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd>horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><b>in_h, ih</b>
<dd><dt><b>in_w, iw</b>
<dd>The input grid cell width and height.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>The input sample aspect ratio.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The x and y coordinates of some point of grid intersection (meant to configure offset).
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>The width and height of the drawn cell.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>The thickness of the drawn cell. 

 These constants allow the <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i>, <i>h</i> and <i>t</i> expressions to refer to each other, so you may for example specify <tt>&quot;y=x/dar&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;h=w/dar&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw a grid with cell 100x100 pixels, thickness 2 pixels, with color red and an opacity of 50%: 

 <pre> drawgrid=width=100:height=100:thickness=2:color=red@0.5</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw a white 3x3 grid with an opacity of 50%: 

 <pre> drawgrid=w=iw/3:h=ih/3:t=2:c=white@0.5</pre></dl><h3>drawtext</h3>Draw a text string or text from a specified file on top of a video, using the libfreetype library. 

 To enable compilation of this filter, you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libfreetype&quot;</tt>. To enable default font fallback and the <i>font</i> option you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libfontconfig&quot;</tt>. To enable the <i>text_shaping</i> option, you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libfribidi&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Syntax</i> 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>box</b>
<dd>Used to draw a box around text using the background color. The value must be either 1 (enable) or 0 (disable). The default value of <i>box</i> is 0.
<dt><b>boxborderw</b>
<dd>Set the width of the border to be drawn around the box using <i>boxcolor</i>. The default value of <i>boxborderw</i> is 0.
<dt><b>boxcolor</b>
<dd>The color to be used for drawing box around text. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. 

 The default value of <i>boxcolor</i> is ``white''.
<dt><b>line_spacing</b>
<dd>Set the line spacing in pixels of the border to be drawn around the box using <i>box</i>. The default value of <i>line_spacing</i> is 0.
<dt><b>borderw</b>
<dd>Set the width of the border to be drawn around the text using <i>bordercolor</i>. The default value of <i>borderw</i> is 0.
<dt><b>bordercolor</b>
<dd>Set the color to be used for drawing border around text. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. 

 The default value of <i>bordercolor</i> is ``black''.
<dt><b>expansion</b>
<dd>Select how the <i>text</i> is expanded. Can be either <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;strftime&quot;</tt> (deprecated) or <tt>&quot;normal&quot;</tt> (default). See the <b>drawtext_expansion, Text expansion</b> section below for details.
<dt><b>basetime</b>
<dd>Set a start time for the count. Value is in microseconds. Only applied in the deprecated strftime expansion mode. To emulate in normal expansion mode use the <tt>&quot;pts&quot;</tt> function, supplying the start time (in seconds) as the second argument.
<dt><b>fix_bounds</b>
<dd>If true, check and fix text coords to avoid clipping.
<dt><b>fontcolor</b>
<dd>The color to be used for drawing fonts. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. 

 The default value of <i>fontcolor</i> is ``black''.
<dt><b>fontcolor_expr</b>
<dd>String which is expanded the same way as <i>text</i> to obtain dynamic <i>fontcolor</i> value. By default this option has empty value and is not processed. When this option is set, it overrides <i>fontcolor</i> option.
<dt><b>font</b>
<dd>The font family to be used for drawing text. By default Sans.
<dt><b>fontfile</b>
<dd>The font file to be used for drawing text. The path must be included. This parameter is mandatory if the fontconfig support is disabled.
<dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd>Draw the text applying alpha blending. The value can be a number between 0.0 and 1.0. The expression accepts the same variables <i>x, y</i> as well. The default value is 1. Please see <i>fontcolor_expr</i>.
<dt><b>fontsize</b>
<dd>The font size to be used for drawing text. The default value of <i>fontsize</i> is 16.
<dt><b>text_shaping</b>
<dd>If set to 1, attempt to shape the text (for example, reverse the order of right-to-left text and join Arabic characters) before drawing it. Otherwise, just draw the text exactly as given. By default 1 (if supported).
<dt><b>ft_load_flags</b>
<dd>The flags to be used for loading the fonts. 

 The flags map the corresponding flags supported by libfreetype, and are a combination of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>default</i>
<dd><dt><i>no_scale</i>
<dd><dt><i>no_hinting</i>
<dd><dt><i>render</i>
<dd><dt><i>no_bitmap</i>
<dd><dt><i>vertical_layout</i>
<dd><dt><i>force_autohint</i>
<dd><dt><i>crop_bitmap</i>
<dd><dt><i>pedantic</i>
<dd><dt><i>ignore_global_advance_width</i>
<dd><dt><i>no_recurse</i>
<dd><dt><i>ignore_transform</i>
<dd><dt><i>monochrome</i>
<dd><dt><i>linear_design</i>
<dd><dt><i>no_autohint</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is ``default''. 

 For more information consult the documentation for the FT_LOAD_* libfreetype flags.</dl><dt><b>shadowcolor</b>
<dd>The color to be used for drawing a shadow behind the drawn text. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. 

 The default value of <i>shadowcolor</i> is ``black''.
<dt><b>shadowx</b>
<dd><dt><b>shadowy</b>
<dd>The x and y offsets for the text shadow position with respect to the position of the text. They can be either positive or negative values. The default value for both is ``0''.
<dt><b>start_number</b>
<dd>The starting frame number for the n/frame_num variable. The default value is ``0''.
<dt><b>tabsize</b>
<dd>The size in number of spaces to use for rendering the tab. Default value is 4.
<dt><b>timecode</b>
<dd>Set the initial timecode representation in ``hh:mm:ss[:;.]ff'' format. It can be used with or without text parameter. <i>timecode_rate</i> option must be specified.
<dt><b>timecode_rate, rate, r</b>
<dd>Set the timecode frame rate (timecode only).
<dt><b>tc24hmax</b>
<dd>If set to 1, the output of the timecode option will wrap around at 24 hours. Default is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>text</b>
<dd>The text string to be drawn. The text must be a sequence of <font SIZE="-1">UTF-8</font> encoded characters. This parameter is mandatory if no file is specified with the parameter <i>textfile</i>.
<dt><b>textfile</b>
<dd>A text file containing text to be drawn. The text must be a sequence of <font SIZE="-1">UTF-8</font> encoded characters. 

 This parameter is mandatory if no text string is specified with the parameter <i>text</i>. 

 If both <i>text</i> and <i>textfile</i> are specified, an error is thrown.
<dt><b>reload</b>
<dd>If set to 1, the <i>textfile</i> will be reloaded before each frame. Be sure to update it atomically, or it may be read partially, or even fail.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The expressions which specify the offsets where text will be drawn within the video frame. They are relative to the top/left border of the output image. 

 The default value of <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> is ``0''. 

 See below for the list of accepted constants and functions.</dl>
 

 The parameters for <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are expressions containing the following constants and functions:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (<i>w</i> / <i>h</i>) * <i>sar</i>
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd><dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd>horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><b>line_h, lh</b>
<dd>the height of each text line
<dt><b>main_h, h, H</b>
<dd>the input height
<dt><b>main_w, w, W</b>
<dd>the input width
<dt><b>max_glyph_a, ascent</b>
<dd>the maximum distance from the baseline to the highest/upper grid coordinate used to place a glyph outline point, for all the rendered glyphs. It is a positive value, due to the grid's orientation with the Y axis upwards.
<dt><b>max_glyph_d, descent</b>
<dd>the maximum distance from the baseline to the lowest grid coordinate used to place a glyph outline point, for all the rendered glyphs. This is a negative value, due to the grid's orientation, with the Y axis upwards.
<dt><b>max_glyph_h</b>
<dd>maximum glyph height, that is the maximum height for all the glyphs contained in the rendered text, it is equivalent to <i>ascent</i> - <i>descent</i>.
<dt><b>max_glyph_w</b>
<dd>maximum glyph width, that is the maximum width for all the glyphs contained in the rendered text
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd>the number of input frame, starting from 0
<dt><b>rand(min, max)</b>
<dd>return a random number included between <i>min</i> and <i>max</i>
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>The input sample aspect ratio.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>timestamp expressed in seconds, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown
<dt><b>text_h, th</b>
<dd>the height of the rendered text
<dt><b>text_w, tw</b>
<dd>the width of the rendered text
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>the x and y offset coordinates where the text is drawn. 

 These parameters allow the <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> expressions to refer each other, so you can for example specify <tt>&quot;y=x/dar&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Text expansion</i> 

 If <b>expansion</b> is set to <tt>&quot;strftime&quot;</tt>, the filter recognizes <i>strftime()</i> sequences in the provided text and expands them accordingly. Check the documentation of <i>strftime()</i>. This feature is deprecated. 

 If <b>expansion</b> is set to <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>, the text is printed verbatim. 

 If <b>expansion</b> is set to <tt>&quot;normal&quot;</tt> (which is the default), the following expansion mechanism is used. 

 The backslash character <b>\</b>, followed by any character, always expands to the second character. 

 Sequences of the form <tt>&quot;%{...}&quot;</tt> are expanded. The text between the braces is a function name, possibly followed by arguments separated by ':'. If the arguments contain special characters or delimiters (':' or '}'), they should be escaped. 

 Note that they probably must also be escaped as the value for the <b>text</b> option in the filter argument string and as the filter argument in the filtergraph description, and possibly also for the shell, that makes up to four levels of escaping; using a text file avoids these problems. 

 The following functions are available:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>expr, e</b>
<dd>The expression evaluation result. 

 It must take one argument specifying the expression to be evaluated, which accepts the same constants and functions as the <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> values. Note that not all constants should be used, for example the text size is not known when evaluating the expression, so the constants <i>text_w</i> and <i>text_h</i> will have an undefined value.
<dt><b>expr_int_format, eif</b>
<dd>Evaluate the expression's value and output as formatted integer. 

 The first argument is the expression to be evaluated, just as for the <i>expr</i> function. The second argument specifies the output format. Allowed values are <b>x</b>, <b>X</b>, <b>d</b> and <b>u</b>. They are treated exactly as in the <tt>&quot;printf&quot;</tt> function. The third parameter is optional and sets the number of positions taken by the output. It can be used to add padding with zeros from the left.
<dt><b>gmtime</b>
<dd>The time at which the filter is running, expressed in <font SIZE="-1">UTC.</font> It can accept an argument: a <i>strftime()</i> format string.
<dt><b>localtime</b>
<dd>The time at which the filter is running, expressed in the local time zone. It can accept an argument: a <i>strftime()</i> format string.
<dt><b>metadata</b>
<dd>Frame metadata. Takes one or two arguments. 

 The first argument is mandatory and specifies the metadata key. 

 The second argument is optional and specifies a default value, used when the metadata key is not found or empty.
<dt><b>n, frame_num</b>
<dd>The frame number, starting from 0.
<dt><b>pict_type</b>
<dd>A 1 character description of the current picture type.
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd>The timestamp of the current frame. It can take up to three arguments. 

 The first argument is the format of the timestamp; it defaults to <tt>&quot;flt&quot;</tt> for seconds as a decimal number with microsecond accuracy; <tt>&quot;hms&quot;</tt> stands for a formatted <i>[-]HH:MM:SS.mmm</i> timestamp with millisecond accuracy. <tt>&quot;gmtime&quot;</tt> stands for the timestamp of the frame formatted as <font SIZE="-1">UTC</font> time; <tt>&quot;localtime&quot;</tt> stands for the timestamp of the frame formatted as local time zone time. 

 The second argument is an offset added to the timestamp. 

 If the format is set to <tt>&quot;localtime&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;gmtime&quot;</tt>, a third argument may be supplied: a <i>strftime()</i> format string. By default, <i>YYYY-MM-DD </i><font SIZE="-1"><i>HH:MM:SS</i></font><i></i> format will be used.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw ``Test Text'' with font FreeSerif, using the default values for the optional parameters. 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/freefont/FreeSerif.ttf: text='Test Text'&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw 'Test Text' with font FreeSerif of size 24 at position x=100 and y=50 (counting from the top-left corner of the screen), text is yellow with a red box around it. Both the text and the box have an opacity of 20%. 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontfile=/usr/share/fonts/truetype/freefont/FreeSerif.ttf: text='Test Text':\
 x=100: y=50: fontsize=24: fontcolor=yellow@0.2: box=1: boxcolor=red@0.2&quot;</pre>Note that the double quotes are not necessary if spaces are not used within the parameter list.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Show the text at the center of the video frame: 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontsize=30:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text='hello world':x=(w-text_w)/2:y=(h-text_h)/2&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Show the text at a random position, switching to a new position every 30 seconds: 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontsize=30:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text='hello world':x=if(eq(mod(t\,30)\,0)\,rand(0\,(w-text_w))\,x):y=if(eq(mod(t\,30)\,0)\,rand(0\,(h-text_h))\,y)&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Show a text line sliding from right to left in the last row of the video frame. The file <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>LONG_LINE</i></font><i></i> is assumed to contain a single line with no newlines. 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontsize=15:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:text=LONG_LINE:y=h-line_h:x=-50*t&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Show the content of file <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CREDITS</i></font><i></i> off the bottom of the frame and scroll up. 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontsize=20:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:textfile=CREDITS:y=h-20*t&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw a single green letter ``g'', at the center of the input video. The glyph baseline is placed at half screen height. 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontsize=60:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:fontcolor=green:text=g:x=(w-max_glyph_w)/2:y=h/2-ascent&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Show text for 1 second every 3 seconds: 

 <pre> drawtext=&quot;fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:fontcolor=white:x=100:y=x/dar:enable=lt(mod(t\,3)\,1):text='blink'&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use fontconfig to set the font. Note that the colons need to be escaped. 

 <pre> drawtext='fontfile=Linux Libertine O-40\:style=Semibold:text=FFmpeg'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Print the date of a real-time encoding (see <i><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/3-strftime/">strftime</a></i>(3)): 

 <pre> drawtext='fontfile=FreeSans.ttf:text=%{localtime\:%a %b %d %Y}'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Show text fading in and out (appearing/disappearing): 

 <pre> #!/bin/sh
 DS=1.0 # display start
 DE=10.0 # display end
 FID=1.5 # fade in duration
 FOD=5 # fade out duration
 ffplay -f lavfi &quot;color,drawtext=text=TEST:fontsize=50:fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:fontcolor_expr=ff0000%{eif\\\\: clip(255*(1*between(t\\, $DS + $FID\\, $DE - $FOD) + ((t - $DS)/$FID)*between(t\\, $DS\\, $DS + $FID) + (-(t - $DE)/$FOD)*between(t\\, $DE - $FOD\\, $DE) )\\, 0\\, 255) \\\\: x\\\\: 2 }&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Horizontally align multiple separate texts. Note that <b>max_glyph_a</b> and the <b>fontsize</b> value are included in the <b>y</b> offset. 

 <pre> drawtext=fontfile=FreeSans.ttf:text=DOG:fontsize=24:x=10:y=20+24-max_glyph_a,
 drawtext=fontfile=FreeSans.ttf:text=cow:fontsize=24:x=80:y=20+24-max_glyph_a</pre></dl>
 

 For more information about libfreetype, check: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.freetype.org/">http://www.freetype.org/</a></b>&gt;. 

 For more information about fontconfig, check: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://freedesktop.org/software/fontconfig/fontconfig-user.html">http://freedesktop.org/software/fontconfig/fontconfig-user.html</a></b>&gt;. 

 For more information about libfribidi, check: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://fribidi.org/">http://fribidi.org/</a></b>&gt;.
<h3>edgedetect</h3>Detect and draw edges. The filter uses the Canny Edge Detection algorithm. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>low</b>
<dd><dt><b>high</b>
<dd>Set low and high threshold values used by the Canny thresholding algorithm. 

 The high threshold selects the ``strong'' edge pixels, which are then connected through 8-connectivity with the ``weak'' edge pixels selected by the low threshold. 

 <i>low</i> and <i>high</i> threshold values must be chosen in the range [0,1], and <i>low</i> should be lesser or equal to <i>high</i>. 

 Default value for <i>low</i> is <tt>&quot;20/255&quot;</tt>, and default value for <i>high</i> is <tt>&quot;50/255&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Define the drawing mode.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>wires</b>
<dd>Draw white/gray wires on black background.
<dt><b>colormix</b>
<dd>Mix the colors to create a paint/cartoon effect.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>wires</i>.</dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Standard edge detection with custom values for the hysteresis thresholding: 

 <pre> edgedetect=low=0.1:high=0.4</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Painting effect without thresholding: 

 <pre> edgedetect=mode=colormix:high=0</pre></dl><h3>eq</h3>Set brightness, contrast, saturation and approximate gamma adjustment. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>contrast</b>
<dd>Set the contrast expression. The value must be a float value in range <tt>&quot;-2.0&quot;</tt> to <tt>2.0</tt>. The default value is ``1''.
<dt><b>brightness</b>
<dd>Set the brightness expression. The value must be a float value in range <tt>&quot;-1.0&quot;</tt> to <tt>1.0</tt>. The default value is ``0''.
<dt><b>saturation</b>
<dd>Set the saturation expression. The value must be a float in range <tt>0.0</tt> to <tt>3.0</tt>. The default value is ``1''.
<dt><b>gamma</b>
<dd>Set the gamma expression. The value must be a float in range <tt>0.1</tt> to <tt>10.0</tt>. The default value is ``1''.
<dt><b>gamma_r</b>
<dd>Set the gamma expression for red. The value must be a float in range <tt>0.1</tt> to <tt>10.0</tt>. The default value is ``1''.
<dt><b>gamma_g</b>
<dd>Set the gamma expression for green. The value must be a float in range <tt>0.1</tt> to <tt>10.0</tt>. The default value is ``1''.
<dt><b>gamma_b</b>
<dd>Set the gamma expression for blue. The value must be a float in range <tt>0.1</tt> to <tt>10.0</tt>. The default value is ``1''.
<dt><b>gamma_weight</b>
<dd>Set the gamma weight expression. It can be used to reduce the effect of a high gamma value on bright image areas, e.g. keep them from getting overamplified and just plain white. The value must be a float in range <tt>0.0</tt> to <tt>1.0</tt>. A value of <tt>0.0</tt> turns the gamma correction all the way down while <tt>1.0</tt> leaves it at its full strength. Default is ``1''.
<dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Set when the expressions for brightness, contrast, saturation and gamma expressions are evaluated. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or when a command is processed
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>evaluate expressions for each incoming frame</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>init</b>.</dl></dl>
 

 The expressions accept the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>frame count of the input frame starting from 0
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd>byte position of the corresponding packet in the input file, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if unspecified
<dt><b>r</b>
<dd>frame rate of the input video, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input frame rate is unknown
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>timestamp expressed in seconds, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 The filter supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>contrast</b>
<dd>Set the contrast expression.
<dt><b>brightness</b>
<dd>Set the brightness expression.
<dt><b>saturation</b>
<dd>Set the saturation expression.
<dt><b>gamma</b>
<dd>Set the gamma expression.
<dt><b>gamma_r</b>
<dd>Set the gamma_r expression.
<dt><b>gamma_g</b>
<dd>Set gamma_g expression.
<dt><b>gamma_b</b>
<dd>Set gamma_b expression.
<dt><b>gamma_weight</b>
<dd>Set gamma_weight expression. 

 The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.</dl><h3>erosion</h3>Apply erosion effect to the video. 

 This filter replaces the pixel by the local(3x3) minimum. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold0</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold1</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold2</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold3</b>
<dd>Limit the maximum change for each plane, default is 65535. If 0, plane will remain unchanged.
<dt><b>coordinates</b>
<dd>Flag which specifies the pixel to refer to. Default is 255 i.e. all eight pixels are used. 

 Flags to local 3x3 coordinates maps like this: 

 <pre> 1 2 3
 4 5
 6 7 8</pre></dl><h3>extractplanes</h3>Extract color channel components from input video stream into separate grayscale video streams. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set plane(s) to extract. 

 Available values for planes are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>y</b>
<dd><dt><b>u</b>
<dd><dt><b>v</b>
<dd><dt><b>a</b>
<dd><dt><b>r</b>
<dd><dt><b>g</b>
<dd><dt><b>b</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Choosing planes not available in the input will result in an error. That means you cannot select <tt>&quot;r&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;g&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;b&quot;</tt> planes with <tt>&quot;y&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;u&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;v&quot;</tt> planes at same time.</dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Extract luma, u and v color channel component from input video frame into 3 grayscale outputs: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i video.avi -filter_complex 'extractplanes=y+u+v[y][u][v]' -map '[y]' y.avi -map '[u]' u.avi -map '[v]' v.avi</pre></dl><h3>elbg</h3>Apply a posterize effect using the <font SIZE="-1">ELBG</font> (Enhanced <font SIZE="-1">LBG</font>) algorithm. 

 For each input image, the filter will compute the optimal mapping from the input to the output given the codebook length, that is the number of distinct output colors. 

 This filter accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>codebook_length, l</b>
<dd>Set codebook length. The value must be a positive integer, and represents the number of distinct output colors. Default value is 256.
<dt><b>nb_steps, n</b>
<dd>Set the maximum number of iterations to apply for computing the optimal mapping. The higher the value the better the result and the higher the computation time. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>seed, s</b>
<dd>Set a random seed, must be an integer included between 0 and <font SIZE="-1">UINT32_MAX.</font> If not specified, or if explicitly set to -1, the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best effort basis.
<dt><b>pal8</b>
<dd>Set pal8 output pixel format. This option does not work with codebook length greater than 256.</dl><h3>fade</h3>Apply a fade-in/out effect to the input video. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>type, t</b>
<dd>The effect type can be either ``in'' for a fade-in, or ``out'' for a fade-out effect. Default is <tt>&quot;in&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>start_frame, s</b>
<dd>Specify the number of the frame to start applying the fade effect at. Default is 0.
<dt><b>nb_frames, n</b>
<dd>The number of frames that the fade effect lasts. At the end of the fade-in effect, the output video will have the same intensity as the input video. At the end of the fade-out transition, the output video will be filled with the selected <b>color</b>. Default is 25.
<dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd>If set to 1, fade only alpha channel, if one exists on the input. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>start_time, st</b>
<dd>Specify the timestamp (in seconds) of the frame to start to apply the fade effect. If both start_frame and start_time are specified, the fade will start at whichever comes last. Default is 0.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd>The number of seconds for which the fade effect has to last. At the end of the fade-in effect the output video will have the same intensity as the input video, at the end of the fade-out transition the output video will be filled with the selected <b>color</b>. If both duration and nb_frames are specified, duration is used. Default is 0 (nb_frames is used by default).
<dt><b>color, c</b>
<dd>Specify the color of the fade. Default is ``black''.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Fade in the first 30 frames of video: 

 <pre> fade=in:0:30</pre>The command above is equivalent to: 

 <pre> fade=t=in:s=0:n=30</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Fade out the last 45 frames of a 200-frame video: 

 <pre> fade=out:155:45
 fade=type=out:start_frame=155:nb_frames=45</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Fade in the first 25 frames and fade out the last 25 frames of a 1000-frame video: 

 <pre> fade=in:0:25, fade=out:975:25</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Make the first 5 frames yellow, then fade in from frame 5-24: 

 <pre> fade=in:5:20:color=yellow</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Fade in alpha over first 25 frames of video: 

 <pre> fade=in:0:25:alpha=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Make the first 5.5 seconds black, then fade in for 0.5 seconds: 

 <pre> fade=t=in:st=5.5:d=0.5</pre></dl><h3>fftfilt</h3>Apply arbitrary expressions to samples in frequency domain
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dc_Y</b>
<dd>Adjust the dc value (gain) of the luma plane of the image. The filter accepts an integer value in range <tt>0</tt> to <tt>1000</tt>. The default value is set to <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>dc_U</b>
<dd>Adjust the dc value (gain) of the 1st chroma plane of the image. The filter accepts an integer value in range <tt>0</tt> to <tt>1000</tt>. The default value is set to <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>dc_V</b>
<dd>Adjust the dc value (gain) of the 2nd chroma plane of the image. The filter accepts an integer value in range <tt>0</tt> to <tt>1000</tt>. The default value is set to <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>weight_Y</b>
<dd>Set the frequency domain weight expression for the luma plane.
<dt><b>weight_U</b>
<dd>Set the frequency domain weight expression for the 1st chroma plane.
<dt><b>weight_V</b>
<dd>Set the frequency domain weight expression for the 2nd chroma plane.
<dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Set when the expressions are evaluated. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>Only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>init</b>. 

 The filter accepts the following variables:</dl><dt><b>X</b>
<dd><dt><b>Y</b>
<dd>The coordinates of the current sample.
<dt><b>W</b>
<dd><dt><b>H</b>
<dd>The width and height of the image.
<dt><b>N</b>
<dd>The number of input frame, starting from 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>High-pass: 

 <pre> fftfilt=dc_Y=128:weight_Y='squish(1-(Y+X)/100)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Low-pass: 

 <pre> fftfilt=dc_Y=0:weight_Y='squish((Y+X)/100-1)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Sharpen: 

 <pre> fftfilt=dc_Y=0:weight_Y='1+squish(1-(Y+X)/100)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Blur: 

 <pre> fftfilt=dc_Y=0:weight_Y='exp(-4 * ((Y+X)/(W+H)))'</pre></dl><h3>field</h3>Extract a single field from an interlaced image using stride arithmetic to avoid wasting <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> time. The output frames are marked as non-interlaced. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>type</b>
<dd>Specify whether to extract the top (if the value is <tt>0</tt> or <tt>&quot;top&quot;</tt>) or the bottom field (if the value is <tt>1</tt> or <tt>&quot;bottom&quot;</tt>).</dl><h3>fieldhint</h3>Create new frames by copying the top and bottom fields from surrounding frames supplied as numbers by the hint file.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>hint</b>
<dd>Set file containing hints: absolute/relative frame numbers. 

 There must be one line for each frame in a clip. Each line must contain two numbers separated by the comma, optionally followed by <tt>&quot;-&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt>. Numbers supplied on each line of file can not be out of [N-1,N+1] where N is current frame number for <tt>&quot;absolute&quot;</tt> mode or out of [-1, 1] range for <tt>&quot;relative&quot;</tt> mode. First number tells from which frame to pick up top field and second number tells from which frame to pick up bottom field. 

 If optionally followed by <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt> output frame will be marked as interlaced, else if followed by <tt>&quot;-&quot;</tt> output frame will be marked as progressive, else it will be marked same as input frame. If line starts with <tt>&quot;#&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;;&quot;</tt> that line is skipped.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Can be item <tt>&quot;absolute&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;relative&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;absolute&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 Example of first several lines of <tt>&quot;hint&quot;</tt> file for <tt>&quot;relative&quot;</tt> mode: 

 <pre> 0,0 - # first frame
 1,0 - # second frame, use third's frame top field and second's frame bottom field
 1,0 - # third frame, use fourth's frame top field and third's frame bottom field
 1,0 -
 0,0 -
 0,0 -
 1,0 -
 1,0 -
 1,0 -
 0,0 -
 0,0 -
 1,0 -
 1,0 -
 1,0 -
 0,0 -</pre><h3>fieldmatch</h3>Field matching filter for inverse telecine. It is meant to reconstruct the progressive frames from a telecined stream. The filter does not drop duplicated frames, so to achieve a complete inverse telecine <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> needs to be followed by a decimation filter such as <b>decimate</b> in the filtergraph. 

 The separation of the field matching and the decimation is notably motivated by the possibility of inserting a de-interlacing filter fallback between the two. If the source has mixed telecined and real interlaced content, <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> will not be able to match fields for the interlaced parts. But these remaining combed frames will be marked as interlaced, and thus can be de-interlaced by a later filter such as <b>yadif</b> before decimation. 

 In addition to the various configuration options, <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> can take an optional second stream, activated through the <b>ppsrc</b> option. If enabled, the frames reconstruction will be based on the fields and frames from this second stream. This allows the first input to be pre-processed in order to help the various algorithms of the filter, while keeping the output lossless (assuming the fields are matched properly). Typically, a field-aware denoiser, or brightness/contrast adjustments can help. 

 Note that this filter uses the same algorithms as <font SIZE="-1">TIVTC/TFM</font> (AviSynth project) and <font SIZE="-1">VIVTC/VFM</font> (VapourSynth project). The later is a light clone of <font SIZE="-1">TFM</font> from which <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> is based on. While the semantic and usage are very close, some behaviour and options names can differ. 

 The <b>decimate</b> filter currently only works for constant frame rate input. If your input has mixed telecined (30fps) and progressive content with a lower framerate like 24fps use the following filterchain to produce the necessary cfr stream: <tt>&quot;dejudder,fps=30000/1001,fieldmatch,decimate&quot;</tt>. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>order</b>
<dd>Specify the assumed field order of the input stream. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Auto detect parity (use FFmpeg's internal parity value).
<dt><b>bff</b>
<dd>Assume bottom field first.
<dt><b>tff</b>
<dd>Assume top field first.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Note that it is sometimes recommended not to trust the parity announced by the stream. 

 Default value is <i>auto</i>.</dl><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set the matching mode or strategy to use. <b>pc</b> mode is the safest in the sense that it won't risk creating jerkiness due to duplicate frames when possible, but if there are bad edits or blended fields it will end up outputting combed frames when a good match might actually exist. On the other hand, <b>pcn_ub</b> mode is the most risky in terms of creating jerkiness, but will almost always find a good frame if there is one. The other values are all somewhere in between <b>pc</b> and <b>pcn_ub</b> in terms of risking jerkiness and creating duplicate frames versus finding good matches in sections with bad edits, orphaned fields, blended fields, etc. 

 More details about p/c/n/u/b are available in <b>p/c/n/u/b meaning</b> section. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>pc</b>
<dd>2-way matching (p/c)
<dt><b>pc_n</b>
<dd>2-way matching, and trying 3rd match if still combed (p/c + n)
<dt><b>pc_u</b>
<dd>2-way matching, and trying 3rd match (same order) if still combed (p/c + u)
<dt><b>pc_n_ub</b>
<dd>2-way matching, trying 3rd match if still combed, and trying 4th/5th matches if still combed (p/c + n + u/b)
<dt><b>pcn</b>
<dd>3-way matching (p/c/n)
<dt><b>pcn_ub</b>
<dd>3-way matching, and trying 4th/5th matches if all 3 of the original matches are detected as combed (p/c/n + u/b)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The parenthesis at the end indicate the matches that would be used for that mode assuming <b>order</b>=<i>tff</i> (and <b>field</b> on <i>auto</i> or <i>top</i>). 

 In terms of speed <b>pc</b> mode is by far the fastest and <b>pcn_ub</b> is the slowest. 

 Default value is <i>pc_n</i>.</dl><dt><b>ppsrc</b>
<dd>Mark the main input stream as a pre-processed input, and enable the secondary input stream as the clean source to pick the fields from. See the filter introduction for more details. It is similar to the <b>clip2</b> feature from <font SIZE="-1">VFM/TFM.</font> 

 Default value is <tt>0</tt> (disabled).
<dt><b>field</b>
<dd>Set the field to match from. It is recommended to set this to the same value as <b>order</b> unless you experience matching failures with that setting. In certain circumstances changing the field that is used to match from can have a large impact on matching performance. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Automatic (same value as <b>order</b>).
<dt><b>bottom</b>
<dd>Match from the bottom field.
<dt><b>top</b>
<dd>Match from the top field.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>auto</i>.</dl><dt><b>mchroma</b>
<dd>Set whether or not chroma is included during the match comparisons. In most cases it is recommended to leave this enabled. You should set this to <tt>0</tt> only if your clip has bad chroma problems such as heavy rainbowing or other artifacts. Setting this to <tt>0</tt> could also be used to speed things up at the cost of some accuracy. 

 Default value is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>y0</b>
<dd><dt><b>y1</b>
<dd>These define an exclusion band which excludes the lines between <b>y0</b> and <b>y1</b> from being included in the field matching decision. An exclusion band can be used to ignore subtitles, a logo, or other things that may interfere with the matching. <b>y0</b> sets the starting scan line and <b>y1</b> sets the ending line; all lines in between <b>y0</b> and <b>y1</b> (including <b>y0</b> and <b>y1</b>) will be ignored. Setting <b>y0</b> and <b>y1</b> to the same value will disable the feature. <b>y0</b> and <b>y1</b> defaults to <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>scthresh</b>
<dd>Set the scene change detection threshold as a percentage of maximum change on the luma plane. Good values are in the <tt>&quot;[8.0, 14.0]&quot;</tt> range. Scene change detection is only relevant in case <b>combmatch</b>=<i>sc</i>. The range for <b>scthresh</b> is <tt>&quot;[0.0, 100.0]&quot;</tt>. 

 Default value is <tt>12.0</tt>.
<dt><b>combmatch</b>
<dd>When <b>combatch</b> is not <i>none</i>, <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> will take into account the combed scores of matches when deciding what match to use as the final match. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>No final matching based on combed scores.
<dt><b>sc</b>
<dd>Combed scores are only used when a scene change is detected.
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd>Use combed scores all the time.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <i>sc</i>.</dl><dt><b>combdbg</b>
<dd>Force <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> to calculate the combed metrics for certain matches and print them. This setting is known as <b>micout</b> in <font SIZE="-1">TFM/VFM</font> vocabulary. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>No forced calculation.
<dt><b>pcn</b>
<dd>Force p/c/n calculations.
<dt><b>pcnub</b>
<dd>Force p/c/n/u/b calculations.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>none</i>.</dl><dt><b>cthresh</b>
<dd>This is the area combing threshold used for combed frame detection. This essentially controls how ``strong'' or ``visible'' combing must be to be detected. Larger values mean combing must be more visible and smaller values mean combing can be less visible or strong and still be detected. Valid settings are from <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt> (every pixel will be detected as combed) to <tt>255</tt> (no pixel will be detected as combed). This is basically a pixel difference value. A good range is <tt>&quot;[8, 12]&quot;</tt>. 

 Default value is <tt>9</tt>.
<dt><b>chroma</b>
<dd>Sets whether or not chroma is considered in the combed frame decision. Only disable this if your source has chroma problems (rainbowing, etc.) that are causing problems for the combed frame detection with chroma enabled. Actually, using <b>chroma</b>=<i>0</i> is usually more reliable, except for the case where there is chroma only combing in the source. 

 Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>blockx</b>
<dd><dt><b>blocky</b>
<dd>Respectively set the x-axis and y-axis size of the window used during combed frame detection. This has to do with the size of the area in which <b>combpel</b> pixels are required to be detected as combed for a frame to be declared combed. See the <b>combpel</b> parameter description for more info. Possible values are any number that is a power of 2 starting at 4 and going up to 512. 

 Default value is <tt>16</tt>.
<dt><b>combpel</b>
<dd>The number of combed pixels inside any of the <b>blocky</b> by <b>blockx</b> size blocks on the frame for the frame to be detected as combed. While <b>cthresh</b> controls how ``visible'' the combing must be, this setting controls ``how much'' combing there must be in any localized area (a window defined by the <b>blockx</b> and <b>blocky</b> settings) on the frame. Minimum value is <tt>0</tt> and maximum is <tt>&quot;blocky x blockx&quot;</tt> (at which point no frames will ever be detected as combed). This setting is known as <font SIZE="-1"><b>MI</b></font> in <font SIZE="-1">TFM/VFM</font> vocabulary. 

 Default value is <tt>80</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>p/c/n/u/b meaning</i> 

 p/c/n 

 We assume the following telecined stream: 

 <pre> Top fields: 1 2 2 3 4
 Bottom fields: 1 2 3 4 4</pre>The numbers correspond to the progressive frame the fields relate to. Here, the first two frames are progressive, the 3rd and 4th are combed, and so on. 

 When <tt>&quot;fieldmatch&quot;</tt> is configured to run a matching from bottom (<b>field</b>=<i>bottom</i>) this is how this input stream get transformed: 

 <pre> Input stream:
 T 1 2 2 3 4
 B 1 2 3 4 4 &lt;-- matching reference
 
 Matches: c c n n c
 
 Output stream:
 T 1 2 3 4 4
 B 1 2 3 4 4</pre>As a result of the field matching, we can see that some frames get duplicated. To perform a complete inverse telecine, you need to rely on a decimation filter after this operation. See for instance the <b>decimate</b> filter. 

 The same operation now matching from top fields (<b>field</b>=<i>top</i>) looks like this: 

 <pre> Input stream:
 T 1 2 2 3 4 &lt;-- matching reference
 B 1 2 3 4 4
 
 Matches: c c p p c
 
 Output stream:
 T 1 2 2 3 4
 B 1 2 2 3 4</pre>In these examples, we can see what <i>p</i>, <i>c</i> and <i>n</i> mean; basically, they refer to the frame and field of the opposite parity:
<dl COMPACT><dt>*&lt;<i>p</i> matches the field of the opposite parity in the previous frame&gt;
<dd><dt>*&lt;<i>c</i> matches the field of the opposite parity in the current frame&gt;
<dd><dt>*&lt;<i>n</i> matches the field of the opposite parity in the next frame&gt;
<dd></dl>
 

 u/b 

 The <i>u</i> and <i>b</i> matching are a bit special in the sense that they match from the opposite parity flag. In the following examples, we assume that we are currently matching the 2nd frame (Top:2, bottom:2). According to the match, a 'x' is placed above and below each matched fields. 

 With bottom matching (<b>field</b>=<i>bottom</i>): 

 <pre> Match: c p n b u
 
 x x x x x
 Top 1 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2
 Bottom 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3
 x x x x x
 
 Output frames:
 2 1 2 2 2
 2 2 2 1 3</pre>With top matching (<b>field</b>=<i>top</i>): 

 <pre> Match: c p n b u
 
 x x x x x
 Top 1 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2
 Bottom 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3
 x x x x x
 
 Output frames:
 2 2 2 1 2
 2 1 3 2 2</pre><i>Examples</i> 

 Simple <font SIZE="-1">IVTC</font> of a top field first telecined stream: 

 <pre> fieldmatch=order=tff:combmatch=none, decimate</pre>Advanced <font SIZE="-1">IVTC,</font> with fallback on <b>yadif</b> for still combed frames: 

 <pre> fieldmatch=order=tff:combmatch=full, yadif=deint=interlaced, decimate</pre><h3>fieldorder</h3>Transform the field order of the input video. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>order</b>
<dd>The output field order. Valid values are <i>tff</i> for top field first or <i>bff</i> for bottom field first.</dl>
 

 The default value is <b>tff</b>. 

 The transformation is done by shifting the picture content up or down by one line, and filling the remaining line with appropriate picture content. This method is consistent with most broadcast field order converters. 

 If the input video is not flagged as being interlaced, or it is already flagged as being of the required output field order, then this filter does not alter the incoming video. 

 It is very useful when converting to or from <font SIZE="-1">PAL DV</font> material, which is bottom field first. 

 For example: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i in.vob -vf &quot;fieldorder=bff&quot; out.dv</pre><h3>fifo, afifo</h3>Buffer input images and send them when they are requested. 

 It is mainly useful when auto-inserted by the libavfilter framework. 

 It does not take parameters.
<h3>find_rect</h3>Find a rectangular object 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>object</b>
<dd>Filepath of the object image, needs to be in gray8.
<dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd>Detection threshold, default is 0.5.
<dt><b>mipmaps</b>
<dd>Number of mipmaps, default is 3.
<dt><b>xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax</b>
<dd>Specifies the rectangle in which to search.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a representative palette of a given video using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i file.ts -vf find_rect=newref.pgm,cover_rect=cover.jpg:mode=cover new.mkv</pre></dl><h3>cover_rect</h3>Cover a rectangular object 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>cover</b>
<dd>Filepath of the optional cover image, needs to be in yuv420.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set covering mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>cover</b>
<dd>cover it by the supplied image
<dt><b>blur</b>
<dd>cover it by interpolating the surrounding pixels</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>blur</i>.</dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a representative palette of a given video using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i file.ts -vf find_rect=newref.pgm,cover_rect=cover.jpg:mode=cover new.mkv</pre></dl><h3>floodfill</h3>Flood area with values of same pixel components with another values. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd>Set pixel x coordinate.
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Set pixel y coordinate.
<dt><b>s0</b>
<dd>Set source #0 component value.
<dt><b>s1</b>
<dd>Set source #1 component value.
<dt><b>s2</b>
<dd>Set source #2 component value.
<dt><b>s3</b>
<dd>Set source #3 component value.
<dt><b>d0</b>
<dd>Set destination #0 component value.
<dt><b>d1</b>
<dd>Set destination #1 component value.
<dt><b>d2</b>
<dd>Set destination #2 component value.
<dt><b>d3</b>
<dd>Set destination #3 component value.</dl><h3>format</h3>Convert the input video to one of the specified pixel formats. Libavfilter will try to pick one that is suitable as input to the next filter. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>pix_fmts</b>
<dd>A '|'-separated list of pixel format names, such as ``pix_fmts=yuv420p|monow|rgb24''.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Convert the input video to the <i>yuv420p</i> format 

 <pre> format=pix_fmts=yuv420p</pre>Convert the input video to any of the formats in the list 

 <pre> format=pix_fmts=yuv420p|yuv444p|yuv410p</pre></dl><h3>fps</h3>Convert the video to specified constant frame rate by duplicating or dropping frames as necessary. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>fps</b>
<dd>The desired output frame rate. The default is <tt>25</tt>.
<dt><b>start_time</b>
<dd>Assume the first <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> should be the given value, in seconds. This allows for padding/trimming at the start of stream. By default, no assumption is made about the first frame's expected <font SIZE="-1">PTS,</font> so no padding or trimming is done. For example, this could be set to 0 to pad the beginning with duplicates of the first frame if a video stream starts after the audio stream or to trim any frames with a negative <font SIZE="-1">PTS.</font>
<dt><b>round</b>
<dd>Timestamp (<font SIZE="-1">PTS</font>) rounding method. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>zero</b>
<dd>round towards 0
<dt><b>inf</b>
<dd>round away from 0
<dt><b>down</b>
<dd>round towards -infinity
<dt><b>up</b>
<dd>round towards +infinity
<dt><b>near</b>
<dd>round to nearest</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The default is <tt>&quot;near&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>eof_action</b>
<dd>Action performed when reading the last frame. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>round</b>
<dd>Use same timestamp rounding method as used for other frames.
<dt><b>pass</b>
<dd>Pass through last frame if input duration has not been reached yet.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The default is <tt>&quot;round&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl>
 

 Alternatively, the options can be specified as a flat string: <i>fps</i>[:<i>start_time</i>[:<i>round</i>]]. 

 See also the <b>setpts</b> filter. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>A typical usage in order to set the fps to 25: 

 <pre> fps=fps=25</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Sets the fps to 24, using abbreviation and rounding method to round to nearest: 

 <pre> fps=fps=film:round=near</pre></dl><h3>framepack</h3>Pack two different video streams into a stereoscopic video, setting proper metadata on supported codecs. The two views should have the same size and framerate and processing will stop when the shorter video ends. Please note that you may conveniently adjust view properties with the <b>scale</b> and <b>fps</b> filters. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>format</b>
<dd>The desired packing format. Supported values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>sbs</b>
<dd>The views are next to each other (default).
<dt><b>tab</b>
<dd>The views are on top of each other.
<dt><b>lines</b>
<dd>The views are packed by line.
<dt><b>columns</b>
<dd>The views are packed by column.
<dt><b>frameseq</b>
<dd>The views are temporally interleaved.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 Some examples: 

 <pre> # Convert left and right views into a frame-sequential video
 ffmpeg -i LEFT -i RIGHT -filter_complex framepack=frameseq OUTPUT
 
 # Convert views into a side-by-side video with the same output resolution as the input
 ffmpeg -i LEFT -i RIGHT -filter_complex [0:v]scale=w=iw/2[left],[1:v]scale=w=iw/2[right],[left][right]framepack=sbs OUTPUT</pre><h3>framerate</h3>Change the frame rate by interpolating new video output frames from the source frames. 

 This filter is not designed to function correctly with interlaced media. If you wish to change the frame rate of interlaced media then you are required to deinterlace before this filter and re-interlace after this filter. 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>fps</b>
<dd>Specify the output frames per second. This option can also be specified as a value alone. The default is <tt>50</tt>.
<dt><b>interp_start</b>
<dd>Specify the start of a range where the output frame will be created as a linear interpolation of two frames. The range is [<tt>0</tt>-<tt>255</tt>], the default is <tt>15</tt>.
<dt><b>interp_end</b>
<dd>Specify the end of a range where the output frame will be created as a linear interpolation of two frames. The range is [<tt>0</tt>-<tt>255</tt>], the default is <tt>240</tt>.
<dt><b>scene</b>
<dd>Specify the level at which a scene change is detected as a value between 0 and 100 to indicate a new scene; a low value reflects a low probability for the current frame to introduce a new scene, while a higher value means the current frame is more likely to be one. The default is <tt>7</tt>.
<dt><b>flags</b>
<dd>Specify flags influencing the filter process. 

 Available value for <i>flags</i> is:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>scene_change_detect, scd</b>
<dd>Enable scene change detection using the value of the option <i>scene</i>. This flag is enabled by default.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>framestep</h3>Select one frame every N-th frame. 

 This filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>step</b>
<dd>Select frame after every <tt>&quot;step&quot;</tt> frames. Allowed values are positive integers higher than 0. Default value is <tt>1</tt>.</dl><h3>frei0r</h3>Apply a frei0r effect to the input video. 

 To enable the compilation of this filter, you need to install the frei0r header and configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-frei0r&quot;</tt>. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filter_name</b>
<dd>The name of the frei0r effect to load. If the environment variable <font SIZE="-1"><b>FREI0R_PATH</b></font> is defined, the frei0r effect is searched for in each of the directories specified by the colon-separated list in <font SIZE="-1"><b>FREI0R_PATH</b></font>. Otherwise, the standard frei0r paths are searched, in this order: <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>HOME/</i></font><i>.frei0r-1/lib/</i>, <i>/usr/local/lib/frei0r-1/</i>, <i>/usr/lib/frei0r-1/</i>.
<dt><b>filter_params</b>
<dd>A '|'-separated list of parameters to pass to the frei0r effect.</dl>
 

 A frei0r effect parameter can be a boolean (its value is either ``y'' or ``n''), a double, a color (specified as <i>R</i>/<i>G</i>/<i>B</i>, where <i>R</i>, <i>G</i>, and <i>B</i> are floating point numbers between 0.0 and 1.0, inclusive) or by a color description specified in the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual), a position (specified as <i>X</i>/<i>Y</i>, where <i>X</i> and <i>Y</i> are floating point numbers) and/or a string. 

 The number and types of parameters depend on the loaded effect. If an effect parameter is not specified, the default value is set. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply the distort0r effect, setting the first two double parameters: 

 <pre> frei0r=filter_name=distort0r:filter_params=0.5|0.01</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply the colordistance effect, taking a color as the first parameter: 

 <pre> frei0r=colordistance:0.2/0.3/0.4
 frei0r=colordistance:violet
 frei0r=colordistance:0x112233</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply the perspective effect, specifying the top left and top right image positions: 

 <pre> frei0r=perspective:0.2/0.2|0.8/0.2</pre></dl>
 

 For more information, see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://frei0r.dyne.org">http://frei0r.dyne.org</a></b>&gt;
<h3>fspp</h3>Apply fast and simple postprocessing. It is a faster version of <b>spp</b>. 

 It splits (I)DCT into horizontal/vertical passes. Unlike the simple post- processing filter, one of them is performed once per block, not per pixel. This allows for much higher speed. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>quality</b>
<dd>Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts an integer in the range 4-5. Default value is <tt>4</tt>.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd>Force a constant quantization parameter. It accepts an integer in range 0-63. If not set, the filter will use the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the video stream (if available).
<dt><b>strength</b>
<dd>Set filter strength. It accepts an integer in range -15 to 32. Lower values mean more details but also more artifacts, while higher values make the image smoother but also blurrier. Default value is <tt>0</tt> X <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> optimal.
<dt><b>use_bframe_qp</b>
<dd>Enable the use of the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the B-Frames if set to <tt>1</tt>. Using this option may cause flicker since the B-Frames have often larger <font SIZE="-1">QP.</font> Default is <tt>0</tt> (not enabled).</dl><h3>gblur</h3>Apply Gaussian blur filter. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>sigma</b>
<dd>Set horizontal sigma, standard deviation of Gaussian blur. Default is <tt>0.5</tt>.
<dt><b>steps</b>
<dd>Set number of steps for Gaussian approximation. Defauls is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes to filter. By default all planes are filtered.
<dt><b>sigmaV</b>
<dd>Set vertical sigma, if negative it will be same as <tt>&quot;sigma&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt>.</dl><h3>geq</h3>The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>lum_expr, lum</b>
<dd>Set the luminance expression.
<dt><b>cb_expr, cb</b>
<dd>Set the chrominance blue expression.
<dt><b>cr_expr, cr</b>
<dd>Set the chrominance red expression.
<dt><b>alpha_expr, a</b>
<dd>Set the alpha expression.
<dt><b>red_expr, r</b>
<dd>Set the red expression.
<dt><b>green_expr, g</b>
<dd>Set the green expression.
<dt><b>blue_expr, b</b>
<dd>Set the blue expression.</dl>
 

 The colorspace is selected according to the specified options. If one of the <b>lum_expr</b>, <b>cb_expr</b>, or <b>cr_expr</b> options is specified, the filter will automatically select a YCbCr colorspace. If one of the <b>red_expr</b>, <b>green_expr</b>, or <b>blue_expr</b> options is specified, it will select an <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> colorspace. 

 If one of the chrominance expression is not defined, it falls back on the other one. If no alpha expression is specified it will evaluate to opaque value. If none of chrominance expressions are specified, they will evaluate to the luminance expression. 

 The expressions can use the following variables and functions:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>N</b>
<dd>The sequential number of the filtered frame, starting from <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>X</b>
<dd><dt><b>Y</b>
<dd>The coordinates of the current sample.
<dt><b>W</b>
<dd><dt><b>H</b>
<dd>The width and height of the image.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SW</b></font>
<dd><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SH</b></font>
<dd>Width and height scale depending on the currently filtered plane. It is the ratio between the corresponding luma plane number of pixels and the current plane ones. E.g. for <font SIZE="-1">YUV4:2:0</font> the values are <tt>&quot;1,1&quot;</tt> for the luma plane, and <tt>&quot;0.5,0.5&quot;</tt> for chroma planes.
<dt><b>T</b>
<dd>Time of the current frame, expressed in seconds.
<dt><b>p(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the value of the pixel at location (<i>x</i>,<i>y</i>) of the current plane.
<dt><b>lum(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the value of the pixel at location (<i>x</i>,<i>y</i>) of the luminance plane.
<dt><b>cb(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the value of the pixel at location (<i>x</i>,<i>y</i>) of the blue-difference chroma plane. Return 0 if there is no such plane.
<dt><b>cr(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the value of the pixel at location (<i>x</i>,<i>y</i>) of the red-difference chroma plane. Return 0 if there is no such plane.
<dt><b>r(x, y)</b>
<dd><dt><b>g(x, y)</b>
<dd><dt><b>b(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the value of the pixel at location (<i>x</i>,<i>y</i>) of the red/green/blue component. Return 0 if there is no such component.
<dt><b>alpha(x, y)</b>
<dd>Return the value of the pixel at location (<i>x</i>,<i>y</i>) of the alpha plane. Return 0 if there is no such plane.</dl>
 

 For functions, if <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are outside the area, the value will be automatically clipped to the closer edge. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Flip the image horizontally: 

 <pre> geq=p(W-X\,Y)</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a bidimensional sine wave, with angle <tt>&quot;PI/3&quot;</tt> and a wavelength of 100 pixels: 

 <pre> geq=128 + 100*sin(2*(PI/100)*(cos(PI/3)*(X-50*T) + sin(PI/3)*Y)):128:128</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a fancy enigmatic moving light: 

 <pre> nullsrc=s=256x256,geq=<a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/1-random/">random</a>(1)/hypot(X-cos(N*0.07)*W/2-W/2\,Y-sin(N*0.09)*H/2-H/2)^2*1000000*sin(N*0.02):128:128</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a quick emboss effect: 

 <pre> format=gray,geq=lum_expr='(p(X,Y)+(256-p(X-4,Y-4)))/2'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Modify <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> components depending on pixel position: 

 <pre> geq=r='X/W*r(X,Y)':g='(1-X/W)*g(X,Y)':b='(H-Y)/H*b(X,Y)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Create a radial gradient that is the same size as the input (also see the <b>vignette</b> filter): 

 <pre> geq=lum=255*gauss((X/W-0.5)*3)*gauss((Y/H-0.5)*3)/gauss(0)/gauss(0),format=gray</pre></dl><h3>gradfun</h3>Fix the banding artifacts that are sometimes introduced into nearly flat regions by truncation to 8-bit color depth. Interpolate the gradients that should go where the bands are, and dither them. 

 It is designed for playback only. Do not use it prior to lossy compression, because compression tends to lose the dither and bring back the bands. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>strength</b>
<dd>The maximum amount by which the filter will change any one pixel. This is also the threshold for detecting nearly flat regions. Acceptable values range from .51 to 64; the default value is 1.2. Out-of-range values will be clipped to the valid range.
<dt><b>radius</b>
<dd>The neighborhood to fit the gradient to. A larger radius makes for smoother gradients, but also prevents the filter from modifying the pixels near detailed regions. Acceptable values are 8-32; the default value is 16. Out-of-range values will be clipped to the valid range.</dl>
 

 Alternatively, the options can be specified as a flat string: <i>strength</i>[:<i>radius</i>] 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply the filter with a <tt>3.5</tt> strength and radius of <tt>8</tt>: 

 <pre> gradfun=3.5:8</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Specify radius, omitting the strength (which will fall-back to the default value): 

 <pre> gradfun=radius=8</pre></dl><h3>haldclut</h3>Apply a Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> to a video stream. 

 First input is the video stream to process, and second one is the Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT.</font> The Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> input can be a simple picture or a complete video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd>Force termination when the shortest input terminates. Default is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>repeatlast</b>
<dd>Continue applying the last <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> after the end of the stream. A value of <tt>0</tt> disable the filter after the last frame of the <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> is reached. Default is <tt>1</tt>.</dl>
 

 <tt>&quot;haldclut&quot;</tt> also has the same interpolation options as <b>lut3d</b> (both filters share the same internals). 

 More information about the Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> can be found on Eskil Steenberg's website (Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> author) at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.quelsolaar.com/technology/clut.html">http://www.quelsolaar.com/technology/clut.html</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Workflow examples</i> 

 Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> video stream 

 Generate an identity Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> stream altered with various effects: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f lavfi -i B&lt;haldclutsrc&gt;=8 -vf &quot;hue=H=2*PI*t:s=sin(2*PI*t)+1, curves=cross_process&quot; -t 10 -c:v ffv1 clut.nut</pre>Note: make sure you use a lossless codec. 

 Then use it with <tt>&quot;haldclut&quot;</tt> to apply it on some random stream: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f lavfi -i mandelbrot -i clut.nut -filter_complex '[0][1] haldclut' -t 20 mandelclut.mkv</pre>The Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> will be applied to the 10 first seconds (duration of <i>clut.nut</i>), then the latest picture of that <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> stream will be applied to the remaining frames of the <tt>&quot;mandelbrot&quot;</tt> stream. 

 Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> with preview 

 A Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> is supposed to be a squared image of <tt>&quot;Level*Level*Level&quot;</tt> by <tt>&quot;Level*Level*Level&quot;</tt> pixels. For a given Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT,</font> FFmpeg will select the biggest possible square starting at the top left of the picture. The remaining padding pixels (bottom or right) will be ignored. This area can be used to add a preview of the Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT.</font> 

 Typically, the following generated Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> will be supported by the <tt>&quot;haldclut&quot;</tt> filter: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f lavfi -i B&lt;haldclutsrc&gt;=8 -vf &quot;
 pad=iw+320 [padded_clut];
 smptebars=s=320x256, split [a][b];
 [padded_clut][a] overlay=W-320:h, curves=color_negative [main];
 [main][b] overlay=W-320&quot; -frames:v 1 clut.png</pre>It contains the original and a preview of the effect of the <font SIZE="-1">CLUT: SMPTE</font> color bars are displayed on the right-top, and below the same color bars processed by the color changes. 

 Then, the effect of this Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT</font> can be visualized with:
