 <pre> ffplay input.mkv -vf &quot;movie=clut.png, [in] haldclut&quot;</pre><h3>hflip</h3>Flip the input video horizontally. 

 For example, to horizontally flip the input video with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf &quot;hflip&quot; out.avi</pre><h3>histeq</h3>This filter applies a global color histogram equalization on a per-frame basis. 

 It can be used to correct video that has a compressed range of pixel intensities. The filter redistributes the pixel intensities to equalize their distribution across the intensity range. It may be viewed as an ``automatically adjusting contrast filter''. This filter is useful only for correcting degraded or poorly captured source video. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>strength</b>
<dd>Determine the amount of equalization to be applied. As the strength is reduced, the distribution of pixel intensities more-and-more approaches that of the input frame. The value must be a float number in the range [0,1] and defaults to 0.200.
<dt><b>intensity</b>
<dd>Set the maximum intensity that can generated and scale the output values appropriately. The strength should be set as desired and then the intensity can be limited if needed to avoid washing-out. The value must be a float number in the range [0,1] and defaults to 0.210.
<dt><b>antibanding</b>
<dd>Set the antibanding level. If enabled the filter will randomly vary the luminance of output pixels by a small amount to avoid banding of the histogram. Possible values are <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;weak&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;strong&quot;</tt>. It defaults to <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.</dl><h3>histogram</h3>Compute and draw a color distribution histogram for the input video. 

 The computed histogram is a representation of the color component distribution in an image. 

 Standard histogram displays the color components distribution in an image. Displays color graph for each color component. Shows distribution of the Y, U, V, A or R, G, B components, depending on input format, in the current frame. Below each graph a color component scale meter is shown. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>level_height</b>
<dd>Set height of level. Default value is <tt>200</tt>. Allowed range is [50, 2048].
<dt><b>scale_height</b>
<dd>Set height of color scale. Default value is <tt>12</tt>. Allowed range is [0, 40].
<dt><b>display_mode</b>
<dd>Set display mode. It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>stack</b>
<dd>Per color component graphs are placed below each other.
<dt><b>parade</b>
<dd>Per color component graphs are placed side by side.
<dt><b>overlay</b>
<dd>Presents information identical to that in the <tt>&quot;parade&quot;</tt>, except that the graphs representing color components are superimposed directly over one another.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;stack&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>levels_mode</b>
<dd>Set mode. Can be either <tt>&quot;linear&quot;</tt>, or <tt>&quot;logarithmic&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;linear&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>components</b>
<dd>Set what color components to display. Default is <tt>7</tt>.
<dt><b>fgopacity</b>
<dd>Set foreground opacity. Default is <tt>0.7</tt>.
<dt><b>bgopacity</b>
<dd>Set background opacity. Default is <tt>0.5</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Calculate and draw histogram: 

 <pre> ffplay -i input -vf histogram</pre></dl><h3>hqdn3d</h3>This is a high precision/quality 3d denoise filter. It aims to reduce image noise, producing smooth images and making still images really still. It should enhance compressibility. 

 It accepts the following optional parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>luma_spatial</b>
<dd>A non-negative floating point number which specifies spatial luma strength. It defaults to 4.0.
<dt><b>chroma_spatial</b>
<dd>A non-negative floating point number which specifies spatial chroma strength. It defaults to 3.0*<i>luma_spatial</i>/4.0.
<dt><b>luma_tmp</b>
<dd>A floating point number which specifies luma temporal strength. It defaults to 6.0*<i>luma_spatial</i>/4.0.
<dt><b>chroma_tmp</b>
<dd>A floating point number which specifies chroma temporal strength. It defaults to <i>luma_tmp</i>*<i>chroma_spatial</i>/<i>luma_spatial</i>.</dl><h3>hwdownload</h3>Download hardware frames to system memory. 

 The input must be in hardware frames, and the output a non-hardware format. Not all formats will be supported on the output - it may be necessary to insert an additional <b>format</b> filter immediately following in the graph to get the output in a supported format.
<h3>hwmap</h3>Map hardware frames to system memory or to another device. 

 This filter has several different modes of operation; which one is used depends on the input and output formats:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Hardware frame input, normal frame output 

 Map the input frames to system memory and pass them to the output. If the original hardware frame is later required (for example, after overlaying something else on part of it), the <b>hwmap</b> filter can be used again in the next mode to retrieve it.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Normal frame input, hardware frame output 

 If the input is actually a software-mapped hardware frame, then unmap it - that is, return the original hardware frame. 

 Otherwise, a device must be provided. Create new hardware surfaces on that device for the output, then map them back to the software format at the input and give those frames to the preceding filter. This will then act like the <b>hwupload</b> filter, but may be able to avoid an additional copy when the input is already in a compatible format.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Hardware frame input and output 

 A device must be supplied for the output, either directly or with the <b>derive_device</b> option. The input and output devices must be of different types and compatible - the exact meaning of this is system-dependent, but typically it means that they must refer to the same underlying hardware context (for example, refer to the same graphics card). 

 If the input frames were originally created on the output device, then unmap to retrieve the original frames. 

 Otherwise, map the frames to the output device - create new hardware frames on the output corresponding to the frames on the input.</dl>
 

 The following additional parameters are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set the frame mapping mode. Some combination of:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>read</i>
<dd>The mapped frame should be readable.
<dt><i>write</i>
<dd>The mapped frame should be writeable.
<dt><i>overwrite</i>
<dd>The mapping will always overwrite the entire frame. 

 This may improve performance in some cases, as the original contents of the frame need not be loaded.
<dt><i>direct</i>
<dd>The mapping must not involve any copying. 

 Indirect mappings to copies of frames are created in some cases where either direct mapping is not possible or it would have unexpected properties. Setting this flag ensures that the mapping is direct and will fail if that is not possible.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Defaults to <i>read+write</i> if not specified.</dl><dt><b>derive_device</b> <i>type</i>
<dd>Rather than using the device supplied at initialisation, instead derive a new device of type <i>type</i> from the device the input frames exist on.
<dt><b>reverse</b>
<dd>In a hardware to hardware mapping, map in reverse - create frames in the sink and map them back to the source. This may be necessary in some cases where a mapping in one direction is required but only the opposite direction is supported by the devices being used. 

 This option is dangerous - it may break the preceding filter in undefined ways if there are any additional constraints on that filter's output. Do not use it without fully understanding the implications of its use.</dl><h3>hwupload</h3>Upload system memory frames to hardware surfaces. 

 The device to upload to must be supplied when the filter is initialised. If using ffmpeg, select the appropriate device with the <b>-filter_hw_device</b> option.
<h3>hwupload_cuda</h3>Upload system memory frames to a <font SIZE="-1">CUDA</font> device. 

 It accepts the following optional parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>device</b>
<dd>The number of the <font SIZE="-1">CUDA</font> device to use</dl><h3>hqx</h3>Apply a high-quality magnification filter designed for pixel art. This filter was originally created by Maxim Stepin. 

 It accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>Set the scaling dimension: <tt>2</tt> for <tt>&quot;hq2x&quot;</tt>, <tt>3</tt> for <tt>&quot;hq3x&quot;</tt> and <tt>4</tt> for <tt>&quot;hq4x&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>3</tt>.</dl><h3>hstack</h3>Stack input videos horizontally. 

 All streams must be of same pixel format and of same height. 

 Note that this filter is faster than using <b>overlay</b> and <b>pad</b> filter to create same output. 

 The filter accept the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>inputs</b>
<dd>Set number of input streams. Default is 2.
<dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd>If set to 1, force the output to terminate when the shortest input terminates. Default value is 0.</dl><h3>hue</h3>Modify the hue and/or the saturation of the input. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>Specify the hue angle as a number of degrees. It accepts an expression, and defaults to ``0''.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd>Specify the saturation in the [-10,10] range. It accepts an expression and defaults to ``1''.
<dt><b>H</b>
<dd>Specify the hue angle as a number of radians. It accepts an expression, and defaults to ``0''.
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Specify the brightness in the [-10,10] range. It accepts an expression and defaults to ``0''.</dl>
 

 <b>h</b> and <b>H</b> are mutually exclusive, and can't be specified at the same time. 

 The <b>b</b>, <b>h</b>, <b>H</b> and <b>s</b> option values are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>frame count of the input frame starting from 0
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd>presentation timestamp of the input frame expressed in time base units
<dt><b>r</b>
<dd>frame rate of the input video, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input frame rate is unknown
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>timestamp expressed in seconds, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown
<dt><b>tb</b>
<dd>time base of the input video</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Set the hue to 90 degrees and the saturation to 1.0: 

 <pre> hue=h=90:s=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Same command but expressing the hue in radians: 

 <pre> hue=H=PI/2:s=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rotate hue and make the saturation swing between 0 and 2 over a period of 1 second: 

 <pre> hue=&quot;H=2*PI*t: s=sin(2*PI*t)+1&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply a 3 seconds saturation fade-in effect starting at 0: 

 <pre> hue=&quot;s=min(t/3\,1)&quot;</pre>The general fade-in expression can be written as: 

 <pre> hue=&quot;s=min(0\, max((t-START)/DURATION\, 1))&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply a 3 seconds saturation fade-out effect starting at 5 seconds: 

 <pre> hue=&quot;s=max(0\, min(1\, (8-t)/3))&quot;</pre>The general fade-out expression can be written as: 

 <pre> hue=&quot;s=max(0\, min(1\, (START+DURATION-t)/DURATION))&quot;</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>b</b>
<dd><dt><b>s</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd><dt><b>H</b>
<dd>Modify the hue and/or the saturation and/or brightness of the input video. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.</dl><h3>hysteresis</h3>Grow first stream into second stream by connecting components. This makes it possible to build more robust edge masks. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed as bitmap, unprocessed planes will be copied from first stream. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
<dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd>Set threshold which is used in filtering. If pixel component value is higher than this value filter algorithm for connecting components is activated. By default value is 0.</dl><h3>idet</h3>Detect video interlacing type. 

 This filter tries to detect if the input frames are interlaced, progressive, top or bottom field first. It will also try to detect fields that are repeated between adjacent frames (a sign of telecine). 

 Single frame detection considers only immediately adjacent frames when classifying each frame. Multiple frame detection incorporates the classification history of previous frames. 

 The filter will log these metadata values:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>single.current_frame</b>
<dd>Detected type of current frame using single-frame detection. One of: ``tff'' (top field first), ``bff'' (bottom field first), ``progressive'', or ``undetermined''
<dt><b>single.tff</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames detected as top field first using single-frame detection.
<dt><b>multiple.tff</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames detected as top field first using multiple-frame detection.
<dt><b>single.bff</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames detected as bottom field first using single-frame detection.
<dt><b>multiple.current_frame</b>
<dd>Detected type of current frame using multiple-frame detection. One of: ``tff'' (top field first), ``bff'' (bottom field first), ``progressive'', or ``undetermined''
<dt><b>multiple.bff</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames detected as bottom field first using multiple-frame detection.
<dt><b>single.progressive</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames detected as progressive using single-frame detection.
<dt><b>multiple.progressive</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames detected as progressive using multiple-frame detection.
<dt><b>single.undetermined</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames that could not be classified using single-frame detection.
<dt><b>multiple.undetermined</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames that could not be classified using multiple-frame detection.
<dt><b>repeated.current_frame</b>
<dd>Which field in the current frame is repeated from the last. One of ``neither'', ``top'', or ``bottom''.
<dt><b>repeated.neither</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames with no repeated field.
<dt><b>repeated.top</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames with the top field repeated from the previous frame's top field.
<dt><b>repeated.bottom</b>
<dd>Cumulative number of frames with the bottom field repeated from the previous frame's bottom field.</dl>
 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>intl_thres</b>
<dd>Set interlacing threshold.
<dt><b>prog_thres</b>
<dd>Set progressive threshold.
<dt><b>rep_thres</b>
<dd>Threshold for repeated field detection.
<dt><b>half_life</b>
<dd>Number of frames after which a given frame's contribution to the statistics is halved (i.e., it contributes only 0.5 to its classification). The default of 0 means that all frames seen are given full weight of 1.0 forever.
<dt><b>analyze_interlaced_flag</b>
<dd>When this is not 0 then idet will use the specified number of frames to determine if the interlaced flag is accurate, it will not count undetermined frames. If the flag is found to be accurate it will be used without any further computations, if it is found to be inaccurate it will be cleared without any further computations. This allows inserting the idet filter as a low computational method to clean up the interlaced flag</dl><h3>il</h3>Deinterleave or interleave fields. 

 This filter allows one to process interlaced images fields without deinterlacing them. Deinterleaving splits the input frame into 2 fields (so called half pictures). Odd lines are moved to the top half of the output image, even lines to the bottom half. You can process (filter) them independently and then re-interleave them. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>luma_mode, l</b>
<dd><dt><b>chroma_mode, c</b>
<dd><dt><b>alpha_mode, a</b>
<dd>Available values for <i>luma_mode</i>, <i>chroma_mode</i> and <i>alpha_mode</i> are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Do nothing.
<dt><b>deinterleave, d</b>
<dd>Deinterleave fields, placing one above the other.
<dt><b>interleave, i</b>
<dd>Interleave fields. Reverse the effect of deinterleaving.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>luma_swap, ls</b>
<dd><dt><b>chroma_swap, cs</b>
<dd><dt><b>alpha_swap, as</b>
<dd>Swap luma/chroma/alpha fields. Exchange even &amp; odd lines. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.</dl><h3>inflate</h3>Apply inflate effect to the video. 

 This filter replaces the pixel by the local(3x3) average by taking into account only values higher than the pixel. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold0</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold1</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold2</b>
<dd><dt><b>threshold3</b>
<dd>Limit the maximum change for each plane, default is 65535. If 0, plane will remain unchanged.</dl><h3>interlace</h3>Simple interlacing filter from progressive contents. This interleaves upper (or lower) lines from odd frames with lower (or upper) lines from even frames, halving the frame rate and preserving image height. 

 <pre> Original Original New Frame
 Frame 'j' Frame 'j+1' (tff)
 ========== =========== ==================
 Line 0 --------------------&gt; Frame 'j' Line 0
 Line 1 Line 1 ----&gt; Frame 'j+1' Line 1
 Line 2 ---------------------&gt; Frame 'j' Line 2
 Line 3 Line 3 ----&gt; Frame 'j+1' Line 3
 ... ... ...
 New Frame + 1 will be generated by Frame 'j+2' and Frame 'j+3' and so on</pre>It accepts the following optional parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>scan</b>
<dd>This determines whether the interlaced frame is taken from the even (tff - default) or odd (bff) lines of the progressive frame.
<dt><b>lowpass</b>
<dd>Vertical lowpass filter to avoid twitter interlacing and reduce moire patterns.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, off</b>
<dd>Disable vertical lowpass filter
<dt><b>1, linear</b>
<dd>Enable linear filter (default)
<dt><b>2, complex</b>
<dd>Enable complex filter. This will slightly less reduce twitter and moire but better retain detail and subjective sharpness impression.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>kerndeint</h3>Deinterlace input video by applying Donald Graft's adaptive kernel deinterling. Work on interlaced parts of a video to produce progressive frames. 

 The description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>thresh</b>
<dd>Set the threshold which affects the filter's tolerance when determining if a pixel line must be processed. It must be an integer in the range [0,255] and defaults to 10. A value of 0 will result in applying the process on every pixels.
<dt><b>map</b>
<dd>Paint pixels exceeding the threshold value to white if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>order</b>
<dd>Set the fields order. Swap fields if set to 1, leave fields alone if 0. Default is 0.
<dt><b>sharp</b>
<dd>Enable additional sharpening if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>twoway</b>
<dd>Enable twoway sharpening if set to 1. Default is 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply default values: 

 <pre> kerndeint=thresh=10:map=0:order=0:sharp=0:twoway=0</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Enable additional sharpening: 

 <pre> kerndeint=sharp=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Paint processed pixels in white: 

 <pre> kerndeint=map=1</pre></dl><h3>lenscorrection</h3>Correct radial lens distortion 

 This filter can be used to correct for radial distortion as can result from the use of wide angle lenses, and thereby re-rectify the image. To find the right parameters one can use tools available for example as part of opencv or simply trial-and-error. To use opencv use the calibration sample (under samples/cpp) from the opencv sources and extract the k1 and k2 coefficients from the resulting matrix. 

 Note that effectively the same filter is available in the open-source tools Krita and Digikam from the <font SIZE="-1">KDE</font> project. 

 In contrast to the <b>vignette</b> filter, which can also be used to compensate lens errors, this filter corrects the distortion of the image, whereas <b>vignette</b> corrects the brightness distribution, so you may want to use both filters together in certain cases, though you will have to take care of ordering, i.e. whether vignetting should be applied before or after lens correction. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>cx</b>
<dd>Relative x-coordinate of the focal point of the image, and thereby the center of the distortion. This value has a range [0,1] and is expressed as fractions of the image width.
<dt><b>cy</b>
<dd>Relative y-coordinate of the focal point of the image, and thereby the center of the distortion. This value has a range [0,1] and is expressed as fractions of the image height.
<dt><b>k1</b>
<dd>Coefficient of the quadratic correction term. 0.5 means no correction.
<dt><b>k2</b>
<dd>Coefficient of the double quadratic correction term. 0.5 means no correction.</dl>
 

 The formula that generates the correction is: 

 <i>r_src</i> = <i>r_tgt</i> * (1 + <i>k1</i> * (<i>r_tgt</i> / <i>r_0</i>)^2 + <i>k2</i> * (<i>r_tgt</i> / <i>r_0</i>)^4) 

 where <i>r_0</i> is halve of the image diagonal and <i>r_src</i> and <i>r_tgt</i> are the distances from the focal point in the source and target images, respectively.
<h3>libvmaf</h3>Obtain the average <font SIZE="-1">VMAF</font> (Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion) score between two input videos. 

 This filter takes two input videos. 

 Both video inputs must have the same resolution and pixel format for this filter to work correctly. Also it assumes that both inputs have the same number of frames, which are compared one by one. 

 The obtained average <font SIZE="-1">VMAF</font> score is printed through the logging system. 

 It requires Netflix's vmaf library (libvmaf) as a pre-requisite. After installing the library it can be enabled using: <tt>&quot;./configure --enable-libvmaf&quot;</tt>. If no model path is specified it uses the default model: <tt>&quot;vmaf_v0.6.1.pkl&quot;</tt>. 

 On the below examples the input file <i>main.mpg</i> being processed is compared with the reference file <i>ref.mpg</i>. 

 The filter has following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>model_path</b>
<dd>Set the model path which is to be used for <font SIZE="-1">SVM.</font> Default value: <tt>&quot;vmaf_v0.6.1.pkl&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>log_path</b>
<dd>Set the file path to be used to store logs.
<dt><b>log_fmt</b>
<dd>Set the format of the log file (xml or json).
<dt><b>enable_transform</b>
<dd>Enables transform for computing vmaf.
<dt><b>phone_model</b>
<dd>Invokes the phone model which will generate <font SIZE="-1">VMAF</font> scores higher than in the regular model, which is more suitable for laptop, <font SIZE="-1">TV,</font> etc. viewing conditions.
<dt><b>psnr</b>
<dd>Enables computing psnr along with vmaf.
<dt><b>ssim</b>
<dd>Enables computing ssim along with vmaf.
<dt><b>ms_ssim</b>
<dd>Enables computing ms_ssim along with vmaf.
<dt><b>pool</b>
<dd>Set the pool method to be used for computing vmaf.</dl>
 

 This filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options. 

 For example: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i main.mpg -i ref.mpg -lavfi libvmaf -f null -</pre>Example with options: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i main.mpg -i ref.mpg -lavfi libvmaf=&quot;psnr=1:enable-transform=1&quot; -f null -</pre><h3>limiter</h3>Limits the pixel components values to the specified range [min, max]. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>min</b>
<dd>Lower bound. Defaults to the lowest allowed value for the input.
<dt><b>max</b>
<dd>Upper bound. Defaults to the highest allowed value for the input.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Specify which planes will be processed. Defaults to all available.</dl><h3>loop</h3>Loop video frames. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>loop</b>
<dd>Set the number of loops.
<dt><b>size</b>
<dd>Set maximal size in number of frames.
<dt><b>start</b>
<dd>Set first frame of loop.</dl><h3>lut3d</h3>Apply a 3D <font SIZE="-1">LUT</font> to an input video. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>file</b>
<dd>Set the 3D <font SIZE="-1">LUT</font> file name. 

 Currently supported formats:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>3dl</b>
<dd>AfterEffects
<dt><b>cube</b>
<dd>Iridas
<dt><b>dat</b>
<dd>DaVinci
<dt><b>m3d</b>
<dd>Pandora</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>interp</b>
<dd>Select interpolation mode. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>nearest</b>
<dd>Use values from the nearest defined point.
<dt><b>trilinear</b>
<dd>Interpolate values using the 8 points defining a cube.
<dt><b>tetrahedral</b>
<dd>Interpolate values using a tetrahedron.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 This filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options.
<h3>lumakey</h3>Turn certain luma values into transparency. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd>Set the luma which will be used as base for transparency. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>tolerance</b>
<dd>Set the range of luma values to be keyed out. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>softness</b>
<dd>Set the range of softness. Default value is <tt>0</tt>. Use this to control gradual transition from zero to full transparency.</dl><h3>lut, lutrgb, lutyuv</h3>Compute a look-up table for binding each pixel component input value to an output value, and apply it to the input video. 

 <i>lutyuv</i> applies a lookup table to a <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> input video, <i>lutrgb</i> to an <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> input video. 

 These filters accept the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>c0</b>
<dd>set first pixel component expression
<dt><b>c1</b>
<dd>set second pixel component expression
<dt><b>c2</b>
<dd>set third pixel component expression
<dt><b>c3</b>
<dd>set fourth pixel component expression, corresponds to the alpha component
<dt><b>r</b>
<dd>set red component expression
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd>set green component expression
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd>set blue component expression
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>alpha component expression
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd>set Y/luminance component expression
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd>set U/Cb component expression
<dt><b>v</b>
<dd>set V/Cr component expression</dl>
 

 Each of them specifies the expression to use for computing the lookup table for the corresponding pixel component values. 

 The exact component associated to each of the <i>c*</i> options depends on the format in input. 

 The <i>lut</i> filter requires either <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> or <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> pixel formats in input, <i>lutrgb</i> requires <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> pixel formats in input, and <i>lutyuv</i> requires <font SIZE="-1">YUV.</font> 

 The expressions can contain the following constants and functions:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>The input width and height.
<dt><b>val</b>
<dd>The input value for the pixel component.
<dt><b>clipval</b>
<dd>The input value, clipped to the <i>minval</i>-<i>maxval</i> range.
<dt><b>maxval</b>
<dd>The maximum value for the pixel component.
<dt><b>minval</b>
<dd>The minimum value for the pixel component.
<dt><b>negval</b>
<dd>The negated value for the pixel component value, clipped to the <i>minval</i>-<i>maxval</i> range; it corresponds to the expression ``maxval-clipval+minval''.
<dt><b>clip(val)</b>
<dd>The computed value in <i>val</i>, clipped to the <i>minval</i>-<i>maxval</i> range.
<dt><b>gammaval(gamma)</b>
<dd>The computed gamma correction value of the pixel component value, clipped to the <i>minval</i>-<i>maxval</i> range. It corresponds to the expression &quot;pow((clipval-minval)/(maxval-minval)\,<i>gamma</i>)*(maxval-minval)+minval&quot;</dl>
 

 All expressions default to ``val''. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Negate input video: 

 <pre> lutrgb=&quot;r=maxval+minval-val:g=maxval+minval-val:b=maxval+minval-val&quot;
 lutyuv=&quot;y=maxval+minval-val:u=maxval+minval-val:v=maxval+minval-val&quot;</pre>The above is the same as: 

 <pre> lutrgb=&quot;r=negval:g=negval:b=negval&quot;
 lutyuv=&quot;y=negval:u=negval:v=negval&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Negate luminance: 

 <pre> lutyuv=y=negval</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Remove chroma components, turning the video into a graytone image: 

 <pre> lutyuv=&quot;u=128:v=128&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply a luma burning effect: 

 <pre> lutyuv=&quot;y=2*val&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Remove green and blue components: 

 <pre> lutrgb=&quot;g=0:b=0&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Set a constant alpha channel value on input: 

 <pre> format=rgba,lutrgb=a=&quot;maxval-minval/2&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Correct luminance gamma by a factor of 0.5: 

 <pre> lutyuv=y=gammaval(0.5)</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Discard least significant bits of luma: 

 <pre> lutyuv=y='bitand(val, 128+64+32)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Technicolor like effect: 

 <pre> lutyuv=u='(val-maxval/2)*2+maxval/2':v='(val-maxval/2)*2+maxval/2'</pre></dl><h3>lut2, tlut2</h3>The <tt>&quot;lut2&quot;</tt> filter takes two input streams and outputs one stream. 

 The <tt>&quot;tlut2&quot;</tt> (time lut2) filter takes two consecutive frames from one single stream. 

 This filter accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>c0</b>
<dd>set first pixel component expression
<dt><b>c1</b>
<dd>set second pixel component expression
<dt><b>c2</b>
<dd>set third pixel component expression
<dt><b>c3</b>
<dd>set fourth pixel component expression, corresponds to the alpha component</dl>
 

 Each of them specifies the expression to use for computing the lookup table for the corresponding pixel component values. 

 The exact component associated to each of the <i>c*</i> options depends on the format in inputs. 

 The expressions can contain the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>The input width and height.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd>The first input value for the pixel component.
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The second input value for the pixel component.
<dt><b>bdx</b>
<dd>The first input video bit depth.
<dt><b>bdy</b>
<dd>The second input video bit depth.</dl>
 

 All expressions default to ``x''. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Highlight differences between two <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> video streams: 

 <pre> lut2='ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Highlight differences between two <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> video streams: 

 <pre> lut2='ifnot(x-y,0,pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,pow(2,bdx-1),pow(2,bdx)-1):ifnot(x-y,pow(2,bdx-1),pow(2,bdx)-1)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Show max difference between two video streams: 

 <pre> lut2='if(lt(x,y),0,if(gt(x,y),pow(2,bdx)-1,pow(2,bdx-1))):if(lt(x,y),0,if(gt(x,y),pow(2,bdx)-1,pow(2,bdx-1))):if(lt(x,y),0,if(gt(x,y),pow(2,bdx)-1,pow(2,bdx-1)))'</pre></dl><h3>maskedclamp</h3>Clamp the first input stream with the second input and third input stream. 

 Returns the value of first stream to be between second input stream - <tt>&quot;undershoot&quot;</tt> and third input stream + <tt>&quot;overshoot&quot;</tt>. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>undershoot</b>
<dd>Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>overshoot</b>
<dd>Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed as bitmap, unprocessed planes will be copied from first stream. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.</dl><h3>maskedmerge</h3>Merge the first input stream with the second input stream using per pixel weights in the third input stream. 

 A value of 0 in the third stream pixel component means that pixel component from first stream is returned unchanged, while maximum value (eg. 255 for 8-bit videos) means that pixel component from second stream is returned unchanged. Intermediate values define the amount of merging between both input stream's pixel components. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed as bitmap, unprocessed planes will be copied from first stream. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.</dl><h3>mcdeint</h3>Apply motion-compensation deinterlacing. 

 It needs one field per frame as input and must thus be used together with yadif=1/3 or equivalent. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set the deinterlacing mode. 

 It accepts one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>fast</b>
<dd><dt><b>medium</b>
<dd><dt><b>slow</b>
<dd>use iterative motion estimation
<dt><b>extra_slow</b>
<dd>like <b>slow</b>, but use multiple reference frames.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>fast</b>.</dl><dt><b>parity</b>
<dd>Set the picture field parity assumed for the input video. It must be one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, tff</b>
<dd>assume top field first
<dt><b>1, bff</b>
<dd>assume bottom field first</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>bff</b>.</dl><dt><b>qp</b>
<dd>Set per-block quantization parameter (<font SIZE="-1">QP</font>) used by the internal encoder. 

 Higher values should result in a smoother motion vector field but less optimal individual vectors. Default value is 1.</dl><h3>mergeplanes</h3>Merge color channel components from several video streams. 

 The filter accepts up to 4 input streams, and merge selected input planes to the output video. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mapping</b>
<dd>Set input to output plane mapping. Default is <tt>0</tt>. 

 The mappings is specified as a bitmap. It should be specified as a hexadecimal number in the form 0xAa[Bb[Cc[Dd]]]. 'Aa' describes the mapping for the first plane of the output stream. 'A' sets the number of the input stream to use (from 0 to 3), and 'a' the plane number of the corresponding input to use (from 0 to 3). The rest of the mappings is similar, 'Bb' describes the mapping for the output stream second plane, 'Cc' describes the mapping for the output stream third plane and 'Dd' describes the mapping for the output stream fourth plane.
<dt><b>format</b>
<dd>Set output pixel format. Default is <tt>&quot;yuva444p&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Merge three gray video streams of same width and height into single video stream: 

 <pre> [a0][a1][a2]mergeplanes=0x001020:yuv444p</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Merge 1st yuv444p stream and 2nd gray video stream into yuva444p video stream: 

 <pre> [a0][a1]mergeplanes=0x00010210:yuva444p</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Swap Y and A plane in yuva444p stream: 

 <pre> format=yuva444p,mergeplanes=0x03010200:yuva444p</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Swap U and V plane in yuv420p stream: 

 <pre> format=yuv420p,mergeplanes=0x000201:yuv420p</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Cast a rgb24 clip to yuv444p: 

 <pre> format=rgb24,mergeplanes=0x000102:yuv444p</pre></dl><h3>mestimate</h3>Estimate and export motion vectors using block matching algorithms. Motion vectors are stored in frame side data to be used by other filters. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>method</b>
<dd>Specify the motion estimation method. Accepts one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>esa</b>
<dd>Exhaustive search algorithm.
<dt><b>tss</b>
<dd>Three step search algorithm.
<dt><b>tdls</b>
<dd>Two dimensional logarithmic search algorithm.
<dt><b>ntss</b>
<dd>New three step search algorithm.
<dt><b>fss</b>
<dd>Four step search algorithm.
<dt><b>ds</b>
<dd>Diamond search algorithm.
<dt><b>hexbs</b>
<dd>Hexagon-based search algorithm.
<dt><b>epzs</b>
<dd>Enhanced predictive zonal search algorithm.
<dt><b>umh</b>
<dd>Uneven multi-hexagon search algorithm.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>esa</b>.</dl><dt><b>mb_size</b>
<dd>Macroblock size. Default <tt>16</tt>.
<dt><b>search_param</b>
<dd>Search parameter. Default <tt>7</tt>.</dl><h3>midequalizer</h3>Apply Midway Image Equalization effect using two video streams. 

 Midway Image Equalization adjusts a pair of images to have the same histogram, while maintaining their dynamics as much as possible. It's useful for e.g. matching exposures from a pair of stereo cameras. 

 This filter has two inputs and one output, which must be of same pixel format, but may be of different sizes. The output of filter is first input adjusted with midway histogram of both inputs. 

 This filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes to process. Default is <tt>15</tt>, which is all available planes.</dl><h3>minterpolate</h3>Convert the video to specified frame rate using motion interpolation. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>fps</b>
<dd>Specify the output frame rate. This can be rational e.g. <tt>&quot;60000/1001&quot;</tt>. Frames are dropped if <i>fps</i> is lower than source fps. Default <tt>60</tt>.
<dt><b>mi_mode</b>
<dd>Motion interpolation mode. Following values are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>dup</b>
<dd>Duplicate previous or next frame for interpolating new ones.
<dt><b>blend</b>
<dd>Blend source frames. Interpolated frame is mean of previous and next frames.
<dt><b>mci</b>
<dd>Motion compensated interpolation. Following options are effective when this mode is selected:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>mc_mode</b>
<dd>Motion compensation mode. Following values are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>obmc</b>
<dd>Overlapped block motion compensation.
<dt><b>aobmc</b>
<dd>Adaptive overlapped block motion compensation. Window weighting coefficients are controlled adaptively according to the reliabilities of the neighboring motion vectors to reduce oversmoothing.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default mode is <b>obmc</b>.</dl><dt><b>me_mode</b>
<dd>Motion estimation mode. Following values are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>bidir</b>
<dd>Bidirectional motion estimation. Motion vectors are estimated for each source frame in both forward and backward directions.
<dt><b>bilat</b>
<dd>Bilateral motion estimation. Motion vectors are estimated directly for interpolated frame.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default mode is <b>bilat</b>.</dl><dt><b>me</b>
<dd>The algorithm to be used for motion estimation. Following values are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>esa</b>
<dd>Exhaustive search algorithm.
<dt><b>tss</b>
<dd>Three step search algorithm.
<dt><b>tdls</b>
<dd>Two dimensional logarithmic search algorithm.
<dt><b>ntss</b>
<dd>New three step search algorithm.
<dt><b>fss</b>
<dd>Four step search algorithm.
<dt><b>ds</b>
<dd>Diamond search algorithm.
<dt><b>hexbs</b>
<dd>Hexagon-based search algorithm.
<dt><b>epzs</b>
<dd>Enhanced predictive zonal search algorithm.
<dt><b>umh</b>
<dd>Uneven multi-hexagon search algorithm.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default algorithm is <b>epzs</b>.</dl><dt><b>mb_size</b>
<dd>Macroblock size. Default <tt>16</tt>.
<dt><b>search_param</b>
<dd>Motion estimation search parameter. Default <tt>32</tt>.
<dt><b>vsbmc</b>
<dd>Enable variable-size block motion compensation. Motion estimation is applied with smaller block sizes at object boundaries in order to make the them less blur. Default is <tt>0</tt> (disabled).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
</dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>scd</b>
<dd>Scene change detection method. Scene change leads motion vectors to be in random direction. Scene change detection replace interpolated frames by duplicate ones. May not be needed for other modes. Following values are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Disable scene change detection.
<dt><b>fdiff</b>
<dd>Frame difference. Corresponding pixel values are compared and if it satisfies <i>scd_threshold</i> scene change is detected.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default method is <b>fdiff</b>.</dl><dt><b>scd_threshold</b>
<dd>Scene change detection threshold. Default is <tt>5.0</tt>.</dl><h3>mpdecimate</h3>Drop frames that do not differ greatly from the previous frame in order to reduce frame rate. 

 The main use of this filter is for very-low-bitrate encoding (e.g. streaming over dialup modem), but it could in theory be used for fixing movies that were inverse-telecined incorrectly. 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>max</b>
<dd>Set the maximum number of consecutive frames which can be dropped (if positive), or the minimum interval between dropped frames (if negative). If the value is 0, the frame is dropped disregarding the number of previous sequentially dropped frames. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>hi</b>
<dd><dt><b>lo</b>
<dd><dt><b>frac</b>
<dd>Set the dropping threshold values. 

 Values for <b>hi</b> and <b>lo</b> are for 8x8 pixel blocks and represent actual pixel value differences, so a threshold of 64 corresponds to 1 unit of difference for each pixel, or the same spread out differently over the block. 

 A frame is a candidate for dropping if no 8x8 blocks differ by more than a threshold of <b>hi</b>, and if no more than <b>frac</b> blocks (1 meaning the whole image) differ by more than a threshold of <b>lo</b>. 

 Default value for <b>hi</b> is 64*12, default value for <b>lo</b> is 64*5, and default value for <b>frac</b> is 0.33.</dl><h3>negate</h3>Negate input video. 

 It accepts an integer in input; if non-zero it negates the alpha component (if available). The default value in input is 0.
<h3>nlmeans</h3>Denoise frames using Non-Local Means algorithm. 

 Each pixel is adjusted by looking for other pixels with similar contexts. This context similarity is defined by comparing their surrounding patches of size <b>p</b>x<b>p</b>. Patches are searched in an area of <b>r</b>x<b>r</b> around the pixel. 

 Note that the research area defines centers for patches, which means some patches will be made of pixels outside that research area. 

 The filter accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>s</b>
<dd>Set denoising strength.
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd>Set patch size.
<dt><b>pc</b>
<dd>Same as <b>p</b> but for chroma planes. 

 The default value is <i>0</i> and means automatic.
<dt><b>r</b>
<dd>Set research size.
<dt><b>rc</b>
<dd>Same as <b>r</b> but for chroma planes. 

 The default value is <i>0</i> and means automatic.</dl><h3>nnedi</h3>Deinterlace video using neural network edge directed interpolation. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>weights</b>
<dd>Mandatory option, without binary file filter can not work. Currently file can be found here: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/dubhater/vapoursynth-nnedi3/blob/master/src/nnedi3_weights.bin">https://github.com/dubhater/vapoursynth-nnedi3/blob/master/src/nnedi3_weights.bin</a>
<dt><b>deint</b>
<dd>Set which frames to deinterlace, by default it is <tt>&quot;all&quot;</tt>. Can be <tt>&quot;all&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;interlaced&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>field</b>
<dd>Set mode of operation. 

 Can be one of the following:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>af</b>
<dd>Use frame flags, both fields.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>Use frame flags, single field.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>Use top field only.
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Use bottom field only.
<dt><b>tf</b>
<dd>Use both fields, top first.
<dt><b>bf</b>
<dd>Use both fields, bottom first.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes to process, by default filter process all frames.
<dt><b>nsize</b>
<dd>Set size of local neighborhood around each pixel, used by the predictor neural network. 

 Can be one of the following:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>s8x6</b>
<dd><dt><b>s16x6</b>
<dd><dt><b>s32x6</b>
<dd><dt><b>s48x6</b>
<dd><dt><b>s8x4</b>
<dd><dt><b>s16x4</b>
<dd><dt><b>s32x4</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>nns</b>
<dd>Set the number of neurons in predictor neural network. Can be one of the following:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>n16</b>
<dd><dt><b>n32</b>
<dd><dt><b>n64</b>
<dd><dt><b>n128</b>
<dd><dt><b>n256</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>qual</b>
<dd>Controls the number of different neural network predictions that are blended together to compute the final output value. Can be <tt>&quot;fast&quot;</tt>, default or <tt>&quot;slow&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>etype</b>
<dd>Set which set of weights to use in the predictor. Can be one of the following:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>a</b>
<dd>weights trained to minimize absolute error
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd>weights trained to minimize squared error</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>pscrn</b>
<dd>Controls whether or not the prescreener neural network is used to decide which pixels should be processed by the predictor neural network and which can be handled by simple cubic interpolation. The prescreener is trained to know whether cubic interpolation will be sufficient for a pixel or whether it should be predicted by the predictor nn. The computational complexity of the prescreener nn is much less than that of the predictor nn. Since most pixels can be handled by cubic interpolation, using the prescreener generally results in much faster processing. The prescreener is pretty accurate, so the difference between using it and not using it is almost always unnoticeable. 

 Can be one of the following:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd><dt><b>original</b>
<dd><dt><b>new</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;new&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>fapprox</b>
<dd>Set various debugging flags.</dl><h3>noformat</h3>Force libavfilter not to use any of the specified pixel formats for the input to the next filter. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>pix_fmts</b>
<dd>A '|'-separated list of pixel format names, such as pix_fmts=yuv420p|monow|rgb24&quot;.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Force libavfilter to use a format different from <i>yuv420p</i> for the input to the vflip filter: 

 <pre> noformat=pix_fmts=yuv420p,vflip</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Convert the input video to any of the formats not contained in the list: 

 <pre> noformat=yuv420p|yuv444p|yuv410p</pre></dl><h3>noise</h3>Add noise on video input frame. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>all_seed</b>
<dd><dt><b>c0_seed</b>
<dd><dt><b>c1_seed</b>
<dd><dt><b>c2_seed</b>
<dd><dt><b>c3_seed</b>
<dd>Set noise seed for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case of <i>all_seed</i>. Default value is <tt>123457</tt>.
<dt><b>all_strength, alls</b>
<dd><dt><b>c0_strength, c0s</b>
<dd><dt><b>c1_strength, c1s</b>
<dd><dt><b>c2_strength, c2s</b>
<dd><dt><b>c3_strength, c3s</b>
<dd>Set noise strength for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case <i>all_strength</i>. Default value is <tt>0</tt>. Allowed range is [0, 100].
<dt><b>all_flags, allf</b>
<dd><dt><b>c0_flags, c0f</b>
<dd><dt><b>c1_flags, c1f</b>
<dd><dt><b>c2_flags, c2f</b>
<dd><dt><b>c3_flags, c3f</b>
<dd>Set pixel component flags or set flags for all components if <i>all_flags</i>. Available values for component flags are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>a</b>
<dd>averaged temporal noise (smoother)
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd>mix random noise with a (semi)regular pattern
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>temporal noise (noise pattern changes between frames)
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd>uniform noise (gaussian otherwise)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 Add temporal and uniform noise to input video: 

 <pre> noise=alls=20:allf=t+u</pre><h3>null</h3>Pass the video source unchanged to the output.
<h3>ocr</h3>Optical Character Recognition 

 This filter uses Tesseract for optical character recognition. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>datapath</b>
<dd>Set datapath to tesseract data. Default is to use whatever was set at installation.
<dt><b>language</b>
<dd>Set language, default is ``eng''.
<dt><b>whitelist</b>
<dd>Set character whitelist.
<dt><b>blacklist</b>
<dd>Set character blacklist.</dl>
 

 The filter exports recognized text as the frame metadata <tt>&quot;lavfi.ocr.text&quot;</tt>.
<h3>ocv</h3>Apply a video transform using libopencv. 

 To enable this filter, install the libopencv library and headers and configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopencv&quot;</tt>. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filter_name</b>
<dd>The name of the libopencv filter to apply.
<dt><b>filter_params</b>
<dd>The parameters to pass to the libopencv filter. If not specified, the default values are assumed.</dl>
 

 Refer to the official libopencv documentation for more precise information: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://docs.opencv.org/master/modules/imgproc/doc/filtering.html">http://docs.opencv.org/master/modules/imgproc/doc/filtering.html</a></b>&gt; 

 Several libopencv filters are supported; see the following subsections. 

 <i>dilate</i> 

 Dilate an image by using a specific structuring element. It corresponds to the libopencv function <tt>&quot;cvDilate&quot;</tt>. 

 It accepts the parameters: <i>struct_el</i>|<i>nb_iterations</i>. 

 <i>struct_el</i> represents a structuring element, and has the syntax: <i>cols</i>x<i>rows</i>+<i>anchor_x</i>x<i>anchor_y</i>/<i>shape</i> 

 <i>cols</i> and <i>rows</i> represent the number of columns and rows of the structuring element, <i>anchor_x</i> and <i>anchor_y</i> the anchor point, and <i>shape</i> the shape for the structuring element. <i>shape</i> must be ``rect'', ``cross'', ``ellipse'', or ``custom''. 

 If the value for <i>shape</i> is ``custom'', it must be followed by a string of the form &quot;=<i>filename</i>&quot;. The file with name <i>filename</i> is assumed to represent a binary image, with each printable character corresponding to a bright pixel. When a custom <i>shape</i> is used, <i>cols</i> and <i>rows</i> are ignored, the number or columns and rows of the read file are assumed instead. 

 The default value for <i>struct_el</i> is ``3x3+0x0/rect''. 

 <i>nb_iterations</i> specifies the number of times the transform is applied to the image, and defaults to 1. 

 Some examples: 

 <pre> # Use the default values
 ocv=dilate
 
 # Dilate using a structuring element with a 5x5 cross, iterating two times
 ocv=filter_name=dilate:filter_params=5x5+2x2/cross|2
 
 # Read the shape from the file diamond.shape, iterating two times.
 # The file diamond.shape may contain a pattern of characters like this
 # *
 # ***
 # *****
 # ***
 # *
 # The specified columns and rows are ignored
 # but the anchor point coordinates are not
 ocv=dilate:0x0+2x2/custom=diamond.shape|2</pre><i>erode</i> 

 Erode an image by using a specific structuring element. It corresponds to the libopencv function <tt>&quot;cvErode&quot;</tt>. 

 It accepts the parameters: <i>struct_el</i>:<i>nb_iterations</i>, with the same syntax and semantics as the <b>dilate</b> filter. 

 <i>smooth</i> 

 Smooth the input video. 

 The filter takes the following parameters: <i>type</i>|<i>param1</i>|<i>param2</i>|<i>param3</i>|<i>param4</i>. 

 <i>type</i> is the type of smooth filter to apply, and must be one of the following values: ``blur'', ``blur_no_scale'', ``median'', ``gaussian'', or ``bilateral''. The default value is ``gaussian''. 

 The meaning of <i>param1</i>, <i>param2</i>, <i>param3</i>, and <i>param4</i> depend on the smooth type. <i>param1</i> and <i>param2</i> accept integer positive values or 0. <i>param3</i> and <i>param4</i> accept floating point values. 

 The default value for <i>param1</i> is 3. The default value for the other parameters is 0. 

 These parameters correspond to the parameters assigned to the libopencv function <tt>&quot;cvSmooth&quot;</tt>.
<h3>oscilloscope</h3>2D Video Oscilloscope. 

 Useful to measure spatial impulse, step responses, chroma delays, etc. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd>Set scope center x position.
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Set scope center y position.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd>Set scope size, relative to frame diagonal.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>Set scope tilt/rotation.
<dt><b>o</b>
<dd>Set trace opacity.
<dt><b>tx</b>
<dd>Set trace center x position.
<dt><b>ty</b>
<dd>Set trace center y position.
<dt><b>tw</b>
<dd>Set trace width, relative to width of frame.
<dt><b>th</b>
<dd>Set trace height, relative to height of frame.
<dt><b>c</b>
<dd>Set which components to trace. By default it traces first three components.
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd>Draw trace grid. By default is enabled.
<dt><b>st</b>
<dd>Draw some statistics. By default is enabled.
<dt><b>sc</b>
<dd>Draw scope. By default is enabled.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Inspect full first row of video frame. 

 <pre> oscilloscope=x=0.5:y=0:s=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Inspect full last row of video frame. 

 <pre> oscilloscope=x=0.5:y=1:s=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Inspect full 5th line of video frame of height 1080. 

 <pre> oscilloscope=x=0.5:y=5/1080:s=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Inspect full last column of video frame. 

 <pre> oscilloscope=x=1:y=0.5:s=1:t=1</pre></dl><h3>overlay</h3>Overlay one video on top of another. 

 It takes two inputs and has one output. The first input is the ``main'' video on which the second input is overlaid. 

 It accepts the following parameters: 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Set the expression for the x and y coordinates of the overlaid video on the main video. Default value is ``0'' for both expressions. In case the expression is invalid, it is set to a huge value (meaning that the overlay will not be displayed within the output visible area).
<dt><b>eof_action</b>
<dd>See <b>framesync</b>.
<dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Set when the expressions for <b>x</b>, and <b>y</b> are evaluated. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or when a command is processed
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>evaluate expressions for each incoming frame</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>frame</b>.</dl><dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd>See <b>framesync</b>.
<dt><b>format</b>
<dd>Set the format for the output video. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>yuv420</b>
<dd>force <font SIZE="-1">YUV420</font> output
<dt><b>yuv422</b>
<dd>force <font SIZE="-1">YUV422</font> output
<dt><b>yuv444</b>
<dd>force <font SIZE="-1">YUV444</font> output
<dt><b>rgb</b>
<dd>force packed <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> output
<dt><b>gbrp</b>
<dd>force planar <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> output
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>automatically pick format</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>yuv420</b>.</dl><dt><b>repeatlast</b>
<dd>See <b>framesync</b>.</dl>
 

 The <b>x</b>, and <b>y</b> expressions can contain the following parameters.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>main_w, W</b>
<dd><dt><b>main_h, H</b>
<dd>The main input width and height.
<dt><b>overlay_w, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>overlay_h, h</b>
<dd>The overlay input width and height.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The computed values for <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>. They are evaluated for each new frame.
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd><dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd>horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values of the output format. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd>the number of input frame, starting from 0
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd>the position in the file of the input frame, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if unknown
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>The timestamp, expressed in seconds. It's <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown.</dl>
 

 This filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options. 

 Note that the <i>n</i>, <i>pos</i>, <i>t</i> variables are available only when evaluation is done <i>per frame</i>, and will evaluate to <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> when <b>eval</b> is set to <b>init</b>. 

 Be aware that frames are taken from each input video in timestamp order, hence, if their initial timestamps differ, it is a good idea to pass the two inputs through a <i>setpts=PTS-STARTPTS</i> filter to have them begin in the same zero timestamp, as the example for the <i>movie</i> filter does. 

 You can chain together more overlays but you should test the efficiency of such approach. 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Modify the x and y of the overlay input. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Draw the overlay at 10 pixels from the bottom right corner of the main video: 

 <pre> overlay=main_w-overlay_w-10:main_h-overlay_h-10</pre>Using named options the example above becomes: 

 <pre> overlay=x=main_w-overlay_w-10:y=main_h-overlay_h-10</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Insert a transparent <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> logo in the bottom left corner of the input, using the <b>ffmpeg</b> tool with the <tt>&quot;-filter_complex&quot;</tt> option: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input -i logo -filter_complex 'overlay=10:main_h-overlay_h-10' output</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Insert 2 different transparent <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> logos (second logo on bottom right corner) using the <b>ffmpeg</b> tool: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input -i logo1 -i logo2 -filter_complex 'overlay=x=10:y=H-h-10,overlay=x=W-w-10:y=H-h-10' output</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Add a transparent color layer on top of the main video; <tt>&quot;WxH&quot;</tt> must specify the size of the main input to the overlay filter: 

 <pre> color=color=red@.3:size=WxH [over]; [in][over] overlay [out]</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Play an original video and a filtered version (here with the deshake filter) side by side using the <b>ffplay</b> tool: 

 <pre> ffplay input.avi -vf 'split[a][b]; [a]pad=iw*2:ih[src]; [b]deshake[filt]; [src][filt]overlay=w'</pre>The above command is the same as: 

 <pre> ffplay input.avi -vf 'split[b], pad=iw*2[src], [b]deshake, [src]overlay=w'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Make a sliding overlay appearing from the left to the right top part of the screen starting since time 2: 

 <pre> overlay=x='if(gte(t,2), -w+(t-2)*20, NAN)':y=0</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Compose output by putting two input videos side to side: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i left.avi -i right.avi -filter_complex &quot;
 nullsrc=size=200x100 [background];
 [0:v] setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, scale=100x100 [left];
 [1:v] setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, scale=100x100 [right];
 [background][left] overlay=shortest=1 [background+left];
 [background+left][right] overlay=shortest=1:x=100 [left+right]
 &quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Mask 10-20 seconds of a video by applying the delogo filter to a section 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i test.avi -codec:v:0 wmv2 -ar 11025 -b:v 9000k
 -vf '[in]split[split_main][split_delogo];[split_delogo]trim=start=360:end=371,delogo=0:0:640:480[delogoed];[split_main][delogoed]overlay=eof_action=pass[out]'
 masked.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Chain several overlays in cascade: 

 <pre> nullsrc=s=200x200 [bg];
 testsrc=s=100x100, split=4 [in0][in1][in2][in3];
 [in0] lutrgb=r=0, [bg] overlay=0:0 [mid0];
 [in1] lutrgb=g=0, [mid0] overlay=100:0 [mid1];
 [in2] lutrgb=b=0, [mid1] overlay=0:100 [mid2];
 [in3] null, [mid2] overlay=100:100 [out0]</pre></dl><h3>owdenoise</h3>Apply Overcomplete Wavelet denoiser. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>depth</b>
<dd>Set depth. 

 Larger depth values will denoise lower frequency components more, but slow down filtering. 

 Must be an int in the range 8-16, default is <tt>8</tt>.
<dt><b>luma_strength, ls</b>
<dd>Set luma strength. 

 Must be a double value in the range 0-1000, default is <tt>1.0</tt>.
<dt><b>chroma_strength, cs</b>
<dd>Set chroma strength. 

 Must be a double value in the range 0-1000, default is <tt>1.0</tt>.</dl><h3>pad</h3>Add paddings to the input image, and place the original input at the provided <i>x</i>, <i>y</i> coordinates. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd>Specify an expression for the size of the output image with the paddings added. If the value for <i>width</i> or <i>height</i> is 0, the corresponding input size is used for the output. 

 The <i>width</i> expression can reference the value set by the <i>height</i> expression, and vice versa. 

 The default value of <i>width</i> and <i>height</i> is 0.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Specify the offsets to place the input image at within the padded area, with respect to the top/left border of the output image. 

 The <i>x</i> expression can reference the value set by the <i>y</i> expression, and vice versa. 

 The default value of <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> is 0. 

 If <i>x</i> or <i>y</i> evaluate to a negative number, they'll be changed so the input image is centered on the padded area.
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd>Specify the color of the padded area. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. 

 The default value of <i>color</i> is ``black''.
<dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Specify when to evaluate <i>width</i>, <i>height</i>, <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> expression. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>Only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or when a command is processed.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>init</b>.</dl><dt><b>aspect</b>
<dd>Pad to aspect instead to a resolution.</dl>
 

 The value for the <i>width</i>, <i>height</i>, <i>x</i>, and <i>y</i> options are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>in_w</b>
<dd><dt><b>in_h</b>
<dd>The input video width and height.
<dt><b>iw</b>
<dd><dt><b>ih</b>
<dd>These are the same as <i>in_w</i> and <i>in_h</i>.
<dt><b>out_w</b>
<dd><dt><b>out_h</b>
<dd>The output width and height (the size of the padded area), as specified by the <i>width</i> and <i>height</i> expressions.
<dt><b>ow</b>
<dd><dt><b>oh</b>
<dd>These are the same as <i>out_w</i> and <i>out_h</i>.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>The x and y offsets as specified by the <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> expressions, or <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if not yet specified.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>same as <i>iw</i> / <i>ih</i>
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>input sample aspect ratio
<dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (<i>iw</i> / <i>ih</i>) * <i>sar</i>
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd><dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd>The horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Add paddings with the color ``violet'' to the input video. The output video size is 640x480, and the top-left corner of the input video is placed at column 0, row 40 

 <pre> pad=640:480:0:40:violet</pre>The example above is equivalent to the following command: 

 <pre> pad=width=640:height=480:x=0:y=40:color=violet</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Pad the input to get an output with dimensions increased by 3/2, and put the input video at the center of the padded area: 

 <pre> pad=&quot;3/2*iw:3/2*ih:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Pad the input to get a squared output with size equal to the maximum value between the input width and height, and put the input video at the center of the padded area: 

 <pre> pad=&quot;max(iw\,ih):ow:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Pad the input to get a final w/h ratio of 16:9: 

 <pre> pad=&quot;ih*16/9:ih:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>In case of anamorphic video, in order to set the output display aspect correctly, it is necessary to use <i>sar</i> in the expression, according to the relation: 

 <pre> (ih * X / ih) * sar = output_dar
 X = output_dar / sar</pre>Thus the previous example needs to be modified to: 

 <pre> pad=&quot;ih*16/9/sar:ih:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Double the output size and put the input video in the bottom-right corner of the output padded area: 

 <pre> pad=&quot;2*iw:2*ih:ow-iw:oh-ih&quot;</pre></dl><h3>palettegen</h3>Generate one palette for a whole video stream. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>max_colors</b>
<dd>Set the maximum number of colors to quantize in the palette. Note: the palette will still contain 256 colors; the unused palette entries will be black.
<dt><b>reserve_transparent</b>
<dd>Create a palette of 255 colors maximum and reserve the last one for transparency. Reserving the transparency color is useful for <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> optimization. If not set, the maximum of colors in the palette will be 256. You probably want to disable this option for a standalone image. Set by default.
<dt><b>stats_mode</b>
<dd>Set statistics mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>full</b>
<dd>Compute full frame histograms.
<dt><b>diff</b>
<dd>Compute histograms only for the part that differs from previous frame. This might be relevant to give more importance to the moving part of your input if the background is static.
<dt><b>single</b>
<dd>Compute new histogram for each frame.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>full</i>.</dl></dl>
 

 The filter also exports the frame metadata <tt>&quot;lavfi.color_quant_ratio&quot;</tt> (<tt>&quot;nb_color_in / nb_color_out&quot;</tt>) which you can use to evaluate the degree of color quantization of the palette. This information is also visible at <i>info</i> logging level. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a representative palette of a given video using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.mkv -vf palettegen palette.png</pre></dl><h3>paletteuse</h3>Use a palette to downsample an input video stream. 

 The filter takes two inputs: one video stream and a palette. The palette must be a 256 pixels image. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dither</b>
<dd>Select dithering mode. Available algorithms are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>bayer</b>
<dd>Ordered 8x8 bayer dithering (deterministic)
<dt><b>heckbert</b>
<dd>Dithering as defined by Paul Heckbert in 1982 (simple error diffusion). Note: this dithering is sometimes considered ``wrong'' and is included as a reference.
<dt><b>floyd_steinberg</b>
<dd>Floyd and Steingberg dithering (error diffusion)
<dt><b>sierra2</b>
<dd>Frankie Sierra dithering v2 (error diffusion)
<dt><b>sierra2_4a</b>
<dd>Frankie Sierra dithering v2 ``Lite'' (error diffusion)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <i>sierra2_4a</i>.</dl><dt><b>bayer_scale</b>
<dd>When <i>bayer</i> dithering is selected, this option defines the scale of the pattern (how much the crosshatch pattern is visible). A low value means more visible pattern for less banding, and higher value means less visible pattern at the cost of more banding. 

 The option must be an integer value in the range [0,5]. Default is <i>2</i>.
<dt><b>diff_mode</b>
<dd>If set, define the zone to process
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>rectangle</b>
<dd>Only the changing rectangle will be reprocessed. This is similar to <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> cropping/offsetting compression mechanism. This option can be useful for speed if only a part of the image is changing, and has use cases such as limiting the scope of the error diffusal <b>dither</b> to the rectangle that bounds the moving scene (it leads to more deterministic output if the scene doesn't change much, and as a result less moving noise and better <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> compression).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <i>none</i>.</dl><dt><b>new</b>
<dd>Take new palette for each output frame.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use a palette (generated for example with <b>palettegen</b>) to encode a <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.mkv -i palette.png -lavfi paletteuse output.gif</pre></dl><h3>perspective</h3>Correct perspective of video not recorded perpendicular to the screen. 

 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x0</b>
<dd><dt><b>y0</b>
<dd><dt><b>x1</b>
<dd><dt><b>y1</b>
<dd><dt><b>x2</b>
<dd><dt><b>y2</b>
<dd><dt><b>x3</b>
<dd><dt><b>y3</b>
<dd>Set coordinates expression for top left, top right, bottom left and bottom right corners. Default values are <tt>&quot;0:0:W:0:0:H:W:H&quot;</tt> with which perspective will remain unchanged. If the <tt>&quot;sense&quot;</tt> option is set to <tt>&quot;source&quot;</tt>, then the specified points will be sent to the corners of the destination. If the <tt>&quot;sense&quot;</tt> option is set to <tt>&quot;destination&quot;</tt>, then the corners of the source will be sent to the specified coordinates. 

 The expressions can use the following variables:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>W</b>
<dd><dt><b>H</b>
<dd>the width and height of video frame.
<dt><b>in</b>
<dd>Input frame count.
<dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Output frame count.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>interpolation</b>
<dd>Set interpolation for perspective correction. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>linear</b>
<dd><dt><b>cubic</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>linear</b>.</dl><dt><b>sense</b>
<dd>Set interpretation of coordinate options. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, source</b>
<dd>Send point in the source specified by the given coordinates to the corners of the destination.
<dt><b>1, destination</b>
<dd>Send the corners of the source to the point in the destination specified by the given coordinates. 

 Default value is <b>source</b>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Set when the expressions for coordinates <b>x0,y0,...x3,y3</b> are evaluated. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or when a command is processed
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>evaluate expressions for each incoming frame</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>init</b>.</dl></dl><h3>phase</h3>Delay interlaced video by one field time so that the field order changes. 

 The intended use is to fix <font SIZE="-1">PAL</font> movies that have been captured with the opposite field order to the film-to-video transfer. 

 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set phase mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>t</b>
<dd>Capture field order top-first, transfer bottom-first. Filter will delay the bottom field.
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd>Capture field order bottom-first, transfer top-first. Filter will delay the top field.
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd>Capture and transfer with the same field order. This mode only exists for the documentation of the other options to refer to, but if you actually select it, the filter will faithfully do nothing.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>Capture field order determined automatically by field flags, transfer opposite. Filter selects among <b>t</b> and <b>b</b> modes on a frame by frame basis using field flags. If no field information is available, then this works just like <b>u</b>.
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd>Capture unknown or varying, transfer opposite. Filter selects among <b>t</b> and <b>b</b> on a frame by frame basis by analyzing the images and selecting the alternative that produces best match between the fields.
<dt><b>T</b>
<dd>Capture top-first, transfer unknown or varying. Filter selects among <b>t</b> and <b>p</b> using image analysis.
<dt><b>B</b>
<dd>Capture bottom-first, transfer unknown or varying. Filter selects among <b>b</b> and <b>p</b> using image analysis.
<dt><b>A</b>
<dd>Capture determined by field flags, transfer unknown or varying. Filter selects among <b>t</b>, <b>b</b> and <b>p</b> using field flags and image analysis. If no field information is available, then this works just like <b>U</b>. This is the default mode.
<dt><b>U</b>
<dd>Both capture and transfer unknown or varying. Filter selects among <b>t</b>, <b>b</b> and <b>p</b> using image analysis only.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>pixdesctest</h3>Pixel format descriptor test filter, mainly useful for internal testing. The output video should be equal to the input video. 

 For example: 

 <pre> format=monow, pixdesctest</pre>can be used to test the monowhite pixel format descriptor definition.
<h3>pixscope</h3>Display sample values of color channels. Mainly useful for checking color and levels. Minimum supported resolution is 640x480. 

 The filters accept the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>x</b>
<dd>Set scope X position, relative offset on X axis.
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Set scope Y position, relative offset on Y axis.
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd>Set scope width.
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd>Set scope height.
<dt><b>o</b>
<dd>Set window opacity. This window also holds statistics about pixel area.
<dt><b>wx</b>
<dd>Set window X position, relative offset on X axis.
<dt><b>wy</b>
<dd>Set window Y position, relative offset on Y axis.</dl><h3>pp</h3>Enable the specified chain of postprocessing subfilters using libpostproc. This library should be automatically selected with a <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> build (<tt>&quot;--enable-gpl&quot;</tt>). Subfilters must be separated by '/' and can be disabled by prepending a '-'. Each subfilter and some options have a short and a long name that can be used interchangeably, i.e. dr/dering are the same. 

 The filters accept the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>subfilters</b>
<dd>Set postprocessing subfilters string.</dl>
 

 All subfilters share common options to determine their scope:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>a/autoq</b>
<dd>Honor the quality commands for this subfilter.
<dt><b>c/chrom</b>
<dd>Do chrominance filtering, too (default).
<dt><b>y/nochrom</b>
<dd>Do luminance filtering only (no chrominance).
<dt><b>n/noluma</b>
<dd>Do chrominance filtering only (no luminance).</dl>
 

 These options can be appended after the subfilter name, separated by a '|'. 

 Available subfilters are:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>hb/hdeblock[|difference[|flatness]]</b>
<dd>Horizontal deblocking filter
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>difference</b>
<dd>Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>32</tt>).
<dt><b>flatness</b>
<dd>Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>39</tt>).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>vb/vdeblock[|difference[|flatness]]</b>
<dd>Vertical deblocking filter
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>difference</b>
<dd>Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>32</tt>).
<dt><b>flatness</b>
<dd>Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>39</tt>).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>ha/hadeblock[|difference[|flatness]]</b>
<dd>Accurate horizontal deblocking filter
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>difference</b>
<dd>Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>32</tt>).
<dt><b>flatness</b>
<dd>Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>39</tt>).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>va/vadeblock[|difference[|flatness]]</b>
<dd>Accurate vertical deblocking filter
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>difference</b>
<dd>Difference factor where higher values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>32</tt>).
<dt><b>flatness</b>
<dd>Flatness threshold where lower values mean more deblocking (default: <tt>39</tt>).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 The horizontal and vertical deblocking filters share the difference and flatness values so you cannot set different horizontal and vertical thresholds.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>h1/x1hdeblock</b>
<dd>Experimental horizontal deblocking filter
<dt><b>v1/x1vdeblock</b>
<dd>Experimental vertical deblocking filter
<dt><b>dr/dering</b>
<dd>Deringing filter
<dt><b>tn/tmpnoise[|threshold1[|threshold2[|threshold3]]], temporal noise reducer</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold1</b>
<dd>larger -&gt; stronger filtering
<dt><b>threshold2</b>
<dd>larger -&gt; stronger filtering
<dt><b>threshold3</b>
<dd>larger -&gt; stronger filtering</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>al/autolevels[:f/fullyrange], automatic brightness / contrast correction</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>f/fullyrange</b>
<dd>Stretch luminance to <tt>&quot;0-255&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>lb/linblenddeint</b>
<dd>Linear blend deinterlacing filter that deinterlaces the given block by filtering all lines with a <tt>&quot;(1 2 1)&quot;</tt> filter.
<dt><b>li/linipoldeint</b>
<dd>Linear interpolating deinterlacing filter that deinterlaces the given block by linearly interpolating every second line.
<dt><b>ci/cubicipoldeint</b>
<dd>Cubic interpolating deinterlacing filter deinterlaces the given block by cubically interpolating every second line.
<dt><b>md/mediandeint</b>
<dd>Median deinterlacing filter that deinterlaces the given block by applying a median filter to every second line.
<dt><b>fd/ffmpegdeint</b>
<dd>FFmpeg deinterlacing filter that deinterlaces the given block by filtering every second line with a <tt>&quot;(-1 4 2 4 -1)&quot;</tt> filter.
<dt><b>l5/lowpass5</b>
<dd>Vertically applied <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> lowpass deinterlacing filter that deinterlaces the given block by filtering all lines with a <tt>&quot;(-1 2 6 2 -1)&quot;</tt> filter.
<dt><b>fq/forceQuant[|quantizer]</b>
<dd>Overrides the quantizer table from the input with the constant quantizer you specify.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>quantizer</b>
<dd>Quantizer to use</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>de/default</b>
<dd>Default pp filter combination (<tt>&quot;hb|a,vb|a,dr|a&quot;</tt>)
<dt><b>fa/fast</b>
<dd>Fast pp filter combination (<tt>&quot;h1|a,v1|a,dr|a&quot;</tt>)
<dt><b>ac</b>
<dd>High quality pp filter combination (<tt>&quot;ha|a|128|7,va|a,dr|a&quot;</tt>)</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply horizontal and vertical deblocking, deringing and automatic brightness/contrast: 

 <pre> pp=hb/vb/dr/al</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply default filters without brightness/contrast correction: 

 <pre> pp=de/-al</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply default filters and temporal denoiser: 

 <pre> pp=default/tmpnoise|1|2|3</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply deblocking on luminance only, and switch vertical deblocking on or off automatically depending on available <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> time: 

 <pre> pp=hb|y/vb|a</pre></dl><h3>pp7</h3>Apply Postprocessing filter 7. It is variant of the <b>spp</b> filter, similar to spp = 6 with 7 point <font SIZE="-1">DCT,</font> where only the center sample is used after <font SIZE="-1">IDCT.</font> 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>qp</b>
<dd>Force a constant quantization parameter. It accepts an integer in range 0 to 63. If not set, the filter will use the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the video stream (if available).
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set thresholding mode. Available modes are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>hard</b>
<dd>Set hard thresholding.
<dt><b>soft</b>
<dd>Set soft thresholding (better de-ringing effect, but likely blurrier).
<dt><b>medium</b>
<dd>Set medium thresholding (good results, default).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>premultiply</h3>Apply alpha premultiply effect to input video stream using first plane of second stream as alpha. 

 Both streams must have same dimensions and same pixel format. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
<dt><b>inplace</b>
<dd>Do not require 2nd input for processing, instead use alpha plane from input stream.</dl><h3>prewitt</h3>Apply prewitt operator to input video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd>Set value which will be multiplied with filtered result.
<dt><b>delta</b>
<dd>Set value which will be added to filtered result.</dl><h3>pseudocolor</h3>Alter frame colors in video with pseudocolors. 

 This filter accept the following options:
