<dl COMPACT><dt><b>c0</b>
<dd>set pixel first component expression
<dt><b>c1</b>
<dd>set pixel second component expression
<dt><b>c2</b>
<dd>set pixel third component expression
<dt><b>c3</b>
<dd>set pixel fourth component expression, corresponds to the alpha component
<dt><b>i</b>
<dd>set component to use as base for altering colors</dl>
 

 Each of them specifies the expression to use for computing the lookup table for the corresponding pixel component values. 

 The expressions can contain the following constants and functions:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>The input width and height.
<dt><b>val</b>
<dd>The input value for the pixel component.
<dt><b>ymin, umin, vmin, amin</b>
<dd>The minimum allowed component value.
<dt><b>ymax, umax, vmax, amax</b>
<dd>The maximum allowed component value.</dl>
 

 All expressions default to ``val''. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Change too high luma values to gradient: 

 <pre> pseudocolor=&quot;'if(between(val,ymax,amax),lerp(ymin,ymax,(val-ymax)/(amax-ymax)),-1):if(between(val,ymax,amax),lerp(umax,umin,(val-ymax)/(amax-ymax)),-1):if(between(val,ymax,amax),lerp(vmin,vmax,(val-ymax)/(amax-ymax)),-1):-1'&quot;</pre></dl><h3>psnr</h3>Obtain the average, maximum and minimum <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> (Peak Signal to Noise Ratio) between two input videos. 

 This filter takes in input two input videos, the first input is considered the ``main'' source and is passed unchanged to the output. The second input is used as a ``reference'' video for computing the <font SIZE="-1">PSNR.</font> 

 Both video inputs must have the same resolution and pixel format for this filter to work correctly. Also it assumes that both inputs have the same number of frames, which are compared one by one. 

 The obtained average <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> is printed through the logging system. 

 The filter stores the accumulated <font SIZE="-1">MSE</font> (mean squared error) of each frame, and at the end of the processing it is averaged across all frames equally, and the following formula is applied to obtain the <font SIZE="-1">PSNR:</font> 

 <pre> PSNR = 10*log10(MAX^2/MSE)</pre>Where <font SIZE="-1">MAX</font> is the average of the maximum values of each component of the image. 

 The description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>stats_file, f</b>
<dd>If specified the filter will use the named file to save the <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> of each individual frame. When filename equals ``-'' the data is sent to standard output.
<dt><b>stats_version</b>
<dd>Specifies which version of the stats file format to use. Details of each format are written below. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>stats_add_max</b>
<dd>Determines whether the max value is output to the stats log. Default value is 0. Requires stats_version &gt;= 2. If this is set and stats_version &lt; 2, the filter will return an error.</dl>
 

 This filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options. 

 The file printed if <i>stats_file</i> is selected, contains a sequence of key/value pairs of the form <i>key</i>:<i>value</i> for each compared couple of frames. 

 If a <i>stats_version</i> greater than 1 is specified, a header line precedes the list of per-frame-pair stats, with key value pairs following the frame format with the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>psnr_log_version</b>
<dd>The version of the log file format. Will match <i>stats_version</i>.
<dt><b>fields</b>
<dd>A comma separated list of the per-frame-pair parameters included in the log.</dl>
 

 A description of each shown per-frame-pair parameter follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>sequential number of the input frame, starting from 1
<dt><b>mse_avg</b>
<dd>Mean Square Error pixel-by-pixel average difference of the compared frames, averaged over all the image components.
<dt><b>mse_y, mse_u, mse_v, mse_r, mse_g, mse_g, mse_a</b>
<dd>Mean Square Error pixel-by-pixel average difference of the compared frames for the component specified by the suffix.
<dt><b>psnr_y, psnr_u, psnr_v, psnr_r, psnr_g, psnr_b, psnr_a</b>
<dd>Peak Signal to Noise ratio of the compared frames for the component specified by the suffix.
<dt><b>max_avg, max_y, max_u, max_v</b>
<dd>Maximum allowed value for each channel, and average over all channels.</dl>
 

 For example: 

 <pre> movie=ref_movie.mpg, setpts=PTS-STARTPTS [main];
 [main][ref] psnr=&quot;stats_file=stats.log&quot; [out]</pre>On this example the input file being processed is compared with the reference file <i>ref_movie.mpg</i>. The <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> of each individual frame is stored in <i>stats.log</i>.
<h3>pullup</h3>Pulldown reversal (inverse telecine) filter, capable of handling mixed hard-telecine, 24000/1001 fps progressive, and 30000/1001 fps progressive content. 

 The pullup filter is designed to take advantage of future context in making its decisions. This filter is stateless in the sense that it does not lock onto a pattern to follow, but it instead looks forward to the following fields in order to identify matches and rebuild progressive frames. 

 To produce content with an even framerate, insert the fps filter after pullup, use <tt>&quot;fps=24000/1001&quot;</tt> if the input frame rate is 29.97fps, <tt>&quot;fps=24&quot;</tt> for 30fps and the (rare) telecined 25fps input. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>jl</b>
<dd><dt><b>jr</b>
<dd><dt><b>jt</b>
<dd><dt><b>jb</b>
<dd>These options set the amount of ``junk'' to ignore at the left, right, top, and bottom of the image, respectively. Left and right are in units of 8 pixels, while top and bottom are in units of 2 lines. The default is 8 pixels on each side.
<dt><b>sb</b>
<dd>Set the strict breaks. Setting this option to 1 will reduce the chances of filter generating an occasional mismatched frame, but it may also cause an excessive number of frames to be dropped during high motion sequences. Conversely, setting it to -1 will make filter match fields more easily. This may help processing of video where there is slight blurring between the fields, but may also cause there to be interlaced frames in the output. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>mp</b>
<dd>Set the metric plane to use. It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>l</b>
<dd>Use luma plane.
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd>Use chroma blue plane.
<dt><b>v</b>
<dd>Use chroma red plane.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>This option may be set to use chroma plane instead of the default luma plane for doing filter's computations. This may improve accuracy on very clean source material, but more likely will decrease accuracy, especially if there is chroma noise (rainbow effect) or any grayscale video. The main purpose of setting <b>mp</b> to a chroma plane is to reduce <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> load and make pullup usable in realtime on slow machines.</dl></dl>
 

 For best results (without duplicated frames in the output file) it is necessary to change the output frame rate. For example, to inverse telecine <font SIZE="-1">NTSC</font> input: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input -vf pullup -r 24000/1001 ...</pre><h3>qp</h3>Change video quantization parameters (<font SIZE="-1">QP</font>). 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>qp</b>
<dd>Set expression for quantization parameter.</dl>
 

 The expression is evaluated through the eval <font SIZE="-1">API</font> and can contain, among others, the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>known</i>
<dd>1 if index is not 129, 0 otherwise.
<dt><i>qp</i>
<dd>Sequential index starting from -129 to 128.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Some equation like: 

 <pre> qp=2+2*sin(PI*qp)</pre></dl><h3>random</h3>Flush video frames from internal cache of frames into a random order. No frame is discarded. Inspired by <b>frei0r</b> nervous filter.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>frames</b>
<dd>Set size in number of frames of internal cache, in range from <tt>2</tt> to <tt>512</tt>. Default is <tt>30</tt>.
<dt><b>seed</b>
<dd>Set seed for random number generator, must be an integer included between <tt>0</tt> and <tt>&quot;UINT32_MAX&quot;</tt>. If not specified, or if explicitly set to less than <tt>0</tt>, the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best effort basis.</dl><h3>readeia608</h3>Read closed captioning (<font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font>) information from the top lines of a video frame. 

 This filter adds frame metadata for <tt>&quot;lavfi.readeia608.X.cc&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;lavfi.readeia608.X.line&quot;</tt>, where <tt>&quot;X&quot;</tt> is the number of the identified line with <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font> data (starting from 0). A description of each metadata value follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>lavfi.readeia608.X.cc</b>
<dd>The two bytes stored as <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font> data (printed in hexadecimal).
<dt><b>lavfi.readeia608.X.line</b>
<dd>The number of the line on which the <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font> data was identified and read.</dl>
 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>scan_min</b>
<dd>Set the line to start scanning for <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font> data. Default is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>scan_max</b>
<dd>Set the line to end scanning for <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font> data. Default is <tt>29</tt>.
<dt><b>mac</b>
<dd>Set minimal acceptable amplitude change for sync codes detection. Default is <tt>0.2</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.001 - 1]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>spw</b>
<dd>Set the ratio of width reserved for sync code detection. Default is <tt>0.27</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.01 - 0.7]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mhd</b>
<dd>Set the max peaks height difference for sync code detection. Default is <tt>0.1</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.0 - 0.5]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mpd</b>
<dd>Set max peaks period difference for sync code detection. Default is <tt>0.1</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.0 - 0.5]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>msd</b>
<dd>Set the first two max start code bits differences. Default is <tt>0.02</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.0 - 0.5]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>bhd</b>
<dd>Set the minimum ratio of bits height compared to 3rd start code bit. Default is <tt>0.75</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.01 - 1]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>th_w</b>
<dd>Set the white color threshold. Default is <tt>0.35</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.1 - 1]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>th_b</b>
<dd>Set the black color threshold. Default is <tt>0.15</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0.0 - 0.5]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>chp</b>
<dd>Enable checking the parity bit. In the event of a parity error, the filter will output <tt>0x00</tt> for that character. Default is false.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Output a csv with presentation time and the first two lines of identified <font SIZE="-1">EIA-608</font> captioning data. 

 <pre> ffprobe -f lavfi -i movie=captioned_video.mov,readeia608 -show_entries frame=pkt_pts_time:frame_tags=lavfi.readeia608.0.cc,lavfi.readeia608.1.cc -of csv</pre></dl><h3>readvitc</h3>Read vertical interval timecode (<font SIZE="-1">VITC</font>) information from the top lines of a video frame. 

 The filter adds frame metadata key <tt>&quot;lavfi.readvitc.tc_str&quot;</tt> with the timecode value, if a valid timecode has been detected. Further metadata key <tt>&quot;lavfi.readvitc.found&quot;</tt> is set to 0/1 depending on whether timecode data has been found or not. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>scan_max</b>
<dd>Set the maximum number of lines to scan for <font SIZE="-1">VITC</font> data. If the value is set to <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt> the full video frame is scanned. Default is <tt>45</tt>.
<dt><b>thr_b</b>
<dd>Set the luma threshold for black. Accepts float numbers in the range [0.0,1.0], default value is <tt>0.2</tt>. The value must be equal or less than <tt>&quot;thr_w&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>thr_w</b>
<dd>Set the luma threshold for white. Accepts float numbers in the range [0.0,1.0], default value is <tt>0.6</tt>. The value must be equal or greater than <tt>&quot;thr_b&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Detect and draw <font SIZE="-1">VITC</font> data onto the video frame; if no valid <font SIZE="-1">VITC</font> is detected, draw <tt>&quot;--:--:--:--&quot;</tt> as a placeholder: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.avi -filter:v 'readvitc,drawtext=fontfile=FreeMono.ttf:text=%{metadata\\:lavfi.readvitc.tc_str\\:--\\\\\\:--\\\\\\:--\\\\\\:--}:x=(w-tw)/2:y=400-ascent'</pre></dl><h3>remap</h3>Remap pixels using 2nd: Xmap and 3rd: Ymap input video stream. 

 Destination pixel at position (X, Y) will be picked from source (x, y) position where x = Xmap(X, Y) and y = Ymap(X, Y). If mapping values are out of range, zero value for pixel will be used for destination pixel. 

 Xmap and Ymap input video streams must be of same dimensions. Output video stream will have Xmap/Ymap video stream dimensions. Xmap and Ymap input video streams are 16bit depth, single channel.
<h3>removegrain</h3>The removegrain filter is a spatial denoiser for progressive video.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>m0</b>
<dd>Set mode for the first plane.
<dt><b>m1</b>
<dd>Set mode for the second plane.
<dt><b>m2</b>
<dd>Set mode for the third plane.
<dt><b>m3</b>
<dd>Set mode for the fourth plane.</dl>
 

 Range of mode is from 0 to 24. Description of each mode follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>0</i>
<dd>Leave input plane unchanged. Default.
<dt><i>1</i>
<dd>Clips the pixel with the minimum and maximum of the 8 neighbour pixels.
<dt><i>2</i>
<dd>Clips the pixel with the second minimum and maximum of the 8 neighbour pixels.
<dt><i>3</i>
<dd>Clips the pixel with the third minimum and maximum of the 8 neighbour pixels.
<dt><i>4</i>
<dd>Clips the pixel with the fourth minimum and maximum of the 8 neighbour pixels. This is equivalent to a median filter.
<dt><i>5</i>
<dd>Line-sensitive clipping giving the minimal change.
<dt><i>6</i>
<dd>Line-sensitive clipping, intermediate.
<dt><i>7</i>
<dd>Line-sensitive clipping, intermediate.
<dt><i>8</i>
<dd>Line-sensitive clipping, intermediate.
<dt><i>9</i>
<dd>Line-sensitive clipping on a line where the neighbours pixels are the closest.
<dt><i>10</i>
<dd>Replaces the target pixel with the closest neighbour.
<dt><i>11</i>
<dd>[1 2 1] horizontal and vertical kernel blur.
<dt><i>12</i>
<dd>Same as mode 11.
<dt><i>13</i>
<dd>Bob mode, interpolates top field from the line where the neighbours pixels are the closest.
<dt><i>14</i>
<dd>Bob mode, interpolates bottom field from the line where the neighbours pixels are the closest.
<dt><i>15</i>
<dd>Bob mode, interpolates top field. Same as 13 but with a more complicated interpolation formula.
<dt><i>16</i>
<dd>Bob mode, interpolates bottom field. Same as 14 but with a more complicated interpolation formula.
<dt><i>17</i>
<dd>Clips the pixel with the minimum and maximum of respectively the maximum and minimum of each pair of opposite neighbour pixels.
<dt><i>18</i>
<dd>Line-sensitive clipping using opposite neighbours whose greatest distance from the current pixel is minimal.
<dt><i>19</i>
<dd>Replaces the pixel with the average of its 8 neighbours.
<dt><i>20</i>
<dd>Averages the 9 pixels ([1 1 1] horizontal and vertical blur).
<dt><i>21</i>
<dd>Clips pixels using the averages of opposite neighbour.
<dt><i>22</i>
<dd>Same as mode 21 but simpler and faster.
<dt><i>23</i>
<dd>Small edge and halo removal, but reputed useless.
<dt><i>24</i>
<dd>Similar as 23.</dl><h3>removelogo</h3>Suppress a <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> station logo, using an image file to determine which pixels comprise the logo. It works by filling in the pixels that comprise the logo with neighboring pixels. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filename, f</b>
<dd>Set the filter bitmap file, which can be any image format supported by libavformat. The width and height of the image file must match those of the video stream being processed.</dl>
 

 Pixels in the provided bitmap image with a value of zero are not considered part of the logo, non-zero pixels are considered part of the logo. If you use white (255) for the logo and black (0) for the rest, you will be safe. For making the filter bitmap, it is recommended to take a screen capture of a black frame with the logo visible, and then using a threshold filter followed by the erode filter once or twice. 

 If needed, little splotches can be fixed manually. Remember that if logo pixels are not covered, the filter quality will be much reduced. Marking too many pixels as part of the logo does not hurt as much, but it will increase the amount of blurring needed to cover over the image and will destroy more information than necessary, and extra pixels will slow things down on a large logo.
<h3>repeatfields</h3>This filter uses the repeat_field flag from the Video <font SIZE="-1">ES</font> headers and hard repeats fields based on its value.
<h3>reverse</h3>Reverse a video clip. 

 Warning: This filter requires memory to buffer the entire clip, so trimming is suggested. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Take the first 5 seconds of a clip, and reverse it. 

 <pre> trim=end=5,reverse</pre></dl><h3>roberts</h3>Apply roberts cross operator to input video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd>Set value which will be multiplied with filtered result.
<dt><b>delta</b>
<dd>Set value which will be added to filtered result.</dl><h3>rotate</h3>Rotate video by an arbitrary angle expressed in radians. 

 The filter accepts the following options: 

 A description of the optional parameters follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>angle, a</b>
<dd>Set an expression for the angle by which to rotate the input video clockwise, expressed as a number of radians. A negative value will result in a counter-clockwise rotation. By default it is set to ``0''. 

 This expression is evaluated for each frame.
<dt><b>out_w, ow</b>
<dd>Set the output width expression, default value is ``iw''. This expression is evaluated just once during configuration.
<dt><b>out_h, oh</b>
<dd>Set the output height expression, default value is ``ih''. This expression is evaluated just once during configuration.
<dt><b>bilinear</b>
<dd>Enable bilinear interpolation if set to 1, a value of 0 disables it. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>fillcolor, c</b>
<dd>Set the color used to fill the output area not covered by the rotated image. For the general syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. If the special value ``none'' is selected then no background is printed (useful for example if the background is never shown). 

 Default value is ``black''.</dl>
 

 The expressions for the angle and the output size can contain the following constants and functions:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>sequential number of the input frame, starting from 0. It is always <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> before the first frame is filtered.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>time in seconds of the input frame, it is set to 0 when the filter is configured. It is always <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> before the first frame is filtered.
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd><dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd>horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><b>in_w, iw</b>
<dd><dt><b>in_h, ih</b>
<dd>the input video width and height
<dt><b>out_w, ow</b>
<dd><dt><b>out_h, oh</b>
<dd>the output width and height, that is the size of the padded area as specified by the <i>width</i> and <i>height</i> expressions
<dt><b>rotw(a)</b>
<dd><dt><b>roth(a)</b>
<dd>the minimal width/height required for completely containing the input video rotated by <i>a</i> radians. 

 These are only available when computing the <b>out_w</b> and <b>out_h</b> expressions.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rotate the input by <font SIZE="-1">PI/6</font> radians clockwise: 

 <pre> rotate=PI/6</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rotate the input by <font SIZE="-1">PI/6</font> radians counter-clockwise: 

 <pre> rotate=-PI/6</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rotate the input by 45 degrees clockwise: 

 <pre> rotate=45*PI/180</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply a constant rotation with period T, starting from an angle of <font SIZE="-1">PI/3:</font> 

 <pre> rotate=PI/3+2*PI*t/T</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Make the input video rotation oscillating with a period of T seconds and an amplitude of A radians: 

 <pre> rotate=A*sin(2*PI/T*t)</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rotate the video, output size is chosen so that the whole rotating input video is always completely contained in the output: 

 <pre> rotate='2*PI*t:ow=hypot(iw,ih):oh=ow'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Rotate the video, reduce the output size so that no background is ever shown: 

 <pre> rotate=2*PI*t:ow='min(iw,ih)/<a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/2-sqrt/">sqrt</a>(2)':oh=ow:c=none</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 The filter supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>a, angle</b>
<dd>Set the angle expression. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.</dl><h3>sab</h3>Apply Shape Adaptive Blur. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>luma_radius, lr</b>
<dd>Set luma blur filter strength, must be a value in range 0.1-4.0, default value is 1.0. A greater value will result in a more blurred image, and in slower processing.
<dt><b>luma_pre_filter_radius, lpfr</b>
<dd>Set luma pre-filter radius, must be a value in the 0.1-2.0 range, default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>luma_strength, ls</b>
<dd>Set luma maximum difference between pixels to still be considered, must be a value in the 0.1-100.0 range, default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>chroma_radius, cr</b>
<dd>Set chroma blur filter strength, must be a value in range -0.9-4.0. A greater value will result in a more blurred image, and in slower processing.
<dt><b>chroma_pre_filter_radius, cpfr</b>
<dd>Set chroma pre-filter radius, must be a value in the -0.9-2.0 range.
<dt><b>chroma_strength, cs</b>
<dd>Set chroma maximum difference between pixels to still be considered, must be a value in the -0.9-100.0 range.</dl>
 

 Each chroma option value, if not explicitly specified, is set to the corresponding luma option value.
<h3>scale</h3>Scale (resize) the input video, using the libswscale library. 

 The scale filter forces the output display aspect ratio to be the same of the input, by changing the output sample aspect ratio. 

 If the input image format is different from the format requested by the next filter, the scale filter will convert the input to the requested format. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The filter accepts the following options, or any of the options supported by the libswscale scaler. 

 See <b>the ffmpeg-scaler manual</b> for the complete list of scaler options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd>Set the output video dimension expression. Default value is the input dimension. 

 If the <i>width</i> or <i>w</i> value is 0, the input width is used for the output. If the <i>height</i> or <i>h</i> value is 0, the input height is used for the output. 

 If one and only one of the values is -n with n &gt;= 1, the scale filter will use a value that maintains the aspect ratio of the input image, calculated from the other specified dimension. After that it will, however, make sure that the calculated dimension is divisible by n and adjust the value if necessary. 

 If both values are -n with n &gt;= 1, the behavior will be identical to both values being set to 0 as previously detailed. 

 See below for the list of accepted constants for use in the dimension expression.
<dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Specify when to evaluate <i>width</i> and <i>height</i> expression. It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>Only evaluate expressions once during the filter initialization or when a command is processed.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>init</b>.</dl><dt><b>interl</b>
<dd>Set the interlacing mode. It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>1</b>
<dd>Force interlaced aware scaling.
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd>Do not apply interlaced scaling.
<dt><b>-1</b>
<dd>Select interlaced aware scaling depending on whether the source frames are flagged as interlaced or not.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>0</b>.</dl><dt><b>flags</b>
<dd>Set libswscale scaling flags. See <b>the ffmpeg-scaler manual</b> for the complete list of values. If not explicitly specified the filter applies the default flags.
<dt><b>param0, param1</b>
<dd>Set libswscale input parameters for scaling algorithms that need them. See <b>the ffmpeg-scaler manual</b> for the complete documentation. If not explicitly specified the filter applies empty parameters.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set the video size. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>in_color_matrix</b>
<dd><dt><b>out_color_matrix</b>
<dd>Set in/output YCbCr color space type. 

 This allows the autodetected value to be overridden as well as allows forcing a specific value used for the output and encoder. 

 If not specified, the color space type depends on the pixel format. 

 Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Choose automatically.
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd>Format conforming to International Telecommunication Union (<font SIZE="-1">ITU</font>) Recommendation <font SIZE="-1">BT.709.</font>
<dt><b>fcc</b>
<dd>Set color space conforming to the United States Federal Communications Commission (<font SIZE="-1">FCC</font>) Code of Federal Regulations (<font SIZE="-1">CFR</font>) Title 47 (2003) 73.682 (a).
<dt><b>bt601</b>
<dd>Set color space conforming to:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd><font SIZE="-1">ITU</font> Radiocommunication Sector (ITU-R) Recommendation <font SIZE="-1">BT.601</font>
<dt>&bull;
<dd>ITU-R Rec. <font SIZE="-1">BT.470-6</font> (1998) Systems B, B1, and G
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (<font SIZE="-1">SMPTE</font>) <font SIZE="-1">ST 170:2004</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>smpte240m</b>
<dd>Set color space conforming to <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE ST 240:1999.</font></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>in_range</b>
<dd><dt><b>out_range</b>
<dd>Set in/output YCbCr sample range. 

 This allows the autodetected value to be overridden as well as allows forcing a specific value used for the output and encoder. If not specified, the range depends on the pixel format. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Choose automatically.
<dt><b>jpeg/full/pc</b>
<dd>Set full range (0-255 in case of 8-bit luma).
<dt><b>mpeg/tv</b>
<dd>Set ``<font SIZE="-1">MPEG''</font> range (16-235 in case of 8-bit luma).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>force_original_aspect_ratio</b>
<dd>Enable decreasing or increasing output video width or height if necessary to keep the original aspect ratio. Possible values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>disable</b>
<dd>Scale the video as specified and disable this feature.
<dt><b>decrease</b>
<dd>The output video dimensions will automatically be decreased if needed.
<dt><b>increase</b>
<dd>The output video dimensions will automatically be increased if needed.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>One useful instance of this option is that when you know a specific device's maximum allowed resolution, you can use this to limit the output video to that, while retaining the aspect ratio. For example, device A allows 1280x720 playback, and your video is 1920x800. Using this option (set it to decrease) and specifying 1280x720 to the command line makes the output 1280x533. 

 Please note that this is a different thing than specifying -1 for <b>w</b> or <b>h</b>, you still need to specify the output resolution for this option to work.</dl></dl>
 

 The values of the <b>w</b> and <b>h</b> options are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>in_w</i>
<dd><dt><i>in_h</i>
<dd>The input width and height
<dt><i>iw</i>
<dd><dt><i>ih</i>
<dd>These are the same as <i>in_w</i> and <i>in_h</i>.
<dt><i>out_w</i>
<dd><dt><i>out_h</i>
<dd>The output (scaled) width and height
<dt><i>ow</i>
<dd><dt><i>oh</i>
<dd>These are the same as <i>out_w</i> and <i>out_h</i>
<dt><i>a</i>
<dd>The same as <i>iw</i> / <i>ih</i>
<dt><i>sar</i>
<dd>input sample aspect ratio
<dt><i>dar</i>
<dd>The input display aspect ratio. Calculated from <tt>&quot;(iw / ih) * sar&quot;</tt>.
<dt><i>hsub</i>
<dd><dt><i>vsub</i>
<dd>horizontal and vertical input chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><i>ohsub</i>
<dd><dt><i>ovsub</i>
<dd>horizontal and vertical output chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Scale the input video to a size of 200x100 

 <pre> scale=w=200:h=100</pre>This is equivalent to: 

 <pre> scale=200:100</pre>or: 

 <pre> scale=200x100</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Specify a size abbreviation for the output size: 

 <pre> scale=qcif</pre>which can also be written as: 

 <pre> scale=size=qcif</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Scale the input to 2x: 

 <pre> scale=w=2*iw:h=2*ih</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>The above is the same as: 

 <pre> scale=2*in_w:2*in_h</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Scale the input to 2x with forced interlaced scaling: 

 <pre> scale=2*iw:2*ih:interl=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Scale the input to half size: 

 <pre> scale=w=iw/2:h=ih/2</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Increase the width, and set the height to the same size: 

 <pre> scale=3/2*iw:ow</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Seek Greek harmony: 

 <pre> scale=iw:1/PHI*iw
 scale=ih*PHI:ih</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Increase the height, and set the width to 3/2 of the height: 

 <pre> scale=w=3/2*oh:h=3/5*ih</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Increase the size, making the size a multiple of the chroma subsample values: 

 <pre> scale=&quot;trunc(3/2*iw/hsub)*hsub:trunc(3/2*ih/vsub)*vsub&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Increase the width to a maximum of 500 pixels, keeping the same aspect ratio as the input: 

 <pre> scale=w='min(500\, iw*3/2):h=-1'</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd>Set the output video dimension expression. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.</dl><h3>scale_npp</h3>Use the <font SIZE="-1">NVIDIA</font> Performance Primitives (libnpp) to perform scaling and/or pixel format conversion on <font SIZE="-1">CUDA</font> video frames. Setting the output width and height works in the same way as for the <i>scale</i> filter. 

 The following additional options are accepted:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>format</b>
<dd>The pixel format of the output <font SIZE="-1">CUDA</font> frames. If set to the string ``same'' (the default), the input format will be kept. Note that automatic format negotiation and conversion is not yet supported for hardware frames
<dt><b>interp_algo</b>
<dd>The interpolation algorithm used for resizing. One of the following:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>nn</b>
<dd>Nearest neighbour.
<dt><b>linear</b>
<dd><dt><b>cubic</b>
<dd><dt><b>cubic2p_bspline</b>
<dd>2-parameter cubic (B=1, C=0)
<dt><b>cubic2p_catmullrom</b>
<dd>2-parameter cubic (B=0, C=1/2)
<dt><b>cubic2p_b05c03</b>
<dd>2-parameter cubic (B=1/2, C=3/10)
<dt><b>super</b>
<dd>Supersampling
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>scale2ref</h3>Scale (resize) the input video, based on a reference video. 

 See the scale filter for available options, scale2ref supports the same but uses the reference video instead of the main input as basis. scale2ref also supports the following additional constants for the <b>w</b> and <b>h</b> options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>main_w</i>
<dd><dt><i>main_h</i>
<dd>The main input video's width and height
<dt><i>main_a</i>
<dd>The same as <i>main_w</i> / <i>main_h</i>
<dt><i>main_sar</i>
<dd>The main input video's sample aspect ratio
<dt><i>main_dar, mdar</i>
<dd>The main input video's display aspect ratio. Calculated from <tt>&quot;(main_w / main_h) * main_sar&quot;</tt>.
<dt><i>main_hsub</i>
<dd><dt><i>main_vsub</i>
<dd>The main input video's horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Scale a subtitle stream (b) to match the main video (a) in size before overlaying 

 <pre> 'scale2ref[b][a];[a][b]overlay'</pre></dl><h3>selectivecolor</h3>Adjust cyan, magenta, yellow and black (<font SIZE="-1">CMYK</font>) to certain ranges of colors (such as ``reds'', ``yellows'', ``greens'', ``cyans'', ...). The adjustment range is defined by the ``purity'' of the color (that is, how saturated it already is). 

 This filter is similar to the Adobe Photoshop Selective Color tool. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>correction_method</b>
<dd>Select color correction method. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>absolute</b>
<dd>Specified adjustments are applied ``as-is'' (added/subtracted to original pixel component value).
<dt><b>relative</b>
<dd>Specified adjustments are relative to the original component value.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;absolute&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>reds</b>
<dd>Adjustments for red pixels (pixels where the red component is the maximum)
<dt><b>yellows</b>
<dd>Adjustments for yellow pixels (pixels where the blue component is the minimum)
<dt><b>greens</b>
<dd>Adjustments for green pixels (pixels where the green component is the maximum)
<dt><b>cyans</b>
<dd>Adjustments for cyan pixels (pixels where the red component is the minimum)
<dt><b>blues</b>
<dd>Adjustments for blue pixels (pixels where the blue component is the maximum)
<dt><b>magentas</b>
<dd>Adjustments for magenta pixels (pixels where the green component is the minimum)
<dt><b>whites</b>
<dd>Adjustments for white pixels (pixels where all components are greater than 128)
<dt><b>neutrals</b>
<dd>Adjustments for all pixels except pure black and pure white
<dt><b>blacks</b>
<dd>Adjustments for black pixels (pixels where all components are lesser than 128)
<dt><b>psfile</b>
<dd>Specify a Photoshop selective color file (<tt>&quot;.asv&quot;</tt>) to import the settings from.</dl>
 

 All the adjustment settings (<b>reds</b>, <b>yellows</b>, ...) accept up to 4 space separated floating point adjustment values in the [-1,1] range, respectively to adjust the amount of cyan, magenta, yellow and black for the pixels of its range. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Increase cyan by 50% and reduce yellow by 33% in every green areas, and increase magenta by 27% in blue areas: 

 <pre> selectivecolor=greens=.5 0 -.33 0:blues=0 .27</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use a Photoshop selective color preset: 

 <pre> selectivecolor=psfile=MySelectiveColorPresets/Misty.asv</pre></dl><h3>separatefields</h3>The <tt>&quot;separatefields&quot;</tt> takes a frame-based video input and splits each frame into its components fields, producing a new half height clip with twice the frame rate and twice the frame count. 

 This filter use field-dominance information in frame to decide which of each pair of fields to place first in the output. If it gets it wrong use <b>setfield</b> filter before <tt>&quot;separatefields&quot;</tt> filter.
<h3>setdar, setsar</h3>The <tt>&quot;setdar&quot;</tt> filter sets the Display Aspect Ratio for the filter output video. 

 This is done by changing the specified Sample (aka Pixel) Aspect Ratio, according to the following equation: 

 <pre> &lt;DAR&gt; = &lt;HORIZONTAL_RESOLUTION&gt; / &lt;VERTICAL_RESOLUTION&gt; * &lt;SAR&gt;</pre>Keep in mind that the <tt>&quot;setdar&quot;</tt> filter does not modify the pixel dimensions of the video frame. Also, the display aspect ratio set by this filter may be changed by later filters in the filterchain, e.g. in case of scaling or if another ``setdar'' or a ``setsar'' filter is applied. 

 The <tt>&quot;setsar&quot;</tt> filter sets the Sample (aka Pixel) Aspect Ratio for the filter output video. 

 Note that as a consequence of the application of this filter, the output display aspect ratio will change according to the equation above. 

 Keep in mind that the sample aspect ratio set by the <tt>&quot;setsar&quot;</tt> filter may be changed by later filters in the filterchain, e.g. if another ``setsar'' or a ``setdar'' filter is applied. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>r, ratio, dar (</b>&quot;setdar&quot;<b> only), sar (</b>&quot;setsar&quot;<b> only)</b>
<dd>Set the aspect ratio used by the filter. 

 The parameter can be a floating point number string, an expression, or a string of the form <i>num</i>:<i>den</i>, where <i>num</i> and <i>den</i> are the numerator and denominator of the aspect ratio. If the parameter is not specified, it is assumed the value ``0''. In case the form &quot;<i>num</i>:<i>den</i>&quot; is used, the <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> character should be escaped.
<dt><b>max</b>
<dd>Set the maximum integer value to use for expressing numerator and denominator when reducing the expressed aspect ratio to a rational. Default value is <tt>100</tt>.</dl>
 

 The parameter <i>sar</i> is an expression containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>E, </b><font SIZE="-1"><b>PI, PHI</b></font>
<dd>These are approximated values for the mathematical constants e (Euler's number), pi (Greek pi), and phi (the golden ratio).
<dt><b>w, h</b>
<dd>The input width and height.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>These are the same as <i>w</i> / <i>h</i>.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>The input sample aspect ratio.
<dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>The input display aspect ratio. It is the same as (<i>w</i> / <i>h</i>) * <i>sar</i>.
<dt><b>hsub, vsub</b>
<dd>Horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example, for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>To change the display aspect ratio to 16:9, specify one of the following: 

 <pre> setdar=dar=1.77777
 setdar=dar=16/9</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>To change the sample aspect ratio to 10:11, specify: 

 <pre> setsar=sar=10/11</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>To set a display aspect ratio of 16:9, and specify a maximum integer value of 1000 in the aspect ratio reduction, use the command: 

 <pre> setdar=ratio=16/9:max=1000</pre></dl><h3>setfield</h3>Force field for the output video frame. 

 The <tt>&quot;setfield&quot;</tt> filter marks the interlace type field for the output frames. It does not change the input frame, but only sets the corresponding property, which affects how the frame is treated by following filters (e.g. <tt>&quot;fieldorder&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;yadif&quot;</tt>). 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>Keep the same field property.
<dt><b>bff</b>
<dd>Mark the frame as bottom-field-first.
<dt><b>tff</b>
<dd>Mark the frame as top-field-first.
<dt><b>prog</b>
<dd>Mark the frame as progressive.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl><h3>showinfo</h3>Show a line containing various information for each input video frame. The input video is not modified. 

 The shown line contains a sequence of key/value pairs of the form <i>key</i>:<i>value</i>. 

 The following values are shown in the output:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>The (sequential) number of the input frame, starting from 0.
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd>The Presentation TimeStamp of the input frame, expressed as a number of time base units. The time base unit depends on the filter input pad.
<dt><b>pts_time</b>
<dd>The Presentation TimeStamp of the input frame, expressed as a number of seconds.
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd>The position of the frame in the input stream, or -1 if this information is unavailable and/or meaningless (for example in case of synthetic video).
<dt><b>fmt</b>
<dd>The pixel format name.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>The sample aspect ratio of the input frame, expressed in the form <i>num</i>/<i>den</i>.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd>The size of the input frame. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>i</b>
<dd>The type of interlaced mode (``P'' for ``progressive'', ``T'' for top field first, ``B'' for bottom field first).
<dt><b>iskey</b>
<dd>This is 1 if the frame is a key frame, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>type</b>
<dd>The picture type of the input frame (``I'' for an I-frame, ``P'' for a P-frame, ``B'' for a B-frame, or ``?'' for an unknown type). Also refer to the documentation of the <tt>&quot;AVPictureType&quot;</tt> enum and of the <tt>&quot;av_get_picture_type_char&quot;</tt> function defined in <i>libavutil/avutil.h</i>.
<dt><b>checksum</b>
<dd>The Adler-32 checksum (printed in hexadecimal) of all the planes of the input frame.
<dt><b>plane_checksum</b>
<dd>The Adler-32 checksum (printed in hexadecimal) of each plane of the input frame, expressed in the form &quot;[<i>c0</i> <i>c1</i> <i>c2</i> <i>c3</i>]&quot;.</dl><h3>showpalette</h3>Displays the 256 colors palette of each frame. This filter is only relevant for <i>pal8</i> pixel format frames. 

 It accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>s</b>
<dd>Set the size of the box used to represent one palette color entry. Default is <tt>30</tt> (for a <tt>&quot;30x30&quot;</tt> pixel box).</dl><h3>shuffleframes</h3>Reorder and/or duplicate and/or drop video frames. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mapping</b>
<dd>Set the destination indexes of input frames. This is space or '|' separated list of indexes that maps input frames to output frames. Number of indexes also sets maximal value that each index may have. '-1' index have special meaning and that is to drop frame.</dl>
 

 The first frame has the index 0. The default is to keep the input unchanged. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Swap second and third frame of every three frames of the input: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf &quot;shuffleframes=0 2 1&quot; OUTPUT</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Swap 10th and 1st frame of every ten frames of the input: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf &quot;shuffleframes=9 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 0&quot; OUTPUT</pre></dl><h3>shuffleplanes</h3>Reorder and/or duplicate video planes. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>map0</b>
<dd>The index of the input plane to be used as the first output plane.
<dt><b>map1</b>
<dd>The index of the input plane to be used as the second output plane.
<dt><b>map2</b>
<dd>The index of the input plane to be used as the third output plane.
<dt><b>map3</b>
<dd>The index of the input plane to be used as the fourth output plane.</dl>
 

 The first plane has the index 0. The default is to keep the input unchanged. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Swap the second and third planes of the input: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf shuffleplanes=0:2:1:3 OUTPUT</pre></dl><h3>signalstats</h3>Evaluate various visual metrics that assist in determining issues associated with the digitization of analog video media. 

 By default the filter will log these metadata values:
<dl COMPACT><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YMIN</b></font>
<dd>Display the minimal Y value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YLOW</b></font>
<dd>Display the Y value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YAVG</b></font>
<dd>Display the average Y value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YHIGH</b></font>
<dd>Display the Y value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YMAX</b></font>
<dd>Display the maximum Y value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UMIN</b></font>
<dd>Display the minimal U value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ULOW</b></font>
<dd>Display the U value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UAVG</b></font>
<dd>Display the average U value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UHIGH</b></font>
<dd>Display the U value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UMAX</b></font>
<dd>Display the maximum U value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VMIN</b></font>
<dd>Display the minimal V value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VLOW</b></font>
<dd>Display the V value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VAVG</b></font>
<dd>Display the average V value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VHIGH</b></font>
<dd>Display the V value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VMAX</b></font>
<dd>Display the maximum V value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATMIN</b></font>
<dd>Display the minimal saturation value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATLOW</b></font>
<dd>Display the saturation value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATAVG</b></font>
<dd>Display the average saturation value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATHIGH</b></font>
<dd>Display the saturation value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATMAX</b></font>
<dd>Display the maximum saturation value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>HUEMED</b></font>
<dd>Display the median value for hue within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-360].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>HUEAVG</b></font>
<dd>Display the average value for hue within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-360].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YDIF</b></font>
<dd>Display the average of sample value difference between all values of the Y plane in the current frame and corresponding values of the previous input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UDIF</b></font>
<dd>Display the average of sample value difference between all values of the U plane in the current frame and corresponding values of the previous input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VDIF</b></font>
<dd>Display the average of sample value difference between all values of the V plane in the current frame and corresponding values of the previous input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YBITDEPTH</b></font>
<dd>Display bit depth of Y plane in current frame. Expressed in range of [0-16].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UBITDEPTH</b></font>
<dd>Display bit depth of U plane in current frame. Expressed in range of [0-16].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VBITDEPTH</b></font>
<dd>Display bit depth of V plane in current frame. Expressed in range of [0-16].</dl>
 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>stat</b>
<dd><dt><b>out</b>
<dd><b>stat</b> specify an additional form of image analysis. <b>out</b> output video with the specified type of pixel highlighted. 

 Both options accept the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>tout</b>
<dd>Identify <i>temporal outliers</i> pixels. A <i>temporal outlier</i> is a pixel unlike the neighboring pixels of the same field. Examples of temporal outliers include the results of video dropouts, head clogs, or tape tracking issues.
<dt><b>vrep</b>
<dd>Identify <i>vertical line repetition</i>. Vertical line repetition includes similar rows of pixels within a frame. In born-digital video vertical line repetition is common, but this pattern is uncommon in video digitized from an analog source. When it occurs in video that results from the digitization of an analog source it can indicate concealment from a dropout compensator.
<dt><b>brng</b>
<dd>Identify pixels that fall outside of legal broadcast range.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>color, c</b>
<dd>Set the highlight color for the <b>out</b> option. The default color is yellow.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Output data of various video metrics: 

 <pre> ffprobe -f lavfi movie=example.mov,signalstats=&quot;stat=tout+vrep+brng&quot; -show_frames</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Output specific data about the minimum and maximum values of the Y plane per frame: 

 <pre> ffprobe -f lavfi movie=example.mov,signalstats -show_entries frame_tags=lavfi.signalstats.YMAX,lavfi.signalstats.YMIN</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Playback video while highlighting pixels that are outside of broadcast range in red. 

 <pre> ffplay example.mov -vf signalstats=&quot;out=brng:color=red&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Playback video with signalstats metadata drawn over the frame. 

 <pre> ffplay example.mov -vf signalstats=stat=brng+vrep+tout,drawtext=fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:textfile=signalstat_drawtext.txt</pre>The contents of signalstat_drawtext.txt used in the command are: 

 <pre> time %{pts:hms}
 Y (%{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.YMIN}-%{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.YMAX})
 U (%{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.UMIN}-%{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.UMAX})
 V (%{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.VMIN}-%{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.VMAX})
 saturation maximum: %{metadata:lavfi.signalstats.SATMAX}</pre></dl><h3>signature</h3>Calculates the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-7</font> Video Signature. The filter can handle more than one input. In this case the matching between the inputs can be calculated additionally. The filter always passes through the first input. The signature of each stream can be written into a file. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>detectmode</b>
<dd>Enable or disable the matching process. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>off</b>
<dd>Disable the calculation of a matching (default).
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd>Calculate the matching for the whole video and output whether the whole video matches or only parts.
<dt><b>fast</b>
<dd>Calculate only until a matching is found or the video ends. Should be faster in some cases.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>nb_inputs</b>
<dd>Set the number of inputs. The option value must be a non negative integer. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>filename</b>
<dd>Set the path to which the output is written. If there is more than one input, the path must be a prototype, i.e. must contain <tt>%d</tt> or <tt>%0nd</tt> (where n is a positive integer), that will be replaced with the input number. If no filename is specified, no output will be written. This is the default.
<dt><b>format</b>
<dd>Choose the output format. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>binary</b>
<dd>Use the specified binary representation (default).
<dt><b>xml</b>
<dd>Use the specified xml representation.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>th_d</b>
<dd>Set threshold to detect one word as similar. The option value must be an integer greater than zero. The default value is 9000.
<dt><b>th_dc</b>
<dd>Set threshold to detect all words as similar. The option value must be an integer greater than zero. The default value is 60000.
<dt><b>th_xh</b>
<dd>Set threshold to detect frames as similar. The option value must be an integer greater than zero. The default value is 116.
<dt><b>th_di</b>
<dd>Set the minimum length of a sequence in frames to recognize it as matching sequence. The option value must be a non negative integer value. The default value is 0.
<dt><b>th_it</b>
<dd>Set the minimum relation, that matching frames to all frames must have. The option value must be a double value between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>To calculate the signature of an input video and store it in signature.bin: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input.mkv -vf signature=filename=signature.bin -map 0:v -f null -</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>To detect whether two videos match and store the signatures in <font SIZE="-1">XML</font> format in signature0.xml and signature1.xml: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input1.mkv -i input2.mkv -filter_complex &quot;[0:v][1:v] signature=nb_inputs=2:detectmode=full:format=xml:filename=signature%d.xml&quot; -map :v -f null -</pre></dl><h3>smartblur</h3>Blur the input video without impacting the outlines. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>luma_radius, lr</b>
<dd>Set the luma radius. The option value must be a float number in the range [0.1,5.0] that specifies the variance of the gaussian filter used to blur the image (slower if larger). Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>luma_strength, ls</b>
<dd>Set the luma strength. The option value must be a float number in the range [-1.0,1.0] that configures the blurring. A value included in [0.0,1.0] will blur the image whereas a value included in [-1.0,0.0] will sharpen the image. Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>luma_threshold, lt</b>
<dd>Set the luma threshold used as a coefficient to determine whether a pixel should be blurred or not. The option value must be an integer in the range [-30,30]. A value of 0 will filter all the image, a value included in [0,30] will filter flat areas and a value included in [-30,0] will filter edges. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>chroma_radius, cr</b>
<dd>Set the chroma radius. The option value must be a float number in the range [0.1,5.0] that specifies the variance of the gaussian filter used to blur the image (slower if larger). Default value is <b>luma_radius</b>.
<dt><b>chroma_strength, cs</b>
<dd>Set the chroma strength. The option value must be a float number in the range [-1.0,1.0] that configures the blurring. A value included in [0.0,1.0] will blur the image whereas a value included in [-1.0,0.0] will sharpen the image. Default value is <b>luma_strength</b>.
<dt><b>chroma_threshold, ct</b>
<dd>Set the chroma threshold used as a coefficient to determine whether a pixel should be blurred or not. The option value must be an integer in the range [-30,30]. A value of 0 will filter all the image, a value included in [0,30] will filter flat areas and a value included in [-30,0] will filter edges. Default value is <b>luma_threshold</b>.</dl>
 

 If a chroma option is not explicitly set, the corresponding luma value is set.
<h3>ssim</h3>Obtain the <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> (Structural SImilarity Metric) between two input videos. 

 This filter takes in input two input videos, the first input is considered the ``main'' source and is passed unchanged to the output. The second input is used as a ``reference'' video for computing the <font SIZE="-1">SSIM.</font> 

 Both video inputs must have the same resolution and pixel format for this filter to work correctly. Also it assumes that both inputs have the same number of frames, which are compared one by one. 

 The filter stores the calculated <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of each frame. 

 The description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>stats_file, f</b>
<dd>If specified the filter will use the named file to save the <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of each individual frame. When filename equals ``-'' the data is sent to standard output.</dl>
 

 The file printed if <i>stats_file</i> is selected, contains a sequence of key/value pairs of the form <i>key</i>:<i>value</i> for each compared couple of frames. 

 A description of each shown parameter follows:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>sequential number of the input frame, starting from 1
<dt><b>Y, U, V, R, G, B</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of the compared frames for the component specified by the suffix.
<dt><b>All</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of the compared frames for the whole frame.
<dt><b>dB</b>
<dd>Same as above but in dB representation.</dl>
 

 This filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options. 

 For example: 

 <pre> movie=ref_movie.mpg, setpts=PTS-STARTPTS [main];
 [main][ref] ssim=&quot;stats_file=stats.log&quot; [out]</pre>On this example the input file being processed is compared with the reference file <i>ref_movie.mpg</i>. The <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of each individual frame is stored in <i>stats.log</i>. 

 Another example with both psnr and ssim at same time: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i main.mpg -i ref.mpg -lavfi &quot;ssim;[0:v][1:v]psnr&quot; -f null -</pre><h3>stereo3d</h3>Convert between different stereoscopic image formats. 

 The filters accept the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>in</b>
<dd>Set stereoscopic image format of input. 

 Available values for input image formats are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>sbsl</b>
<dd>side by side parallel (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbsr</b>
<dd>side by side crosseye (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2l</b>
<dd>side by side parallel with half width resolution (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2r</b>
<dd>side by side crosseye with half width resolution (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>abl</b>
<dd>above-below (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>abr</b>
<dd>above-below (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>ab2l</b>
<dd>above-below with half height resolution (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>ab2r</b>
<dd>above-below with half height resolution (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>al</b>
<dd>alternating frames (left eye first, right eye second)
<dt><b>ar</b>
<dd>alternating frames (right eye first, left eye second)
<dt><b>irl</b>
<dd>interleaved rows (left eye has top row, right eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>irr</b>
<dd>interleaved rows (right eye has top row, left eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>icl</b>
<dd>interleaved columns, left eye first
<dt><b>icr</b>
<dd>interleaved columns, right eye first 

 Default value is <b>sbsl</b>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>out</b>
<dd>Set stereoscopic image format of output.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>sbsl</b>
<dd>side by side parallel (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbsr</b>
<dd>side by side crosseye (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2l</b>
<dd>side by side parallel with half width resolution (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2r</b>
<dd>side by side crosseye with half width resolution (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>abl</b>
<dd>above-below (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>abr</b>
<dd>above-below (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>ab2l</b>
<dd>above-below with half height resolution (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>ab2r</b>
<dd>above-below with half height resolution (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>al</b>
<dd>alternating frames (left eye first, right eye second)
<dt><b>ar</b>
<dd>alternating frames (right eye first, left eye second)
<dt><b>irl</b>
<dd>interleaved rows (left eye has top row, right eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>irr</b>
<dd>interleaved rows (right eye has top row, left eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>arbg</b>
<dd>anaglyph red/blue gray (red filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>argg</b>
<dd>anaglyph red/green gray (red filter on left eye, green filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arcg</b>
<dd>anaglyph red/cyan gray (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arch</b>
<dd>anaglyph red/cyan half colored (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arcc</b>
<dd>anaglyph red/cyan color (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arcd</b>
<dd>anaglyph red/cyan color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmg</b>
<dd>anaglyph green/magenta gray (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmh</b>
<dd>anaglyph green/magenta half colored (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmc</b>
<dd>anaglyph green/magenta colored (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmd</b>
<dd>anaglyph green/magenta color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybg</b>
<dd>anaglyph yellow/blue gray (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybh</b>
<dd>anaglyph yellow/blue half colored (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybc</b>
<dd>anaglyph yellow/blue colored (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybd</b>
<dd>anaglyph yellow/blue color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>ml</b>
<dd>mono output (left eye only)
<dt><b>mr</b>
<dd>mono output (right eye only)
<dt><b>chl</b>
<dd>checkerboard, left eye first
<dt><b>chr</b>
<dd>checkerboard, right eye first
<dt><b>icl</b>
<dd>interleaved columns, left eye first
<dt><b>icr</b>
<dd>interleaved columns, right eye first
<dt><b>hdmi</b>
<dd><font SIZE="-1">HDMI</font> frame pack</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>arcd</b>.</dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Convert input video from side by side parallel to anaglyph yellow/blue dubois: 

 <pre> stereo3d=sbsl:aybd</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Convert input video from above below (left eye above, right eye below) to side by side crosseye. 

 <pre> stereo3d=abl:sbsr</pre></dl><h3>streamselect, astreamselect</h3>Select video or audio streams. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>inputs</b>
<dd>Set number of inputs. Default is 2.
<dt><b>map</b>
<dd>Set input indexes to remap to outputs.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 The <tt>&quot;streamselect&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;astreamselect&quot;</tt> filter supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>map</b>
<dd>Set input indexes to remap to outputs.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Select first 5 seconds 1st stream and rest of time 2nd stream: 

 <pre> sendcmd='5.0 streamselect map 1',streamselect=inputs=2:map=0</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Same as above, but for audio: 

 <pre> asendcmd='5.0 astreamselect map 1',astreamselect=inputs=2:map=0</pre></dl><h3>sobel</h3>Apply sobel operator to input video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd>Set value which will be multiplied with filtered result.
<dt><b>delta</b>
<dd>Set value which will be added to filtered result.</dl><h3>spp</h3>Apply a simple postprocessing filter that compresses and decompresses the image at several (or - in the case of <b>quality</b> level <tt>6</tt> - all) shifts and average the results. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>quality</b>
<dd>Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts an integer in the range 0-6. If set to <tt>0</tt>, the filter will have no effect. A value of <tt>6</tt> means the higher quality. For each increment of that value the speed drops by a factor of approximately 2. Default value is <tt>3</tt>.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd>Force a constant quantization parameter. If not set, the filter will use the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the video stream (if available).
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set thresholding mode. Available modes are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>hard</b>
<dd>Set hard thresholding (default).
<dt><b>soft</b>
<dd>Set soft thresholding (better de-ringing effect, but likely blurrier).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>use_bframe_qp</b>
<dd>Enable the use of the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the B-Frames if set to <tt>1</tt>. Using this option may cause flicker since the B-Frames have often larger <font SIZE="-1">QP.</font> Default is <tt>0</tt> (not enabled).</dl><h3>subtitles</h3>Draw subtitles on top of input video using the libass library. 

 To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libass&quot;</tt>. This filter also requires a build with libavcodec and libavformat to convert the passed subtitles file to <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> (Advanced Substation Alpha) subtitles format. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filename, f</b>
<dd>Set the filename of the subtitle file to read. It must be specified.
<dt><b>original_size</b>
<dd>Specify the size of the original video, the video for which the <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> file was composed. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Due to a misdesign in <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> aspect ratio arithmetic, this is necessary to correctly scale the fonts if the aspect ratio has been changed.
<dt><b>fontsdir</b>
<dd>Set a directory path containing fonts that can be used by the filter. These fonts will be used in addition to whatever the font provider uses.
<dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd>Process alpha channel, by default alpha channel is untouched.
<dt><b>charenc</b>
<dd>Set subtitles input character encoding. <tt>&quot;subtitles&quot;</tt> filter only. Only useful if not <font SIZE="-1">UTF-8.</font>
<dt><b>stream_index, si</b>
<dd>Set subtitles stream index. <tt>&quot;subtitles&quot;</tt> filter only.
<dt><b>force_style</b>
<dd>Override default style or script info parameters of the subtitles. It accepts a string containing <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> style format <tt>&quot;KEY=VALUE&quot;</tt> couples separated by ``,''.</dl>
 

 If the first key is not specified, it is assumed that the first value specifies the <b>filename</b>. 

 For example, to render the file <i>sub.srt</i> on top of the input video, use the command: 

 <pre> subtitles=sub.srt</pre>which is equivalent to: 

 <pre> subtitles=filename=sub.srt</pre>To render the default subtitles stream from file <i>video.mkv</i>, use: 

 <pre> subtitles=video.mkv</pre>To render the second subtitles stream from that file, use: 

 <pre> subtitles=video.mkv:si=1</pre>To make the subtitles stream from <i>sub.srt</i> appear in transparent green <tt>&quot;DejaVu Serif&quot;</tt>, use: 

 <pre> subtitles=sub.srt:force_style='FontName=DejaVu Serif,PrimaryColour=&amp;HAA00FF00'</pre><h3>super2xsai</h3>Scale the input by 2x and smooth using the Super2xSaI (Scale and Interpolate) pixel art scaling algorithm. 

 Useful for enlarging pixel art images without reducing sharpness.
<h3>swaprect</h3>Swap two rectangular objects in video. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>w</b>
<dd>Set object width.
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd>Set object height.
<dt><b>x1</b>
<dd>Set 1st rect x coordinate.
<dt><b>y1</b>
<dd>Set 1st rect y coordinate.
<dt><b>x2</b>
<dd>Set 2nd rect x coordinate.
<dt><b>y2</b>
<dd>Set 2nd rect y coordinate. 

 All expressions are evaluated once for each frame.</dl>
 

 The all options are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>The input width and height.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>same as <i>w</i> / <i>h</i>
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>input sample aspect ratio
<dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (<i>w</i> / <i>h</i>) * <i>sar</i>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd>The number of the input frame, starting from 0.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>The timestamp expressed in seconds. It's <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown.
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd>the position in the file of the input frame, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if unknown</dl><h3>swapuv</h3>Swap U &amp; V plane.
<h3>telecine</h3>Apply telecine process to the video. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>first_field</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>top, t</b>
<dd>top field first
<dt><b>bottom, b</b>
<dd>bottom field first The default value is <tt>&quot;top&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>pattern</b>
<dd>A string of numbers representing the pulldown pattern you wish to apply. The default value is <tt>23</tt>.</dl>
 

 <pre> Some typical patterns:
 
 NTSC output (30i):
 27.5p: 32222
 24p: 23 (classic)
 24p: 2332 (preferred)
 20p: 33
 18p: 334
 16p: 3444
 
 PAL output (25i):
 27.5p: 12222
 24p: 222222222223 (&quot;Euro pulldown&quot;)
 16.67p: 33
 16p: 33333334</pre><h3>threshold</h3>Apply threshold effect to video stream. 

 This filter needs four video streams to perform thresholding. First stream is stream we are filtering. Second stream is holding threshold values, third stream is holding min values, and last, fourth stream is holding max values. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.</dl>
 

 For example if first stream pixel's component value is less then threshold value of pixel component from 2nd threshold stream, third stream value will picked, otherwise fourth stream pixel component value will be picked. 

 Using color source filter one can perform various types of thresholding: 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Binary threshold, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=black -f lavfi -i color=white -lavfi threshold output.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Inverted binary threshold, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=white -f lavfi -i color=black -lavfi threshold output.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Truncate binary threshold, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -lavfi threshold output.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Threshold to zero, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=white -i 320x240.avi -lavfi threshold output.avi</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Inverted threshold to zero, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=white -lavfi threshold output.avi</pre></dl><h3>thumbnail</h3>Select the most representative frame in a given sequence of consecutive frames. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>Set the frames batch size to analyze; in a set of <i>n</i> frames, the filter will pick one of them, and then handle the next batch of <i>n</i> frames until the end. Default is <tt>100</tt>.</dl>
 

 Since the filter keeps track of the whole frames sequence, a bigger <i>n</i> value will result in a higher memory usage, so a high value is not recommended. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Extract one picture each 50 frames: 

 <pre> thumbnail=50</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Complete example of a thumbnail creation with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf thumbnail,scale=300:200 -frames:v 1 out.png</pre></dl><h3>tile</h3>Tile several successive frames together. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>layout</b>
<dd>Set the grid size (i.e. the number of lines and columns). For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>nb_frames</b>
<dd>Set the maximum number of frames to render in the given area. It must be less than or equal to <i>w</i>x<i>h</i>. The default value is <tt>0</tt>, meaning all the area will be used.
<dt><b>margin</b>
<dd>Set the outer border margin in pixels.
<dt><b>padding</b>
<dd>Set the inner border thickness (i.e. the number of pixels between frames). For more advanced padding options (such as having different values for the edges), refer to the pad video filter.
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd>Specify the color of the unused area. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. The default value of <i>color</i> is ``black''.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Produce 8x8 <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> tiles of all keyframes (<b>-skip_frame nokey</b>) in a movie: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -skip_frame nokey -i file.avi -vf 'scale=128:72,tile=8x8' -an -vsync 0 keyframes%03d.png</pre>The <b>-vsync 0</b> is necessary to prevent <b>ffmpeg</b> from duplicating each output frame to accommodate the originally detected frame rate.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Display <tt>5</tt> pictures in an area of <tt>&quot;3x2&quot;</tt> frames, with <tt>7</tt> pixels between them, and <tt>2</tt> pixels of initial margin, using mixed flat and named options: 

 <pre> tile=3x2:nb_frames=5:padding=7:margin=2</pre></dl><h3>tinterlace</h3>Perform various types of temporal field interlacing. 

 Frames are counted starting from 1, so the first input frame is considered odd. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Specify the mode of the interlacing. This option can also be specified as a value alone. See below for a list of values for this option. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>merge, 0</b>
<dd>Move odd frames into the upper field, even into the lower field, generating a double height frame at half frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 
 Output:
 11111 33333
 22222 44444
 11111 33333
 22222 44444
 11111 33333
 22222 44444
 11111 33333
 22222 44444</pre><dt><b>drop_even, 1</b>
<dd>Only output odd frames, even frames are dropped, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 
 Output:
 11111 33333
 11111 33333
 11111 33333
 11111 33333</pre><dt><b>drop_odd, 2</b>
<dd>Only output even frames, odd frames are dropped, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 
 Output:
 22222 44444
 22222 44444
 22222 44444
 22222 44444</pre><dt><b>pad, 3</b>
<dd>Expand each frame to full height, but pad alternate lines with black, generating a frame with double height at the same input frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 
 Output:
 11111 ..... 33333 .....
 ..... 22222 ..... 44444
 11111 ..... 33333 .....
 ..... 22222 ..... 44444
 11111 ..... 33333 .....
 ..... 22222 ..... 44444
 11111 ..... 33333 .....
 ..... 22222 ..... 44444</pre><dt><b>interleave_top, 4</b>
<dd>Interleave the upper field from odd frames with the lower field from even frames, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111&lt;- 22222 33333&lt;- 44444
 11111 22222&lt;- 33333 44444&lt;-
 11111&lt;- 22222 33333&lt;- 44444
 11111 22222&lt;- 33333 44444&lt;-
 
 Output:
 11111 33333
 22222 44444
 11111 33333
 22222 44444</pre><dt><b>interleave_bottom, 5</b>
<dd>Interleave the lower field from odd frames with the upper field from even frames, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222&lt;- 33333 44444&lt;-
 11111&lt;- 22222 33333&lt;- 44444
 11111 22222&lt;- 33333 44444&lt;-
 11111&lt;- 22222 33333&lt;- 44444
 
 Output:
 22222 44444
 11111 33333
 22222 44444
 11111 33333</pre><dt><b>interlacex2, 6</b>
<dd>Double frame rate with unchanged height. Frames are inserted each containing the second temporal field from the previous input frame and the first temporal field from the next input frame. This mode relies on the top_field_first flag. Useful for interlaced video displays with no field synchronisation. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 
 Output:
 11111 22222 22222 33333 33333 44444 44444
 11111 11111 22222 22222 33333 33333 44444
 11111 22222 22222 33333 33333 44444 44444
 11111 11111 22222 22222 33333 33333 44444</pre><dt><b>mergex2, 7</b>
<dd>Move odd frames into the upper field, even into the lower field, generating a double height frame at same frame rate. 

 <pre> ------&gt; time
 Input:
 Frame 1 Frame 2 Frame 3 Frame 4
 
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 11111 22222 33333 44444
 
 Output:
 11111 33333 33333 55555
 22222 22222 44444 44444
 11111 33333 33333 55555
 22222 22222 44444 44444
 11111 33333 33333 55555
 22222 22222 44444 44444
 11111 33333 33333 55555
 22222 22222 44444 44444</pre></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Numeric values are deprecated but are accepted for backward compatibility reasons. 

 Default mode is <tt>&quot;merge&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>flags</b>
<dd>Specify flags influencing the filter process. 

 Available value for <i>flags</i> is:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>low_pass_filter, vlfp</b>
<dd>Enable linear vertical low-pass filtering in the filter. Vertical low-pass filtering is required when creating an interlaced destination from a progressive source which contains high-frequency vertical detail. Filtering will reduce interlace 'twitter' and Moire patterning.
<dt><b>complex_filter, cvlfp</b>
<dd>Enable complex vertical low-pass filtering. This will slightly less reduce interlace 'twitter' and Moire patterning but better retain detail and subjective sharpness impression.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Vertical low-pass filtering can only be enabled for <b>mode</b> <i>interleave_top</i> and <i>interleave_bottom</i>.</dl></dl><h3>tonemap</h3>Tone map colors from different dynamic ranges. 

 This filter expects data in single precision floating point, as it needs to operate on (and can output) out-of-range values. Another filter, such as <b>zscale</b>, is needed to convert the resulting frame to a usable format. 

 The tonemapping algorithms implemented only work on linear light, so input data should be linearized beforehand (and possibly correctly tagged). 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf zscale=transfer=linear,tonemap=clip,zscale=transfer=bt709,format=yuv420p OUTPUT</pre><i>Options</i> 

 The filter accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>tonemap</b>
<dd>Set the tone map algorithm to use. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>none</i>
<dd>Do not apply any tone map, only desaturate overbright pixels.
<dt><i>clip</i>
<dd>Hard-clip any out-of-range values. Use it for perfect color accuracy for in-range values, while distorting out-of-range values.
<dt><i>linear</i>
<dd>Stretch the entire reference gamut to a linear multiple of the display.
<dt><i>gamma</i>
<dd>Fit a logarithmic transfer between the tone curves.
<dt><i>reinhard</i>
<dd>Preserve overall image brightness with a simple curve, using nonlinear contrast, which results in flattening details and degrading color accuracy.
<dt><i>hable</i>
<dd>Preserve both dark and bright details better than <i>reinhard</i>, at the cost of slightly darkening everything. Use it when detail preservation is more important than color and brightness accuracy.
<dt><i>mobius</i>
<dd>Smoothly map out-of-range values, while retaining contrast and colors for in-range material as much as possible. Use it when color accuracy is more important than detail preservation.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is none.</dl><dt><b>param</b>
<dd>Tune the tone mapping algorithm. 

 This affects the following algorithms:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>none</i>
<dd>Ignored.
