<dt><i>linear</i>
<dd>Specifies the scale factor to use while stretching. Default to 1.0.
<dt><i>gamma</i>
<dd>Specifies the exponent of the function. Default to 1.8.
<dt><i>clip</i>
<dd>Specify an extra linear coefficient to multiply into the signal before clipping. Default to 1.0.
<dt><i>reinhard</i>
<dd>Specify the local contrast coefficient at the display peak. Default to 0.5, which means that in-gamut values will be about half as bright as when clipping.
<dt><i>hable</i>
<dd>Ignored.
<dt><i>mobius</i>
<dd>Specify the transition point from linear to mobius transform. Every value below this point is guaranteed to be mapped 1:1. The higher the value, the more accurate the result will be, at the cost of losing bright details. Default to 0.3, which due to the steep initial slope still preserves in-range colors fairly accurately.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>desat</b>
<dd>Apply desaturation for highlights that exceed this level of brightness. The higher the parameter, the more color information will be preserved. This setting helps prevent unnaturally blown-out colors for super-highlights, by (smoothly) turning into white instead. This makes images feel more natural, at the cost of reducing information about out-of-range colors. 

 The default of 2.0 is somewhat conservative and will mostly just apply to skies or directly sunlit surfaces. A setting of 0.0 disables this option. 

 This option works only if the input frame has a supported color tag.
<dt><b>peak</b>
<dd>Override signal/nominal/reference peak with this value. Useful when the embedded peak information in display metadata is not reliable or when tone mapping from a lower range to a higher range.</dl><h3>transpose</h3>Transpose rows with columns in the input video and optionally flip it. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dir</b>
<dd>Specify the transposition direction. 

 Can assume the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, 4, cclock_flip</b>
<dd>Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise and vertically flip (default), that is: 

 <pre> L.R L.l
 . . -&gt; . .
 l.r R.r</pre><dt><b>1, 5, clock</b>
<dd>Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise, that is: 

 <pre> L.R l.L
 . . -&gt; . .
 l.r r.R</pre><dt><b>2, 6, cclock</b>
<dd>Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise, that is: 

 <pre> L.R R.r
 . . -&gt; . .
 l.r L.l</pre><dt><b>3, 7, clock_flip</b>
<dd>Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and vertically flip, that is: 

 <pre> L.R r.R
 . . -&gt; . .
 l.r l.L</pre></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>For values between 4-7, the transposition is only done if the input video geometry is portrait and not landscape. These values are deprecated, the <tt>&quot;passthrough&quot;</tt> option should be used instead. 

 Numerical values are deprecated, and should be dropped in favor of symbolic constants.</dl><dt><b>passthrough</b>
<dd>Do not apply the transposition if the input geometry matches the one specified by the specified value. It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Always apply transposition.
<dt><b>portrait</b>
<dd>Preserve portrait geometry (when <i>height</i> &gt;= <i>width</i>).
<dt><b>landscape</b>
<dd>Preserve landscape geometry (when <i>width</i> &gt;= <i>height</i>).</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl>
 

 For example to rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and preserve portrait layout: 

 <pre> transpose=dir=1:passthrough=portrait</pre>The command above can also be specified as: 

 <pre> transpose=1:portrait</pre><h3>trim</h3>Trim the input so that the output contains one continuous subpart of the input. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>start</b>
<dd>Specify the time of the start of the kept section, i.e. the frame with the timestamp <i>start</i> will be the first frame in the output.
<dt><b>end</b>
<dd>Specify the time of the first frame that will be dropped, i.e. the frame immediately preceding the one with the timestamp <i>end</i> will be the last frame in the output.
<dt><b>start_pts</b>
<dd>This is the same as <i>start</i>, except this option sets the start timestamp in timebase units instead of seconds.
<dt><b>end_pts</b>
<dd>This is the same as <i>end</i>, except this option sets the end timestamp in timebase units instead of seconds.
<dt><b>duration</b>
<dd>The maximum duration of the output in seconds.
<dt><b>start_frame</b>
<dd>The number of the first frame that should be passed to the output.
<dt><b>end_frame</b>
<dd>The number of the first frame that should be dropped.</dl>
 

 <b>start</b>, <b>end</b>, and <b>duration</b> are expressed as time duration specifications; see <b>the Time duration section in the </b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a><b>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. 

 Note that the first two sets of the start/end options and the <b>duration</b> option look at the frame timestamp, while the _frame variants simply count the frames that pass through the filter. Also note that this filter does not modify the timestamps. If you wish for the output timestamps to start at zero, insert a setpts filter after the trim filter. 

 If multiple start or end options are set, this filter tries to be greedy and keep all the frames that match at least one of the specified constraints. To keep only the part that matches all the constraints at once, chain multiple trim filters. 

 The defaults are such that all the input is kept. So it is possible to set e.g. just the end values to keep everything before the specified time. 

 Examples:
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Drop everything except the second minute of input: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf trim=60:120</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Keep only the first second: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf trim=duration=1</pre></dl><h3>unpremultiply</h3>Apply alpha unpremultiply effect to input video stream using first plane of second stream as alpha. 

 Both streams must have same dimensions and same pixel format. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed. 

 If the format has 1 or 2 components, then luma is bit 0. If the format has 3 or 4 components: for <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> formats bit 0 is green, bit 1 is blue and bit 2 is red; for <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> formats bit 0 is luma, bit 1 is chroma-U and bit 2 is chroma-V. If present, the alpha channel is always the last bit.
<dt><b>inplace</b>
<dd>Do not require 2nd input for processing, instead use alpha plane from input stream.</dl><h3>unsharp</h3>Sharpen or blur the input video. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>luma_msize_x, lx</b>
<dd>Set the luma matrix horizontal size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>luma_msize_y, ly</b>
<dd>Set the luma matrix vertical size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>luma_amount, la</b>
<dd>Set the luma effect strength. It must be a floating point number, reasonable values lay between -1.5 and 1.5. 

 Negative values will blur the input video, while positive values will sharpen it, a value of zero will disable the effect. 

 Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>chroma_msize_x, cx</b>
<dd>Set the chroma matrix horizontal size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>chroma_msize_y, cy</b>
<dd>Set the chroma matrix vertical size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>chroma_amount, ca</b>
<dd>Set the chroma effect strength. It must be a floating point number, reasonable values lay between -1.5 and 1.5. 

 Negative values will blur the input video, while positive values will sharpen it, a value of zero will disable the effect. 

 Default value is 0.0.
<dt><b>opencl</b>
<dd>If set to 1, specify using OpenCL capabilities, only available if FFmpeg was configured with <tt>&quot;--enable-opencl&quot;</tt>. Default value is 0.</dl>
 

 All parameters are optional and default to the equivalent of the string '5:5:1.0:5:5:0.0'. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply strong luma sharpen effect: 

 <pre> unsharp=luma_msize_x=7:luma_msize_y=7:luma_amount=2.5</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply a strong blur of both luma and chroma parameters: 

 <pre> unsharp=7:7:-2:7:7:-2</pre></dl><h3>uspp</h3>Apply ultra slow/simple postprocessing filter that compresses and decompresses the image at several (or - in the case of <b>quality</b> level <tt>8</tt> - all) shifts and average the results. 

 The way this differs from the behavior of spp is that uspp actually encodes &amp; decodes each case with libavcodec Snow, whereas spp uses a simplified intra only 8x8 <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> similar to <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG.</font> 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>quality</b>
<dd>Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts an integer in the range 0-8. If set to <tt>0</tt>, the filter will have no effect. A value of <tt>8</tt> means the higher quality. For each increment of that value the speed drops by a factor of approximately 2. Default value is <tt>3</tt>.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd>Force a constant quantization parameter. If not set, the filter will use the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the video stream (if available).</dl><h3>vaguedenoiser</h3>Apply a wavelet based denoiser. 

 It transforms each frame from the video input into the wavelet domain, using Cohen-Daubechies-Feauveau 9/7. Then it applies some filtering to the obtained coefficients. It does an inverse wavelet transform after. Due to wavelet properties, it should give a nice smoothed result, and reduced noise, without blurring picture features. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd>The filtering strength. The higher, the more filtered the video will be. Hard thresholding can use a higher threshold than soft thresholding before the video looks overfiltered. Default value is 2.
<dt><b>method</b>
<dd>The filtering method the filter will use. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>hard</b>
<dd>All values under the threshold will be zeroed.
<dt><b>soft</b>
<dd>All values under the threshold will be zeroed. All values above will be reduced by the threshold.
<dt><b>garrote</b>
<dd>Scales or nullifies coefficients - intermediary between (more) soft and (less) hard thresholding.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is garrote.</dl><dt><b>nsteps</b>
<dd>Number of times, the wavelet will decompose the picture. Picture can't be decomposed beyond a particular point (typically, 8 for a 640x480 frame - as 2^9 = 512 &gt; 480). Valid values are integers between 1 and 32. Default value is 6.
<dt><b>percent</b>
<dd>Partial of full denoising (limited coefficients shrinking), from 0 to 100. Default value is 85.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd>A list of the planes to process. By default all planes are processed.</dl><h3>vectorscope</h3>Display 2 color component values in the two dimensional graph (which is called a vectorscope). 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode, m</b>
<dd>Set vectorscope mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>gray</b>
<dd>Gray values are displayed on graph, higher brightness means more pixels have same component color value on location in graph. This is the default mode.
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd>Gray values are displayed on graph. Surrounding pixels values which are not present in video frame are drawn in gradient of 2 color components which are set by option <tt>&quot;x&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;y&quot;</tt>. The 3rd color component is static.
<dt><b>color2</b>
<dd>Actual color components values present in video frame are displayed on graph.
<dt><b>color3</b>
<dd>Similar as color2 but higher frequency of same values <tt>&quot;x&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;y&quot;</tt> on graph increases value of another color component, which is luminance by default values of <tt>&quot;x&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;y&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>color4</b>
<dd>Actual colors present in video frame are displayed on graph. If two different colors map to same position on graph then color with higher value of component not present in graph is picked.
<dt><b>color5</b>
<dd>Gray values are displayed on graph. Similar to <tt>&quot;color&quot;</tt> but with 3rd color component picked from radial gradient.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>x</b>
<dd>Set which color component will be represented on X-axis. Default is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Set which color component will be represented on Y-axis. Default is <tt>2</tt>.
<dt><b>intensity, i</b>
<dd>Set intensity, used by modes: gray, color, color3 and color5 for increasing brightness of color component which represents frequency of (X, Y) location in graph.
<dt><b>envelope, e</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>No envelope, this is default.
<dt><b>instant</b>
<dd>Instant envelope, even darkest single pixel will be clearly highlighted.
<dt><b>peak</b>
<dd>Hold maximum and minimum values presented in graph over time. This way you can still spot out of range values without constantly looking at vectorscope.
<dt><b>peak+instant</b>
<dd>Peak and instant envelope combined together.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>graticule, g</b>
<dd>Set what kind of graticule to draw.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd><dt><b>green</b>
<dd><dt><b>color</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>opacity, o</b>
<dd>Set graticule opacity.
<dt><b>flags, f</b>
<dd>Set graticule flags.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>white</b>
<dd>Draw graticule for white point.
<dt><b>black</b>
<dd>Draw graticule for black point.
<dt><b>name</b>
<dd>Draw color points short names.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>bgopacity, b</b>
<dd>Set background opacity.
<dt><b>lthreshold, l</b>
<dd>Set low threshold for color component not represented on X or Y axis. Values lower than this value will be ignored. Default is 0. Note this value is multiplied with actual max possible value one pixel component can have. So for 8-bit input and low threshold value of 0.1 actual threshold is 0.1 * 255 = 25.
<dt><b>hthreshold, h</b>
<dd>Set high threshold for color component not represented on X or Y axis. Values higher than this value will be ignored. Default is 1. Note this value is multiplied with actual max possible value one pixel component can have. So for 8-bit input and high threshold value of 0.9 actual threshold is 0.9 * 255 = 230.
<dt><b>colorspace, c</b>
<dd>Set what kind of colorspace to use when drawing graticule.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>auto</b>
<dd><dt><b>601</b>
<dd><dt><b>709</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is auto.</dl></dl><h3>vidstabdetect</h3>Analyze video stabilization/deshaking. Perform pass 1 of 2, see <b>vidstabtransform</b> for pass 2. 

 This filter generates a file with relative translation and rotation transform information about subsequent frames, which is then used by the <b>vidstabtransform</b> filter. 

 To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvidstab&quot;</tt>. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>result</b>
<dd>Set the path to the file used to write the transforms information. Default value is <i>transforms.trf</i>.
<dt><b>shakiness</b>
<dd>Set how shaky the video is and how quick the camera is. It accepts an integer in the range 1-10, a value of 1 means little shakiness, a value of 10 means strong shakiness. Default value is 5.
<dt><b>accuracy</b>
<dd>Set the accuracy of the detection process. It must be a value in the range 1-15. A value of 1 means low accuracy, a value of 15 means high accuracy. Default value is 15.
<dt><b>stepsize</b>
<dd>Set stepsize of the search process. The region around minimum is scanned with 1 pixel resolution. Default value is 6.
<dt><b>mincontrast</b>
<dd>Set minimum contrast. Below this value a local measurement field is discarded. Must be a floating point value in the range 0-1. Default value is 0.3.
<dt><b>tripod</b>
<dd>Set reference frame number for tripod mode. 

 If enabled, the motion of the frames is compared to a reference frame in the filtered stream, identified by the specified number. The idea is to compensate all movements in a more-or-less static scene and keep the camera view absolutely still. 

 If set to 0, it is disabled. The frames are counted starting from 1.
<dt><b>show</b>
<dd>Show fields and transforms in the resulting frames. It accepts an integer in the range 0-2. Default value is 0, which disables any visualization.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use default values: 

 <pre> vidstabdetect</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Analyze strongly shaky movie and put the results in file <i>mytransforms.trf</i>: 

 <pre> vidstabdetect=shakiness=10:accuracy=15:result=&quot;mytransforms.trf&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Visualize the result of internal transformations in the resulting video: 

 <pre> vidstabdetect=show=1</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Analyze a video with medium shakiness using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i input -vf vidstabdetect=shakiness=5:show=1 dummy.avi</pre></dl><h3>vidstabtransform</h3>Video stabilization/deshaking: pass 2 of 2, see <b>vidstabdetect</b> for pass 1. 

 Read a file with transform information for each frame and apply/compensate them. Together with the <b>vidstabdetect</b> filter this can be used to deshake videos. See also &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://public.hronopik.de/vid.stab">http://public.hronopik.de/vid.stab</a></b>&gt;. It is important to also use the <b>unsharp</b> filter, see below. 

 To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvidstab&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>input</b>
<dd>Set path to the file used to read the transforms. Default value is <i>transforms.trf</i>.
<dt><b>smoothing</b>
<dd>Set the number of frames (value*2 + 1) used for lowpass filtering the camera movements. Default value is 10. 

 For example a number of 10 means that 21 frames are used (10 in the past and 10 in the future) to smoothen the motion in the video. A larger value leads to a smoother video, but limits the acceleration of the camera (pan/tilt movements). 0 is a special case where a static camera is simulated.
<dt><b>optalgo</b>
<dd>Set the camera path optimization algorithm. 

 Accepted values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd>gaussian kernel low-pass filter on camera motion (default)
<dt><b>avg</b>
<dd>averaging on transformations</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>maxshift</b>
<dd>Set maximal number of pixels to translate frames. Default value is -1, meaning no limit.
<dt><b>maxangle</b>
<dd>Set maximal angle in radians (degree*PI/180) to rotate frames. Default value is -1, meaning no limit.
<dt><b>crop</b>
<dd>Specify how to deal with borders that may be visible due to movement compensation. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>keep</b>
<dd>keep image information from previous frame (default)
<dt><b>black</b>
<dd>fill the border black</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>invert</b>
<dd>Invert transforms if set to 1. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>relative</b>
<dd>Consider transforms as relative to previous frame if set to 1, absolute if set to 0. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>zoom</b>
<dd>Set percentage to zoom. A positive value will result in a zoom-in effect, a negative value in a zoom-out effect. Default value is 0 (no zoom).
<dt><b>optzoom</b>
<dd>Set optimal zooming to avoid borders. 

 Accepted values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0</b>
<dd>disabled
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd>optimal static zoom value is determined (only very strong movements will lead to visible borders) (default)
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd>optimal adaptive zoom value is determined (no borders will be visible), see <b>zoomspeed</b></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Note that the value given at zoom is added to the one calculated here.</dl><dt><b>zoomspeed</b>
<dd>Set percent to zoom maximally each frame (enabled when <b>optzoom</b> is set to 2). Range is from 0 to 5, default value is 0.25.
<dt><b>interpol</b>
<dd>Specify type of interpolation. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>no</b>
<dd>no interpolation
<dt><b>linear</b>
<dd>linear only horizontal
<dt><b>bilinear</b>
<dd>linear in both directions (default)
<dt><b>bicubic</b>
<dd>cubic in both directions (slow)</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>tripod</b>
<dd>Enable virtual tripod mode if set to 1, which is equivalent to <tt>&quot;relative=0:smoothing=0&quot;</tt>. Default value is 0. 

 Use also <tt>&quot;tripod&quot;</tt> option of <b>vidstabdetect</b>.
<dt><b>debug</b>
<dd>Increase log verbosity if set to 1. Also the detected global motions are written to the temporary file <i>global_motions.trf</i>. Default value is 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use <b>ffmpeg</b> for a typical stabilization with default values: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i inp.mpeg -vf vidstabtransform,unsharp=5:5:0.8:3:3:0.4 inp_stabilized.mpeg</pre>Note the use of the <b>unsharp</b> filter which is always recommended.
<dt>&bull;
<dd>Zoom in a bit more and load transform data from a given file: 

 <pre> vidstabtransform=zoom=5:input=&quot;mytransforms.trf&quot;</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Smoothen the video even more: 

 <pre> vidstabtransform=smoothing=30</pre></dl><h3>vflip</h3>Flip the input video vertically. 

 For example, to vertically flip a video with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf &quot;vflip&quot; out.avi</pre><h3>vignette</h3>Make or reverse a natural vignetting effect. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>angle, a</b>
<dd>Set lens angle expression as a number of radians. 

 The value is clipped in the <tt>&quot;[0,PI/2]&quot;</tt> range. 

 Default value: <tt>&quot;PI/5&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>x0</b>
<dd><dt><b>y0</b>
<dd>Set center coordinates expressions. Respectively <tt>&quot;w/2&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;h/2&quot;</tt> by default.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set forward/backward mode. 

 Available modes are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>forward</b>
<dd>The larger the distance from the central point, the darker the image becomes.
<dt><b>backward</b>
<dd>The larger the distance from the central point, the brighter the image becomes. This can be used to reverse a vignette effect, though there is no automatic detection to extract the lens <b>angle</b> and other settings (yet). It can also be used to create a burning effect.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>forward</b>.</dl><dt><b>eval</b>
<dd>Set evaluation mode for the expressions (<b>angle</b>, <b>x0</b>, <b>y0</b>). 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>init</b>
<dd>Evaluate expressions only once during the filter initialization.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Evaluate expressions for each incoming frame. This is way slower than the <b>init</b> mode since it requires all the scalers to be re-computed, but it allows advanced dynamic expressions.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>init</b>.</dl><dt><b>dither</b>
<dd>Set dithering to reduce the circular banding effects. Default is <tt>1</tt> (enabled).
<dt><b>aspect</b>
<dd>Set vignette aspect. This setting allows one to adjust the shape of the vignette. Setting this value to the <font SIZE="-1">SAR</font> of the input will make a rectangular vignetting following the dimensions of the video. 

 Default is <tt>&quot;1/1&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Expressions</i> 

 The <b>alpha</b>, <b>x0</b> and <b>y0</b> expressions can contain the following parameters.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>w</b>
<dd><dt><b>h</b>
<dd>input width and height
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd>the number of input frame, starting from 0
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd>the <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> (Presentation TimeStamp) time of the filtered video frame, expressed in <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>TB</i></font><i></i> units, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if undefined
<dt><b>r</b>
<dd>frame rate of the input video, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input frame rate is unknown
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd>the <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> (Presentation TimeStamp) of the filtered video frame, expressed in seconds, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if undefined
<dt><b>tb</b>
<dd>time base of the input video</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Apply simple strong vignetting effect: 

 <pre> vignette=PI/4</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Make a flickering vignetting: 

 <pre> vignette='PI/4+<a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/1-random/">random</a>(1)*PI/50':eval=frame</pre></dl><h3>vmafmotion</h3>Obtain the average vmaf motion score of a video. It is one of the component filters of <font SIZE="-1">VMAF.</font> 

 The obtained average motion score is printed through the logging system. 

 In the below example the input file <i>ref.mpg</i> is being processed and score is computed. 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i ref.mpg -lavfi vmafmotion -f null -</pre><h3>vstack</h3>Stack input videos vertically. 

 All streams must be of same pixel format and of same width. 

 Note that this filter is faster than using <b>overlay</b> and <b>pad</b> filter to create same output. 

 The filter accept the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>inputs</b>
<dd>Set number of input streams. Default is 2.
<dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd>If set to 1, force the output to terminate when the shortest input terminates. Default value is 0.</dl><h3>w3fdif</h3>Deinterlace the input video (``w3fdif'' stands for ``Weston 3 Field Deinterlacing Filter''). 

 Based on the process described by Martin Weston for <font SIZE="-1">BBC R&amp;D,</font> and implemented based on the de-interlace algorithm written by Jim Easterbrook for <font SIZE="-1">BBC R&amp;D,</font> the Weston 3 field deinterlacing filter uses filter coefficients calculated by <font SIZE="-1">BBC R&amp;D.</font> 

 There are two sets of filter coefficients, so called ``simple'': and ``complex''. Which set of filter coefficients is used can be set by passing an optional parameter:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filter</b>
<dd>Set the interlacing filter coefficients. Accepts one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>simple</b>
<dd>Simple filter coefficient set.
<dt><b>complex</b>
<dd>More-complex filter coefficient set.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>complex</b>.</dl><dt><b>deint</b>
<dd>Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accept one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>all</b>
<dd>Deinterlace all frames,
<dt><b>interlaced</b>
<dd>Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>all</b>.</dl></dl><h3>waveform</h3>Video waveform monitor. 

 The waveform monitor plots color component intensity. By default luminance only. Each column of the waveform corresponds to a column of pixels in the source video. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode, m</b>
<dd>Can be either <tt>&quot;row&quot;</tt>, or <tt>&quot;column&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;column&quot;</tt>. In row mode, the graph on the left side represents color component value 0 and the right side represents value = 255. In column mode, the top side represents color component value = 0 and bottom side represents value = 255.
<dt><b>intensity, i</b>
<dd>Set intensity. Smaller values are useful to find out how many values of the same luminance are distributed across input rows/columns. Default value is <tt>0.04</tt>. Allowed range is [0, 1].
<dt><b>mirror, r</b>
<dd>Set mirroring mode. <tt>0</tt> means unmirrored, <tt>1</tt> means mirrored. In mirrored mode, higher values will be represented on the left side for <tt>&quot;row&quot;</tt> mode and at the top for <tt>&quot;column&quot;</tt> mode. Default is <tt>1</tt> (mirrored).
<dt><b>display, d</b>
<dd>Set display mode. It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>overlay</b>
<dd>Presents information identical to that in the <tt>&quot;parade&quot;</tt>, except that the graphs representing color components are superimposed directly over one another. 

 This display mode makes it easier to spot relative differences or similarities in overlapping areas of the color components that are supposed to be identical, such as neutral whites, grays, or blacks.
<dt><b>stack</b>
<dd>Display separate graph for the color components side by side in <tt>&quot;row&quot;</tt> mode or one below the other in <tt>&quot;column&quot;</tt> mode.
<dt><b>parade</b>
<dd>Display separate graph for the color components side by side in <tt>&quot;column&quot;</tt> mode or one below the other in <tt>&quot;row&quot;</tt> mode. 

 Using this display mode makes it easy to spot color casts in the highlights and shadows of an image, by comparing the contours of the top and the bottom graphs of each waveform. Since whites, grays, and blacks are characterized by exactly equal amounts of red, green, and blue, neutral areas of the picture should display three waveforms of roughly equal width/height. If not, the correction is easy to perform by making level adjustments the three waveforms.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;stack&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>components, c</b>
<dd>Set which color components to display. Default is 1, which means only luminance or red color component if input is in <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> colorspace. If is set for example to 7 it will display all 3 (if) available color components.
<dt><b>envelope, e</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>No envelope, this is default.
<dt><b>instant</b>
<dd>Instant envelope, minimum and maximum values presented in graph will be easily visible even with small <tt>&quot;step&quot;</tt> value.
<dt><b>peak</b>
<dd>Hold minimum and maximum values presented in graph across time. This way you can still spot out of range values without constantly looking at waveforms.
<dt><b>peak+instant</b>
<dd>Peak and instant envelope combined together.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>filter, f</b>
<dd><dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>lowpass</b>
<dd>No filtering, this is default.
<dt><b>flat</b>
<dd>Luma and chroma combined together.
<dt><b>aflat</b>
<dd>Similar as above, but shows difference between blue and red chroma.
<dt><b>chroma</b>
<dd>Displays only chroma.
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd>Displays actual color value on waveform.
<dt><b>acolor</b>
<dd>Similar as above, but with luma showing frequency of chroma values.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>graticule, g</b>
<dd>Set which graticule to display.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>none</b>
<dd>Do not display graticule.
<dt><b>green</b>
<dd>Display green graticule showing legal broadcast ranges.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>opacity, o</b>
<dd>Set graticule opacity.
<dt><b>flags, fl</b>
<dd>Set graticule flags.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>numbers</b>
<dd>Draw numbers above lines. By default enabled.
<dt><b>dots</b>
<dd>Draw dots instead of lines.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>scale, s</b>
<dd>Set scale used for displaying graticule.
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>digital</b>
<dd><dt><b>millivolts</b>
<dd><dt><b>ire</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is digital.</dl><dt><b>bgopacity, b</b>
<dd>Set background opacity.</dl><h3>weave, doubleweave</h3>The <tt>&quot;weave&quot;</tt> takes a field-based video input and join each two sequential fields into single frame, producing a new double height clip with half the frame rate and half the frame count. 

 The <tt>&quot;doubleweave&quot;</tt> works same as <tt>&quot;weave&quot;</tt> but without halving frame rate and frame count. 

 It accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>first_field</b>
<dd>Set first field. Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>top, t</b>
<dd>Set the frame as top-field-first.
<dt><b>bottom, b</b>
<dd>Set the frame as bottom-field-first.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Interlace video using <b>select</b> and <b>separatefields</b> filter: 

 <pre> separatefields,select=eq(mod(n,4),0)+eq(mod(n,4),3),weave</pre></dl><h3>xbr</h3>Apply the xBR high-quality magnification filter which is designed for pixel art. It follows a set of edge-detection rules, see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.libretro.com/forums/viewtopic.php?f=6">http://www.libretro.com/forums/viewtopic.php?f=6</a>&amp;t=134</b>&gt;. 

 It accepts the following option:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>Set the scaling dimension: <tt>2</tt> for <tt>&quot;2xBR&quot;</tt>, <tt>3</tt> for <tt>&quot;3xBR&quot;</tt> and <tt>4</tt> for <tt>&quot;4xBR&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>3</tt>.</dl><h3>yadif</h3>Deinterlace the input video (``yadif'' means ``yet another deinterlacing filter''). 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>The interlacing mode to adopt. It accepts one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, send_frame</b>
<dd>Output one frame for each frame.
<dt><b>1, send_field</b>
<dd>Output one frame for each field.
<dt><b>2, send_frame_nospatial</b>
<dd>Like <tt>&quot;send_frame&quot;</tt>, but it skips the spatial interlacing check.
<dt><b>3, send_field_nospatial</b>
<dd>Like <tt>&quot;send_field&quot;</tt>, but it skips the spatial interlacing check.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The default value is <tt>&quot;send_frame&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>parity</b>
<dd>The picture field parity assumed for the input interlaced video. It accepts one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, tff</b>
<dd>Assume the top field is first.
<dt><b>1, bff</b>
<dd>Assume the bottom field is first.
<dt><b>-1, auto</b>
<dd>Enable automatic detection of field parity.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The default value is <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt>. If the interlacing is unknown or the decoder does not export this information, top field first will be assumed.</dl><dt><b>deint</b>
<dd>Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accept one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>0, all</b>
<dd>Deinterlace all frames.
<dt><b>1, interlaced</b>
<dd>Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The default value is <tt>&quot;all&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl><h3>zoompan</h3>Apply Zoom &amp; Pan effect. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>zoom, z</b>
<dd>Set the zoom expression. Default is 1.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Set the x and y expression. Default is 0.
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd>Set the duration expression in number of frames. This sets for how many number of frames effect will last for single input image.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd>Set the output image size, default is 'hd720'.
<dt><b>fps</b>
<dd>Set the output frame rate, default is '25'.</dl>
 

 Each expression can contain the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>in_w, iw</b>
<dd>Input width.
<dt><b>in_h, ih</b>
<dd>Input height.
<dt><b>out_w, ow</b>
<dd>Output width.
<dt><b>out_h, oh</b>
<dd>Output height.
<dt><b>in</b>
<dd>Input frame count.
<dt><b>on</b>
<dd>Output frame count.
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd><dt><b>y</b>
<dd>Last calculated 'x' and 'y' position from 'x' and 'y' expression for current input frame.
<dt><b>px</b>
<dd><dt><b>py</b>
<dd>'x' and 'y' of last output frame of previous input frame or 0 when there was not yet such frame (first input frame).
<dt><b>zoom</b>
<dd>Last calculated zoom from 'z' expression for current input frame.
<dt><b>pzoom</b>
<dd>Last calculated zoom of last output frame of previous input frame.
<dt><b>duration</b>
<dd>Number of output frames for current input frame. Calculated from 'd' expression for each input frame.
<dt><b>pduration</b>
<dd>number of output frames created for previous input frame
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>Rational number: input width / input height
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>sample aspect ratio
<dt><b>dar</b>
<dd>display aspect ratio</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Zoom-in up to 1.5 and pan at same time to some spot near center of picture: 

 <pre> zoompan=z='min(zoom+0.0015,1.5)':d=700:x='if(gte(zoom,1.5),x,x+1/a)':y='if(gte(zoom,1.5),y,y+1)':s=640x360</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Zoom-in up to 1.5 and pan always at center of picture: 

 <pre> zoompan=z='min(zoom+0.0015,1.5)':d=700:x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)'</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Same as above but without pausing: 

 <pre> zoompan=z='min(max(zoom,pzoom)+0.0015,1.5)':d=1:x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/2-(ih/zoom/2)'</pre></dl><h3>zscale</h3>Scale (resize) the input video, using the z.lib library: <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/sekrit-twc/zimg.">https://github.com/sekrit-twc/zimg.</a> 

 The zscale filter forces the output display aspect ratio to be the same as the input, by changing the output sample aspect ratio. 

 If the input image format is different from the format requested by the next filter, the zscale filter will convert the input to the requested format. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The filter accepts the following options.
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd><dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd>Set the output video dimension expression. Default value is the input dimension. 

 If the <i>width</i> or <i>w</i> value is 0, the input width is used for the output. If the <i>height</i> or <i>h</i> value is 0, the input height is used for the output. 

 If one and only one of the values is -n with n &gt;= 1, the zscale filter will use a value that maintains the aspect ratio of the input image, calculated from the other specified dimension. After that it will, however, make sure that the calculated dimension is divisible by n and adjust the value if necessary. 

 If both values are -n with n &gt;= 1, the behavior will be identical to both values being set to 0 as previously detailed. 

 See below for the list of accepted constants for use in the dimension expression.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set the video size. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>dither, d</b>
<dd>Set the dither type. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>none</i>
<dd><dt><i>ordered</i>
<dd><dt><i>random</i>
<dd><dt><i>error_diffusion</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is none.</dl><dt><b>filter, f</b>
<dd>Set the resize filter type. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>point</i>
<dd><dt><i>bilinear</i>
<dd><dt><i>bicubic</i>
<dd><dt><i>spline16</i>
<dd><dt><i>spline36</i>
<dd><dt><i>lanczos</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is bilinear.</dl><dt><b>range, r</b>
<dd>Set the color range. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>limited</i>
<dd><dt><i>full</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>primaries, p</b>
<dd>Set the color primaries. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>709</i>
<dd><dt><i>unspecified</i>
<dd><dt><i>170m</i>
<dd><dt><i>240m</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>transfer, t</b>
<dd>Set the transfer characteristics. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>709</i>
<dd><dt><i>unspecified</i>
<dd><dt><i>601</i>
<dd><dt><i>linear</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_10</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_12</i>
<dd><dt><i>smpte2084</i>
<dd><dt><i>iec61966-2-1</i>
<dd><dt><i>arib-std-b67</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>matrix, m</b>
<dd>Set the colorspace matrix. 

 Possible value are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>709</i>
<dd><dt><i>unspecified</i>
<dd><dt><i>470bg</i>
<dd><dt><i>170m</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_ncl</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_cl</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>rangein, rin</b>
<dd>Set the input color range. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>limited</i>
<dd><dt><i>full</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>primariesin, pin</b>
<dd>Set the input color primaries. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>709</i>
<dd><dt><i>unspecified</i>
<dd><dt><i>170m</i>
<dd><dt><i>240m</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>transferin, tin</b>
<dd>Set the input transfer characteristics. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>709</i>
<dd><dt><i>unspecified</i>
<dd><dt><i>601</i>
<dd><dt><i>linear</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_10</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_12</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is same as input.</dl><dt><b>matrixin, min</b>
<dd>Set the input colorspace matrix. 

 Possible value are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>709</i>
<dd><dt><i>unspecified</i>
<dd><dt><i>470bg</i>
<dd><dt><i>170m</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_ncl</i>
<dd><dt><i>2020_cl</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>chromal, c</b>
<dd>Set the output chroma location. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>left</i>
<dd><dt><i>center</i>
<dd><dt><i>topleft</i>
<dd><dt><i>top</i>
<dd><dt><i>bottomleft</i>
<dd><dt><i>bottom</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>chromalin, cin</b>
<dd>Set the input chroma location. 

 Possible values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><i>input</i>
<dd><dt><i>left</i>
<dd><dt><i>center</i>
<dd><dt><i>topleft</i>
<dd><dt><i>top</i>
<dd><dt><i>bottomleft</i>
<dd><dt><i>bottom</i>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl><dt><b>npl</b>
<dd>Set the nominal peak luminance.</dl>
 

 The values of the <b>w</b> and <b>h</b> options are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl COMPACT><dt><i>in_w</i>
<dd><dt><i>in_h</i>
<dd>The input width and height
<dt><i>iw</i>
<dd><dt><i>ih</i>
<dd>These are the same as <i>in_w</i> and <i>in_h</i>.
<dt><i>out_w</i>
<dd><dt><i>out_h</i>
<dd>The output (scaled) width and height
<dt><i>ow</i>
<dd><dt><i>oh</i>
<dd>These are the same as <i>out_w</i> and <i>out_h</i>
<dt><i>a</i>
<dd>The same as <i>iw</i> / <i>ih</i>
<dt><i>sar</i>
<dd>input sample aspect ratio
<dt><i>dar</i>
<dd>The input display aspect ratio. Calculated from <tt>&quot;(iw / ih) * sar&quot;</tt>.
<dt><i>hsub</i>
<dd><dt><i>vsub</i>
<dd>horizontal and vertical input chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.
<dt><i>ohsub</i>
<dd><dt><i>ovsub</i>
<dd>horizontal and vertical output chroma subsample values. For example for the pixel format ``yuv422p'' <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.</dl><h2>Video Sources</h2>Below is a description of the currently available video sources.
<h3>buffer</h3>Buffer video frames, and make them available to the filter chain. 

 This source is mainly intended for a programmatic use, in particular through the interface defined in <i>libavfilter/vsrc_buffer.h</i>. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd>Specify the size (width and height) of the buffered video frames. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>width</b>
<dd>The input video width.
<dt><b>height</b>
<dd>The input video height.
<dt><b>pix_fmt</b>
<dd>A string representing the pixel format of the buffered video frames. It may be a number corresponding to a pixel format, or a pixel format name.
<dt><b>time_base</b>
<dd>Specify the timebase assumed by the timestamps of the buffered frames.
<dt><b>frame_rate</b>
<dd>Specify the frame rate expected for the video stream.
<dt><b>pixel_aspect, sar</b>
<dd>The sample (pixel) aspect ratio of the input video.
<dt><b>sws_param</b>
<dd>Specify the optional parameters to be used for the scale filter which is automatically inserted when an input change is detected in the input size or format.
<dt><b>hw_frames_ctx</b>
<dd>When using a hardware pixel format, this should be a reference to an AVHWFramesContext describing input frames.</dl>
 

 For example: 

 <pre> buffer=width=320:height=240:pix_fmt=yuv410p:time_base=1/24:sar=1</pre>will instruct the source to accept video frames with size 320x240 and with format ``yuv410p'', assuming 1/24 as the timestamps timebase and square pixels (1:1 sample aspect ratio). Since the pixel format with name ``yuv410p'' corresponds to the number 6 (check the enum AVPixelFormat definition in <i>libavutil/pixfmt.h</i>), this example corresponds to: 

 <pre> buffer=size=320x240:pixfmt=6:time_base=1/24:pixel_aspect=1/1</pre>Alternatively, the options can be specified as a flat string, but this syntax is deprecated: 

 <i>width</i>:<i>height</i>:<i>pix_fmt</i>:<i>time_base.num</i>:<i>time_base.den</i>:<i>pixel_aspect.num</i>:<i>pixel_aspect.den</i>[:<i>sws_param</i>]
<h3>cellauto</h3>Create a pattern generated by an elementary cellular automaton. 

 The initial state of the cellular automaton can be defined through the <b>filename</b> and <b>pattern</b> options. If such options are not specified an initial state is created randomly. 

 At each new frame a new row in the video is filled with the result of the cellular automaton next generation. The behavior when the whole frame is filled is defined by the <b>scroll</b> option. 

 This source accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filename, f</b>
<dd>Read the initial cellular automaton state, i.e. the starting row, from the specified file. In the file, each non-whitespace character is considered an alive cell, a newline will terminate the row, and further characters in the file will be ignored.
<dt><b>pattern, p</b>
<dd>Read the initial cellular automaton state, i.e. the starting row, from the specified string. 

 Each non-whitespace character in the string is considered an alive cell, a newline will terminate the row, and further characters in the string will be ignored.
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set the video rate, that is the number of frames generated per second. Default is 25.
<dt><b>random_fill_ratio, ratio</b>
<dd>Set the random fill ratio for the initial cellular automaton row. It is a floating point number value ranging from 0 to 1, defaults to 1/PHI. 

 This option is ignored when a file or a pattern is specified.
<dt><b>random_seed, seed</b>
<dd>Set the seed for filling randomly the initial row, must be an integer included between 0 and <font SIZE="-1">UINT32_MAX.</font> If not specified, or if explicitly set to -1, the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best effort basis.
<dt><b>rule</b>
<dd>Set the cellular automaton rule, it is a number ranging from 0 to 255. Default value is 110.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set the size of the output video. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. 

 If <b>filename</b> or <b>pattern</b> is specified, the size is set by default to the width of the specified initial state row, and the height is set to <i>width</i> * <font SIZE="-1">PHI.</font> 

 If <b>size</b> is set, it must contain the width of the specified pattern string, and the specified pattern will be centered in the larger row. 

 If a filename or a pattern string is not specified, the size value defaults to ``320x518'' (used for a randomly generated initial state).
<dt><b>scroll</b>
<dd>If set to 1, scroll the output upward when all the rows in the output have been already filled. If set to 0, the new generated row will be written over the top row just after the bottom row is filled. Defaults to 1.
<dt><b>start_full, full</b>
<dd>If set to 1, completely fill the output with generated rows before outputting the first frame. This is the default behavior, for disabling set the value to 0.
<dt><b>stitch</b>
<dd>If set to 1, stitch the left and right row edges together. This is the default behavior, for disabling set the value to 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Read the initial state from <i>pattern</i>, and specify an output of size 200x400. 

 <pre> cellauto=f=pattern:s=200x400</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a random initial row with a width of 200 cells, with a fill ratio of 2/3: 

 <pre> cellauto=ratio=2/3:s=200x200</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Create a pattern generated by rule 18 starting by a single alive cell centered on an initial row with width 100: 

 <pre> cellauto=p=@s=100x400:full=0:rule=18</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Specify a more elaborated initial pattern: 

 <pre> cellauto=p='@@ @ @@':s=100x400:full=0:rule=18</pre></dl><h3>coreimagesrc</h3>Video source generated on <font SIZE="-1">GPU</font> using Apple's CoreImage <font SIZE="-1">API</font> on <font SIZE="-1">OSX.</font> 

 This video source is a specialized version of the <b>coreimage</b> video filter. Use a core image generator at the beginning of the applied filterchain to generate the content. 

 The coreimagesrc video source accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>list_generators</b>
<dd>List all available generators along with all their respective options as well as possible minimum and maximum values along with the default values. 

 <pre> list_generators=true</pre><dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Specify the size of the sourced video. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. The default value is <tt>&quot;320x240&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Specify the frame rate of the sourced video, as the number of frames generated per second. It has to be a string in the format <i>frame_rate_num</i>/<i>frame_rate_den</i>, an integer number, a floating point number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. The default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>Set the sample aspect ratio of the sourced video.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd>Set the duration of the sourced video. See <b>the Time duration section in the </b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a><b>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. 

 If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the video is supposed to be generated forever.</dl>
 

 Additionally, all options of the <b>coreimage</b> video filter are accepted. A complete filterchain can be used for further processing of the generated input without CPU-HOST transfer. See <b>coreimage</b> documentation and examples for details. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Use CIQRCodeGenerator to create a <font SIZE="-1">QR</font> code for the FFmpeg homepage, given as complete and escaped command-line for Apple's standard bash shell: 

 <pre> ffmpeg -f lavfi -i coreimagesrc=s=100x100:filter=CIQRCodeGenerator [at] inputMessage=https\\\\\://FFmpeg.org/@inputCorrectionLevel=H -frames:v 1 QRCode.png</pre>This example is equivalent to the QRCode example of <b>coreimage</b> without the need for a nullsrc video source.</dl><h3>mandelbrot</h3>Generate a Mandelbrot set fractal, and progressively zoom towards the point specified with <i>start_x</i> and <i>start_y</i>. 

 This source accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>end_pts</b>
<dd>Set the terminal pts value. Default value is 400.
<dt><b>end_scale</b>
<dd>Set the terminal scale value. Must be a floating point value. Default value is 0.3.
<dt><b>inner</b>
<dd>Set the inner coloring mode, that is the algorithm used to draw the Mandelbrot fractal internal region. 

 It shall assume one of the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>black</b>
<dd>Set black mode.
<dt><b>convergence</b>
<dd>Show time until convergence.
<dt><b>mincol</b>
<dd>Set color based on point closest to the origin of the iterations.
<dt><b>period</b>
<dd>Set period mode.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>mincol</i>.</dl><dt><b>bailout</b>
<dd>Set the bailout value. Default value is 10.0.
<dt><b>maxiter</b>
<dd>Set the maximum of iterations performed by the rendering algorithm. Default value is 7189.
<dt><b>outer</b>
<dd>Set outer coloring mode. It shall assume one of following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>iteration_count</b>
<dd>Set iteration cound mode.
<dt><b>normalized_iteration_count</b>
<dd>set normalized iteration count mode.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <i>normalized_iteration_count</i>.</dl><dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set frame rate, expressed as number of frames per second. Default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set frame size. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual. Default value is ``640x480''.
<dt><b>start_scale</b>
<dd>Set the initial scale value. Default value is 3.0.
<dt><b>start_x</b>
<dd>Set the initial x position. Must be a floating point value between -100 and 100. Default value is -0.743643887037158704752191506114774.
<dt><b>start_y</b>
<dd>Set the initial y position. Must be a floating point value between -100 and 100. Default value is -0.131825904205311970493132056385139.</dl><h3>mptestsrc</h3>Generate various test patterns, as generated by the MPlayer test filter. 

 The size of the generated video is fixed, and is 256x256. This source is useful in particular for testing encoding features. 

 This source accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Specify the frame rate of the sourced video, as the number of frames generated per second. It has to be a string in the format <i>frame_rate_num</i>/<i>frame_rate_den</i>, an integer number, a floating point number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. The default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd>Set the duration of the sourced video. See <b>the Time duration section in the </b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a><b>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. 

 If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the video is supposed to be generated forever.
<dt><b>test, t</b>
<dd>Set the number or the name of the test to perform. Supported tests are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>dc_luma</b>
<dd><dt><b>dc_chroma</b>
<dd><dt><b>freq_luma</b>
<dd><dt><b>freq_chroma</b>
<dd><dt><b>amp_luma</b>
<dd><dt><b>amp_chroma</b>
<dd><dt><b>cbp</b>
<dd><dt><b>mv</b>
<dd><dt><b>ring1</b>
<dd><dt><b>ring2</b>
<dd><dt><b>all</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is ``all'', which will cycle through the list of all tests.</dl></dl>
 

 Some examples: 

 <pre> mptestsrc=t=dc_luma</pre>will generate a ``dc_luma'' test pattern.
<h3>frei0r_src</h3>Provide a frei0r source. 

 To enable compilation of this filter you need to install the frei0r header and configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-frei0r&quot;</tt>. 

 This source accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>size</b>
<dd>The size of the video to generate. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd>The framerate of the generated video. It may be a string of the form <i>num</i>/<i>den</i> or a frame rate abbreviation.
<dt><b>filter_name</b>
<dd>The name to the frei0r source to load. For more information regarding frei0r and how to set the parameters, read the <b>frei0r</b> section in the video filters documentation.
<dt><b>filter_params</b>
<dd>A '|'-separated list of parameters to pass to the frei0r source.</dl>
 

 For example, to generate a frei0r partik0l source with size 200x200 and frame rate 10 which is overlaid on the overlay filter main input: 

 <pre> frei0r_src=size=200x200:framerate=10:filter_name=partik0l:filter_params=1234 [overlay]; [in][overlay] overlay</pre><h3>life</h3>Generate a life pattern. 

 This source is based on a generalization of John Conway's life game. 

 The sourced input represents a life grid, each pixel represents a cell which can be in one of two possible states, alive or dead. Every cell interacts with its eight neighbours, which are the cells that are horizontally, vertically, or diagonally adjacent. 

 At each interaction the grid evolves according to the adopted rule, which specifies the number of neighbor alive cells which will make a cell stay alive or born. The <b>rule</b> option allows one to specify the rule to adopt. 

 This source accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>filename, f</b>
<dd>Set the file from which to read the initial grid state. In the file, each non-whitespace character is considered an alive cell, and newline is used to delimit the end of each row. 

 If this option is not specified, the initial grid is generated randomly.
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set the video rate, that is the number of frames generated per second. Default is 25.
<dt><b>random_fill_ratio, ratio</b>
<dd>Set the random fill ratio for the initial random grid. It is a floating point number value ranging from 0 to 1, defaults to 1/PHI. It is ignored when a file is specified.
<dt><b>random_seed, seed</b>
<dd>Set the seed for filling the initial random grid, must be an integer included between 0 and <font SIZE="-1">UINT32_MAX.</font> If not specified, or if explicitly set to -1, the filter will try to use a good random seed on a best effort basis.
<dt><b>rule</b>
<dd>Set the life rule. 

 A rule can be specified with a code of the kind &quot;S<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NS</i></font><i></i>/B<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NB</i></font><i></i>&quot;, where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NS</i></font><i></i> and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NB</i></font><i></i> are sequences of numbers in the range 0-8, <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NS</i></font><i></i> specifies the number of alive neighbor cells which make a live cell stay alive, and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NB</i></font><i></i> the number of alive neighbor cells which make a dead cell to become alive (i.e. to ``born''). ``s'' and ``b'' can be used in place of ``S'' and ``B'', respectively. 

 Alternatively a rule can be specified by an 18-bits integer. The 9 high order bits are used to encode the next cell state if it is alive for each number of neighbor alive cells, the low order bits specify the rule for ``borning'' new cells. Higher order bits encode for an higher number of neighbor cells. For example the number 6153 = <tt>&quot;(12&lt;&lt;9)+9&quot;</tt> specifies a stay alive rule of 12 and a born rule of 9, which corresponds to ``S23/B03''. 

 Default value is ``S23/B3'', which is the original Conway's game of life rule, and will keep a cell alive if it has 2 or 3 neighbor alive cells, and will born a new cell if there are three alive cells around a dead cell.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set the size of the output video. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. 

 If <b>filename</b> is specified, the size is set by default to the same size of the input file. If <b>size</b> is set, it must contain the size specified in the input file, and the initial grid defined in that file is centered in the larger resulting area. 

 If a filename is not specified, the size value defaults to ``320x240'' (used for a randomly generated initial grid).
<dt><b>stitch</b>
<dd>If set to 1, stitch the left and right grid edges together, and the top and bottom edges also. Defaults to 1.
<dt><b>mold</b>
<dd>Set cell mold speed. If set, a dead cell will go from <b>death_color</b> to <b>mold_color</b> with a step of <b>mold</b>. <b>mold</b> can have a value from 0 to 255.
<dt><b>life_color</b>
<dd>Set the color of living (or new born) cells.
<dt><b>death_color</b>
<dd>Set the color of dead cells. If <b>mold</b> is set, this is the first color used to represent a dead cell.
<dt><b>mold_color</b>
<dd>Set mold color, for definitely dead and moldy cells. 

 For the syntax of these 3 color options, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Read a grid from <i>pattern</i>, and center it on a grid of size 300x300 pixels: 

 <pre> life=f=pattern:s=300x300</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Generate a random grid of size 200x200, with a fill ratio of 2/3: 

 <pre> life=ratio=2/3:s=200x200</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Specify a custom rule for evolving a randomly generated grid: 

 <pre> life=rule=S14/B34</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Full example with slow death effect (mold) using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi life=s=300x200:mold=10:r=60:ratio=0.1:death_color=#C83232:life_color=#00ff00,scale=1200:800:flags=16</pre></dl><h3>allrgb, allyuv, color, haldclutsrc, nullsrc, rgbtestsrc, smptebars, smptehdbars, testsrc, testsrc2, yuvtestsrc</h3>The <tt>&quot;allrgb&quot;</tt> source returns frames of size 4096x4096 of all rgb colors. 

 The <tt>&quot;allyuv&quot;</tt> source returns frames of size 4096x4096 of all yuv colors. 

 The <tt>&quot;color&quot;</tt> source provides an uniformly colored input. 

 The <tt>&quot;haldclutsrc&quot;</tt> source provides an identity Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT.</font> See also <b>haldclut</b> filter. 

 The <tt>&quot;nullsrc&quot;</tt> source returns unprocessed video frames. It is mainly useful to be employed in analysis / debugging tools, or as the source for filters which ignore the input data. 

 The <tt>&quot;rgbtestsrc&quot;</tt> source generates an <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> test pattern useful for detecting <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> vs <font SIZE="-1">BGR</font> issues. You should see a red, green and blue stripe from top to bottom. 

 The <tt>&quot;smptebars&quot;</tt> source generates a color bars pattern, based on the <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE</font> Engineering Guideline <font SIZE="-1">EG 1-1990.</font> 

 The <tt>&quot;smptehdbars&quot;</tt> source generates a color bars pattern, based on the <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE RP 219-2002.</font> 

 The <tt>&quot;testsrc&quot;</tt> source generates a test video pattern, showing a color pattern, a scrolling gradient and a timestamp. This is mainly intended for testing purposes. 

 The <tt>&quot;testsrc2&quot;</tt> source is similar to testsrc, but supports more pixel formats instead of just <tt>&quot;rgb24&quot;</tt>. This allows using it as an input for other tests without requiring a format conversion. 

 The <tt>&quot;yuvtestsrc&quot;</tt> source generates an <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> test pattern. You should see a y, cb and cr stripe from top to bottom. 

 The sources accept the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd>Specify the alpha (opacity) of the background, only available in the <tt>&quot;testsrc2&quot;</tt> source. The value must be between 0 (fully transparent) and 255 (fully opaque, the default).
<dt><b>color, c</b>
<dd>Specify the color of the source, only available in the <tt>&quot;color&quot;</tt> source. For the syntax of this option, check the ``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual.
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd>Specify the level of the Hald <font SIZE="-1">CLUT,</font> only available in the <tt>&quot;haldclutsrc&quot;</tt> source. A level of <tt>&quot;N&quot;</tt> generates a picture of <tt>&quot;N*N*N&quot;</tt> by <tt>&quot;N*N*N&quot;</tt> pixels to be used as identity matrix for 3D lookup tables. Each component is coded on a <tt>&quot;1/(N*N)&quot;</tt> scale.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Specify the size of the sourced video. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. The default value is <tt>&quot;320x240&quot;</tt>. 

 This option is not available with the <tt>&quot;haldclutsrc&quot;</tt> filter.
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Specify the frame rate of the sourced video, as the number of frames generated per second. It has to be a string in the format <i>frame_rate_num</i>/<i>frame_rate_den</i>, an integer number, a floating point number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. The default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd>Set the sample aspect ratio of the sourced video.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd>Set the duration of the sourced video. See <b>the Time duration section in the </b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a><b>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. 

 If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the video is supposed to be generated forever.
<dt><b>decimals, n</b>
<dd>Set the number of decimals to show in the timestamp, only available in the <tt>&quot;testsrc&quot;</tt> source. 

 The displayed timestamp value will correspond to the original timestamp value multiplied by the power of 10 of the specified value. Default value is 0.</dl>
 

 For example the following: 

 <pre> testsrc=duration=5.3:size=qcif:rate=10</pre>will generate a video with a duration of 5.3 seconds, with size 176x144 and a frame rate of 10 frames per second. 

 The following graph description will generate a red source with an opacity of 0.2, with size ``qcif'' and a frame rate of 10 frames per second. 

 <pre> color=c=red@0.2:s=qcif:r=10</pre>If the input content is to be ignored, <tt>&quot;nullsrc&quot;</tt> can be used. The following command generates noise in the luminance plane by employing the <tt>&quot;geq&quot;</tt> filter: 

 <pre> nullsrc=s=256x256, geq=<a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/1-random/">random</a>(1)*255:128:128</pre><i>Commands</i> 

 The <tt>&quot;color&quot;</tt> source supports the following commands:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>c, color</b>
<dd>Set the color of the created image. Accepts the same syntax of the corresponding <b>color</b> option.</dl><h2>Video Sinks</h2>Below is a description of the currently available video sinks.
<h3>buffersink</h3>Buffer video frames, and make them available to the end of the filter graph. 

 This sink is mainly intended for programmatic use, in particular through the interface defined in <i>libavfilter/buffersink.h</i> or the options system. 

 It accepts a pointer to an AVBufferSinkContext structure, which defines the incoming buffers' formats, to be passed as the opaque parameter to <tt>&quot;avfilter_init_filter&quot;</tt> for initialization.
<h3>nullsink</h3>Null video sink: do absolutely nothing with the input video. It is mainly useful as a template and for use in analysis / debugging tools.
<h2>Multimedia Filters</h2>Below is a description of the currently available multimedia filters.
<h3>abitscope</h3>Convert input audio to a video output, displaying the audio bit scope. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set frame rate, expressed as number of frames per second. Default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;1024x256&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>colors</b>
<dd>Specify list of colors separated by space or by '|' which will be used to draw channels. Unrecognized or missing colors will be replaced by white color.</dl><h3>ahistogram</h3>Convert input audio to a video output, displaying the volume histogram. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>dmode</b>
<dd>Specify how histogram is calculated. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>single</b>
<dd>Use single histogram for all channels.
<dt><b>separate</b>
<dd>Use separate histogram for each channel.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;single&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set frame rate, expressed as number of frames per second. Default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;hd720&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd>Set display scale. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>log</b>
<dd>logarithmic
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd>square root
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd>cubic root
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd>linear
<dt><b>rlog</b>
<dd>reverse logarithmic</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>ascale</b>
<dd>Set amplitude scale. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>log</b>
<dd>logarithmic
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd>linear</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>acount</b>
<dd>Set how much frames to accumulate in histogram. Defauls is 1. Setting this to -1 accumulates all frames.
<dt><b>rheight</b>
<dd>Set histogram ratio of window height.
<dt><b>slide</b>
<dd>Set sonogram sliding. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>replace</b>
<dd>replace old rows with new ones.
<dt><b>scroll</b>
<dd>scroll from top to bottom.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;replace&quot;</tt>.</dl></dl><h3>aphasemeter</h3>Convert input audio to a video output, displaying the audio phase. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set the output frame rate. Default value is <tt>25</tt>.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;800x400&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rc</b>
<dd><dt><b>gc</b>
<dd><dt><b>bc</b>
<dd>Specify the red, green, blue contrast. Default values are <tt>2</tt>, <tt>7</tt> and <tt>1</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0, 255]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mpc</b>
<dd>Set color which will be used for drawing median phase. If color is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt> which is default, no median phase value will be drawn.
<dt><b>video</b>
<dd>Enable video output. Default is enabled.</dl>
 

 The filter also exports the frame metadata <tt>&quot;lavfi.aphasemeter.phase&quot;</tt> which represents mean phase of current audio frame. Value is in range <tt>&quot;[-1, 1]&quot;</tt>. The <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt> means left and right channels are completely out of phase and <tt>1</tt> means channels are in phase.
<h3>avectorscope</h3>Convert input audio to a video output, representing the audio vector scope. 

 The filter is used to measure the difference between channels of stereo audio stream. A monoaural signal, consisting of identical left and right signal, results in straight vertical line. Any stereo separation is visible as a deviation from this line, creating a Lissajous figure. If the straight (or deviation from it) but horizontal line appears this indicates that the left and right channels are out of phase. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>mode, m</b>
<dd>Set the vectorscope mode. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>lissajous</b>
<dd>Lissajous rotated by 45 degrees.
<dt><b>lissajous_xy</b>
<dd>Same as above but not rotated.
<dt><b>polar</b>
<dd>Shape resembling half of circle.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>lissajous</b>.</dl><dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd>Set the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;400x400&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd>Set the output frame rate. Default value is <tt>25</tt>.
<dt><b>rc</b>
<dd><dt><b>gc</b>
<dd><dt><b>bc</b>
<dd><dt><b>ac</b>
<dd>Specify the red, green, blue and alpha contrast. Default values are <tt>40</tt>, <tt>160</tt>, <tt>80</tt> and <tt>255</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0, 255]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rf</b>
<dd><dt><b>gf</b>
<dd><dt><b>bf</b>
<dd><dt><b>af</b>
<dd>Specify the red, green, blue and alpha fade. Default values are <tt>15</tt>, <tt>10</tt>, <tt>5</tt> and <tt>5</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0, 255]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>zoom</b>
<dd>Set the zoom factor. Default value is <tt>1</tt>. Allowed range is <tt>&quot;[0, 10]&quot;</tt>. Values lower than <i>1</i> will auto adjust zoom factor to maximal possible value.
<dt><b>draw</b>
<dd>Set the vectorscope drawing mode. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>dot</b>
<dd>Draw dot for each sample.
<dt><b>line</b>
<dd>Draw line between previous and current sample.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default value is <b>dot</b>.</dl><dt><b>scale</b>
<dd>Specify amplitude scale of audio samples. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>lin</b>
<dd>Linear.
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd>Square root.
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd>Cubic root.
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd>Logarithmic.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Complete example using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre> ffplay -f lavfi 'amovie=input.mp3, asplit [a][out1];
 [a] avectorscope=zoom=1.3:rc=2:gc=200:bc=10:rf=1:gf=8:bf=7 [out0]'</pre></dl><h3>bench, abench</h3>Benchmark part of a filtergraph. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>action</b>
<dd>Start or stop a timer. 

 Available values are:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>start</b>
<dd>Get the current time, set it as frame metadata (using the key <tt>&quot;lavfi.bench.start_time&quot;</tt>), and forward the frame to the next filter.
<dt><b>stop</b>
<dd>Get the current time and fetch the <tt>&quot;lavfi.bench.start_time&quot;</tt> metadata from the input frame metadata to get the time difference. Time difference, average, maximum and minimum time (respectively <tt>&quot;t&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;avg&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;max&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;min&quot;</tt>) are then printed. The timestamps are expressed in seconds.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd></dl></dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Benchmark <b>selectivecolor</b> filter: 

 <pre> bench=start,selectivecolor=reds=-.2 .12 -.49,bench=stop</pre></dl><h3>concat</h3>Concatenate audio and video streams, joining them together one after the other. 

 The filter works on segments of synchronized video and audio streams. All segments must have the same number of streams of each type, and that will also be the number of streams at output. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>n</b>
<dd>Set the number of segments. Default is 2.
<dt><b>v</b>
<dd>Set the number of output video streams, that is also the number of video streams in each segment. Default is 1.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd>Set the number of output audio streams, that is also the number of audio streams in each segment. Default is 0.
<dt><b>unsafe</b>
<dd>Activate unsafe mode: do not fail if segments have a different format.</dl>
 

 The filter has <i>v</i>+<i>a</i> outputs: first <i>v</i> video outputs, then <i>a</i> audio outputs. 

 There are <i>n</i>x(<i>v</i>+<i>a</i>) inputs: first the inputs for the first segment, in the same order as the outputs, then the inputs for the second segment, etc. 

 Related streams do not always have exactly the same duration, for various reasons including codec frame size or sloppy authoring. For that reason, related synchronized streams (e.g. a video and its audio track) should be concatenated at once. The concat filter will use the duration of the longest stream in each segment (except the last one), and if necessary pad shorter audio streams with silence. 

 For this filter to work correctly, all segments must start at timestamp 0. 

 All corresponding streams must have the same parameters in all segments; the filtering system will automatically select a common pixel format for video streams, and a common sample format, sample rate and channel layout for audio streams, but other settings, such as resolution, must be converted explicitly by the user. 

 Different frame rates are acceptable but will result in variable frame rate at output; be sure to configure the output file to handle it. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl COMPACT><dt>&bull;
<dd>Concatenate an opening, an episode and an ending, all in bilingual version (video in stream 0, audio in streams 1 and 2): 

 <pre> ffmpeg -i opening.mkv -i episode.mkv -i ending.mkv -filter_complex \
 '[0:0] [0:1] [0:2] [1:0] [1:1] [1:2] [2:0] [2:1] [2:2]
 concat=n=3:v=1:a=2 [v] [a1] [a2]' \
 -map '[v]' -map '[a1]' -map '[a2]' output.mkv</pre><dt>&bull;
<dd>Concatenate two parts, handling audio and video separately, using the (a)movie sources, and adjusting the resolution: 

 <pre> movie=part1.mp4, scale=512:288 [v1] ; amovie=part1.mp4 [a1] ;
 movie=part2.mp4, scale=512:288 [v2] ; amovie=part2.mp4 [a2] ;
 [v1] [v2] concat [outv] ; [a1] [a2] concat=v=0:a=1 [outa]</pre>Note that a desync will happen at the stitch if the audio and video streams do not have exactly the same duration in the first file.</dl><h3>drawgraph, adrawgraph</h3>Draw a graph using input video or audio metadata. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>m1</b>
<dd>Set 1st frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
<dt><b>fg1</b>
<dd>Set 1st foreground color expression.
<dt><b>m2</b>
<dd>Set 2nd frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
<dt><b>fg2</b>
<dd>Set 2nd foreground color expression.
<dt><b>m3</b>
<dd>Set 3rd frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
<dt><b>fg3</b>
<dd>Set 3rd foreground color expression.
<dt><b>m4</b>
<dd>Set 4th frame metadata key from which metadata values will be used to draw a graph.
<dt><b>fg4</b>
<dd>Set 4th foreground color expression.
<dt><b>min</b>
<dd>Set minimal value of metadata value.
<dt><b>max</b>
<dd>Set maximal value of metadata value.
<dt><b>bg</b>
<dd>Set graph background color. Default is white.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd>Set graph mode. 

 Available values for mode is:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>bar</b>
<dd><dt><b>dot</b>
<dd><dt><b>line</b>
<dd></dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;line&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>slide</b>
<dd>Set slide mode. 

 Available values for slide is:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><b>frame</b>
<dd>Draw new frame when right border is reached.
<dt><b>replace</b>
<dd>Replace old columns with new ones.
<dt><b>scroll</b>
<dd>Scroll from right to left.
<dt><b>rscroll</b>
<dd>Scroll from left to right.
<dt><b>picture</b>
<dd>Draw single picture.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>Default is <tt>&quot;frame&quot;</tt>.</dl><dt><b>size</b>
<dd>Set size of graph video. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. The default value is <tt>&quot;900x256&quot;</tt>. 

 The foreground color expressions can use the following variables:
<dl COMPACT><dd><dl COMPACT><dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>MIN</b></font>
<dd>Minimal value of metadata value.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>MAX</b></font>
<dd>Maximal value of metadata value.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VAL</b></font>
<dd>Current metadata key value.</dl></dl><dl COMPACT><dd>The color is defined as 0xAABBGGRR.</dl></dl>
 

 Example using metadata from <b>signalstats</b> filter: 

 <pre> signalstats,drawgraph=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:min=0:max=255</pre>Example using metadata from <b>ebur128</b> filter: 

 <pre> ebur128=metadata=1,adrawgraph=lavfi.r128.M:min=-120:max=5</pre><h3>ebur128</h3><font SIZE="-1">EBU R128</font> scanner filter. This filter takes an audio stream as input and outputs it unchanged. By default, it logs a message at a frequency of 10Hz with the Momentary loudness (identified by <tt>&quot;M&quot;</tt>), Short-term loudness (<tt>&quot;S&quot;</tt>), Integrated loudness (<tt>&quot;I&quot;</tt>) and Loudness Range (<tt>&quot;LRA&quot;</tt>). 

 The filter also has a video output (see the <i>video</i> option) with a real time graph to observe the loudness evolution. The graphic contains the logged message mentioned above, so it is not printed anymore when this option is set, unless the verbose logging is set. The main graphing area contains the short-term loudness (3 seconds of analysis), and the gauge on the right is for the momentary loudness (400 milliseconds). 

 More information about the Loudness Recommendation <font SIZE="-1">EBU R128</font> on &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://tech.ebu.ch/loudness">http://tech.ebu.ch/loudness</a></b>&gt;. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl COMPACT><dt><b>video</b>
<dd>Activate the video output. The audio stream is passed unchanged whether this option is set or no. The video stream will be the first output stream if activated. Default is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>size</b>
<dd>Set the video size. This option is for video only. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default and minimum resolution is <tt>&quot;640x480&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>meter</b>
